Defence Force service reported at the 2021 Census, split by regular against reserves and by current against previous service. The ABS defines it as \"The Australian Defence Force (ADF) consists of regulars and reservists, and this variable provides a detailed breakdown of current and previous service for both\", and it is new in 2021, so the ACLD data item list marks the 2011 and 2016 columns \"Not available\". ADFP_21 on the same row is the four-category summary of the same answer, and both are asked only of people aged 15 years and over.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian Defence Force service, detailed (ADCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/service-australian-defence-force/australian-defence-force-service-detailed-adcp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Australian Defence Force Service, Detailed","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 Australian Defence Force service, detailed (8 categories)","def":"Codes 1 to 8 covering the eight combinations of regular and reserves service, current and previous, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. The ACLD recodes the Census supplementary categories as two-digit numbers here, unlike the 997/998/999 used on the age items.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian Defence Force service, detailed (ADCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/service-australian-defence-force/australian-defence-force-service-detailed-adcp","lim":"It cannot date or measure service. The categories say whether service happened, not when it began, how long it ran or whether it was broken, and the ABS notes the variable does not capture breaks in service. Because there is no 2011 or 2016 column, a person cannot be tracked into or out of the ADF across the ACLD panel; 2021 is the only observation.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":0},{"n":"ADFP_21","d":"Whether the person was serving in, or had previously served in, the Australian Defence Force at the 2021 Census.","full":"Whether the person was serving in, or had previously served in, the Australian Defence Force at the 2021 Census. The ABS defines it as \"This variable describes whether a person is currently serving or has previously served in the Australian Defence Force (ADF)\", asked of people aged 15 years and over, with a non-response rate of 6.0% in 2021. The question was asked for the first time in 2021, so the ACLD has no 2011 or 2016 counterpart, and ADCP_21 splits the same answer into eight regular-and-reserves combinations.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian Defence Force service (ADFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/service-australian-defence-force/australian-defence-force-service-adfp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Australian Defence Force Service","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 Australian Defence Force service (4 categories)","def":"Codes 1 to 4: currently serving in the regular service, currently serving in the reserves service, not currently serving but has previously served, and has never served. Supplementary codes are 97 not stated, 98 not applicable for people under 15 years, and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian Defence Force service (ADFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/service-australian-defence-force/australian-defence-force-service-adfp","lim":"It only counts Australian service. A veteran of a foreign defence force reads as \"Has never served in the Australian Defence Force\", so the column cannot be used to identify ex-service people in migrant populations. Category 3 also merges former regulars with former reservists, and ADCP_21 is needed to separate them.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":1},{"n":"AGEN_11","d":"Age in completed years at the 2011 Census, held as a continuous variable so that sums, means and medians can be taken.","full":"Age in completed years at the 2011 Census, held as a continuous variable so that sums, means and medians can be taken. The ABS data item list defines it as \"a person's age at last birthday\", adding that \"Age is calculated from date of birth, however if this is not provided, stated age will be used. If neither is provided, age is imputed.\" AGEP_11 carries the same answer as a categorical item capped at 85 years and over, so AGEN_11 is the column to use for arithmetic; its range runs to 110, wider than the 0 to 105 used for 2016 and 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Continuous Variables, Age of Person (continuous)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Person (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 age in completed years (continuous)","def":"Whole years, 0 to 110 singly, with 999 for an unlinked record. There is no not-stated code, because age is imputed when neither date of birth nor stated age is given.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Continuous Variables, Age of Person (continuous)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"999 is a linkage marker, not an age, and averaging it in as a number pulls a mean age up by orders of magnitude. AGEN_11 also exists only on the 2011-2016-2021 table, so a cohort assembled from the 2016-2021 table has no 2011 age at all and cannot be aligned to this column.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":2},{"n":"AGEN_16","d":"Age in completed years at the 2016 Census, held as a continuous variable for sums, means and medians.","full":"Age in completed years at the 2016 Census, held as a continuous variable for sums, means and medians. The ABS data item list gives the same derivation as at 2011 — date of birth first, stated age next, imputation last — and notes that \"For continuous variables range, sum, mean and medians can be calculated\"; it narrows the range to 0 to 105 years, where the 2011 column ran to 110. It appears on both ACLD tables, the 2011-2016-2021 file and the 2016-2021 file, and AGEP_16 holds the same answer in categorical form capped at 85 years and over.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Continuous Variables, Age of Person (continuous)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Person (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 age in completed years (continuous)","def":"Whole years, 0 to 105 singly, with 999 for an unlinked record and no not-stated code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Continuous Variables, Age of Person (continuous)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"A difference between AGEN_11 and AGEN_16 is not a clean five-year ageing check. The ACLD ships CFAGEP_11_16 precisely because linked records disagree, with categories running to \"Age inconsistent by 10 or more years\", so an implausible gap is usually a linkage or reporting problem rather than a data error to correct.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":3},{"n":"AGEN_21","d":"Age in completed years at the 2021 Census, held as a continuous variable for sums, means and medians.","full":"Age in completed years at the 2021 Census, held as a continuous variable for sums, means and medians. The derivation is unchanged from earlier Censuses, but the 2021 online form asked for date of birth first and relegated age to a secondary option, which the ABS says was done to encourage more accurate reporting; the range is 0 to 105 years, as at 2016. AGEP_21 is the categorical version of the same answer, capped at 85 years and over.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Continuous Variables, Age of Person (continuous)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Person (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 age in completed years (continuous)","def":"Whole years, 0 to 105 singly, with 999 for an unlinked record. No not-stated code exists because unreported age is imputed.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Continuous Variables, Age of Person (continuous)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"It is the age of the person who was linked to the 2021 Census, so 999 marks non-linkage rather than death or emigration. Attrition from the ACLD panel comes from mortality, overseas migration and linkage failure together, and this column cannot tell those three apart.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":3},{"n":"AGEP_11","d":"Age at the 2011 Census, as a categorical item in single years topped out at 85 years and over.","full":"Age at the 2011 Census, as a categorical item in single years topped out at 85 years and over. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines AGEP as a variable that \"Contains a person's age at last birthday, and is collected for each person. Age is calculated from date of birth, however if this is not provided, stated age will be used.\" The Census itself published age 0 to 115 singly, so the ACLD's top code at 85 is a confidentiality restriction imposed on the longitudinal file, and AGEN_11 is the continuous version to use for arithmetic.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), AGEP Age","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Person","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 age in single years, top-coded at 85 and over","def":"Codes 0 to 84 for single years, 85 for 85 years and over, and 999 for an unlinked record. There is no not-stated category, because unreported age is imputed at Census processing.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), AGEP Age","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302011","lim":"It cannot support any analysis of the old. Everyone from 85 to the oldest person in the panel is one category, so life expectancy, aged-care entry age and the age profile of deaths in the linked spine all collapse at the top. The absence of a not-stated code also hides imputation: an imputed age looks exactly like a reported one in this column.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":4},{"n":"AGEP_16","d":"Age at the 2016 Census, as a categorical item in single years topped out at 85 years and over.","full":"Age at the 2016 Census, as a categorical item in single years topped out at 85 years and over. The 2016 Census Dictionary defines AGEP as a variable that \"Contains a person's age, and is collected for each person. Age is calculated from date of birth, however if this is not provided, stated age will be used.\" Age non-response was 5.6% in 2016, and every one of those records was imputed rather than left blank, so this column has no not-stated category.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), AGEP Age","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Person","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 age in single years, top-coded at 85 and over","def":"Codes 0 to 84 for single years, 85 for 85 years and over, and 999 for an unlinked record. The categories match AGEP_11 and AGEP_21 exactly, so the three years can be tabulated on one axis.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), AGEP Age","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302016","lim":"AGEP_16 minus AGEP_11 need not equal five. The ACLD ships CFAGEP_11_16 for this reason, whose worst category is \"Age inconsistent by 10 or more years\", so a person's implied ageing between waves has to be checked against that flag before it is used to date events.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":4},{"n":"AGEP_21","d":"Age at the 2021 Census, as a categorical item in single years topped out at 85 years and over.","full":"Age at the 2021 Census, as a categorical item in single years topped out at 85 years and over. The 2021 Census changed the question rather than the concept: the online form asked for date of birth first and offered age as a secondary option, and the non-response rate fell to 4.4% from 5.6% in 2016. Missing age is still imputed rather than coded not stated, and the Census imputation flag IFAGEP, not this column, is what marks an imputed value.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Person","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 age in single years, top-coded at 85 and over","def":"Codes 0 to 84 for single years, 85 for 85 years and over, and 999 for an unlinked record, identical in shape to AGEP_11 and AGEP_16.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","lim":"An age here is not necessarily a reported age. About one record in twenty-three was imputed in 2021, and the ACLD carries no imputation flag alongside this column, so a study of a narrow birth cohort will silently include people whose age was filled in by the ABS. Top-coding at 85 also makes the column useless for anything about the very old.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":4},{"n":"AGEP_FP_11","d":"The age of the person's female parent at the 2011 Census, in five-year groups, attached to the child's own record.","full":"The age of the person's female parent at the 2011 Census, in five-year groups, attached to the child's own record. The ABS defines it as a variable that \"records a person's female parent's age at last birthday\", adding that it \"includes the female parent of nominal children\" and that \"For female same-sex couple families, this variable refers to the reference person.\" It applies only to people whose household relationship is a child under 15, a dependent student or a non-dependent child, and it exists only on the 2011-2016-2021 table, since the 2016-2021 file has no 2011 columns.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Female Parent Related Data Items, Age of Female Parent","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 age of female parent, five-year groups","def":"Codes 1 to 15 for five-year groups from 15-19 years up to 85 years and over, plus 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record. The person's own age, AGEP_11, is in single years, so parent and child ages are not on the same scale.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Female Parent Related Data Items, Age of Female Parent","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"998 is not evidence that the person has no mother. A child living in a male lone parent family, a child in a male same-sex couple family and a child whose female parent was temporarily absent on Census Night all fall into not applicable, alongside every adult who was not classified as a child in their household.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":5},{"n":"AGEP_FP_16","d":"The age of the person's female parent at the 2016 Census, in five-year groups, attached to the child's own record.","full":"The age of the person's female parent at the 2016 Census, in five-year groups, attached to the child's own record. The ABS records the derivation as \"Age is calculated from date of birth, however if this is not provided, stated age will be used\", and the group boundaries are unchanged from 2011, and the column appears on both ACLD tables; what changes between waves is who qualifies, because the item is populated only while the person is enumerated as a child under 15, a dependent student or a non-dependent child in the family. The matching ANC1P_FP_16 and ANC2P_FP_16 describe the same parent's ancestry at the same Census.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Female Parent Related Data Items, Age of Female Parent","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 age of female parent, five-year groups","def":"Codes 1 to 15 for five-year groups from 15-19 years up to 85 years and over, with 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Female Parent Related Data Items, Age of Female Parent","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"A move from a code at 2011 to 998 at 2016 records a change in living arrangements, not in the parent. Young adults leaving home are the largest source of that transition, so a fall in the count of people with a female parent age between waves measures household formation and cannot be read as parental death or estrangement.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":5},{"n":"AGEP_FP_21","d":"The age of the person's female parent at the 2021 Census, in five-year groups, attached to the child's own record.","full":"The age of the person's female parent at the 2021 Census, in five-year groups, attached to the child's own record. The item is derived from the family record on Census Night 2021, with \"Persons whose relationship in household is not a child under 15, dependent student or non-dependent child\" put into the not applicable category, so it is present only where the person was still enumerated as a child in a family that included a female parent, and by the fourth wave of the 2011 panel that population is much reduced. It sits beside AGEP_MP_21, the male parent's age, and both use the same banding as AGEP_SP_21 for a spouse or partner.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Female Parent Related Data Items, Age of Female Parent","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 age of female parent, five-year groups","def":"Codes 1 to 15 for five-year groups from 15-19 years up to 85 years and over, with 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record. The ABS notes that \"Each Census cycle code to the most up to date ASCCEG at the time\", so the 2021 parent columns use a different edition from 2016 and 2011, with separate Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander mark boxes new to the 2021 form. ANC2P_FP_21 carries the same parent's second ancestry.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Female Parent Related Data Items, Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Female Parent","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Female Parent","k":"ASCCEG 2019 four-digit ancestry code, female parent","def":"A four-digit ASCCEG 2019 code, plus 99997 not stated, 99998 not applicable and 99999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Female Parent Related Data Items, Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Female Parent","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"A parent's ancestry code that changes between 2016 and 2021 is not evidence the parent changed. The ABS defines it as a variable that \"indicates how a person's male parent identifies their ancestry\", including the male parent of nominal children and, in male same-sex couple families, the reference person. Ancestry at 2011 is coded to ASCCEG second edition revision 1, and the column exists only on the 2011-2016-2021 table.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Male Parent Related Data Items, Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Male Parent","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Male Parent","k":"ASCCEG second edition revision 1 (2011) four-digit ancestry code, male parent","def":"A four-digit ASCCEG code from the second edition, revision 1, plus 99997 not stated, 99998 not applicable and 99999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Male Parent Related Data Items, Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Male Parent","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"It cannot be combined with the mother's column to build a child's heritage. The column appears on both ACLD tables, and ANC1P_FP_16 gives the female parent's first ancestry.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Male Parent Related Data Items, Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Male Parent","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Male Parent","k":"ASCCEG 2016 four-digit ancestry code, male parent","def":"A four-digit ASCCEG 2016 code, plus 99997 not stated, 99998 not applicable and 99999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Male Parent Related Data Items, Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Male Parent","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"99997 and 99998 mean different things and must not be pooled. The 2021 edition added Norfolk Islander and the form added separate Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander mark boxes, so the parent columns change with the classification even where the parent's answer does not. Not applicable covers \"Persons whose relationship in household is not a child under 15, dependent student or non-dependent child\". ANC2P_MP_21 carries the same parent's second ancestry, and AGEP_MP_21 the parent's age band.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Male Parent Related Data Items, Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Male Parent","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Male Parent","k":"ASCCEG 2019 four-digit ancestry code, male parent","def":"A four-digit ASCCEG 2019 code, plus 99997 not stated, 99998 not applicable and 99999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Male Parent Related Data Items, Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Male Parent","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"By 2021 the column is empty for most of the 2011 panel, and that is about age, not fathers. Ancestry at 2011 is coded to ASCCEG second edition revision 1, and the column exists only on the 2011-2016-2021 table.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Spouse and Partner Related Data Items, Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Spouse or Partner","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Spouse or Partner","k":"ASCCEG second edition revision 1 (2011) four-digit ancestry code, spouse or partner","def":"A four-digit ASCCEG code from the second edition, revision 1, plus 99997 not stated, 99998 not applicable and 99999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Spouse and Partner Related Data Items, Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Spouse or Partner","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"Comparing it with ANC1P_11 does not measure partnership across ancestry groups. The ABS defines it as a variable that \"indicates how a person's spouse or partner identifies their ancestry\", rebuilt from the 2016 Census Night household, so it describes whoever was enumerated as the partner that night, and it appears on both ACLD tables. AGEP_SP_16 gives the same partner's age band.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Spouse and Partner Related Data Items, Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Spouse or Partner","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Spouse or Partner","k":"ASCCEG 2016 four-digit ancestry code, spouse or partner","def":"A four-digit ASCCEG 2016 code, plus 99997 not stated, 99998 not applicable and 99999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Spouse and Partner Related Data Items, Ancestry 1 - 1st Response of Spouse or Partner","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"A value at 2011 and a value at 2016 need not describe the same partner. The second ancestry provided is output into Ancestry 2nd response (ANC2P).\" On the 2021 Census output the second response carries no not-stated code, so a person who gave no ancestry appears as not stated on ANC1P and not applicable here; the ACLD adds its own 99997 not stated to this column.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Ancestry 2nd response (ANC2P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/ancestry-2nd-response-anc2p","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Ancestry - 2nd Response","k":"ASCCEG 2019 four-digit ancestry code, second response","def":"A four-digit ASCCEG 2019 code, plus 99997 not stated, 99998 not applicable and 99999 unlinked record on the ACLD file.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Ancestry 2nd response (ANC2P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/ancestry-2nd-response-anc2p","lim":"A person whose two ancestry codes swap between 2016 and 2021 has not changed identification. It comes from the 2016 Census Night family record and appears on both ACLD tables; the same parent's first response is ANC1P_MP_16 and their age band is AGEP_MP_16. The ABS notes that ASCCEG \"revisions to the second edition were published in 2011, 2016 and 2019\", so the 2016 codes are not the 2011 codes, and the ACLD carries CFBPMP_11_16, a male parent birthplace consistency flag, as the nearest check on whether the same man was recorded at both waves.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Male Parent Related Data Items, Ancestry 2 - 2nd Response of Male Parent","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Ancestry 2 - 2nd Response of Male Parent","k":"ASCCEG 2016 four-digit ancestry code, male parent second response","def":"A four-digit ASCCEG 2016 code, plus 99997 not stated, 99998 not applicable and 99999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items, Male Parent Related Data Items, Ancestry 2 - 2nd Response of Male Parent","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"A change between 2011 and 2016 is not evidence that the father's identification changed. The ABS states that \"The basis for allocating ancestries to the two ancestry variables is administrative only and is based on the order in which they are processed\", so this is not a lesser answer. Coverage is the narrowest of the three waves, because the item is populated only while the person is still enumerated as a child in a family with a male parent. The assistance questions did not change between 2011 and 2016, but non-response to them rose from 5.7 per cent to 7.1 per cent, so more families in 2016 have an unresolved assistance status behind this figure. AOPASSNF_S_P_16 holds the same measure as a continuous age.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27102016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Family With Core Activity Need for Assistance","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age in whole years, coded form, with a not applicable code where no member of the family carried a core activity need for assistance at that Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27102016","lim":"A rise between 2011 and 2016 does not mean a family member aged into a need. It can also mean an older person with a need joined the family, or that the 2011 value was suppressed by a not stated response that was answered in 2016.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":10},{"n":"AOPASSNF_P_21","d":"The age of the oldest person in the sampled person's family who was coded as having a core activity need for assistance at the 2021 Census.","full":"The age of the oldest person in the sampled person's family who was coded as having a core activity need for assistance at the 2021 Census. The ABS records no change to the underlying ASSNP questions for 2021 and reports non-response falling to 5.9 per cent from 7.1 per cent in 2016, so the 2021 figure rests on a more complete set of answers than the 2016 one. The 2021 dictionary also restyles the concept as a profound or severe core activity limitation rather than a profound or severe disability.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Family With Core Activity Need for Assistance","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age in whole years, coded form, with a not applicable code where no family member carried a core activity need for assistance in 2021. AOPASSNF_S_P_21 is the continuous version.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","lim":"It cannot be paired with AYPASSNF_P_21 to count how many family members need assistance. Two members of the same age produce equal oldest and youngest values, so equality does not establish that exactly one person in the family has a need.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":10},{"n":"AOPASSNF_S_P_11","d":"The continuous form of the age of the oldest family member with a core activity need for assistance at the 2011 Census.","full":"The continuous form of the age of the oldest family member with a core activity need for assistance at the 2011 Census. The custodian's \"(Continuous)\" label separates it from AOPASSNF_P_11, which holds the same measure in coded form. In 2011 the ABS coded an assistance need from a long-term health condition, a disability, or, for people aged 40 and over, old age alone.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27202011","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Family With Core Activity Need for Assistance (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A whole number of years held as an age rather than a category, so it can be averaged across families. A not applicable code stands where no family member carried an assistance need.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27202011","lim":"It cannot separate an age-related need from a disability. A person aged 40 or over who gave only old age as the reason is coded as having a need, so high values in this column mix ageing families with families supporting a member with a long-term disability.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":11},{"n":"AOPASSNF_S_P_16","d":"The continuous form of the age of the oldest family member with a core activity need for assistance at the 2016 Census.","full":"The continuous form of the age of the oldest family member with a core activity need for assistance at the 2016 Census. Being a single-year age, it can be differenced or averaged, which the coded AOPASSNF_P_16 cannot. The 2016 assistance questions are the same instrument used in 2011, so a change across the two waves is a change in the family, not in the question.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27102016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Family With Core Activity Need for Assistance (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A whole number of years held as an age, with a not applicable code where no family member carried an assistance need at the 2016 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27102016","lim":"The measure describes the family, not the sampled person, and it is silent where a family member with a need lives elsewhere. A person providing care to a parent in another dwelling has no assistance need recorded in this column at all.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":11},{"n":"AOPASSNF_S_P_21","d":"The continuous form of the age of the oldest family member with a core activity need for assistance at the 2021 Census.","full":"The continuous form of the age of the oldest family member with a core activity need for assistance at the 2021 Census. The ABS made no change to the ASSNP questions for 2021, so the single-year age can be compared across the 2011, 2016 and 2021 columns on the same row. What changes across waves is who counts as family, which the ACLD re-derives from each Census.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Family With Core Activity Need for Assistance (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A whole number of years held as an age rather than a category, with a not applicable code where no family member carried an assistance need in 2021.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","lim":"It is not a disability severity measure. The Census flag is binary, so a family whose oldest member with a need requires occasional help reads the same as one whose oldest member needs constant care, and this column adds only that person's age.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":11},{"n":"AOPF_P_11","d":"The age of the oldest member of the sampled person's family at the 2011 Census, the earliest of the three waves carried in acld_1121.","full":"The age of the oldest member of the sampled person's family at the 2011 Census, the earliest of the three waves carried in acld_1121. An ABS family needs at least one member aged 15 or over, so the column never reads below 15 for a person in a family. It is not applicable where the person was a visitor to the household or was not in a family.","dsrc":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Family","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age in whole years in coded form, taken over all family members enumerated in the household. AOPF_S_P_11 carries the same measure as a single-year age.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","lim":"It does not identify a relationship. It appears in both the acld_1121 and acld_1621 tables, so the same 2016 family is described whichever ACLD panel a user starts from. AOPH_P_16 gives the equivalent figure for the whole household, which is at least as large.","dsrc":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Family","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age in whole years in coded form, computed across family members present in the household; the continuous counterpart is AOPF_S_P_16.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","lim":"It is not the sampled person's own age. Where the sampled person happens to be the oldest in the family this column simply repeats AGEP_16, and nothing in the column marks which of those two cases applies.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":12},{"n":"AOPF_P_21","d":"The age of the oldest member of the sampled person's family at the 2021 Census.","full":"The age of the oldest member of the sampled person's family at the 2021 Census. Family membership is rebuilt from the 2021 Census alone, so a person who left the parental home between 2016 and 2021 will show a much lower value without anyone having died or moved out of the original family. It is not applicable where the person was a visitor or was not in a family on Census Night.","dsrc":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Family","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age in whole years in coded form, over the family as enumerated in 2021, with not applicable and not stated codes. AOPF_S_P_21 holds the single-year form.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","lim":"Differencing it against AOPF_P_16 does not measure family ageing. Census age itself runs 0 to 115 in whole years, so the family maximum is bounded by the same range. This is the earliest wave in the acld_1121 table.","dsrc":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Family (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A single-year age as a whole number, so it can be averaged, banded by the user or differenced against later waves. A lone parent aged 44 and a nine-person extended family whose eldest member is 44 read the same, so the column cannot be used on its own to describe living arrangements.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":11},{"n":"AOPF_S_P_16","d":"The continuous form of the oldest family member's age at the 2016 Census.","full":"The continuous form of the oldest family member's age at the 2016 Census. Census age is derived from date of birth where it was given and from stated age otherwise, and is imputed when neither was reported, so a small share of these family maxima rest on an imputed age. AOPF_P_16 is the coded form of the same measure.","dsrc":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Family (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A single-year age as a whole number, taken as the maximum over family members enumerated in 2016, with a not applicable code for people not in a family.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","lim":"A maximum is fragile to imputation. The single-year form supports arithmetic that the coded AOPF_P_21 does not.","dsrc":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Family (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A single-year age as a whole number, the maximum over family members enumerated in 2021, with a not applicable code where the person was not in a family.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","lim":"It cannot be read as a life-course transition. A large fall from AOPF_S_P_16 to AOPF_S_P_21 most often means a young adult formed a new family of their own rather than that an older relative died.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":11},{"n":"AOPH_P_11","d":"The age of the oldest usual resident of the sampled person's household at the 2011 Census.","full":"The age of the oldest usual resident of the sampled person's household at the 2011 Census. Household scope takes in boarders, unrelated flatmates and a second family in the same dwelling, none of which enter the family version AOPF_P_11. The ACLD publishes no continuous companion for the household measure, so this coded column is the only form available.","dsrc":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Household","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age in whole years in coded form, taken as the maximum over all usual residents of the dwelling, with the ACLD's not applicable and not stated codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","lim":"It cannot be used as a proxy for a parent's or a grandparent's age. Read against AOPF_P_16 on the same row, a gap between the two says the household contains someone outside the sampled person's family who is older than anyone in it. The column appears in both ACLD tables, acld_1121 and acld_1621.","dsrc":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Household","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age in whole years in coded form, the maximum over all usual residents of the dwelling as enumerated in 2016.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","lim":"It is not a measure of a multi-generation household. It describes the dwelling as counted on Census Night, 10 August 2021, when movement restrictions in several states kept some people away from the household they usually live in. Where the sampled person moved between 2016 and 2021, this column describes a different dwelling from AOPH_P_16.","dsrc":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Oldest Person in Household","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age in whole years in coded form, the maximum over usual residents of the 2021 dwelling, with the ACLD's not applicable and not stated codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","lim":"It cannot support a claim about older Australians living alone or in care. The ABS defines the population as \"those people needing help or assistance in one or more of the three core activity areas of self-care, mobility and communication, because of a long-term health condition (lasting six months or more), a disability (lasting six months or more), or old age\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2011). The concept was introduced at the 2006 Census, so 2011 is the second Census to carry it, and the ABS reports 5.7 per cent non-response for the year.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Core Activity Need for Assistance","t":"categorical","k":"Census core activity need for assistance flag","def":"Four categories: has need for assistance with core activities, does not have need for assistance with core activities, not stated, and overseas visitor. A person aged 40 or over who gives only old or young age as the reason is coded as having a need; a person under 40 giving the same reason is not.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27202011","lim":"It is not a disability measure and it is not comparable with the Survey of Disability, Ageing and Carers. The ABS keeps the 2011 wording, defining the population as \"Those people needing help or assistance in one or more of the three core activity areas of self-care, mobility and communication, because of a long-term health condition (lasting six months or more), a disability (lasting six months or more), or old age\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2016). What changed is completeness rather than concept: ABS reports non-response rising from 5.7 per cent in 2011 to 7.1 per cent in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27102016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Core Activity Need for Assistance","t":"categorical","k":"Census core activity need for assistance flag","def":"Four categories: has need for assistance, does not have need for assistance, not stated, and overseas visitor. Short-term conditions of under six months, difficulty with English and other causes are all coded to no need.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27102016","lim":"A move from need to no need between 2011 and 2016 is not evidence of recovery. The 2021 dictionary recasts the concept as a core activity limitation, saying \"People with a profound or severe core activity limitation are those needing assistance in their day to day lives in one or more of the three core activity areas of self-care, mobility and communication\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), and states that \"No changes have been made for 2021\" to the questions themselves. Non-response fell to 5.9 per cent from 7.1 per cent in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Core Activity Need for Assistance","t":"categorical","k":"Census core activity need for assistance flag","def":"Four categories, coded 1 has need for assistance with core activities, 2 does not have need for assistance with core activities, & not stated, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","lim":"It cannot be used to size the NDIS-eligible population or any service caseload. The Census screens for help with three core activities only, so people with psychosocial, sensory or intellectual disability who do not need help with self-care, mobility or communication are coded to category 2.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":13},{"n":"ASSNP_FP_11","d":"The core activity need for assistance recorded for the female parent of the sampled person at the 2011 Census.","full":"The core activity need for assistance recorded for the female parent of the sampled person at the 2011 Census. The ABS defines the underlying flag as covering people \"needing help or assistance in one or more of the three core activity areas of self-care, mobility and communication\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2011), and the ACLD copies that flag from the female parent onto the child's own record, alongside AGEP_FP_11 and the other female-parent columns.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Core Activity Need for Assistance of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census core activity need for assistance flag, female parent","def":"The same four ASSNP categories used for the person, plus the ACLD's not applicable code where no female parent was enumerated in the household.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27202011","lim":"It is blank where no female parent was counted in the household, and that covers a lone-father family, a mother counted elsewhere on Census Night and a person who is not a child in their family at all. A blank therefore says nothing about whether a mother exists.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":14},{"n":"ASSNP_FP_16","d":"The core activity need for assistance recorded for the female parent of the sampled person at the 2016 Census.","full":"The core activity need for assistance recorded for the female parent of the sampled person at the 2016 Census. Whether the column is populated depends on co-residence, so a young adult who moved out between waves loses the value even though the parent's own circumstances have not changed.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":14},{"n":"ASSNP_FP_21","d":"The core activity need for assistance recorded for the female parent of the sampled person at the 2021 Census.","full":"The core activity need for assistance recorded for the female parent of the sampled person at the 2021 Census. A mother coded as having a need may be cared for by a service, a partner or another child, and this column carries nothing about who provides the assistance or whether the sampled person does.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":14},{"n":"ASSNP_MP_11","d":"The core activity need for assistance recorded for the male parent of the sampled person at the 2011 Census.","full":"The core activity need for assistance recorded for the male parent of the sampled person at the 2011 Census. AGEP_MP_11 on the same row gives that parent's age.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Core Activity Need for Assistance of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census core activity need for assistance flag, male parent","def":"The four ASSNP categories as recorded for the male parent, with a not applicable code where no male parent was enumerated in the household.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27202011","lim":"The male and female parent columns cannot be added to count parents with a need. Non-response to the assistance questions was 7.1 per cent in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27102016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Core Activity Need for Assistance of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census core activity need for assistance flag, male parent","def":"The four ASSNP categories as recorded for the male parent, plus a not applicable code where no male parent was a usual resident of the household in 2016.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27102016","lim":"It cannot distinguish a step, foster or adoptive father from a biological one. Its 2021 population is whoever was the male parent in the household counted on 10 August 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Core Activity Need for Assistance of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census core activity need for assistance flag, male parent","def":"Codes 1 has need, 2 does not have need, & not stated and V overseas visitor as recorded for the male parent, with a not applicable code where no male parent was in the household.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","lim":"It cannot be differenced against ASSNP_MP_16 as a health trajectory. The relationship includes de facto and same-sex partners as reported on the Census form.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27102016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Core Activity Need for Assistance of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census core activity need for assistance flag, spouse or partner","def":"The four ASSNP categories as recorded for the spouse or partner, with a not applicable code where no partner was a usual resident of the household in 2016.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27102016","lim":"It cannot be used to identify spousal carers.
