The Census flag is a self-reported screen rather than an eligibility test, and a family with an NDIS participant may show not applicable if the participant does not need help with self-care, mobility or communication.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":10},{"n":"AYPASSNF_S_P_11","d":"The continuous form of the age of the youngest family member with a core activity need for assistance at the 2011 Census.","full":"The continuous form of the age of the youngest family member with a core activity need for assistance at the 2011 Census. The custodian's \"(Continuous)\" label separates it from the coded AYPASSNF_P_11. Because it is a single-year age it can be used directly to select families with a young member needing assistance. The 2011 wave is the earliest carried in the acld_1121 table.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27202011","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age of Youngest Person in Family With Core Activity Need for Assistance (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A whole number of years held as an age rather than a category, with a not applicable code where no family member carried an assistance need at the 2011 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter27202011","lim":"A not applicable value does not establish that nobody in the family needs help. A family in which the relevant person did not answer the assistance questions is coded not stated on ASSNP and drops out of this aggregate, so under-reporting appears as absence.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":11},{"n":"AYPASSNF_S_P_16","d":"The age in single years of the youngest member of the person's family who had a core activity need for assistance at the 2016 Census.","full":"The age in single years of the youngest member of the person's family who had a core activity need for assistance at the 2016 Census. The need itself is the Census ASSNP flag, which the 2016 Census Dictionary sets on people \"needing help or assistance in one or more of the three core activity areas of self-care, mobility and communication\". The value is a family attribute copied onto every person record in that family, so all its members carry the same number, and CASSNF_P_16 on the same row says how many family members had the need. The ACLD carries this item only from the 2016 wave, so there is no 2011 counterpart to difference it against.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter702016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Youngest Person in Family With Core Activity Need for Assistance (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Whole years on the Census age scale of 0 to 115, plus a not-applicable code where nobody in the family had a core activity need for assistance. The underlying need measure is the two-category ASSNP flag, not a graded severity scale.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter702016","lim":"It does not identify the person. A value of 8 could be the respondent's own child, a sibling or a grandchild, and because ASSNP is a single yes or no flag it cannot grade severity among the people it does flag. It also says nothing about people outside the family, so a household member who is a boarder with a need for assistance never appears here.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":11},{"n":"AYPASSNF_S_P_21","d":"The age in single years of the youngest member of the person's family who had a core activity need for assistance at the 2021 Census.","full":"The age in single years of the youngest member of the person's family who had a core activity need for assistance at the 2021 Census. The 2021 Census Dictionary defines that need as \"needing assistance in their day to day lives in one or more of the three core activity areas of self-care, mobility and communication\" because of a long-term health condition, a disability or old age, and records \"No changes have been made for 2021\", so the 2016 and 2021 values of this column are on the same basis. It is a family attribute written onto every person record in the family, and CASSNF_P_21 counts how many family members carried the need.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Youngest Person in Family With Core Activity Need for Assistance (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Whole years on the Census age scale of 0 to 115, plus a not-applicable code where no family member had a core activity need for assistance. Need is the two-category ASSNP flag with separate not stated and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","lim":"A change in this value between 2016 and 2021 is not evidence that anyone's health changed. The youngest person with a need can change because a family member moved in or out, died, or was enumerated elsewhere on Census Night, and the column carries no relationship field to tell those cases apart.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":11},{"n":"AYPF_P_11","d":"The age of the youngest person in the person's Census family at the 2011 Census, in age groups.","full":"The age of the youngest person in the person's Census family at the 2011 Census, in age groups. The family is the Census unit, which the 2011 Census Dictionary defines as \"Two or more persons, one of whom is at least 15 years of age, who are related by blood, marriage (registered or de facto), adoption, step or fostering, and who are usually resident in the same household\", so it covers related adults as well as children. AYPF_S_P_11 holds the same measure in single years, and the value is written onto every person record in the family.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Family","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter32102011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Youngest Person in Family","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age ranges rather than single years, with a not-applicable code for people who are not in a family household. The continuous companion AYPF_S_P_11 uses the Census age scale of 0 to 115.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Family","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter32102011","lim":"It is not the age of the youngest child. A couple in their seventies living with a related adult in their fifties returns a value in the fifties, and a person living alone or in a group household has no family at all, so CACF_P_11 and the family composition items are needed before this number can be read as anything about children.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":15},{"n":"AYPF_P_16","d":"The age of the youngest person in the person's Census family at the 2016 Census, in age groups.","full":"The age of the youngest person in the person's Census family at the 2016 Census, in age groups. The ages it is taken over are the Census AGEP values, which the 2016 Census Dictionary describes as \"Contains a person's age, and is collected for each person. Age is calculated from date of birth, however if this is not provided, stated age will be used.\" Neither the age question nor the Census definition of a family changed between 2011 and 2016, so AYPF_P_11 and this column are directly comparable; AYPF_S_P_16 holds the same measure in single years.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Youngest Person in Family","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age ranges rather than single years, with a not-applicable code for people not in a family household. Ages are drawn from AGEP, which runs 0 to 115 in single years at the 2016 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302016","lim":"It cannot distinguish a family that gained a baby from one that gained a young relative or was joined by an adult child's family, because any related person usually resident in the household enters the calculation. Nor does it flag imputed ages, so a family whose youngest member had age imputed looks the same as one that reported it.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":15},{"n":"AYPF_P_21","d":"The age of the youngest person in the person's Census family at the 2021 Census, in age groups.","full":"The age of the youngest person in the person's Census family at the 2021 Census, in age groups. The underlying ages come from AGEP, of which the 2021 Census Dictionary says \"This variable collects each person's age. If age is not reported, it is imputed.\" The 2021 question was reworded to ask for date of birth first and to fall back to age in years, and the ABS puts the age non-response rate at 4.4 per cent, so a small share of the minima behind this column rest on imputed ages.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Youngest Person in Family","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age ranges rather than single years, with a not-applicable code for people not in a family household. Ages are drawn from AGEP, which is recorded individually from 0 to 115 years at the 2021 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","lim":"It cannot be differenced against AYPF_P_16 to measure ageing within a family. The set of people counted as the family changes between Censuses through births, deaths, partnering and separation, so a fall in this value usually signals a change in who is present rather than anything about the same individuals.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":15},{"n":"AYPF_S_P_11","d":"The age in single years of the youngest person in the person's Census family at the 2011 Census.","full":"The age in single years of the youngest person in the person's Census family at the 2011 Census. It is the continuous form of AYPF_P_11, which holds the same measure in age groups, and it rests on the Census age variable AGEP, which in 2011 \"Contains a person's age at last birthday, and is collected for each person.\" Age at last birthday means an infant under one year is recorded as 0, so a family with a newborn returns 0 rather than a fraction.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Youngest Person in Family (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Whole years from 0 to 115 on the Census age scale, plus a not-applicable code for people who are not in a family household. There is no fractional part, because Census age is age at last birthday.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302011","lim":"A value of 0 does not date a birth. It means only that the youngest family member had not reached their first birthday on Census Night in August 2011, so births anywhere in the preceding twelve months share the same code and the column cannot be used to place a birth within the year.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":11},{"n":"AYPF_S_P_16","d":"The age in single years of the youngest person in the person's Census family at the 2016 Census.","full":"The age in single years of the youngest person in the person's Census family at the 2016 Census. It is the continuous form of AYPF_P_16 and is built from AGEP, which the 2016 Census Dictionary describes as \"Contains a person's age, and is collected for each person.\" The age question was unchanged between 2011 and 2016, so this column and AYPF_S_P_11 are measured the same way, five years apart.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Youngest Person in Family (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Whole years from 0 to 115 on the Census age scale, with a not-applicable code for people not in a family household. Values are the minimum age across the family's usual residents present on Census Night.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302016","lim":"Subtracting AYPF_S_P_11 from this column does not give five for a stable family. Any birth, any related person moving in, and any temporary absence resets the minimum, so the difference measures a change in family composition at least as often as it measures the passage of time.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":11},{"n":"AYPF_S_P_21","d":"The age in single years of the youngest person in the person's Census family at the 2021 Census.","full":"The age in single years of the youngest person in the person's Census family at the 2021 Census. It is the continuous form of AYPF_P_21 and rests on AGEP, which the 2021 Census Dictionary codes as \"0 to 115 years of age singly\" and imputes where \"age is not reported\". The 2021 question put date of birth first with age in years as the fallback, a change from 2016 that affects reporting precision rather than the scale.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Youngest Person in Family (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Whole years from 0 to 115 on the Census age scale, plus a not-applicable code for people not in a family household. The value is the smallest AGEP among the family's usual residents.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","lim":"It says nothing about how many young people are in the family. One infant and four infants both return 0, so CACF_P_21 and the dependent child counts are needed before this column can support any statement about family size or child load.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":11},{"n":"AYPH_P_11","d":"The age of the youngest usual resident of the person's household at the 2011 Census.","full":"The age of the youngest usual resident of the person's household at the 2011 Census. The household is the dwelling-level unit, so unlike AYPF_P_11 it takes in boarders, flatmates and unrelated residents as well as relatives, and the two columns differ exactly where an unrelated person is the youngest in the dwelling. The ages behind it are Census AGEP values, described in 2011 as \"a person's age at last birthday\".","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Youngest Person in Household","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age ranges rather than single years, taken as the minimum age across the household's usual residents. A not-applicable code applies to people enumerated in non-private dwellings and to unoccupied or non-classifiable households.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302011","lim":"It is a household minimum, not a family one, so a share house with a young flatmate and a couple with a baby can return the same value. Reading it as a proxy for the presence of a young child in the respondent's own family will misclassify group households and multi-family dwellings.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":15},{"n":"AYPH_P_16","d":"The age of the youngest usual resident of the person's household at the 2016 Census.","full":"The age of the youngest usual resident of the person's household at the 2016 Census. The household is the dwelling-level unit that HHCD classifies, and the 2016 Census Dictionary explains that household composition \"indicates whether a family is present or not and whether or not other unrelated household members are present\", which is why this minimum can fall below the family minimum in AYPF_P_16. The definition of a household did not change between 2011 and 2016, so this column and AYPH_P_11 are on the same basis.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Household Composition (HHCD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter35002016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Youngest Person in Household","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age ranges rather than single years, taken across all usual residents of the occupied private dwelling. A not-applicable code covers non-private dwellings, unoccupied dwellings and households the ABS could not classify.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Household Composition (HHCD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter35002016","lim":"It does not cover people who were away on Census Night. The Census counts usual residents present, so a household whose only child was staying elsewhere returns the age of the youngest adult, and the temporary absence counts CPAD and CPAF are what reveal that.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":15},{"n":"AYPH_P_21","d":"The age of the youngest usual resident of the person's household at the 2021 Census.","full":"The age of the youngest usual resident of the person's household at the 2021 Census. It is the household counterpart of AYPF_P_21 and rests on AGEP, of which the 2021 Census Dictionary says \"If age is not reported, it is imputed\", with a 4.4 per cent age non-response rate in 2021. The 2021 Census was taken during COVID-19 lockdowns in several states, so household membership on Census Night is more likely than usual to differ from ordinary living arrangements.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of Youngest Person in Household","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"Age ranges rather than single years, taken as the minimum age across the household's usual residents at the 2021 Census. A not-applicable code applies outside occupied private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","lim":"It cannot tell you the youngest person is a child of anyone in the dwelling. Grandchildren, unrelated children of a housemate and a young boarder all set the minimum, and the relationship items RLHP and RLGP are the only way to establish who the youngest person is to the respondent.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":15},{"n":"BEDRD_P_11","d":"The number of bedrooms in the private dwelling the person was counted in at the 2011 Census, grouped.","full":"The number of bedrooms in the private dwelling the person was counted in at the 2011 Census, grouped. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines BEDRD as a variable that \"Contains the number of bedrooms in each occupied private dwelling in ranges\", and BEDD is the ungrouped form. Because the ACLD attaches dwelling attributes to the person record, the value describes the dwelling and not the person, and it is read with the household size item to judge crowding.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Number of Bedrooms in Private Dwelling (ranges) (BEDRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter902011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Bedrooms in Private Dwelling (Ranges)","t":"categorical","k":"Census bedroom count in ranges (0 to 6 or more)","def":"Nine codes: 0 for none, including bedsitters, then one to five bedrooms individually, 6 for six or more, & for not stated and @ for not applicable. Applicable to occupied private dwellings only.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Number of Bedrooms in Private Dwelling (ranges) (BEDRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter902011","lim":"A bedroom count is not a measure of crowding on its own. The Census counts rooms the household describes as bedrooms, so a study used for sleeping may or may not be included, and the housing suitability item is the ABS measure that pairs bedrooms with the age and sex composition of the residents.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":16},{"n":"BEDRD_P_16","d":"The number of bedrooms in the private dwelling the person was counted in at the 2016 Census, grouped.","full":"The number of bedrooms in the private dwelling the person was counted in at the 2016 Census, grouped. The 2016 Census Dictionary uses the same definition as 2011, that the variable \"Contains the number of bedrooms in each occupied private dwelling in ranges\", and the code list is unchanged, so BEDRD_P_11 and this column can be compared directly. The ABS later reported the underlying bedroom question had a 7.4 per cent non-response rate in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Number of Bedrooms in Private Dwelling (ranges) (BEDRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter902016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Bedrooms in Private Dwelling (Ranges)","t":"categorical","k":"Census bedroom count in ranges (0 to 6 or more)","def":"Nine codes: 0 for none, including bedsitters, one to five bedrooms individually, 6 for six or more, & for not stated and @ for not applicable. Scope is occupied private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Number of Bedrooms in Private Dwelling (ranges) (BEDRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter902016","lim":"A change between 2011 and 2016 does not mean the dwelling was altered. The ACLD follows people, not dwellings, so almost every change in this column reflects a move to a different home, and it cannot be read as renovation or subdivision.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":16},{"n":"BEDRD_P_21","d":"The number of bedrooms in the private dwelling the person was counted in at the 2021 Census, grouped.","full":"The number of bedrooms in the private dwelling the person was counted in at the 2021 Census, grouped. The 2021 Census Dictionary says the variable \"records the number of bedrooms in each occupied private dwelling in ranges\", and the only change from 2016 is the wording of the lowest category, from none including bedsitters to \"None (includes studio apartments or bedsitters)\". Non-response on the underlying bedroom question fell from 7.4 per cent in 2016 to 5.4 per cent in 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of bedrooms in private dwelling (ranges) (BEDRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/number-bedrooms-private-dwelling-ranges-bedrd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Bedrooms in Private Dwelling (Ranges)","t":"categorical","k":"Census bedroom count in ranges (0 to 6 or more)","def":"Nine codes: 0 for none, including studio apartments and bedsitters, one to five bedrooms individually, 6 for six or more, & for not stated and @ for not applicable. Scope is occupied private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of bedrooms in private dwelling (ranges) (BEDRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/number-bedrooms-private-dwelling-ranges-bedrd","lim":"The top code hides the range above it. Six bedrooms and twelve bedrooms share code 6, so this column cannot be used to study large dwellings, and BEDD is the ungrouped variable that can.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":16},{"n":"BPFP_11","d":"Whether the person's mother was born in Australia or overseas, as reported at the 2011 Census.","full":"Whether the person's mother was born in Australia or overseas, as reported at the 2011 Census. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines BPFP as a variable that \"Indicates whether a person's mother was born in Australia or overseas\", which is all the Census collected before 2016: the specific country was not asked for parents until the 2016 form. BPLP_FP_11 gives the mother's actual country where she was enumerated in the same household, and BPMP_11 is the same two-way measure for the father.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Birthplace of Female Parent (BPFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1002011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Birthplace of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Birthplace of mother, Australia or overseas","def":"Four codes: 1 born in Australia, 2 born overseas, & not stated and V overseas visitor. Applicable to all persons.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Birthplace of Female Parent (BPFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1002011","lim":"It cannot be lined up with BPFPR_16 or BPFPR_21 without collapsing them. The 2011 item has two substantive categories against 293 four-digit countries from 2016, so a longitudinal user has to recode the later waves down, not the 2011 wave up.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":17},{"n":"BPFP_16","d":"The birthplace of the person's mother at the 2016 Census, the first Census to ask for the country rather than just Australia or overseas.","full":"The birthplace of the person's mother at the 2016 Census, the first Census to ask for the country rather than just Australia or overseas. The ABS renamed the mnemonic in 2016 from Birthplace of Female Parent to Country of Birth of Mother, and the 2016 Census Dictionary says the variable \"contains the specific country of birth of each person's mother\", coded to SACC 2016. The ACLD keeps the older Birthplace of Female Parent label on this column and publishes the detailed country as BPFPR_16, so check the ACLD data item list before assuming which of the two classifications this column carries.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Country of Birth of Mother (BPFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1002016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Birthplace of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Birthplace of mother (SACC 2016 country, or Australia and overseas)","def":"Either the two-category Australia and overseas split inherited from earlier Censuses, or the full Standard Australian Classification of Countries 2016 with 293 four-digit countries, 36 two-digit groups and 9 one-digit regions. Supplementary codes cover not stated and overseas visitors.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Country of Birth of Mother (BPFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1002016","lim":"The label alone does not settle which classification is in the column. Because the mnemonic and its name changed in the same Census, a reader who assumes the ACLD label matches the ABS 2016 definition may treat a two-way flag as a country code, and the ACLD data item list is the only authority on which it is.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":17},{"n":"BPFP_21","d":"The birthplace of the person's mother as reported at the 2021 Census.","full":"The birthplace of the person's mother as reported at the 2021 Census. The 2021 Census Dictionary defines BPFP as a variable that \"indicates the country in which a person's mother was born\", coded to SACC 2016, and records two 2021 changes: new instructions for people with an unknown birth parent where a second parent is present or with same-sex parents, and four country name updates including Czech Republic to Czechia and Swaziland to Eswatini. It is the person's own answer, so it does not depend on anyone else in the household being enumerated.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Country of Birth of Person (BPLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1102011","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Country of Birth of Person","k":"SACC Second Edition Revision 1 country of birth","def":"SACC Second Edition Revision 1, with 293 countries at the four-digit level, 36 groups at two digits and 9 regions at one digit, plus supplementary codes for not stated and inadequately described responses.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Country of Birth of Person (BPLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1102011","lim":"Country of birth is not a proxy for ethnicity, ancestry or language. The 2016 Census Dictionary defines BPLP as a variable that \"Indicates in which country a person was born and is coded using the Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), 2016\", so the classification edition changed from the one used in 2011 even though the question did not. BPMP_11, the item on the respondent's own form, recorded only Australia or overseas in 2011, so this column is the only source of the father's specific country at that wave.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Country of Birth of Person (BPLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1102011","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Country of Birth of Male Parent","k":"SACC Second Edition Revision 1 country of birth","def":"SACC Second Edition Revision 1, with 293 four-digit countries, 36 two-digit groups and 9 one-digit regions, plus a not-applicable code where no male parent was enumerated in the household.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Country of Birth of Person (BPLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1102011","lim":"Coverage is systematically uneven. The slot is also empty when both parents are women, when the father was temporarily absent on Census Night, and when the person no longer lives with a parent, and the relationship and family composition items are needed to tell those cases apart.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"BPLP_SP_11","d":"The country of birth of the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census, taken from the partner's own Census record.","full":"The country of birth of the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census, taken from the partner's own Census record. The same partner can be recoded when SACC changes, and a person can also lose the value entirely through separation, death or the partner being absent on Census Night, none of which the column distinguishes.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"BPLP_SP_21","d":"The country of birth of the person's spouse or partner at the 2021 Census, taken from the partner's own Census record.","full":"The country of birth of the person's spouse or partner at the 2021 Census, taken from the partner's own Census record. The classification edition is the same as 2016, so a 2016 to 2021 comparison is affected only by the four country renames the ABS made for 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of person (BPLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-person-bplp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Country of Birth of Spouse or Partner","k":"SACC 2016 country of birth","def":"SACC 2016, with 293 four-digit countries, 39 two-digit groups and 12 one-digit regions, plus a not-applicable code for people with no co-resident spouse or partner.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of person (BPLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-person-bplp","lim":"Closed international borders in 2021 make an empty value harder to read than usual. Partners stranded overseas on Census Night were not enumerated in the household, so the 2021 wave undercounts couples where one member was abroad, which is precisely the group most likely to be overseas-born.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"BPMP_11","d":"Whether the person's father was born in Australia or overseas, as reported at the 2011 Census.","full":"Whether the person's father was born in Australia or overseas, as reported at the 2011 Census. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines BPMP as a variable that \"Indicates whether a person's father was born in Australia or overseas\", which is the most the Census collected about parents before 2016. BPLP_MP_11 gives the father's actual country where he was enumerated in the same household, and BPPP combines this item with the mother's to classify the pair.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Birthplace of Male Parent (BPMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Birthplace of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Birthplace of father, Australia or overseas","def":"Four codes: 1 born in Australia, 2 born overseas, & not stated and V overseas visitor. The ACLD keeps the older Birthplace of Male Parent label on this column and publishes the detailed country as BPMPR_16, so the data item list is what settles which classification this column carries.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Country of Birth of Father (BPMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1202016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Birthplace of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Birthplace of father (SACC 2016 country, or Australia and overseas)","def":"Either the two-category Australia and overseas split inherited from earlier Censuses, or the full Standard Australian Classification of Countries 2016 with 293 four-digit countries, 36 two-digit groups and 9 one-digit regions, plus not stated and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Country of Birth of Father (BPMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1202016","lim":"The label alone does not settle which classification is in the column, because the ABS changed both the name and the classification of this mnemonic in the same Census. Non-response fell from 6.9 per cent in 2016 to 5.7 per cent in 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of father (BPMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-father-bpmp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Birthplace of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Birthplace of father (SACC 2016 country, or Australia and overseas)","def":"Either the two-category Australia and overseas split carried forward for comparability, or SACC 2016 with 293 four-digit countries, 39 two-digit groups and 12 one-digit regions, plus supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated and overseas visitor responses.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of father (BPMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-father-bpmp","lim":"It reports the father the respondent names, not a verified parent. The specific country was collected from parents for the first time in 2016, and the Census Dictionary for that year says the variable \"contains the specific country of birth of each person's father\", coded to SACC 2016. That is why the ACLD carries this column only from the 2016 wave, while the two-category BPMP series runs back to 2006.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Country of Birth of Father (BPMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1202016","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Country of Birth of Father","k":"SACC 2016 country of birth of father","def":"Standard Australian Classification of Countries 2016, with 293 countries at the four-digit level, 36 groups at two digits and 9 regions at one digit, plus supplementary codes for not stated and overseas visitor. Non-response on the item was 5.7 per cent in 2021, down from 6.9 per cent in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of father (BPMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-father-bpmp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Country of Birth of Father","k":"SACC 2016 country of birth of father","def":"Standard Australian Classification of Countries 2016, with 293 four-digit countries, 39 two-digit groups and 12 one-digit regions, plus supplementary codes for inadequately described, at sea, not stated and overseas visitor. It includes up to three children who were temporarily absent from the household on Census night.\" It is a family attribute copied onto the person record, so every member of the family carries the same count.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Count of All Children in Family (CACF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1402011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of All Children in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Count of children in family, 1 to 6 or more","def":"Seven codes: 1 to 5 children individually, 6 for six or more, and @ for not applicable, which covers couple families with no children, other families, non-family and non-classifiable households, unoccupied and non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping areas.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Count of All Children in Family (CACF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1402011","lim":"It counts children of any age, not children in the ordinary sense. The 2016 Census Dictionary repeats the 2011 definition word for word, that the variable \"Counts the number of dependent and non-dependent children in the family. It includes up to three children who were temporarily absent from the household on Census night\", so CACF_P_11 and this column are on identical footing. The cap on temporarily absent children means a family with four children away is undercounted at both waves in the same way.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Count of All Children in Family (CACF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1402016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of All Children in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Count of children in family, 1 to 6 or more","def":"Seven codes: 1 to 5 children individually, 6 for six or more, and @ for not applicable, covering couple families with no children, other family types, non-family households, unoccupied and non-private dwellings, and migratory, off-shore and shipping areas.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Count of All Children in Family (CACF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter1402016","lim":"A rise between 2011 and 2016 is not necessarily a birth. It is built from relationship in household, age, educational institution attendance and the temporary absence questions.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of all children in family (CACF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-all-children-family-cacf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of All Children in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Count of children in family, 1 to 6 or more","def":"Seven codes: 1 to 5 children individually, 6 for six or more, and @ for not applicable, which takes in couple families with no children, other family types, non-family and non-classifiable households, unoccupied and non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping areas.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of all children in family (CACF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-all-children-family-cacf","lim":"The ABS warns that family definitions differ across its collections, so this count will not match a child count from the household surveys or from administrative data such as DOMINO family payments, where a child is defined by dependency rules rather than by co-residence on one night.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":20},{"n":"CASSNF_P_11","d":"How many people in the person's Census family had a core activity need for assistance at the 2011 Census.","full":"How many people in the person's Census family had a core activity need for assistance at the 2011 Census. The need is the Census ASSNP flag, set on people \"needing help or assistance in one or more of the three core activity areas of self-care, mobility and communication\" because of a disability, a long term health condition or old age, in the words of the 2011 Census Dictionary. The count is a family attribute written onto every person record in the family, so it does not say whether the person on the row is one of those counted.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter702011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of Persons in Family With Core Activity Need for Assistance","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A small whole number counting family members with the ASSNP flag set, with a not-applicable code for people who are not in a family household. AYPASSNF_S_P_16, new at this wave, gives the age of the youngest family member carrying the need.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Core Activity Need for Assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter702016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of Persons in Family With Core Activity Need for Assistance","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A small whole number counting family members with the ASSNP flag set, plus a not-applicable code for people not in a family household. The 2021 Census Dictionary describes the underlying ASSNP flag as identifying people \"needing assistance in their day to day lives in one or more of the three core activity areas of self-care, mobility and communication\" and states \"No changes have been made for 2021\", so the count is comparable with the 2016 and 2011 waves. One coding rule matters for the count: where old age is the reason given, people under 40 are coded as not having a need and people aged 40 and over are coded as having one.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of Persons in Family With Core Activity Need for Assistance","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A small whole number counting family members with the ASSNP flag set, plus a not-applicable code for people not in a family household. The count is built from the household's own person records, so it includes the person themselves if they reported the need; ASSNP_11 is that person's individual answer and CASSNF_P_11 is the same count taken over the family rather than the household. Because 2011 is the base wave of the 2011 panel, this column is populated for all 1,221,059 records in the panel, while its 2016 and 2021 counterparts are only populated where the person linked forward.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Household Related Data Items","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household With Core Activity Need for Assistance as Stated","t":"categorical","k":"Count of persons in household with core activity need for assistance, 0 to 2 or more","def":"For the 2011 Census: 0 no persons, 1 one person, 2 two or more persons, plus 97 where all persons in the household left the question blank, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record in the DataLab file (X, @ and U in TableBuilder).","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Household Related Data Items","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"Code 97 is not a zero. The underlying Census concept is ASSNP, which in 2016 the Census Dictionary described as measuring people with a profound or severe disability: \"People with a profound or severe disability are defined as those people needing help or assistance in one or more of the three core activity areas of self-care, mobility and communication, because of a disability, long-term health condition (lasting six months or more) or old age.\" The ACLD carries the count only where the person's 2011 record linked to 2016, which was 927,517 of the 1,221,059 records in the 2011 panel, a rate of 76.0%.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), ASSNP Core Activity Need for Assistance","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter702016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household With Core Activity Need for Assistance as Stated","t":"categorical","k":"Count of persons in household with core activity need for assistance, 0 to 2 or more","def":"For the 2016 Census: 0 no persons, 1 one person, 2 two or more persons, with 97 where all persons in the household left the question blank, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record in the DataLab file.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), ASSNP Core Activity Need for Assistance","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter702016","lim":"A 99 is not an empty household. It marks a person whose 2011 record did not link to a 2016 Census record, so dropping 99 changes the population under study rather than the variable, and LINKFLAG_16 is the column that says so directly. Code 97 applies only where every person in the household left the question blank, so a household in which some members answered and some did not is counted from the answers given and its number is a floor rather than a total.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":22},{"n":"CASSNH_P_21","d":"How many people in the person's household reported needing help with core activities at the 2021 Census.","full":"How many people in the person's household reported needing help with core activities at the 2021 Census. By 2021 the ABS had restated the concept in terms of limitation rather than disability: \"This variable records the number of people with a profound or severe core activity limitation\", covering self-care, mobility and communication needs arising from a long-term health condition, a disability or old age, where the 2016 Dictionary spoke of a profound or severe disability. The 2021 column appears in both ACLD tables, populated for 814,337 of the 2011 panel (66.7%) and for 1,088,307 of the 2016 panel (83.2%).","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household With Core Activity Need for Assistance as Stated","t":"categorical","k":"Count of persons in household with core activity need for assistance, 0 to 2 or more","def":"For the 2021 Census: 0 no persons, 1 one person, 2 two or more persons, with 97 where all persons in the household left the question blank, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record in the DataLab file.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","lim":"It is not a disability prevalence measure. The Census asks only about needing help with self-care, mobility and communication, so a household with a member who has a long-term condition that does not create those needs counts as zero, and the count cannot be lined up with NDIS participation or with the SDAC definition of disability.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":22},{"n":"CDC05H_P_11","d":"How many children aged 5 to 9 were in the person's household at the 2011 Census, capped at three or more.","full":"How many children aged 5 to 9 were in the person's household at the 2011 Census, capped at three or more. The 2011 column exists only in the 2011 panel table, since it is that panel's base wave.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Household Related Data Items","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Children in Household Aged 5-9 Years","t":"categorical","k":"Count of children aged 5-9 in household, 0 to 3 or more","def":"A single digit for the 2011 Census: 0 none, 1 one child, 2 two children, 3 three or more children aged 5-9, with 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record in the DataLab file (@ and U in TableBuilder).","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Household Related Data Items","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"The household counts stop at three or more while the matching family counts stop at two or more, so CDC05H_P_11 and CDC5F_P_11 cannot be differenced to get children outside the family. As the base wave of the 2011 panel, the column is populated for all 1,221,059 panel records.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Household Related Data Items","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Dependent Students in Household Aged 15-24 Years","t":"categorical","k":"Count of dependent students aged 15-24 in household, 0 to 3 or more","def":"A single digit for the 2011 Census counting dependent students across the whole household: 0 none, 1 one, 2 two, 3 three or more, with 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record in the DataLab file (@ and U in TableBuilder).","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Household Related Data Items","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"It is not a count of students in the dwelling. It is populated for the 76.0% of the 2011 panel that linked to 2016, and appears again in the 2016 panel table as a base wave.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Household Related Data Items","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Dependent Students in Household Aged 15-24 Years","t":"categorical","k":"Count of dependent students aged 15-24 in household, 0 to 3 or more","def":"A single digit for the 2016 Census counting dependent students across the whole household: 0 none, 1 one, 2 two, 3 three or more, with 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record in the DataLab file.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Household Related Data Items","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"The ten-year age span makes this the widest band in the household series, so its cap at three binds more often than the caps on the two-, three- and five-year child bands, and comparing top-code frequencies between the bands measures band width rather than household size.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":32},{"n":"CDSH_P_21","d":"The number of dependent students aged 15 to 24 in the person's household at the 2021 Census, capped at three or more and on categories unchanged since 2011.","full":"The number of dependent students aged 15 to 24 in the person's household at the 2021 Census, capped at three or more and on categories unchanged since 2011. In the 2011 panel a student counted here was aged 5 to 14 at the 2011 Census, so the household child bands at 2011 and this column at 2021 bracket a decade of schooling. It is populated for 814,337 records of the 2011 panel and 1,088,307 of the 2016 panel.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Household Related Data Items","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Dependent Students in Household Aged 15-24 Years","t":"categorical","k":"Count of dependent students aged 15-24 in household, 0 to 3 or more","def":"A single digit for the 2021 Census: 0 no dependent students, 1 one, 2 two, 3 three or more, with 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record in the DataLab file.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Household Related Data Items","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"A student enumerated at a university residence or a boarding house on Census Night belongs to that dwelling's household, not their family home's, so the 2021 column understates households whose young adults were living away while studying.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":32},{"n":"CFAGEP_11_16","d":"How far the person's age at the 2016 Census departs from their 2011 Census age, once the five years between the Censuses are allowed for.","full":"How far the person's age at the 2016 Census departs from their 2011 Census age, once the five years between the Censuses are allowed for. It is a linkage quality indicator rather than a characteristic of the person: a large discrepancy is evidence that the 2011 and 2016 records may belong to different people. This column exists only in the 2011 panel table, and the ACLD published no equivalent flag for the 2006 to 2011 pair in this release.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Quality Indicators","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age Consistency Flag","t":"categorical","k":"ACLD age consistency flag, 2011 to 2016","def":"A two-digit code for the 2011 to 2016 pair: 01 consistent within 0 years, 11 inconsistent within 1 year, 12 from 2 to less than 5 years, 13 from 5 to less than 10 years, and 14 by 10 or more years, plus 999 unlinked record in the DataLab file (UU in TableBuilder).","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Quality Indicators","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"It never says which Census carries the wrong age, and it never declares a link false. The bands are identical to the 2011 to 2016 flag, so the two can be read side by side to see whether a record's age has drifted at one join or at both. This flag appears in both ACLD tables, because the 2016 to 2021 pair is shared by the 2011 panel and the 2016 panel.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Quality Indicators","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Age Consistency Flag","t":"categorical","k":"ACLD age consistency flag, 2016 to 2021","def":"A two-digit code for the 2016 to 2021 pair: 01 consistent within 0 years, 11 inconsistent within 1 year, 12 from 2 to less than 5 years, 13 from 5 to less than 10 years, and 14 by 10 or more years, plus 999 unlinked record in the DataLab file.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Quality Indicators","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"The 2016 and 2021 Censuses were linked to the ABS Person Linkage Spine rather than directly to each other, at rates of 93.68% and 96.26%, so an inconsistency here can arise from either Census-to-Spine step, and the flag cannot tell a reporting error from a spine linkage error.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":33},{"n":"CFBPFP_11_16","d":"Whether the country of birth reported for the person's mother agrees between their 2011 and 2016 Census records.","full":"Whether the country of birth reported for the person's mother agrees between their 2011 and 2016 Census records. This flag exists only in the 2011 panel table, alongside the matching male parent flag CFBPMP_11_16.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Quality Indicators","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Birthplace of Female Parent Consistency Flag","t":"categorical","k":"ACLD birthplace of female parent consistency flag, 2011 to 2016","def":"A two-digit code for the 2011 to 2016 pair: 01 consistent, 02 consistent with one year not stated, 11 inconsistent, plus 997 not stated in both years and 999 unlinked record in the DataLab file (XX and UU in TableBuilder).","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Quality Indicators","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"Code 02 folds a missing answer into the consistent group, so the consistent share is not the agreement rate. The comparison spans a change in the question: the ABS records that \"For the first time, the 2021 Census included instructions to provide guidance on situations where the birth parent is unknown and there is a second parent, or the person has same-sex parents\", so a household that answered for a different parent in 2021 can register as inconsistent without anyone making a mistake. This flag appears in both ACLD tables, since the 2016 to 2021 pair is shared by the two panels.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of mother (BPFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-mother-bpfp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Birthplace of Female Parent Consistency Flag","t":"categorical","k":"ACLD birthplace of female parent consistency flag, 2016 to 2021","def":"A two-digit code for the 2016 to 2021 pair: 01 consistent, 02 consistent with one year not stated, 11 inconsistent, plus 997 not stated in both years and 999 unlinked record in the DataLab file.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of mother (BPFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-mother-bpfp","lim":"Non-response is unevenly spread across the two Censuses being compared. The ABS reports the non-response rate for BPFP as 5.6% in 2021, down from 6.7% in 2016, so codes 02 and 997 are more likely to be driven by the 2016 answer, and a rise in measured consistency over time partly reflects better response rather than steadier reporting.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":34},{"n":"CFBPLP_11_16","d":"Whether the person's own country of birth agrees between their 2011 and 2016 Census records.","full":"Whether the person's own country of birth agrees between their 2011 and 2016 Census records. This flag appears in both ACLD tables because the 2016 to 2021 pair is shared by the two panels.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of person (BPLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-person-bplp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Birthplace of Person Consistency Flag","t":"categorical","k":"ACLD country of birth of person consistency flag, 2016 to 2021","def":"A two-digit code for the 2016 to 2021 pair: 01 consistent, 02 consistent with one year not stated or inadequately described, 11 inconsistent, 21 inconsistent with one year not applicable, plus 997 not stated or inadequately described in both years, 998 not applicable in both years and 999 unlinked record in the DataLab file.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of person (BPLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-person-bplp","lim":"It measures the answers, not the truth. The ABS reports non-response to BPLP of 5.3% in 2021 and 6.9% in 2016, and those records land in codes 02 or 997 rather than being counted as disagreement, so the flag cannot be used as a denominator for a data quality rate without separating the not stated codes out first.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":35},{"n":"CFBPMP_11_16","d":"Whether the country of birth reported for the person's father agrees between their 2011 and 2016 Census records.","full":"Whether the country of birth reported for the person's father agrees between their 2011 and 2016 Census records. The ABS reports non-response to BPMP of 5.7% in 2021 and 6.9% in 2016, against 5.6% and 6.7% for BPFP, so missing answers run 0.1 to 0.2 percentage points higher for fathers at each Census, and the two questions are answered separately rather than as a pair.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":36},{"n":"CFBPSP_11_16","d":"Whether the country of birth of the person's spouse or partner agrees between their 2011 and 2016 Census records.","full":"Whether the country of birth of the person's spouse or partner agrees between their 2011 and 2016 Census records. The ABS defines it as \"This variable indicates whether the person's linked records between Census cycles have consistent Country of Birth of Spouse or Partner information or not.\" A year in which the spouse's birthplace was not stated still counts as consistent and is coded 02, while 998 marks a person with no spouse or partner present and 999 a record that did not link across the pair. The ABS defines it as \"This variable indicates whether the person's linked records between Census cycles have consistent Highest Year of School Completed information or not\", and treats one year not stated as consistent under code 02. The ABS also notes that the inconsistent code 11 \"Includes records where highest year of school completed is higher in 2011 than in 2016\", so an apparent fall in schooling sits inside that one category. A household member away on Census Night is excluded here and a visitor is never counted, so this column and CLFEF_P_16 will not agree even for a single-family household.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":49},{"n":"CLFEH_P_21","d":"How many usual residents of the person's household were employed at the 2021 Census, counted only from stated answers.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's household were employed at the 2021 Census, counted only from stated answers. The ABS defines it as \"This variable counts the number of employed persons, as stated, in the household in which the person was usually resident.\" The 2021 measurement week fell during lockdowns in several states, and the ABS told people stood down because of a lockdown to report that they had a job but were absent from work, so they are counted as employed in this column.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items data item list, Household Related Data Items sheet","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Employed Usually Resident Persons in Household as Stated","t":"categorical","k":"Count of employed usually resident persons in household, as stated (0 to 4 or more)","def":"A single digit topcoded at four: 0 through 4 four or more employed persons, 97 all persons did not state labour force status, 98 not applicable, 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 Microdata Items data item list, Household Related Data Items sheet","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"A count that holds steady between 2016 and 2021 need not mean the household kept working. Stood down members still count as employed under the 2021 instruction, and the 'as stated' rule means improvements in labour force non-response, from 6.7% in 2016 to 5.8% in 2021, also lift the count without any change in employment.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":49},{"n":"CLFNF_P_11","d":"How many people in the person's 2011 Census family were not in the labour force.","full":"How many people in the person's 2011 Census family were not in the labour force. It aggregates the 2011 Census variable Labour Force Status (LFSP), which the dictionary defines as recording \"for the week prior to Census Night, a person's labour force status\" for persons aged 15 years and over. The family is the one the person belonged to on 2011 Census night, so this sits beside CLFEF_P_11 for employed family members and CLFUF_P_11 for unemployed ones, and the three do not add to family size.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Count of Persons in Family Not in the Labour Force","t":"categorical","k":"Count of family members not in the labour force, 2011 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of people in the family. The classification underneath it is 2011 Census Labour Force Status, in which \"Not in the labour force\" is one of nine categories and the not-applicable category covers everyone aged under 15.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It cannot say why anyone is outside the labour force, so a retired couple, a full-time carer and a discouraged job seeker all read the same. Because labour force status is not collected under 15, children never enter this count, and a family of two working parents with three young children scores zero here just as a childless working couple does.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":50},{"n":"CLFNF_P_16","d":"How many people in the person's 2016 Census family were not in the labour force.","full":"How many people in the person's 2016 Census family were not in the labour force. The 2016 dictionary gives the underlying classification as recording \"for the week prior to Census night, a person's labour force status\", applicable to persons aged 15 years and over. Two of the five questions that feed labour force status were amended for 2016, so a difference between this column and CLFNF_P_11 mixes real change with a change in the instrument.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter6402016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Count of Persons in Family Not in the Labour Force","t":"categorical","k":"Count of family members not in the labour force, 2016 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of people in the family, resting on the 2016 Census Labour Force Status classification, where \"Not in the labour force\" is one of nine categories and persons under 15 are coded not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter6402016","lim":"It does not identify the person's own labour force status, which is carried separately, so a lone 60-year-old retiree in a family of four cannot be picked out from this column. It also hides the composition of the family: two retired grandparents and two adult children studying full time produce the same value as any other four adults outside the labour force.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":50},{"n":"CLFNF_P_21","d":"How many people in the person's 2021 Census family were not in the labour force.","full":"How many people in the person's 2021 Census family were not in the labour force. The 2021 dictionary defines the underlying variable as \"a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night\" for persons aged 15 and over, and records that an extra online form instruction was added for respondents in areas under COVID-19 lockdown. Non-response to labour force status fell from 6.7 per cent in 2016 to 5.8 per cent in 2021, which lifts this count slightly for reasons that have nothing to do with the labour market.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Count of Persons in Family Not in the Labour Force","t":"categorical","k":"Count of family members not in the labour force, 2021 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of people in the family, built on the 2021 Census Labour force status classification, whose nine categories include \"Not in the labour force\" and a not-applicable code for everyone under 15.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","lim":"The 2021 count is not a clean successor to 2016. Census night fell on 10 August 2021 while several capital cities were locked down, and the ABS had to add form guidance for those respondents, so movements out of the labour force between the 2016 and 2021 waves cannot be read as a settled change in behaviour. The column also gives no reason for being outside the labour force.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":50},{"n":"CLFNH_P_11","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2011 Census household were not in the labour force, counting only those whose status was stated.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2011 Census household were not in the labour force, counting only those whose status was stated. It aggregates the same 2011 classification as CLFNF_P_11, but over the whole dwelling rather than the family, so lodgers, flatmates and members of a second family in the dwelling are inside this count and outside the family one. The 2011 dictionary defines the classification as recording \"for the week prior to Census Night, a person's labour force status\" for persons aged 15 years and over.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Usually Resident Persons Not in the Labour Force in Household as Stated","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members not in the labour force, 2011 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents. It draws on 2011 Census Labour Force Status, one of whose nine categories is \"Not in the labour force\", and the custodian's \"as stated\" qualifier means residents with a not-stated status are left out rather than counted.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"Because the count is restricted to stated responses, it does not sum with the employed and unemployed household counts to the number of usual residents, and a household with poor form completion looks smaller on every one of these columns. It also cannot be turned into a household non-participation rate without the household size variables, which are separate columns.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":51},{"n":"CLFNH_P_16","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2016 Census household were not in the labour force, counting only those whose status was stated.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2016 Census household were not in the labour force, counting only those whose status was stated. The 2016 dictionary defines the underlying classification as recording \"for the week prior to Census night, a person's labour force status\" for persons aged 15 years and over.
