Two of the five contributing questions changed for 2016, so the household total shifts a little for instrument reasons as well as real ones.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter6402016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Usually Resident Persons Not in the Labour Force in Household as Stated","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members not in the labour force, 2016 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents whose 2016 labour force status was stated and fell in the \"Not in the labour force\" category, one of the nine categories in the 2016 classification.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter6402016","lim":"The household is the one the person lived in on 2016 Census night, not a stable unit across the panel. A person who moved between the 2011 and 2016 waves has a count for a different set of people, so a change in this column can reflect a change of address rather than a change in anyone's labour force status.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":51},{"n":"CLFNH_P_21","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2021 Census household were not in the labour force, counting only those whose status was stated.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2021 Census household were not in the labour force, counting only those whose status was stated. The 2021 dictionary defines the source variable as \"a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night\" and notes an online form instruction added for respondents in COVID-19 lockdown areas. Non-response to the underlying question fell to 5.8 per cent in 2021 from 6.7 per cent in 2016, which mechanically raises an \"as stated\" count like this one.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Usually Resident Persons Not in the Labour Force in Household as Stated","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members not in the labour force, 2021 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents whose stated 2021 labour force status was \"Not in the labour force\", one of the nine categories of the 2021 classification, which is not applicable to persons under 15.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","lim":"Rising response to the labour force question means a higher 2021 value can be pure measurement: an \"as stated\" count grows when fewer residents leave the question blank, whatever they were doing. Combined with the August 2021 lockdowns, this makes the 2016-to-2021 movement in the column unsafe as an estimate of change in household non-participation.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":51},{"n":"CLFUF_P_11","d":"How many people in the person's 2011 Census family were unemployed.","full":"How many people in the person's 2011 Census family were unemployed. It counts family members in either of the two unemployed categories of the 2011 Labour Force Status classification, looking for full-time work and looking for part-time work, which the dictionary records \"for the week prior to Census Night\". CLFEF_P_11 and CLFNF_P_11 hold the employed and not-in-the-labour-force counts for the same family.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Count of Unemployed Persons in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Count of unemployed family members, 2011 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of family members. It rests on the 2011 Census Labour Force Status classification, whose unemployed component is split into categories 4 and 5, looking for full-time and looking for part-time work, and which is not applicable to persons under 15.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"Census unemployment is not the labour force survey measure and is known to run higher, because a single self-completed form cannot apply the survey's tests of active search and availability. The count therefore should not be read against ABS labour force survey unemployment, and it says nothing about how long anyone had been out of work.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":52},{"n":"CLFUF_P_16","d":"How many people in the person's 2016 Census family were unemployed.","full":"How many people in the person's 2016 Census family were unemployed. The 2016 dictionary defines the source classification as recording \"for the week prior to Census night, a person's labour force status\", with unemployment split between looking for full-time and looking for part-time work. Two of the five questions feeding labour force status were amended for 2016, which matters more for unemployment than for the other categories because the job search and availability questions are what separate the unemployed from those not in the labour force.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter6402016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Count of Unemployed Persons in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Count of unemployed family members, 2016 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of family members in either of the two 2016 unemployed categories of Labour Force Status, which has nine categories in all and does not apply to persons under 15.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter6402016","lim":"A count of unemployed family members is not a family unemployment rate, because the denominator is the employed plus unemployed count and has to be built from CLFEF_P_16. The column also cannot separate a family where one of four adults is out of work from one where the sole adult is.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":52},{"n":"CLFUF_P_21","d":"How many people in the person's 2021 Census family were unemployed.","full":"How many people in the person's 2021 Census family were unemployed. The 2021 dictionary defines the source variable as \"a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night\", built from five questions on work, hours, job search and availability. The ABS added an online form instruction for respondents in COVID-19 lockdown areas, and 2021 Census night fell on 10 August while Sydney and Melbourne were locked down.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Count of Unemployed Persons in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Count of unemployed family members, 2021 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of family members classified in either 2021 unemployed category, looking for full-time work or looking for part-time work, out of the nine categories of Labour force status.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","lim":"Unemployment is the category the August 2021 lockdowns disturb most, because job search and availability were both constrained and the ABS had to issue extra guidance to affected respondents. A family whose unemployed count rose between 2016 and 2021 may simply have been enumerated under restrictions, so this column should not carry a causal reading of the pandemic's labour market effect on its own.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":52},{"n":"CLFUH_P_11","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2011 Census household were unemployed, counting only those whose status was stated.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2011 Census household were unemployed, counting only those whose status was stated. The household unit takes in everyone usually resident in the dwelling, so a share house of unrelated job seekers registers here while the family column CLFUF_P_11 leaves them out. The 2011 dictionary records the underlying classification \"for the week prior to Census Night\" and applies it to persons aged 15 years and over.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Unemployed Usually Resident Persons in Household as Stated","t":"categorical","k":"Count of unemployed household members, 2011 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents whose 2011 labour force status was stated as unemployed, that is either of categories 4 and 5 of Labour Force Status, looking for full-time and looking for part-time work.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"The count is silent about who in the household is unemployed and about their relationship to the person on the row, so it cannot be used to say whether a child grew up in a jobless household. That question needs the household composition and relationship columns as well as this one.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":53},{"n":"CLFUH_P_16","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2016 Census household were unemployed, counting only those whose status was stated.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2016 Census household were unemployed, counting only those whose status was stated. The 2016 dictionary defines the source variable as recording \"for the week prior to Census night, a person's labour force status\" for persons aged 15 years and over. Two of the five contributing questions were amended for 2016, and those questions are the ones that decide whether a person counts as unemployed rather than outside the labour force.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter6402016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Unemployed Usually Resident Persons in Household as Stated","t":"categorical","k":"Count of unemployed household members, 2016 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents in either 2016 unemployed category of Labour Force Status, restricted to residents whose status was stated on the form.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Labour Force Status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter6402016","lim":"A zero here is ambiguous. It can mean nobody in the household was looking for work, or that the residents who were looking left the question blank and so fell outside the \"as stated\" scope, and the column carries nothing that separates the two cases.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":53},{"n":"CLFUH_P_21","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2021 Census household were unemployed, counting only those whose status was stated.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2021 Census household were unemployed, counting only those whose status was stated. The 2021 dictionary defines the source variable as \"a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night\" and records that the online form gained an instruction for respondents in areas under COVID-19 lockdown. Non-response to the question fell from 6.7 per cent in 2016 to 5.8 per cent in 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Unemployed Usually Resident Persons in Household as Stated","t":"categorical","k":"Count of unemployed household members, 2021 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents whose stated 2021 labour force status was unemployed, spanning both the looking-for-full-time-work and looking-for-part-time-work categories of the nine-category classification.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","lim":"This column cannot be used to date a household job loss. The Census asks about the week before Census night only, so a resident who lost work in the 2020 shutdowns and had found new work by August 2021 leaves no trace here, and the ACLD's five-year gaps between waves hide everything that happened in between.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":53},{"n":"CLTHP_P_21","d":"How many of ten named long-term health conditions the person reported at the 2021 Census, the first Census to ask the question.","full":"How many of ten named long-term health conditions the person reported at the 2021 Census, the first Census to ask the question. The dictionary defines it as \"the number of selected long-term health conditions a person has reported\", the ten being arthritis, asthma, cancer, dementia, diabetes, heart disease, kidney disease, lung condition, mental health condition and stroke. There is no 2011 or 2016 counterpart in the ACLD because the question is new for 2021, so this column cannot open a health trajectory that starts at an earlier wave.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of selected long-term health conditions (CLTHP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/count-selected-long-term-health-conditions-cthp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Count of Selected Long-term Health Conditions","k":"Census 2021 count of selected long-term health conditions (0, 1, 2, 3 or more)","def":"Six categories: 0 for none of the selected conditions, 1, 2, and 3 or more, plus & for not stated and V for overseas visitor. Reporting only \"any other long-term health condition\" scores 0, while a named condition plus \"any other\" scores 1.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of selected long-term health conditions (CLTHP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/count-selected-long-term-health-conditions-cthp","lim":"It is a count of ticked boxes, not a measure of severity or of burden. Three well-managed conditions outrank one disabling one, and any condition outside the ten named ones is invisible however serious. Non-response ran at 8.1 per cent in 2021, and those people sit in the separate not stated code rather than in the zero count, so any prevalence rate built from this column has to decide what to do with them.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"CNDCF_P_11","d":"How many non-dependent children were in the person's family at the 2011 Census, the first Census for which the ABS published this variable.","full":"How many non-dependent children were in the person's family at the 2011 Census, the first Census for which the ABS published this variable. The dictionary defines it as counting \"the number of non-dependent children in the family\" and adds that \"it includes up to three non-dependent children who were temporarily absent from the household on Census night\". A non-dependent child is a natural, adopted, step or foster child aged 15 or over who is not a full-time student aged 15 to 24 and has no partner or child of their own in the household.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Count of Non-Dependent Children in Family (CNDCF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of Non-dependent Children in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 Count of Non-Dependent Children in Family (CNDCF)","def":"A coded category rather than a plain integer: codes 00 to 06 give none through six or more non-dependent children in a couple family, and codes 07 to 13 repeat the range for a one-parent family, with @ for not applicable. The code therefore carries family type as well as the count.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Count of Non-Dependent Children in Family (CNDCF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It counts a relationship position, not an age. An adult son who has moved out is not here, and one who has moved back in with a partner is reclassified out of the count, so this column cannot be used to trace whether an adult child stayed at home. It also cannot be read as an integer without first mapping the couple-family and one-parent-family code blocks.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":54},{"n":"CNDCF_P_16","d":"How many non-dependent children were in the person's family at the 2016 Census.","full":"How many non-dependent children were in the person's family at the 2016 Census. The 2016 dictionary gives the same definition as 2011, \"Counts the number of non-dependent children in the family. It includes up to three non-dependent children who were temporarily absent from the household on Census night\", and the classification was not changed between the two Censuses. That makes CNDCF_P_11 and this column directly comparable, which is unusual among the ACLD's family variables.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Count of Non-Dependent Children in Family (CNDCF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter2102016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of Non-dependent Children in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 Count of Non-Dependent Children in Family (CNDCF)","def":"A category code split by family type: a run of codes for couple families from no non-dependent children to six or more, a parallel run for one-parent families, and a not-applicable code for households with no family or no children.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Count of Non-Dependent Children in Family (CNDCF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter2102016","lim":"The three-person cap on temporarily absent children bites hardest on large families, so a family with four adult children of whom all were away on Census night is understated. The count also has no bearing on whether those children were financially dependent, which is a matter of the Census relationship coding rather than of income.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":54},{"n":"CNDCF_P_21","d":"How many non-dependent children were in the person's family at the 2021 Census.","full":"How many non-dependent children were in the person's family at the 2021 Census. The dictionary counts \"the number of non-dependent children in the family\", including up to three who were temporarily absent on Census night, and states that no changes were made for 2021. It is derived from the relationship in household, age, education attendance and temporary absence questions, and picks up the non-dependent natural or adopted, step and foster child categories of Relationship in household.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of non-dependent children in family (CNDCF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-non-dependent-children-family-cndcf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of Non-dependent Children in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 Count of non-dependent children in family (CNDCF)","def":"Fifteen categories in 2021: none through six or more non-dependent children for couple families, the same range again for one-parent families, and one not-applicable category covering households without families and other non-family arrangements.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of non-dependent children in family (CNDCF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-non-dependent-children-family-cndcf","lim":"A young adult who stayed home through the 2021 lockdowns and one who returned home because of them are indistinguishable here, since the Census records only the arrangement on the night. Nor does the column say anything about the children themselves, whose own records in the ACLD are separate rows if they were sampled at all.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":54},{"n":"CNDCH_P_11","d":"How many non-dependent children lived in the person's 2011 Census household, summing across every family in the dwelling.","full":"How many non-dependent children lived in the person's 2011 Census household, summing across every family in the dwelling. The concept of a non-dependent child is the Census one used in CNDCF: a natural, adopted, step or foster child aged 15 or over who is not a full-time student aged 15 to 24 and has no partner or child of their own usually resident in the household. Where CNDCF_P_11 is confined to the person's own family, this column adds the non-dependent children of any second family sharing the dwelling.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Count of Non-Dependent Children in Family (CNDCF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Non-dependent Children in Household","t":"categorical","k":"Count of non-dependent children in household, 2011 Census","def":"A whole-number count of usual residents in the dwelling who meet the Census non-dependent child definition. Unlike the family version it is a straight count rather than a code split by family type.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Count of Non-Dependent Children in Family (CNDCF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It cannot tell you whose children they are. In a two-family household the count mixes both families' adult children, and in the person's own record there is nothing to say whether the person is one of those non-dependent children or one of the parents.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":54},{"n":"CNDCH_P_16","d":"How many non-dependent children lived in the person's 2016 Census household, across all families in the dwelling.","full":"How many non-dependent children lived in the person's 2016 Census household, across all families in the dwelling. The 2016 dictionary defines the family version as counting \"the number of non-dependent children in the family\" and including up to three who were temporarily absent on Census night, and the underlying relationship coding did not change between 2011 and 2016. A move between the two waves changes the dwelling being counted, so this column tracks the person's living arrangement rather than a fixed household.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Count of Non-Dependent Children in Family (CNDCF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter2102016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Non-dependent Children in Household","t":"categorical","k":"Count of non-dependent children in household, 2016 Census","def":"A whole-number count of usual residents of the dwelling classified as non-dependent children, that is children aged 15 and over who are not dependent students and have no partner or child of their own in the household.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Count of Non-Dependent Children in Family (CNDCF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter2102016","lim":"Because the concept turns on relationships within the dwelling, a young adult who moves out to a share house stops being anyone's non-dependent child and appears in nobody's count, even though the Census still enumerates them. The column therefore undercounts adult children in the population and should not be used as a measure of how many young adults live outside the family home.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":54},{"n":"CNDCH_P_21","d":"How many non-dependent children lived in the person's 2021 Census household, across all families in the dwelling.","full":"How many non-dependent children lived in the person's 2021 Census household, across all families in the dwelling. The 2021 dictionary sets out the concept on the family version: a child aged 15 or over who is not a full-time student aged 15 to 24 and has no identified partner or child usually resident in the household, and it records that nothing changed for 2021. Because the definition held steady from 2011, the movement in this column across the three waves is a movement in living arrangements rather than in classification.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of non-dependent children in family (CNDCF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-non-dependent-children-family-cndcf","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Non-dependent Children in Household","t":"categorical","k":"Count of non-dependent children in household, 2021 Census","def":"A whole-number count of usual residents of the dwelling meeting the 2021 Census non-dependent child definition, derived from the relationship in household, age, education attendance and temporary absence questions.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of non-dependent children in family (CNDCF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-non-dependent-children-family-cndcf","lim":"The count says nothing about age beyond the 15-year floor, so a household with one 16-year-old school leaver and one with a 45-year-old son both read as one. Reading it as a measure of adults living with their parents requires the age columns as well.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":54},{"n":"CNOSH_P_11","d":"Whether the person's 2011 Census dwelling had spare bedrooms or needed more, on the Canadian National Occupancy Standard.","full":"Whether the person's 2011 Census dwelling had spare bedrooms or needed more, on the Canadian National Occupancy Standard. The 2016 dictionary, which first defined it, calls it \"a housing utilisation measure based upon a comparison of the number of bedrooms in a dwelling together with a series of household demographics such as the number of usual residents, their relationship to one another, their age and sex\". It was not a standard Census output variable in 2011, being \"a new derived item for 2016\", so the 2011 value in the ACLD is the same derivation applied retrospectively to 2011 records.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Housing Suitability (HOSD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter36002016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Housing Utilisation","t":"categorical","k":"Housing utilisation on the Canadian National Occupancy Standard, 2011 Census","def":"An ordered category running from four or more extra bedrooms needed, through no bedrooms needed or spare, to four or more bedrooms spare, with codes for unable to determine, not stated and not applicable. It applies to occupied private dwellings only.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Housing Suitability (HOSD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter36002016","lim":"A dwelling short of bedrooms on this standard is not the same as an overcrowded one in any legal or policy sense, and the standard's assumptions about who may share a room are cultural, which the ABS has noted makes the measure a poor fit for some Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander households. The measure also takes no account of room size, dwelling condition or tenure.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":55},{"n":"CNOSH_P_16","d":"Whether the person's 2016 Census dwelling had spare bedrooms or needed more, on the Canadian National Occupancy Standard.","full":"Whether the person's 2016 Census dwelling had spare bedrooms or needed more, on the Canadian National Occupancy Standard. The ABS calls it \"a housing utilisation measure based upon a comparison of the number of bedrooms in a dwelling together with a series of household demographics such as the number of usual residents, their relationship to one another, their age and sex\", and 2016 is the first Census at which it was published as a standard derived item. The standard allows no more than two people per bedroom, lets children under five of different sexes share and children under 18 of the same sex share, and gives single adults and couples a bedroom each.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Housing Suitability (HOSD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter36002016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Housing Utilisation","t":"categorical","k":"Housing utilisation on the Canadian National Occupancy Standard, 2016 Census","def":"Twelve categories: codes 01 to 04 for four, three, two and one extra bedrooms needed, 05 for none needed or spare, 06 to 09 for one to four or more bedrooms spare, 10 for unable to determine, && for not stated and @@ for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Housing Suitability (HOSD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter36002016","lim":"The bedroom count comes from the dwelling form, so a study, sleepout or converted garage used for sleeping may not be counted as a bedroom and the dwelling looks more crowded than it is. Non-private dwellings, unoccupied dwellings and visitor-only households are all not applicable, so an absent value here is often a statement about the dwelling type rather than about crowding.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":55},{"n":"CNOSH_P_21","d":"Whether the person's 2021 Census dwelling had spare bedrooms or needed more, on the Canadian National Occupancy Standard.","full":"Whether the person's 2021 Census dwelling had spare bedrooms or needed more, on the Canadian National Occupancy Standard. The 2021 dictionary states that \"no changes have been made for 2021\" and that the variable was first introduced in the 2016 Census, having been available only through customised data requests before then. The 2016 and 2021 values are therefore on the same basis, while the 2011 value in the ACLD predates the variable's standard release.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Housing suitability (HOSD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/housing-suitability-hosd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Housing Utilisation","t":"categorical","k":"Housing utilisation on the Canadian National Occupancy Standard, 2021 Census","def":"Twelve ordered categories from four or more extra bedrooms needed to four or more bedrooms spare, with separate codes for unable to determine, not stated and not applicable, applying to occupied private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Housing suitability (HOSD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/housing-suitability-hosd","lim":"The 2021 measure describes the household as enumerated on 10 August 2021, when lockdowns kept many people at addresses they would not normally have occupied, so a shortfall of bedrooms in that year can be a pandemic artefact. It also carries no information about whether the household chose its arrangement or could afford a larger dwelling.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":55},{"n":"CPR65D_P_11","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2011 Census household were aged 65 to 74.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2011 Census household were aged 65 to 74. Age comes from the 2011 Census variable AGEP, which \"contains a person's age at last birthday\" calculated from date of birth where given, from stated age otherwise, and imputed where neither is supplied. It sits with CPR75D_P_11 and CPR85D_P_11, which cover 75 to 84 and 85 and over, so the three together describe the older people in the dwelling.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household Aged 65-74","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members aged 65 to 74, 2011 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents whose 2011 Census age fell in the 65 to 74 band. Age is output in whole years only, so the band edges are exact birthdays at Census night rather than approximations.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"The person on the row is included in their own household count if they fall in the band, so this is not a count of other older people in the dwelling. Where age was imputed the resident may have been placed in the band by the ABS rather than by their own answer, and IFAGEP, not this column, is what flags that.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":56},{"n":"CPR65D_P_16","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2016 Census household were aged 65 to 74.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2016 Census household were aged 65 to 74. The 2016 dictionary defines age as \"a person's age, and is collected for each person\", calculated from date of birth where provided, from stated age where not, and imputed where neither is available. Everyone in the ACLD panel is five years older at each wave, so a household that scored zero in 2011 can score one in 2016 with no change in who lives there.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household Aged 65-74","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members aged 65 to 74, 2016 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents whose 2016 Census age was between 65 and 74 inclusive, age being reported in completed whole years at Census night.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302016","lim":"The band boundaries move through the panel rather than staying with the same people, so a rise from CPR65D_P_11 to CPR65D_P_16 usually means someone crossed 65, and a fall usually means someone crossed 75 into CPR75D_P_16. Reading the change as arrival or departure of an older resident is the mistake this column invites.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":56},{"n":"CPR65D_P_21","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2021 Census household were aged 65 to 74.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2021 Census household were aged 65 to 74. The 2021 dictionary says the age variable \"collects each person's age\" and that \"if age is not reported, it is imputed\", with date of birth preferred over stated age where both are given. The age question changed slightly for 2021: the online form asks for date of birth first and offers a checkbox for people who do not know it, and non-response was 4.4 per cent.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household Aged 65-74","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members aged 65 to 74, 2021 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents aged 65 to 74 at 10 August 2021, age being output in whole years and imputed where the form gave neither a date of birth nor a stated age.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","lim":"Age imputation is invisible in this count, and the imputed ages are drawn against a population age distribution, so band counts in poorly completed households carry more ABS modelling than reported fact. The column also gives no sex or relationship detail, so it cannot separate an older couple from a lone older person sharing with younger residents.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":56},{"n":"CPR75D_P_11","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2011 Census household were aged 75 to 84.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2011 Census household were aged 75 to 84. It uses the 2011 Census age variable AGEP, which \"contains a person's age at last birthday\" and is available singly for 0 to 115 years. The band sits between CPR65D_P_11 and CPR85D_P_11, and the three bands together cover everyone in the dwelling aged 65 and over.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household Aged 75-84","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members aged 75 to 84, 2011 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents whose 2011 Census age was between 75 and 84 inclusive, taken from the whole-year age output.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It counts residents, not need. A household with two people in their late seventies may be entirely independent, while one with a single 76-year-old may need daily care, and nothing in this column separates them. The core activity need for assistance and unpaid care columns are what carry that information.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":57},{"n":"CPR75D_P_16","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2016 Census household were aged 75 to 84.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2016 Census household were aged 75 to 84. The 2016 dictionary defines age as calculated from date of birth where provided, from stated age where not, and imputed where neither is available. Because the ACLD follows the same people forward, a resident who was in the 65 to 74 band in 2011 will usually have moved into this band by 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household Aged 75-84","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members aged 75 to 84, 2016 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents aged 75 to 84 at the 2016 Census, from the whole-year age output that runs singly across the full age range.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302016","lim":"Residents in aged care are outside the scope of this count, because a residential aged care facility is a non-private dwelling and is not enumerated as a household. A person whose parent moved into care between waves therefore shows a fall in this column that records a change of dwelling type, not a death or a move away.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":57},{"n":"CPR75D_P_21","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2021 Census household were aged 75 to 84.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2021 Census household were aged 75 to 84. The 2021 dictionary states that the age variable \"collects each person's age\" and that ages outside the acceptable range, or inconsistent with the relationship answers, are imputed. Age is the one variable in this family of columns whose 2021 wording changed, with the online form asking for date of birth before stated age.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household Aged 75-84","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members aged 75 to 84, 2021 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents aged 75 to 84 at 10 August 2021, on the whole-year age output, with imputation applied where age was missing or implausible.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","lim":"The column cannot support a mortality analysis. A resident who died between the 2016 and 2021 waves and a resident who moved out both reduce the count by one, and the ACLD carries no death indicator inside these Census aggregates to separate the two.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":57},{"n":"CPR85D_P_11","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2011 Census household were aged 85 or over.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2011 Census household were aged 85 or over. It is the open-ended top band of the three household age counts, built on the 2011 Census age variable AGEP, which is \"available for 0 to 115 years singly\". Unlike CPR65D_P_11 and CPR75D_P_11, this band has no upper edge, so nobody leaves it by ageing.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household Aged 85 and Over","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members aged 85 and over, 2011 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents aged 85 years or more at the 2011 Census, from an age variable that runs singly to 115 years.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"Very old ages are the ones most exposed to reporting and imputation error, and the count offers no way to check them: a household recorded with a resident of 103 cannot be distinguished from one where a date of birth was mistyped. The band is also so thin in a 5 per cent sample that household-level analysis of it will run into small-cell suppression.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":58},{"n":"CPR85D_P_16","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2016 Census household were aged 85 or over.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2016 Census household were aged 85 or over. The 2016 dictionary defines the age variable as collected for each person and derived from date of birth in preference to stated age. As the top band it only ever gains members through ageing, so a fall between CPR85D_P_11 and this column means a resident left the household or died, never that they aged out.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household Aged 85 and Over","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members aged 85 and over, 2016 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents aged 85 years or more at the 2016 Census, with no upper bound on the band.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter302016","lim":"The count is confined to private dwellings, and by 85 a large share of the population lives in residential aged care, which the Census enumerates as a non-private dwelling. This column therefore describes the minority of the very old who remain in private households and cannot be scaled up to the age group as a whole.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":58},{"n":"CPR85D_P_21","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2021 Census household were aged 85 or over.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2021 Census household were aged 85 or over. The 2021 dictionary records that age \"is imputed\" where it is not reported, using other information on the form and a population age distribution, and puts non-response to the age question at 4.4 per cent. Age was one of the few Census questions whose wording changed for 2021, with the online form asking for date of birth first.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household Aged 85 and Over","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members aged 85 and over, 2021 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents aged 85 years or more at 10 August 2021, an open-ended top band on a whole-year age variable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","lim":"The 2021 value describes where people were on Census night during a pandemic, when some very old people were staying with family and others were locked out of visits, so an 85-and-over resident recorded in a household in 2021 need not have been living there ordinarily. The column carries no usual-residence check of its own.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":58},{"n":"CPRF_P_11","d":"How many people were in the person's family at the 2011 Census, the first Census for which the ABS published this variable.","full":"How many people were in the person's family at the 2011 Census, the first Census for which the ABS published this variable. The dictionary defines it as counting \"the number of persons in a family\" and says it \"includes other related individuals who are not part of the primary couple relationship, and other related individuals who are not part of a lone parent-child relationship or other blood relationship (e.g. it includes in-laws)\". It counts a family, not a dwelling, so unrelated residents of the same household are excluded.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Count of Persons in Family (CPRF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of All Persons in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 Count of Persons in Family (CPRF)","def":"Six categories: 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 or more persons in family, plus @ for not applicable. The value can include up to three people who were temporarily absent from the family on Census night.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Count of Persons in Family (CPRF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"A family cannot have fewer than two people, so a person living alone is coded not applicable rather than one, and the same code covers unrelated people in family households, non-classifiable households and non-private dwellings. Treating @ as a household of one is the error this column invites.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":59},{"n":"CPRF_P_16","d":"How many people were in the person's family at the 2016 Census.","full":"How many people were in the person's family at the 2016 Census. The 2016 dictionary repeats the 2011 wording word for word, counting \"the number of persons in a family\" including in-laws and other related individuals outside the primary couple or lone parent relationship, and allowing \"up to three persons who were temporarily absent from the family on Census night\". Nothing changed between 2011 and 2016, so this column and CPRF_P_11 measure the same thing.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Count of Persons in Family (CPRF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter2402016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of All Persons in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 Count of Persons in Family (CPRF)","def":"Six categories running from two persons in family to six or more, with @ for not applicable, covering families in family households only.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Count of Persons in Family (CPRF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter2402016","lim":"The top category collapses everything from six people upward, so growth in large families is invisible and the column cannot produce a mean family size. A household containing two families also produces two family counts, only one of which is on this person's row.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":59},{"n":"CPRF_P_21","d":"How many people were in the person's family at the 2021 Census.","full":"How many people were in the person's family at the 2021 Census. The dictionary says the variable \"counts the number of people in a family\" including people outside the primary couple or lone parent-child relationship and non-blood relatives such as in-laws, and confirms no changes were made for 2021. It is derived from Relationship in household (RLHP) and Count of persons temporarily absent from family (CPAF), the second of which is worth reading alongside it.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of persons in family (CPRF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-persons-family-cprf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of All Persons in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 Count of persons in family (CPRF)","def":"Six categories from two persons in family to six or more, plus not applicable, which covers unrelated persons in family households, non-family and non-classifiable households, unoccupied dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory or off-shore areas.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of persons in family (CPRF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-persons-family-cprf","lim":"The Census form has room for only three temporarily absent people, so a large family with four or more members away on 2021 Census night is understated, and the 2021 lockdowns made temporary absence unusually common in some places. The column also says nothing about who the family members are, which needs the relationship and family composition variables.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":59},{"n":"CTGP_11","d":"What kind of child the person was in their family at the 2011 Census, on the version of the classification that treats grandchildren as children.","full":"What kind of child the person was in their family at the 2011 Census, on the version of the classification that treats grandchildren as children. The dictionary says it \"records the different parent-child relationship within families\" and \"differs from the standard CTPP Child Type variable in that it recognises grandparent-grandchild relationships as parent-child relationships, regardless of the age of the grandchild\". It was new for the 2011 Census Dictionary, so there is no earlier ACLD wave to compare it with.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Child Type (including grandchildren) (CTGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child Type (including grandchildren)","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 Child Type including grandchildren (CTGP)","def":"A category code covering natural or adopted child, step child of a male parent, step child of a female parent, foster child, grandchild, otherwise related child under 15 and unrelated child under 15, with not applicable and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Child Type (including grandchildren) (CTGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"The ABS warns that this variable \"cannot be used with standard family classifications\": crossing it with family composition or child type produces double counting, because a grandchild is coded as a child here and as something else in the standard family coding. It also says nothing about the age of the child beyond the under-15 categories.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":60},{"n":"CTGP_16","d":"What kind of child the person was in their family at the 2016 Census, on the classification that counts grandchildren as children.","full":"What kind of child the person was in their family at the 2016 Census, on the classification that counts grandchildren as children. The 2016 dictionary keeps the 2011 wording, that it \"records the different parent-child relationship within families\" and \"differs from the standard Child Type (CTPP) variable in that it recognises grandparent-grandchild relationships as parent-child relationships, regardless of the age of the grandchild\". Because the wording is unchanged, a person who moved between CTGP_11 and this column changed household, not classification.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Child Type (including grandchildren) (CTGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter2502016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child Type (including grandchildren)","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 Child Type including grandchildren (CTGP)","def":"A category code with a grandchild category alongside the natural or adopted, step, foster, otherwise related and unrelated child categories, plus not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Child Type (including grandchildren) (CTGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter2502016","lim":"It has to be paired with the grandparent versions of the other family variables, Relationship in household (including grandchildren) and Grandparent families, and cannot be crossed with the standard family classifications without double counting. It also gives no information about the grandparent, whose own record is a separate row if that person was sampled.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":60},{"n":"CTGP_21","d":"What kind of child the person was in their family at the 2021 Census, on the classification that counts grandchildren as children.","full":"What kind of child the person was in their family at the 2021 Census, on the classification that counts grandchildren as children. The 2021 dictionary states that \"no changes have been made for 2021\" and that the variable is derived from Relationship in household (including grandchildren) (RLGP), coding a person as a grandchild where their relationship code is grandchild under 15, dependent student grandchild or non-dependent grandchild. A 15-year-old or older grandchild is coded 5 Grandchild here and not applicable in CTPP_21, which is the practical difference between the two columns.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Child type (including grandchildren) (CTGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/child-type-including-grandchildren-ctgp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child Type (including grandchildren)","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 Child type including grandchildren (CTGP)","def":"Nine categories: natural or adopted child of both parents or lone parent, step child of male parent, step child of female parent, foster child so stated, grandchild, otherwise related child under 15, unrelated child under 15, plus @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Child type (including grandchildren) (CTGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/child-type-including-grandchildren-ctgp","lim":"The variable can only be used with the grandparent versions of the family classifications, so it does not slot into an analysis built on family composition or relationship in household. It is also blind to grandchildren living apart from their grandparents, which is the great majority of them.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":61},{"n":"CTPP_11","d":"What kind of child the person was in their family at the 2011 Census, on the standard classification.","full":"What kind of child the person was in their family at the 2011 Census, on the standard classification. The dictionary defines it in one line, that it \"records the different parent-child relationships within families\", and applies it to all children. It is the counterpart of CTGP_11, which differs only in treating grandchildren as children.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Child Type (CTPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 Child Type (CTPP)","def":"Eight categories: 1 natural or adopted child of both parents or lone parent, 2 step-child of male parent, 3 step-child of female parent, 4 foster child so stated, 5 otherwise related child under 15, 6 unrelated child under 15, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Child Type (CTPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"Being a child here is a position in a household, not an age. A 40-year-old living with a parent is coded as a natural or adopted child, while a 16-year-old living with a grandparent falls to not applicable, so the column cannot be used to identify children in the ordinary sense without the age variable.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":62},{"n":"CTPP_16","d":"What kind of child the person was in their family at the 2016 Census, on the standard classification.","full":"What kind of child the person was in their family at the 2016 Census, on the standard classification. The 2016 dictionary keeps the same one-line definition as 2011, that the variable \"records the different parent-child relationships within families\", and the category list is unchanged. A person whose CTPP_11 and CTPP_16 values differ has therefore changed their position in a household, most often by leaving home or by a parent repartnering.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Child Type (CTPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter2602016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 Child Type (CTPP)","def":"Eight categories covering natural or adopted child, step child of a male or female parent, foster child, otherwise related child under 15 and unrelated child under 15, with not applicable and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Child Type (CTPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter2602016","lim":"The step child categories rest on how the form was filled in rather than on any legal status, and the ABS relies on secondary evidence such as surnames when a child is listed as Person 2 with both parents present. Transitions into and out of the step categories between waves are therefore partly a coding artefact.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":62},{"n":"CTPP_21","d":"What kind of child the person was in their family at the 2021 Census, on the standard classification.","full":"What kind of child the person was in their family at the 2021 Census, on the standard classification. The dictionary records that \"no changes have been made for 2021\" and that the variable is derived from the relationship in household question, with people aged 15 and over classified as children only where they live with a natural, adoptive, step, foster or grandparent. The ABS has identified an overcount of step children in some states and territories in 2021, affecting couple families where one spouse was temporarily absent.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Child type (CTPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/child-type-ctpp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Child Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 Child type (CTPP)","def":"Eight categories: natural or adopted child of both parents or lone parent, step child of male parent, step child of female parent, foster child so stated, otherwise related child under 15, unrelated child under 15, plus @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Child type (CTPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/child-type-ctpp","lim":"The known 2021 step child overcount means a change from natural child in 2016 to step child in 2021 can be a processing error rather than a real change in family structure, and the affected states are not flagged in the data itself. Beyond that, the classification cannot identify a child's non-resident parent, since the Census only sees the dwelling.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":63},{"n":"CUNCAREF_P_11","d":"How many people in the person's 2011 Census family provided unpaid care to someone with a disability.","full":"How many people in the person's 2011 Census family provided unpaid care to someone with a disability. It aggregates the 2011 Census variable UNCAREP, which \"records people who in the two weeks prior to Census Night spent time providing unpaid care, help or assistance to family members or others because of a disability, a long term illness or problems related to old age\". The dictionary adds that it takes in people receiving Carer Allowance or Carer Payment and excludes work done through a voluntary organisation.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Assistance to a Person with a Disability (UNCAREP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of Persons in Family Who Provide Unpaid Assistance to a Person With a Disability","t":"categorical","k":"Count of family members providing unpaid assistance, 2011 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of family members. The underlying variable is a yes or no answer, applicable to persons aged 15 years and over, with separate codes for not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Assistance to a Person with a Disability (UNCAREP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"No hours are collected, so a family member giving occasional help with shopping counts the same as one providing full-time care. The person receiving the care may also live somewhere else entirely, which means this column cannot be read as evidence that anyone in the family needs assistance.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":64},{"n":"CUNCAREF_P_16","d":"How many people in the person's 2016 Census family provided unpaid care to someone with a disability.","full":"How many people in the person's 2016 Census family provided unpaid care to someone with a disability. The 2016 dictionary defines the underlying variable as recording \"people who in the two weeks prior to Census night spent time providing unpaid care, help or assistance to family members or others because of a disability, a long-term health condition or problems related to old age\". The 2016 wording says long-term health condition where 2011 said long term illness, but the scope of the question is the same.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Assistance to a Person with a Disability (UNCAREP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10602016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of Persons in Family Who Provide Unpaid Assistance to a Person With a Disability","t":"categorical","k":"Count of family members providing unpaid assistance, 2016 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of family members who answered yes to the 2016 unpaid assistance question, which is asked of persons aged 15 years and over and has a two-week reference period.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Assistance to a Person with a Disability (UNCAREP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10602016","lim":"Non-response to the underlying question was 8.9 per cent in 2016, and a family member who left it blank is not counted, so a zero can mean nobody cared or nobody answered. This bites hardest in the households least likely to complete a form fully, which are not a random subset.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":64},{"n":"CUNCAREF_P_21","d":"How many people in the person's 2021 Census family provided unpaid care to someone with a disability, a health condition or because of old age.","full":"How many people in the person's 2021 Census family provided unpaid care to someone with a disability, a health condition or because of old age. The 2021 dictionary defines the underlying variable as recording \"the number of people who in the two weeks prior to Census Night spent time providing unpaid care, help or assistance to family members or others because of: a disability, a long-term health condition, problems related to old age\". The variable was renamed for 2021 from Unpaid assistance to a person with a disability, with scope and content unchanged, so the ACLD's shorter 2011 and 2016 labels describe the same question.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid assistance to a person with a disability, health condition, or due to old age (UNCAREP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/unpaid-assistance-person-disability-health-condition-or-due-old-age-uncarep","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of Persons in Family Who Provide Unpaid Assistance to a Person With a Disability","t":"categorical","k":"Count of family members providing unpaid assistance, 2021 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of family members answering yes to the 2021 question, which is asked of persons aged 15 years and over and has five categories at the person level: no assistance, provided assistance, not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid assistance to a person with a disability, health condition, or due to old age (UNCAREP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/unpaid-assistance-person-disability-health-condition-or-due-old-age-uncarep","lim":"The count rose partly for measurement reasons: non-response to the question fell from 8.9 per cent in 2016 to 6.7 per cent in 2021, so more family members were classifiable in 2021 than in 2016. A rise in this column between the two waves is therefore not by itself evidence of more caring.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":64},{"n":"CUNCAREH_P_11","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2011 Census household provided unpaid care to someone with a disability.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2011 Census household provided unpaid care to someone with a disability. It counts over the whole dwelling rather than the family, so a flatmate who cares for a parent living elsewhere is inside this count and outside CUNCAREF_P_11. The 2011 dictionary defines the underlying variable as recording people who \"spent time providing unpaid care, help or assistance to family members or others because of a disability, a long term illness or problems related to old age\" in the two weeks before Census night.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Assistance to a Person with a Disability (UNCAREP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household Who Provide Unpaid Assistance to a Person With a Disability","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members providing unpaid assistance, 2011 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents aged 15 and over who answered yes to the 2011 unpaid assistance question, which has five categories including not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Assistance to a Person with a Disability (UNCAREP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It does not say whether the care was given inside the household. A household count of two carers may be two people looking after each other, two people looking after a third resident, or two people travelling out to care for relatives, and nothing here separates those cases from the core activity need for assistance columns.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":65},{"n":"CUNCAREH_P_16","d":"How many usual residents of the person's 2016 Census household provided unpaid care to someone with a disability.","full":"How many usual residents of the person's 2016 Census household provided unpaid care to someone with a disability. The 2016 dictionary defines the underlying question as recording people who in the two weeks before Census night \"spent time providing unpaid care, help or assistance to family members or others because of a disability, a long-term health condition or problems related to old age\". The question itself did not change between 2011 and 2016, so the difference between this column and CUNCAREH_P_11 reflects who was in the dwelling as much as who was caring.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Assistance to a Person with a Disability (UNCAREP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10602016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household Who Provide Unpaid Assistance to a Person With a Disability","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members providing unpaid assistance, 2016 Census","def":"A small whole-number count of usual residents aged 15 and over who answered yes to the 2016 unpaid assistance question, a binary item with no measure of hours or intensity.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Assistance to a Person with a Disability (UNCAREP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10602016","lim":"Households are not stable across the ACLD panel, so this count follows the person to whatever dwelling they were in on 2016 Census night. Someone who moved out of a caring household between 2011 and 2016 shows a fall here that describes their new address rather than any change in the care being given.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":65},{"n":"CUNCAREH_P_21","d":"How many people in the person's 2021 Census household reported providing unpaid assistance because of disability, illness or old age.","full":"How many people in the person's 2021 Census household reported providing unpaid assistance because of disability, illness or old age. It aggregates the person-level UNCAREP item, which the ABS scopes to usual residents aged 15 and over and to the two weeks before Census night, up to the household. The _P suffix marks a household attribute copied onto every person record in that household, so two people in the same dwelling carry the same value. For 2021 the underlying item was renamed to add health condition and old age to its title, with no change to what it collects.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid assistance to a person with a disability, health condition, or due to old age (UNCAREP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/unpaid-assistance-person-disability-health-condition-or-due-old-age-uncarep","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Persons in Household Who Provide Unpaid Assistance to a Person With a Disability","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A small non-negative count of persons, bounded above by the number of usual residents aged 15 and over, with separate codes for not stated and for records where the item does not apply. The underlying UNCAREP response is a yes or no, so each contributing person adds exactly one.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid assistance to a person with a disability, health condition, or due to old age (UNCAREP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/unpaid-assistance-person-disability-health-condition-or-due-old-age-uncarep","lim":"It cannot measure how much care a household provides. The Census records only whether unpaid assistance was given in the two weeks before Census night, so a household with one person helping a neighbour for an hour scores the same as a household with two full-time carers. The people receiving the care need not live in the household, so this is not a count of household members who need assistance.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":65},{"n":"DLOD_P_11","d":"Whether the person's dwelling at the 2011 Census stood in a communal location such as a caravan park, marina or self-contained retirement village.","full":"Whether the person's dwelling at the 2011 Census stood in a communal location such as a caravan park, marina or self-contained retirement village. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as \"Describes the location of a private dwelling. The majority of private dwellings appear in the 'Other' category.\" In 2011 the information was collected by ABS field officers at enumeration; from 2016 it is taken from the ABS Address Register, so this column rests on a different collection method from DLOD_P_16 and DLOD_P_21. The _P suffix marks a dwelling attribute carried on the person's record.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Location (DLOD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Dwelling Location","t":"categorical","k":"Census dwelling location code (2011)","def":"Six categories: 1 caravan/residential park or camping ground, 2 marina, 3 manufactured home estate, 4 retirement village (self-contained), 5 other, and @ not applicable.
