The labels have been stable since 2006, when category 1 changed from 'Caravan park' and category 4 from 'Accommodation for the retired or aged (self-care)'.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Location (DLOD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It does not say what kind of dwelling the person lives in. A separate house, a flat and a caravan can all sit in the 'Other' category, and Dwelling Structure (STRD) is the column that separates them. Non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping records are coded not applicable, so an empty value is a scope exclusion rather than a non-response.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":66},{"n":"DLOD_P_16","d":"Whether the person's dwelling at the 2016 Census stood in a communal location such as a caravan park, marina or manufactured home estate.","full":"Whether the person's dwelling at the 2016 Census stood in a communal location such as a caravan park, marina or manufactured home estate. The change that matters against 2011 is the source rather than the concept: from 2016 dwelling location is taken from the ABS Address Register, recorded by address canvassing officers while the mail-out frame was built, with ABS field officers still collecting it in traditionally enumerated areas. The categories did not change, so a movement in the caravan park count between DLOD_P_11 and DLOD_P_16 can reflect the new frame rather than people moving.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Location (DLOD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter29802016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Dwelling Location","t":"categorical","k":"Census dwelling location code (2016)","def":"Six categories: 1 caravan/residential park or camping ground, 2 marina, 3 manufactured home estate, 4 retirement village (self-contained), 5 other, and @ not applicable. The great majority of private dwellings are coded 'Other'.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Location (DLOD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter29802016","lim":"It cannot be read as a count of people living in caravans or manufactured homes, because the category describes the site and not the structure standing on it: a permanent house inside a residential park is coded to the park. Because the value now comes from an administrative register rather than an observation on the night, a dwelling whose use changed after the register was compiled can be misplaced.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":66},{"n":"DLOD_P_21","d":"Whether the person's dwelling at the 2021 Census stood in a communal location such as a caravan park, marina or retirement village.","full":"Whether the person's dwelling at the 2021 Census stood in a communal location such as a caravan park, marina or retirement village. The ABS says \"This variable describes the location of dwellings.\", and for 2021 it comes from the ABS Address Register with verification by field officers during collection; where the location cannot be determined the record defaults to 'Other'. Nothing changed in the categories between 2016 and 2021, so DLOD_P_16 and DLOD_P_21 are directly comparable, while DLOD_P_11 was collected a different way.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Dwelling location (DLOD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/dwelling-location-dlod","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Dwelling Location","t":"categorical","k":"Census dwelling location code (2021)","def":"Six categories: 1 caravan/residential park or camping ground, 2 marina, 3 manufactured home estate, 4 retirement village (self-contained), 5 other, and @ not applicable. There is no non-response rate, because the value is administrative rather than reported.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Dwelling location (DLOD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/dwelling-location-dlod","lim":"The 'Other' category is not evidence of an ordinary house: it also absorbs every dwelling whose location could not be determined during processing, so it mixes true negatives with unresolved cases. Where an establishment could fit more than one category a single code was chosen during processing, so a retirement village inside a residential park appears under one heading only.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":66},{"n":"DOMP_11","d":"Hours the person spent on unpaid domestic work in the week before the 2011 Census, in five broad bands.","full":"Hours the person spent on unpaid domestic work in the week before the 2011 Census, in five broad bands. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as, \"For each person aged 15 years and over, records the number of hours spent performing unpaid domestic work. It includes work that the person did without pay, in their own home and in other places, for themselves, their family and other people in the household, in the week prior to Census Night.\" The question, the reference week and the five bands are unchanged at 2016 and 2021, so DOMP_11, DOMP_16 and DOMP_21 form a comparable series.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours","t":"categorical","k":"Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2011)","def":"Eight codes: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 5 to 14 hours, 4 15 to 29 hours, 5 30 hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"The bands cannot be added up as hours. The top band is open, so '30 hours or more' has no ceiling and any average built from band midpoints understates the heaviest workloads. The measure also covers only the single week before Census night, so a person who was ill, travelling or on holiday that week records a figure that is not their usual pattern.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":67},{"n":"DOMP_16","d":"Hours the person spent on unpaid domestic work in the week before the 2016 Census, in the same five bands used in 2011.","full":"Hours the person spent on unpaid domestic work in the week before the 2016 Census, in the same five bands used in 2011. The 2016 Census Dictionary describes the item as \"Time people spent in the previous week doing domestic work without pay for themselves and their household.\" Neither the question nor the bands changed between 2011 and 2016, so this column is directly comparable with DOMP_11; what did move is response, with 8.8 per cent of in-scope persons not answering the item at 2016 against 6.6 per cent at 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid work variables including Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58002016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours","t":"categorical","k":"Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2016)","def":"Eight codes: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 5 to 14 hours, 4 15 to 29 hours, 5 30 hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid work variables including Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58002016","lim":"A rise or fall against 2011 or 2021 can be a change in who answered rather than a change in behaviour, because non-response to this item is high by Census standards and is not imputed. Treating 'not stated' as nil hours therefore biases the 2016 wave more than the 2021 wave, since fewer people left the question blank in 2021.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":67},{"n":"DOMP_21","d":"Hours the person spent on unpaid domestic work in the week before the 2021 Census, in five broad bands.","full":"Hours the person spent on unpaid domestic work in the week before the 2021 Census, in five broad bands. The ABS defines it as \"This variable records the number of hours people spent in the previous week doing domestic work without pay.\" No changes were made for 2021, so the column lines up with DOMP_16 and DOMP_11, and non-response fell from 8.8 per cent in 2016 to 6.6 per cent in 2021. Where a respondent marked more than one box, the highest 'yes' band was accepted.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid domestic work: number of hours (DOMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/unpaid-work-and-care/unpaid-domestic-work-number-hours-domp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours","t":"categorical","k":"Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2021)","def":"Eight codes: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 5 to 14 hours, 4 15 to 29 hours, 5 30 hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid domestic work: number of hours (DOMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/unpaid-work-and-care/unpaid-domestic-work-number-hours-domp","lim":"It cannot separate the kind of work done. Cooking, cleaning, home maintenance, shopping and household administration all fall into the same hours count, and unpaid child care and unpaid assistance to a person with a disability are collected in separate items rather than here, so the bands understate total unpaid work.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":67},{"n":"DOMP_FP_11","d":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's female parent at the 2011 Census, on the same five bands as DOMP_11.","full":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's female parent at the 2011 Census, on the same five bands as DOMP_11. The Census Dictionary defines the underlying item as work \"that the person did without pay, in their own home and in other places, for themselves, their family and other people in the household, in the week prior to Census Night\". This column is filled only where a female parent was enumerated in the same household on Census night, so it is empty for people living apart from a parent. Paired with DOMP_MP_11 it lets the domestic workload of two parents in one household be compared directly.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours by Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2011)","def":"Eight codes: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 5 to 14 hours, 4 15 to 29 hours, 5 30 hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"A missing value here is usually a missing parent, not a missing answer. Adults who had left home, children in one-parent families headed by a father, and anyone counted in a non-private dwelling have no female parent on their 2011 record, so restricting analysis to filled values quietly selects for co-resident two-parent households.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":67},{"n":"DOMP_FP_16","d":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's female parent at the 2016 Census, in the same five bands as 2011.","full":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's female parent at the 2016 Census, in the same five bands as 2011. Because the parent link is redrawn from the household enumerated on each Census night, the female parent behind DOMP_FP_16 need not be the same woman as the female parent behind DOMP_FP_11: a person who moved out, or whose family composition changed, gets a different attachment or none at all. The 2016 Census Dictionary keeps the item unchanged, so any difference between the two waves is about who the parent is, not about how the question was asked.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid work variables including Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58002016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours by Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2016)","def":"Eight codes: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 5 to 14 hours, 4 15 to 29 hours, 5 30 hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid work variables including Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58002016","lim":"It cannot support a claim that a mother's domestic workload changed, because the column is not a fixed-person panel. Comparing DOMP_FP_11 with DOMP_FP_16 compares whoever occupied the female parent role in each Census household, and the ACLD links the child, not the parent, so a change can be a change of household rather than a change of hours.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":67},{"n":"DOMP_FP_21","d":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's female parent at the 2021 Census, on bands the ABS did not change for 2021.","full":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's female parent at the 2021 Census, on bands the ABS did not change for 2021. The ABS records that \"No changes have been made for 2021\", so the value is comparable with DOMP_FP_16 and DOMP_FP_11 as an item, and non-response on the underlying question fell to 6.6 per cent. For most ACLD members who were children in 2011, this column is either empty by 2021 or refers to a parent they still live with, which is itself informative about leaving home.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid domestic work: number of hours (DOMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/unpaid-work-and-care/unpaid-domestic-work-number-hours-domp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours by Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2021)","def":"Eight codes: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 5 to 14 hours, 4 15 to 29 hours, 5 30 hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid domestic work: number of hours (DOMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/unpaid-work-and-care/unpaid-domestic-work-number-hours-domp","lim":"An empty value at 2021 does not mean the parent has died or that the relationship ended. The Census only records people present in the same household on Census night, so a parent living next door, interstate or in residential aged care produces the same blank as a parent who is no longer alive.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":67},{"n":"DOMP_MP_11","d":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's male parent at the 2011 Census, on the same five bands as DOMP_11.","full":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's male parent at the 2011 Census, on the same five bands as DOMP_11. The 2011 Census Dictionary scopes the item to \"Persons aged 15 years and over\" and to the week before Census night, so a male parent under 15 cannot occur and the value is a band rather than a count. It is filled only where a male parent was enumerated in the same household on Census night. Read against DOMP_FP_11 it gives the within-household split of domestic work between two parents at the 2011 wave.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours by Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2011)","def":"Eight codes: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 5 to 14 hours, 4 15 to 29 hours, 5 30 hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"Coverage is much thinner than for the female parent column, because one-parent families in Australia are predominantly mother-headed, so an analysis conditioned on a non-empty male parent value excludes a large and non-random group of children. The column also cannot identify a stepfather or a non-resident father separately from a biological co-resident father.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":67},{"n":"DOMP_MP_16","d":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's male parent at the 2016 Census, in bands unchanged from 2011.","full":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's male parent at the 2016 Census, in bands unchanged from 2011. The 2016 Census Dictionary defines the underlying item as \"Time people spent in the previous week doing domestic work without pay for themselves and their household.\" The male parent is whoever held that role in the household enumerated on 9 August 2016, so a father who separated between waves drops out of DOMP_MP_16 even though he answered the 2011 Census.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid work variables including Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58002016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours by Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2016)","def":"Eight codes: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 5 to 14 hours, 4 15 to 29 hours, 5 30 hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid work variables including Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58002016","lim":"It cannot be differenced against DOMP_MP_11 to measure a father's change in behaviour, because the two values may belong to different men. The ACLD follows the sampled person, not the parent, so a wave-on-wave change mixes real change with a change in who the co-resident male parent is.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":67},{"n":"DOMP_MP_21","d":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's male parent at the 2021 Census, on bands the ABS left unchanged for 2021.","full":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's male parent at the 2021 Census, on bands the ABS left unchanged for 2021. The 2021 Census was taken on 10 August 2021 while much of New South Wales and Victoria was in lockdown, so a male parent working from home that week may report more domestic hours than he would in an ordinary year. Where more than one box was marked, the ABS accepted the highest 'yes' band, which pushes borderline records upward.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid domestic work: number of hours (DOMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/unpaid-work-and-care/unpaid-domestic-work-number-hours-domp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours by Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2021)","def":"Eight codes: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 5 to 14 hours, 4 15 to 29 hours, 5 30 hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid domestic work: number of hours (DOMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/unpaid-work-and-care/unpaid-domestic-work-number-hours-domp","lim":"It does not identify the relationship type. A stepfather, an adoptive father and a biological father in the same household all appear as the male parent, and Relationship in Household is the column that separates them, so a 2011 to 2021 comparison can silently switch between different men in the same role.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":67},{"n":"DOMP_SP_11","d":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census, on the same five bands as DOMP_11.","full":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census, on the same five bands as DOMP_11. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines the item as recording \"the number of hours spent performing unpaid domestic work\" in the week before Census night for persons aged 15 and over. It is filled only where a spouse or partner was enumerated in the same household, which at 2011 covers registered marriages and de facto partners, including same-sex de facto couples. Paired with DOMP_11 it gives the within-couple division of domestic work.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours by Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2011)","def":"Eight codes: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 5 to 14 hours, 4 15 to 29 hours, 5 30 hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It cannot see a partner who lives elsewhere. A couple living apart, a fly-in fly-out worker away on Census night and a partner in hospital all produce an empty value, so the column measures co-residence as much as partnership, and treating a blank as 'single' overstates the number of people without a partner.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":67},{"n":"DOMP_SP_16","d":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's spouse or partner at the 2016 Census, in bands unchanged from 2011.","full":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's spouse or partner at the 2016 Census, in bands unchanged from 2011. The 2016 Census predates the December 2017 change to the Marriage Act, so a same-sex couple in this wave appears as a de facto partnership rather than a marriage, though both are picked up as a spouse or partner here. The item itself did not change, so a difference against DOMP_SP_11 reflects the partner rather than the question.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid work variables including Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58002016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours by Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2016)","def":"Eight codes: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 5 to 14 hours, 4 15 to 29 hours, 5 30 hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Unpaid work variables including Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours (DOMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58002016","lim":"It cannot be used to track one partnership over time. The spouse or partner is re-identified from the 2016 household, so a person who repartnered between waves carries a different person's hours in DOMP_SP_16 than in DOMP_SP_11, with nothing in this column to flag the substitution.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":67},{"n":"DOMP_SP_21","d":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's spouse or partner at the 2021 Census, on bands the ABS did not change for 2021.","full":"The unpaid domestic work hours reported by the person's spouse or partner at the 2021 Census, on bands the ABS did not change for 2021. Unlike 2011 and 2016, the 2021 wave can include a legally married same-sex spouse, since the Marriage Act was amended in December 2017; the ABS did not change the DOMP question itself, and non-response on it fell to 6.6 per cent. Reading it beside DOMP_21 gives the couple's split of domestic hours at the most recent wave.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid domestic work: number of hours (DOMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/unpaid-work-and-care/unpaid-domestic-work-number-hours-domp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours by Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census unpaid domestic work hours band (2021)","def":"Eight codes: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 5 to 14 hours, 4 15 to 29 hours, 5 30 hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid domestic work: number of hours (DOMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/unpaid-work-and-care/unpaid-domestic-work-number-hours-domp","lim":"It does not tell you the couple's total unpaid workload. Only domestic work is counted, so child care and care for a person with a disability sit in other columns, and a couple sharing heavy caring duties can both record low domestic hours.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":67},{"n":"DWTD_P_11","d":"The basic type of dwelling in which the person was counted at the 2011 Census: private, non-private, migratory, off-shore or shipping.","full":"The basic type of dwelling in which the person was counted at the 2011 Census: private, non-private, migratory, off-shore or shipping. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as \"Classifies dwellings into basic dwelling types.\" and notes that the definition of a private dwelling covers residences in caravan and residential parks, camping grounds, marinas, manufactured home estates and self-contained retirement villages, so a caravan resident is an occupied private dwelling rather than a non-private one. The _P suffix marks a dwelling attribute carried on the person's record.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Type (DWTD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Dwelling Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census dwelling type code (2011)","def":"Six categories: 1 occupied private dwellings, 2 unoccupied private dwellings, 3 non-private dwellings, 4 migratory, 5 off-shore and 6 shipping.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Type (DWTD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It is not a measure of housing type or quality. A boarding house, a hostel, a hotel, a hospital, a prison and a defence establishment are all 'non-private dwellings', and Type of Non-Private Dwelling (NPDD) is the column that separates them. Because the value hangs off a person record, category 2 has no live occupant behind it, so the column is coarser here than in dwelling-level Census output.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":68},{"n":"DWTD_P_16","d":"The basic type of dwelling in which the person was counted at the 2016 Census, on the same six categories used in 2011.","full":"The basic type of dwelling in which the person was counted at the 2016 Census, on the same six categories used in 2011. The 2016 Census Dictionary defines it as \"This variable classifies all dwellings into the basic dwelling types.\" The 2016 Census was the first run largely from the ABS Address Register with a digital-first collection, so dwelling type is now settled from register information and field officer observation rather than from a form completed at the door, while the categories themselves are unchanged from DWTD_P_11.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Type (DWTD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter30002016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Dwelling Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census dwelling type code (2016)","def":"Six categories: 1 occupied private dwellings, 2 unoccupied private dwellings, 3 non-private dwellings, 4 migratory, 5 off-shore and 6 shipping.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Type (DWTD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter30002016","lim":"It cannot tell you whether a person usually lives at the address. Dwelling type describes where the person was enumerated on Census night, so a hotel guest away from home appears in a non-private dwelling, and the place-of-usual-residence columns are what identify their normal home.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":68},{"n":"DWTD_P_21","d":"The basic type of dwelling in which the person was counted at the 2021 Census, on the same six categories used in 2011 and 2016.","full":"The basic type of dwelling in which the person was counted at the 2021 Census, on the same six categories used in 2011 and 2016. The ABS explains the underlying concept as \"A dwelling is a structure which is intended to have people live in it, that is it was established for short-stay or long-stay accommodation.\" Occupancy at 2021 was settled from returned forms, 'not at home' returns, contact with residents, field follow-up and, where none of those worked, a Census Occupancy Model, so a small share of records is modelled rather than observed.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Dwelling type (DWTD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/dwelling-type-dwtd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Dwelling Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census dwelling type code (2021)","def":"Six categories: 1 occupied private dwellings, 2 unoccupied private dwellings, 3 non-private dwellings, 4 migratory, 5 off-shore and 6 shipping.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Dwelling type (DWTD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/dwelling-type-dwtd","lim":"The migratory, off-shore and shipping codes are known to carry a small number of incorrectly coded people, so they should not be treated as an exact count of offshore or seagoing workers. Mixed-use buildings are also hard to classify, and a dwelling above a shop or a room in a partly commercial building can fall either side of the private and non-private boundary.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":68},{"n":"EETP_16","d":"Whether the person was engaged in work or study at the 2016 Census, the first Census for which the ABS reported it.","full":"Whether the person was engaged in work or study at the 2016 Census, the first Census for which the ABS reported it. The ABS defines it as \"Engagement in Employment, Education and Training (EETP) classifies persons aged 15 years and over as Engaged or Not engaged in work and study according to the criteria outlined below.\" It is derived rather than asked, being built from age, full-time and part-time student status, labour force status and hours worked. There is no EETP_11 in the ACLD because the variable was new for 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Engagement in Employment, Education and Training (EETP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter31202016","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Engagement in Employment, Education and Training","k":"Census engagement in employment, education and training code (2016)","def":"Four substantive categories at 2016 — fully engaged, partially engaged, at least partially engaged and not engaged — plus an engagement status undetermined or not stated code, a not-applicable code for persons under 15 and a code for overseas visitors.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Engagement in Employment, Education and Training (EETP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter31202016","lim":"It cannot separate a full-time worker from a full-time student. Both are 'fully engaged' at 2016, and the sub-categories that make that split possible only exist from 2021, so a 2016 to 2021 comparison has to be made at the one-digit level. 'Not engaged' also merges retirees, people with a disability, carers and discouraged job seekers, so it is not by itself a measure of disadvantage.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"EETP_21","d":"Whether the person was engaged in work or study at the 2021 Census, on the expanded 2021 category set.","full":"Whether the person was engaged in work or study at the 2021 Census, on the expanded 2021 category set. The ABS defines it as \"This variable indicates whether a person is engaged or not engaged in work and/or study.\" For 2021 the ABS split 'fully engaged' and 'partially engaged' into detailed sub-categories, so EETP_21 is finer than EETP_16 and the two waves line up only at the one-digit level. It is derived from labour force status and hours worked (LFHRP), full-time and part-time student status (STUP) and age (AGEP), and therefore has no non-response rate of its own.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Engagement in employment, education and training (EETP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/engagement-employment-education-and-training-eetp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Engagement in Employment, Education and Training","k":"Census engagement in employment, education and training code (2021)","def":"One-digit codes 1 fully engaged, 2 partially engaged, 3 at least partially engaged and 4 not engaged, each with two-digit detail from 2021: 11 full-time study and full-time employment, 12 primarily full-time study, 13 primarily full-time employment, 14 part-time study and part-time employment, 15 engaged other, 21 part-time study only, 22 part-time work only, 31 at least partially engaged, 41 not engaged. & is undetermined or not stated, @ is not applicable for persons under 15 and V is overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Engagement in employment, education and training (EETP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/engagement-employment-education-and-training-eetp","lim":"The two-digit codes cannot be traced back to 2016, because they did not exist then; only the four one-digit classes carry across the waves. The variable also says nothing about the quality of the engagement, so one hour of paid work a week is enough to reach 'partially engaged', and 'at least partially engaged' is a residual for records with too little information to place properly rather than a middle rung.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"EETP_FP_16","d":"The female parent's engagement in work or study at the 2016 Census, on the five-category scheme the ABS introduced that year.","full":"The female parent's engagement in work or study at the 2016 Census, on the five-category scheme the ABS introduced that year. The item is derived from the parent's own age, student status, labour force status and hours worked, not from anything the sampled person reported. It is filled only where a female parent was enumerated in the same household on Census night, which for a child in the ACLD is the ordinary case and for an adult who has left home is not.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Engagement in Employment, Education and Training (EETP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter31202016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Engagement in Employment, Education and Training of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census engagement in employment, education and training code (2016)","def":"Four substantive categories at 2016 — fully engaged, partially engaged, at least partially engaged and not engaged — plus an engagement status undetermined or not stated code, a not-applicable code for persons under 15 and a code for overseas visitors.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Engagement in Employment, Education and Training (EETP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter31202016","lim":"A 'not engaged' mother is not necessarily out of the workforce by choice or in difficulty: unpaid care for a young child, for an older relative or for a person with a disability all place her outside employment and study, and this column carries none of that context. The unpaid care columns in the same wave are what supply it.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":69},{"n":"EETP_FP_21","d":"The female parent's engagement in work or study at the 2021 Census, on the expanded 2021 code set.","full":"The female parent's engagement in work or study at the 2021 Census, on the expanded 2021 code set. The 2021 detail separates primarily full-time employment from primarily full-time study and from the combination of both, so a mother returning to study while working part-time can be identified here in a way she could not be in EETP_FP_16. The 2021 reference week fell during extended lockdowns in New South Wales and Victoria, which moved many people out of employment for that week without ending their job.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Engagement in employment, education and training (EETP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/engagement-employment-education-and-training-eetp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Engagement in Employment, Education and Training of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census engagement in employment, education and training code (2021)","def":"One-digit codes 1 fully engaged, 2 partially engaged, 3 at least partially engaged and 4 not engaged, with two-digit detail 11 to 15, 21, 22, 31 and 41 available from 2021, plus & undetermined or not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15 and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Engagement in employment, education and training (EETP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/engagement-employment-education-and-training-eetp","lim":"It cannot be differenced against EETP_FP_16 at the detailed level, because the two-digit codes are new in 2021, and it cannot be differenced at all as a measure of one woman's history, since the ACLD follows the sampled person rather than the parent and the female parent may be a different person between waves.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":69},{"n":"EETP_MP_16","d":"The male parent's engagement in work or study at the 2016 Census, on the five-category scheme introduced that year.","full":"The male parent's engagement in work or study at the 2016 Census, on the five-category scheme introduced that year. The value is derived from the parent's age, student status, labour force status and hours worked, so it exists for any co-resident male parent aged 15 and over regardless of whether he completed the education questions. Together with EETP_FP_16 it gives the household's parental engagement pattern, which is the form these items take in national reporting on children in jobless families.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Engagement in Employment, Education and Training (EETP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter31202016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Engagement in Employment, Education and Training of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census engagement in employment, education and training code (2016)","def":"Four substantive categories at 2016 — fully engaged, partially engaged, at least partially engaged and not engaged — plus an engagement status undetermined or not stated code, a not-applicable code for persons under 15 and a code for overseas visitors.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Engagement in Employment, Education and Training (EETP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter31202016","lim":"It cannot support a jobless-family measure on its own, because an empty male parent column is far more often an absent father than an unemployed one. Coverage of a co-resident male parent is markedly lower than of a female parent, so any rate computed over records with both parents present describes a selected group of households.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":69},{"n":"EETP_MP_21","d":"The male parent's engagement in work or study at the 2021 Census, on the expanded 2021 code set.","full":"The male parent's engagement in work or study at the 2021 Census, on the expanded 2021 code set. Because the value is derived from the parent's labour force status in the week before 10 August 2021, a father stood down or on reduced hours during the lockdowns of that winter can fall out of 'fully engaged' without losing his job. The ABS built the 2021 sub-categories to support national reporting measures, so the detailed codes are the ones those measures use.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Engagement in employment, education and training (EETP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/engagement-employment-education-and-training-eetp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Engagement in Employment, Education and Training of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census engagement in employment, education and training code (2021)","def":"One-digit codes 1 fully engaged, 2 partially engaged, 3 at least partially engaged and 4 not engaged, with two-digit detail 11 to 15, 21, 22, 31 and 41 available from 2021, plus & undetermined or not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15 and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Engagement in employment, education and training (EETP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/engagement-employment-education-and-training-eetp","lim":"The 'at least partially engaged' code is a data-quality residual rather than a level of engagement, used when the record has study or labour force information but not enough of it to classify further. Counting it as a middle category between fully and partially engaged produces an ordering the ABS did not intend.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":69},{"n":"EETP_SP_16","d":"The spouse or partner's engagement in work or study at the 2016 Census, on the five-category scheme introduced that year.","full":"The spouse or partner's engagement in work or study at the 2016 Census, on the five-category scheme introduced that year. Read with EETP_16 it gives the couple's joint engagement, which is the pairing behind measures of jobless couple households. The column exists only where a spouse or partner was enumerated in the same household on Census night, so a partner working away or living elsewhere leaves it empty.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Engagement in Employment, Education and Training (EETP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter31202016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Engagement in Employment, Education and Training of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census engagement in employment, education and training code (2016)","def":"Four substantive categories at 2016 — fully engaged, partially engaged, at least partially engaged and not engaged — plus an engagement status undetermined or not stated code, a not-applicable code for persons under 15 and a code for overseas visitors.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Engagement in Employment, Education and Training (EETP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter31202016","lim":"It cannot distinguish a partner who is retired from one who is unemployed, since both land in 'not engaged'. For couples over about 60 that makes the category almost uninformative on its own, and age and labour force status are needed alongside it.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":69},{"n":"EETP_SP_21","d":"The spouse or partner's engagement in work or study at the 2021 Census, on the expanded 2021 code set.","full":"The spouse or partner's engagement in work or study at the 2021 Census, on the expanded 2021 code set. The 2021 detail makes it possible to see whether a partner combines part-time work with part-time study, a pattern that fell inside a single 'fully engaged' code at 2016. As at every wave the value is derived, so it carries no non-response rate of its own even where the partner skipped individual questions.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Engagement in employment, education and training (EETP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/engagement-employment-education-and-training-eetp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Engagement in Employment, Education and Training of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census engagement in employment, education and training code (2021)","def":"One-digit codes 1 fully engaged, 2 partially engaged, 3 at least partially engaged and 4 not engaged, with two-digit detail 11 to 15, 21, 22, 31 and 41 available from 2021, plus & undetermined or not stated, @ not applicable for persons under 15 and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Engagement in employment, education and training (EETP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/engagement-employment-education-and-training-eetp","lim":"A change from EETP_SP_16 to EETP_SP_21 need not describe the same person. The ACLD links the sampled person and re-reads the household at each Census, so repartnering between waves substitutes a different partner's engagement with nothing in this column to mark the change.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":69},{"n":"EMPP_11","d":"How many employees the person's own business had at the 2011 Census, in three bands, asked only of owner managers.","full":"How many employees the person's own business had at the 2011 Census, in three bands, asked only of owner managers. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as \"Records the number of employees (in ranges) employed by owner managers.\" and scopes it to \"Persons aged 15 years and over, who are owner managers of incorporated or unincorporated enterprises\". Everyone else is coded not applicable, including employees, contributing family workers, unemployed people and people not in the labour force. It is a second-release Census item, so it appeared later than the first-release columns beside it.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Number of Employees (EMPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Employees","t":"categorical","k":"Census number of employees band (2011)","def":"Six codes: 1 nil employees, 2 1-19 employees, 3 20 or more employees, & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Number of Employees (EMPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It is not a business size measure across the population. Only owner managers are in scope, so most person records are 'not applicable', and a tabulation over all persons measures how common self-employment is rather than how large firms are. The top band is open, so a business with 25 staff cannot be told apart from one with 2,500.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":70},{"n":"EMPP_16","d":"How many employees the person's own business had at the 2016 Census, in three bands, asked only of owner managers.","full":"How many employees the person's own business had at the 2016 Census, in three bands, asked only of owner managers. The 2016 wording is \"Records the number of employees (in ranges) employed by owner managers (excluding the owner managers themselves).\" The parenthesis is the change from 2011: 2016 added the explicit instruction for owners to leave themselves out of the count, and the question was extended to the interviewer household form used in discrete Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, so a small level shift against EMPP_11 is expected at the boundary between nil and one to nineteen employees.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Number of Employees (EMPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3002016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Employees","t":"categorical","k":"Census number of employees band (2016)","def":"Six codes: 1 nil employees, 2 1-19 employees, 3 20 or more employees, & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Number of Employees (EMPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3002016","lim":"It counts employees of the person's own business, not the size of the workplace where an employee works, so it cannot be used to describe employer size for the workforce at large. Non-response at 2016 was 1.2 per cent of the in-scope group, which is small in absolute terms but three times the 2021 rate, so a wave-on-wave shift in the 'not stated' code is expected.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":70},{"n":"EMPP_21","d":"How many employees the person's own business had at the 2021 Census, in three bands, asked only of owner managers.","full":"How many employees the person's own business had at the 2021 Census, in three bands, asked only of owner managers. The ABS defines it as \"This variable records the number of employees (in ranges) employed by owner managers (excluding the owner managers themselves).\" No changes were made for 2021, so the column is comparable with EMPP_16, and non-response fell to 0.4 per cent from 1.2 per cent in 2016. Records imputed by the ABS fall into the not-applicable category rather than into 'not stated', which is why the non-response rate behaves differently from other Census items.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of employees (EMPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/number-employees-empp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Employees","t":"categorical","k":"Census number of employees band (2021)","def":"Six codes: 1 nil employees, 2 1-19 employees, 3 20 or more employees, & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of employees (EMPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/number-employees-empp","lim":"The not-applicable code cannot be read as 'not an owner manager', because imputed person records land there too. Treating '@' as a clean complement to the owner-manager population therefore mixes people who genuinely do not run a business with people whose whole record was imputed, and Status in employment (SIEMP) is what actually identifies owner managers.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":70},{"n":"EMTP_11","d":"Employment type in the person's main job at the 2011 Census, in four classes.","full":"Employment type in the person's main job at the 2011 Census, in four classes. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as \"For employed persons, defines their employment type for the main job held in the week prior to Census Night.\" EMTP was introduced at the 2006 Census, carved out of Labour Force Status (LFSP), and 2011 was the last Census at which it was the published item; from 2016 mainstream Census output replaced it with Status in employment (SIEMP).","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Employment Type (EMTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Employment Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census employment type code (2011)","def":"Seven codes: 1 employee not owning business, 2 owner managers of incorporated enterprises, 3 owner managers of unincorporated enterprises, 4 contributing family workers, & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Employment Type (EMTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It describes the main job only, so a person who is an employee by day and runs a business at night appears purely as an employee. It also carries no information about hours, permanence or casual status, and none about whether the business has staff, which is Number of Employees (EMPP) on the same wave.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":71},{"n":"EMTP_16","d":"Employment type in the person's main job at the 2016 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011.","full":"Employment type in the person's main job at the 2016 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011. Mainstream 2016 Census output dropped the item: the ABS states that \"Status in employment (SEIMP) was first introduced in 2016 to replace Employment type (EMTP) which was discontinued\", SIEMP collecting the same information more finely by splitting owner managers into those with and without employees. The ACLD keeps the EMTP name at 2016 so that the wave lines up with EMTP_11, which means the value corresponds to SIEMP collapsed back to its four top-level classes; check the ACLD data item list before assuming the codes match 2011 exactly.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Employment Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census employment type code (2016, EMTP-equivalent of SIEMP)","def":"Four substantive classes — employee, owner manager of an incorporated enterprise, owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise, and contributing family worker — plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes, matching the 2011 EMTP structure rather than SIEMP's eleven categories.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"It cannot be treated as a like-for-like 2011 code without checking. Because 2016 collected Status in employment rather than Employment type, the 'not stated' and owner-manager categories can behave differently from EMTP_11, and the with-employees and without-employees detail SIEMP carries is lost in this column. As at every wave it describes the main job only.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":71},{"n":"EMTP_21","d":"Employment type in the person's main job at the 2021 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011.","full":"Employment type in the person's main job at the 2021 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011. The 2021 Census, like 2016, collected Status in employment (SIEMP) rather than Employment type; the ABS says of SIEMP that \"No changes have been made for 2021\", so its eleven categories are stable across the last two waves and collapse the same way into the four EMTP classes. Where the finer detail matters, SIEMP itself separates owner managers with employees from those without, and Number of Employees (EMPP_21) gives the band.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Employment Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census employment type code (2021, EMTP-equivalent of SIEMP)","def":"Four substantive classes — employee, owner manager of an incorporated enterprise, owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise, and contributing family worker — plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes, matching the 2011 EMTP structure rather than SIEMP's eleven categories.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"Collapsing SIEMP loses the 'employees not stated' owner-manager categories, which SIEMP keeps separate; those records have to be folded into one of the two owner-manager classes here, so counts of incorporated and unincorporated owner managers at 2021 are not exactly reproducible from this column. Like every wave it says nothing about hours, casual status or job security.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":71},{"n":"EMTP_FP_11","d":"The female parent's employment type in her main job at the 2011 Census, in four classes.","full":"The female parent's employment type in her main job at the 2011 Census, in four classes. The 2011 Census Dictionary scopes the underlying item to \"Employed persons\", so a mother who was unemployed or not in the labour force on Census night is coded not applicable rather than left blank. The column is filled only where a female parent was enumerated in the same household. Read with EMTP_MP_11 it shows whether both parents were employees, or whether one ran a family business.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Employment Type (EMTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Employment Type of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census employment type code (2011)","def":"Seven codes: 1 employee not owning business, 2 owner managers of incorporated enterprises, 3 owner managers of unincorporated enterprises, 4 contributing family workers, & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Employment Type (EMTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"A not-applicable code here does not distinguish a mother who was out of work from one who has no employment because she was not in the labour force, and both look the same as a mother who is absent from the household. Labour force status and the presence of a parent have to be checked separately before a zero can be interpreted.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":71},{"n":"EMTP_FP_16","d":"The female parent's employment type in her main job at the 2016 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011.","full":"The female parent's employment type in her main job at the 2016 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011. The 2016 Census itself collected Status in employment (SIEMP), which the ABS introduced \"to replace Employment type (EMTP) which was discontinued\", so this column represents SIEMP folded back to four classes for longitudinal use. It is filled only where a female parent was enumerated in the same household on Census night.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Employment Type of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census employment type code (2016, EMTP-equivalent of SIEMP)","def":"Four substantive classes — employee, owner manager of an incorporated enterprise, owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise, and contributing family worker — plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes, matching the 2011 EMTP structure rather than SIEMP's eleven categories.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"A move from EMTP_FP_11 to EMTP_FP_16 mixes three different things: a real change in the mother's job, a change in which woman occupies the female parent role, and the switch in the underlying Census item from EMTP to SIEMP. None of the three can be separated using this column alone.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":71},{"n":"EMTP_FP_21","d":"The female parent's employment type in her main job at the 2021 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011.","full":"The female parent's employment type in her main job at the 2021 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011. The 2021 Census collected Status in employment (SIEMP), which the ABS left unchanged from 2016, so the 2016 and 2021 values of this column rest on the same underlying item while the 2011 value rests on EMTP itself. For most ACLD members sampled as children in 2011, a filled value here means they were still living with their mother in 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Employment Type of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census employment type code (2021, EMTP-equivalent of SIEMP)","def":"Four substantive classes — employee, owner manager of an incorporated enterprise, owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise, and contributing family worker — plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes, matching the 2011 EMTP structure rather than SIEMP's eleven categories.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"The 2021 reference week fell during extended lockdowns in the two largest states, so a mother stood down from a job she still held can be coded not applicable through Labour Force Status rather than appearing as an employee. Comparing the 2021 wave with earlier ones therefore picks up a pandemic effect on top of any genuine change.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":71},{"n":"EMTP_MP_11","d":"The male parent's employment type in his main job at the 2011 Census, in four classes.","full":"The male parent's employment type in his main job at the 2011 Census, in four classes. The 2011 Census Dictionary lists the not-applicable category as covering \"Persons aged under 15 years, Persons who are unemployed, Persons with Labour Force Status (LFSP) not stated, Persons not in the labour force\", which is why an employed father is the only case that carries a substantive code. It is filled only where a male parent was enumerated in the same household on Census night.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Employment Type (EMTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Employment Type of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census employment type code (2011)","def":"Seven codes: 1 employee not owning business, 2 owner managers of incorporated enterprises, 3 owner managers of unincorporated enterprises, 4 contributing family workers, & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Employment Type (EMTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It cannot identify a family business as such. A father coded as an owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise and a mother coded as a contributing family worker are strong evidence of one, but the codes are assigned person by person and nothing links the two records to the same business.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":71},{"n":"EMTP_MP_16","d":"The male parent's employment type in his main job at the 2016 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011.","full":"The male parent's employment type in his main job at the 2016 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011. The 2016 Census collected Status in employment (SIEMP) instead, which the ABS says collects \"the same information at a more detailed level on whether the incorporated or unincorporated enterprise is with or without employees\", so this column is that item folded back to four classes. It is filled only where a male parent was enumerated in the same household.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Employment Type of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census employment type code (2016, EMTP-equivalent of SIEMP)","def":"Four substantive classes — employee, owner manager of an incorporated enterprise, owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise, and contributing family worker — plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes, matching the 2011 EMTP structure rather than SIEMP's eleven categories.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"Coverage is uneven across household types, because a co-resident male parent is present far less often than a co-resident female parent, so a distribution of fathers' employment types computed from this column describes couple and father-headed households rather than all children in the sample.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":71},{"n":"EMTP_MP_21","d":"The male parent's employment type in his main job at the 2021 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011.","full":"The male parent's employment type in his main job at the 2021 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011. The 2021 Census collected Status in employment (SIEMP), unchanged from 2016, so this column and EMTP_MP_16 rest on the same item while EMTP_MP_11 rests on EMTP proper. Where the with-employees and without-employees split matters, SIEMP and Number of Employees (EMPP_21) carry it and this column does not.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Employment Type of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census employment type code (2021, EMTP-equivalent of SIEMP)","def":"Four substantive classes — employee, owner manager of an incorporated enterprise, owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise, and contributing family worker — plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes, matching the 2011 EMTP structure rather than SIEMP's eleven categories.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"It cannot distinguish a father who has retired from one who lost work, since both fall into the not-applicable code through Labour Force Status. For ACLD members sampled as adults in 2011, a large share of male parents will have reached retirement age by 2021, so an apparent collapse in employment types is largely ageing.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":71},{"n":"EMTP_SP_11","d":"The spouse or partner's employment type in their main job at the 2011 Census, in four classes.","full":"The spouse or partner's employment type in their main job at the 2011 Census, in four classes. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines the item for \"Employed persons\" only, so an unemployed partner or one outside the labour force takes the not-applicable code. It is filled only where a spouse or partner was enumerated in the same household. Read with EMTP_11 it shows whether a couple were both employees or whether one was an owner manager and the other a contributing family worker.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Employment Type (EMTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Employment Type of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census employment type code (2011)","def":"Seven codes: 1 employee not owning business, 2 owner managers of incorporated enterprises, 3 owner managers of unincorporated enterprises, 4 contributing family workers, & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Employment Type (EMTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It cannot measure a couple's joint labour market attachment, because the not-applicable code absorbs unemployment, retirement and being outside the labour force alike, and the absence of a co-resident partner produces an empty value that looks similar in a simple cross-tabulation.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":71},{"n":"EMTP_SP_16","d":"The spouse or partner's employment type in their main job at the 2016 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011.","full":"The spouse or partner's employment type in their main job at the 2016 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011. The item the 2016 Census actually collected was Status in employment (SIEMP), which replaced the discontinued EMTP, so this column is SIEMP folded back to four classes for comparison with EMTP_SP_11. It is filled only where a spouse or partner was enumerated in the same household on Census night.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Employment Type of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census employment type code (2016, EMTP-equivalent of SIEMP)","def":"Four substantive classes — employee, owner manager of an incorporated enterprise, owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise, and contributing family worker — plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes, matching the 2011 EMTP structure rather than SIEMP's eleven categories.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"It cannot be used to study one partnership over time, because the ACLD follows the sampled person and re-reads the household at each Census, so a person who repartnered between 2011 and 2016 carries a different person's employment type here with nothing in the column to flag it.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":71},{"n":"EMTP_SP_21","d":"The spouse or partner's employment type in their main job at the 2021 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011.","full":"The spouse or partner's employment type in their main job at the 2021 Census, on the four-class scheme the ABS used up to 2011. The 2021 Census collected Status in employment (SIEMP) with no change from 2016, so this column and EMTP_SP_16 share an underlying item that EMTP_SP_11 does not. Unlike the two earlier waves, a legally married same-sex spouse can appear here, the Marriage Act having been amended in December 2017.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Employment Type of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census employment type code (2021, EMTP-equivalent of SIEMP)","def":"Four substantive classes — employee, owner manager of an incorporated enterprise, owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise, and contributing family worker — plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes, matching the 2011 EMTP structure rather than SIEMP's eleven categories.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"It gives no basis for inferring household income or business scale. An owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise can be a sole trader with no assets or a partner in a substantial practice, and neither this column nor its 2011 and 2016 counterparts carry turnover, hours or earnings.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":71},{"n":"ENGLP_11","d":"Self-assessed proficiency in spoken English at the 2011 Census, on a scale that also carries people who speak only English.","full":"Self-assessed proficiency in spoken English at the 2011 Census, on a scale that also carries people who speak only English. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as \"Classifies each person's self-assessed proficiency in spoken English.\" and scopes it to all persons, which is what separates it from ENGP, the companion variable restricted to people who use a language other than English at home.
