The mnemonic itself was new at 2011: the 2006 item ENGP01 was renamed ENGLP and its codes amended, so a 2006 to 2011 comparison needs the code change checked.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English/Language (ENGLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English/Language","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English/language code (2011)","def":"Eight codes: 1 speaks English only; 2 very well, 3 well, 4 not well and 5 not at all for people who speak another language; 6 not stated where both language and proficiency are missing; & not stated where language is given but proficiency is not; and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English/Language (ENGLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"The answer is the respondent's own judgement, and on a household form it is often given by another household member on their behalf, so 'well' does not carry the same standard across records. It also covers spoken English only, so it cannot stand in for reading or writing ability, and it is not a literacy measure.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":72},{"n":"ENGLP_16","d":"Self-assessed proficiency in spoken English at the 2016 Census, covering the whole population rather than only people who use another language.","full":"Self-assessed proficiency in spoken English at the 2016 Census, covering the whole population rather than only people who use another language. The 2016 Census Dictionary defines it as \"This variable encompasses Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP), and applies to all persons i.e. people who speak English only, as well as those who speak a language at home other than English.\" Neither the concept nor the codes changed between 2011 and 2016, so ENGLP_11 and ENGLP_16 are directly comparable; non-response at 2016 was 6.5 per cent.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English/Language (ENGLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48202016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English/Language","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English/language code (2016)","def":"Eight codes: 1 speaks English only; 2 very well, 3 well, 4 not well and 5 not at all for people who speak another language; 6 not stated where both language and proficiency are missing; & not stated where language is given but proficiency is not; and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English/Language (ENGLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48202016","lim":"The two not-stated codes mean different things and must not be pooled. Code 6 marks a record where neither the language question nor the proficiency question was answered, so the person's language status is unknown, while & marks a record where a non-English language was reported but proficiency was left blank, which is evidence of a language other than English at home.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":72},{"n":"ENGLP_21","d":"Self-assessed proficiency in spoken English at the 2021 Census, with a separate code for people who speak only English.","full":"Self-assessed proficiency in spoken English at the 2021 Census, with a separate code for people who speak only English. The ABS defines it as \"This variable classifies a person's self-assessed proficiency in spoken English where they have identified they use a main language other than English at home.\" Two things changed for 2021: the item was renamed from 'Proficiency in spoken English/language' to 'Proficiency in spoken English', and the ABS removed the companion ENGP variable from Census output to stop the two being confused. Category labels also changed, with 'Speaks other languages' becoming 'Uses other language', and non-response fell from 6.5 per cent in 2016 to 5.5 per cent in 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Proficiency in spoken English (ENGLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/proficiency-spoken-english-englp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English/Language","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English code (2021)","def":"Eight codes: 1 speaks English only; 2 very well, 3 well, 4 not well and 5 not at all for people who use another language; 6 not stated where both language and proficiency are missing; & not stated where language is stated but proficiency is not; and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Proficiency in spoken English (ENGLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/proficiency-spoken-english-englp","lim":"The 2021 label change does not make the column a different measure, but it does mean a search of ABS documentation for 'Proficiency in spoken English' at 2021 returns ENGLP rather than the older ENGP, so a reader chasing a 2011 or 2016 ENGP series will not find its 2021 continuation in Census output. Within the wave, the responses remain subjective and are frequently given by another household member.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":73},{"n":"ENGP_11","d":"Self-assessed proficiency in spoken English at the 2011 Census, asked only of people who used a language other than English at home.","full":"Self-assessed proficiency in spoken English at the 2011 Census, asked only of people who used a language other than English at home. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as \"For each person who speaks a language other than English at home, classifies their self-assessed proficiency in spoken English\", scored Very well, Well, Not well or Not at all. People who spoke only English are coded Not applicable rather than to a proficiency level, so the population at risk is the language-other-than-English group, not everyone. Read it against LANP_11, which is the language question that decides whether this one was asked at all.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English code","def":"A single character: 1 Very well, 2 Well, 3 Not well, 4 Not at all, two distinct not-stated codes separating the case where language was also missing from the case where language was given, @ for not applicable and V for overseas visitors.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302011","lim":"It is not a tested measure of English ability. One household member usually completes the form for everyone, so a child's or an older parent's rating is generally someone else's opinion of them, and the categories have no external calibration. The @ code is also not weak English; it is the English-only majority of the population.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":74},{"n":"ENGP_16","d":"Self-assessed proficiency in spoken English at the 2016 Census, on exactly the basis used in 2011.","full":"Self-assessed proficiency in spoken English at the 2016 Census, on exactly the basis used in 2011. The 2016 Census Dictionary repeats the 2011 wording, \"For each person who speaks a language other than English at home, classifies their self-assessed proficiency in spoken English\", and the code list is unchanged, so ENGP_16 and ENGP_11 can be compared directly. Non-response was 1.1 per cent in 2016 against 1.3 per cent in 2011, as published in the ABS quality statement for the variable. The 2016 Census also released ENGLP, a wider version of the same concept covering English-only speakers as well.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English code","def":"A single character over the same eight-way frame as 2011: four proficiency levels, two not-stated codes distinguishing whether language was stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302016","lim":"A stable code list is not a stable population. The share of people the question reaches moves with migration and with how households answer the language question, so a rise in the Not well count between 2011 and 2016 can reflect a larger non-English-speaking base rather than any change in how well people speak English.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":74},{"n":"ENGP_21","d":"Proficiency in spoken English at the 2021 Census, the wave at which the ABS retired ENGP and published the concept as ENGLP instead.","full":"Proficiency in spoken English at the 2021 Census, the wave at which the ABS retired ENGP and published the concept as ENGLP instead. The 2021 Census Dictionary states that \"ENGP has been removed for the 2021 Census to avoid data misuse\", the reason being that ENGP applied only to people using another language at home while ENGLP applies to everyone and adds a Speaks English only category. A 2021 column carrying the ENGP name therefore holds the proficiency answer on the older, restricted base and is not the same object as a published 2021 ENGLP figure. Non-response on ENGLP was 5.5 per cent in 2021, down from 6.5 per cent in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Proficiency in spoken English (ENGLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/proficiency-spoken-english-englp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English code","def":"A single character over the four proficiency levels, two not-stated codes and the not applicable and overseas visitor codes. The 2021 released form, ENGLP, prefixes the same levels with a Speaks English only category, so a 2021 code has to be read against the frame it was drawn from.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Proficiency in spoken English (ENGLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/proficiency-spoken-english-englp","lim":"Lining ENGP_21 up beside ENGP_16 and ENGP_11 as a trend is the trap. The ABS withdrew ENGP for 2021 because its restricted base was being read as a whole-of-population measure, so a 2021 value carries a live risk that its denominator differs from the earlier waves, and no version of the variable says anything about reading or writing English.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":74},{"n":"ENGP_FP_11","d":"The female parent's proficiency in spoken English at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's own record.","full":"The female parent's proficiency in spoken English at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's own record. The underlying measure is ENGP, which the 2011 Census Dictionary defines as classifying, \"For each person who speaks a language other than English at home ... their self-assessed proficiency in spoken English\", so the value is that parent's own answer rather than the sampled person's. The female parent is whoever the Census identified as such in the same family on Census Night, which makes this a household-context variable: it exists for children and other family members, not for the woman herself.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English code","def":"The same single-character ENGP frame as the person's own column: four proficiency levels, two not-stated codes, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302011","lim":"A missing or not-applicable value here is mostly about family structure, not language. It is set where no female parent was enumerated in the family, where the sampled person was a visitor to the household, or where the female parent spoke only English, and those three very different situations are not separable from this column alone.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":74},{"n":"ENGP_FP_16","d":"The female parent's proficiency in spoken English at the 2016 Census, attached to the sampled person's record.","full":"The female parent's proficiency in spoken English at the 2016 Census, attached to the sampled person's record. The 2016 Census Dictionary keeps the 2011 definition word for word, classifying \"For each person who speaks a language other than English at home ... their self-assessed proficiency in spoken English\", so this column lines up with ENGP_FP_11 on both concept and codes. What can move between the two waves is the family itself, because a person's female parent in 2016 need not be the person recorded in 2011.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English code","def":"A single character over the four proficiency levels, two not-stated codes, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor, identical to the 2011 frame.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302016","lim":"It cannot be used to track one woman's English over time. The column identifies a role in the sampled person's 2016 household, so a change between the 2011 and 2016 values can mean the parent's rating changed, or simply that a different person filled the role or that the sampled person moved out of the family home.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":74},{"n":"ENGP_FP_21","d":"The female parent's proficiency in spoken English at the 2021 Census, attached to the sampled person's record.","full":"The female parent's proficiency in spoken English at the 2021 Census, attached to the sampled person's record. The base variable changed at this Census: the 2021 Census Dictionary records that \"ENGP has been removed for the 2021 Census to avoid data misuse\" and released the concept as ENGLP, which covers English-only speakers as a category of its own. The parent link also weakened in 2021, because the dictionary's Parent indicator page reports an error that pushed 97,359 parents in couple families into the Not applicable category when all their children were away on Census Night.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Proficiency in spoken English (ENGLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/proficiency-spoken-english-englp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English code","def":"A single character over the proficiency levels, not-stated codes, @ and V. The 2021 released frame, ENGLP, adds a Speaks English only category ahead of the levels, so the 2021 codes are not necessarily positionally aligned with the 2011 and 2016 ones.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Proficiency in spoken English (ENGLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/proficiency-spoken-english-englp","lim":"A jump in Not applicable between 2016 and 2021 should not be read as fewer mothers or better English. The documented 2021 parent-identification error removes real female parents from the column, and the retirement of ENGP separately changes which population the proficiency codes describe, so both the numerator and the denominator moved at the same wave.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":74},{"n":"ENGP_MP_11","d":"The male parent's proficiency in spoken English at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's record.","full":"The male parent's proficiency in spoken English at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's record. It is the ENGP question answered by that parent, which the 2011 Census Dictionary defines as classifying, \"For each person who speaks a language other than English at home ... their self-assessed proficiency in spoken English\". Paired with ENGP_FP_11 it gives the language environment of a child's family, and the two can disagree, because proficiency is reported for each adult separately.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English code","def":"The same single-character ENGP frame the person carries for themselves: four proficiency levels, two not-stated codes, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302011","lim":"It is not a father indicator. The value is set from whoever the Census classified as the male parent in the family on Census Night, so a non-resident father contributes nothing and a resident stepfather or a grandfather acting as parent may occupy the slot, and none of that is visible in the code itself.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":74},{"n":"ENGP_MP_16","d":"The male parent's proficiency in spoken English at the 2016 Census, attached to the sampled person's record.","full":"The male parent's proficiency in spoken English at the 2016 Census, attached to the sampled person's record. The 2016 Census Dictionary carries the 2011 definition unaltered, classifying \"For each person who speaks a language other than English at home ... their self-assessed proficiency in spoken English\", so the concept and the codes are stable across the two waves. Non-response on the underlying question was low, 1.1 per cent in 2016 against 1.3 per cent in 2011, but that figure applies to the parent's own record and not to the success of the link between parent and child.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English code","def":"A single character over four proficiency levels plus the two not-stated codes, @ and V, identical to the 2011 code list.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302016","lim":"The low non-response on the question does not carry over to this column. Most of the missingness here comes from families with no male parent enumerated, so treating a blank as an item non-response and imputing it would fabricate fathers who were never in the household.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":74},{"n":"ENGP_MP_21","d":"The male parent's proficiency in spoken English at the 2021 Census, attached to the sampled person's record.","full":"The male parent's proficiency in spoken English at the 2021 Census, attached to the sampled person's record. Two things moved at this wave: the 2021 Census Dictionary states that \"ENGP has been removed for the 2021 Census to avoid data misuse\" in favour of ENGLP, and the dictionary's Parent indicator page reports a 2021 processing error that misclassified parents in couple families to Not applicable when every child was temporarily absent. The corrected 2021 count of male parents is 3,062,913, against 3,788,471 female parents, so the two parent columns do not cover the same number of families.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Proficiency in spoken English (ENGLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/proficiency-spoken-english-englp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English code","def":"A single character over the proficiency levels and the not-stated, not-applicable and overseas-visitor codes. The 2021 published frame is ENGLP, which inserts a Speaks English only category, so the 2021 codes need to be checked against the frame actually supplied.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Proficiency in spoken English (ENGLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/proficiency-spoken-english-englp","lim":"It cannot support a claim about fathers' English improving or worsening between 2016 and 2021. Both the variable definition and the parent link changed at the 2021 Census, and male parents are identified less often than female parents in every wave, so a cross-wave difference mixes measurement change with family composition.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":74},{"n":"ENGP_SP_11","d":"The spouse or partner's proficiency in spoken English at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's record.","full":"The spouse or partner's proficiency in spoken English at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's record. It reproduces the ENGP answer given by the partner, defined in the 2011 Census Dictionary as classifying, \"For each person who speaks a language other than English at home ... their self-assessed proficiency in spoken English\". Because it is set only where the Census recorded a co-resident husband, wife, spouse or partner, the column doubles as a marker of couple status at that Census.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English code","def":"A single character over the ENGP code list: four proficiency levels, two not-stated codes distinguishing whether language was stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302011","lim":"The partner has to be living in the same dwelling. A married person whose spouse lives elsewhere, works away or is in care has no value here, so this column cannot be used to test whether people partner across language groups in the population at large, only within co-resident couples.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":74},{"n":"ENGP_SP_16","d":"The spouse or partner's proficiency in spoken English at the 2016 Census, attached to the sampled person's record.","full":"The spouse or partner's proficiency in spoken English at the 2016 Census, attached to the sampled person's record. The 2016 Census Dictionary repeats the 2011 definition without change, classifying \"For each person who speaks a language other than English at home ... their self-assessed proficiency in spoken English\", so a 2011-to-2016 comparison is safe on the measure even where it is not safe on the couple. Sitting beside ENGP_16, the pair shows whether both members of a couple report the same level.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English code","def":"A single character over the four proficiency levels plus the two not-stated codes, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor, unchanged from 2011.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Proficiency in Spoken English (ENGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3302016","lim":"A change between the 2011 and 2016 values is not evidence that one person's English changed. The partner recorded in 2016 may be a different person, or the same couple may have been enumerated apart, and the column carries no partner identifier to tell those cases from a genuine change in the answer.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":74},{"n":"ENGP_SP_21","d":"The spouse or partner's proficiency in spoken English at the 2021 Census, attached to the sampled person's record.","full":"The spouse or partner's proficiency in spoken English at the 2021 Census, attached to the sampled person's record. The base measure changed at this Census: the 2021 Census Dictionary records that \"ENGP has been removed for the 2021 Census to avoid data misuse\", with the concept released as ENGLP over the whole population rather than only over people using another language at home. Non-response on ENGLP was 5.5 per cent in 2021, and that missingness lands on the partner's record, not on the sampled person's.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Proficiency in spoken English (ENGLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/proficiency-spoken-english-englp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Proficiency in Spoken English of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census proficiency in spoken English code","def":"A single character over the proficiency levels and the not-stated, not-applicable and overseas-visitor codes, with the 2021 ENGLP frame adding a Speaks English only category ahead of the four levels.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Proficiency in spoken English (ENGLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/proficiency-spoken-english-englp","lim":"The 2021 value cannot be pooled with the 2011 and 2016 partner columns as a single series. ENGP was withdrawn for 2021 because its restricted base invited exactly that misuse, and adding a partner link on top means a difference across waves can come from the measure, from the partner, or from both.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":74},{"n":"FBLF_P_11","d":"Whether the sampled person's couple family at the 2011 Census was intact, step or blended, judged from the parent-child links inside it.","full":"Whether the sampled person's couple family at the 2011 Census was intact, step or blended, judged from the parent-child links inside it. The 2011 Census Dictionary says the variable \"was introduced in the 2006 Census\" and \"classifies families based on the parent-child relationships within the family\", and that it is applicable to couple families. The _P suffix marks the family-level classification carried on the person record, which is how the ACLD publishes household and family variables. Children reported as temporarily absent on Census Night are counted when the family type is worked out.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Blending (FBLF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter32202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Family Blending","t":"categorical","k":"Census family blending code","def":"A single-character code, 1 to 7, over intact, step and blended couple families, each split by whether other children such as foster or related children are also present, plus a category for couple families with other children only and @ for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Blending (FBLF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter32202011","lim":"It says nothing about one-parent families, which are all coded not applicable, so a not-applicable value is not the absence of step relationships. It also describes the family in the dwelling on one night: a child who lives mainly with the other parent does not make that household a step family here.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":75},{"n":"FBLF_P_16","d":"Whether the sampled person's couple family at the 2016 Census was intact, step or blended.","full":"Whether the sampled person's couple family at the 2016 Census was intact, step or blended. The 2016 Census Dictionary keeps the 2011 text word for word, that the variable \"classifies families based on the parent-child relationships within the family\" and \"is applicable to couple families\", so the 2011 and 2016 columns sit on the same seven-way frame. The classification is built during processing from the relationship and temporarily-absent questions rather than from a single tick box, so it has no non-response rate of its own.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Blending (FBLF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter32202016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Family Blending","t":"categorical","k":"Census family blending code","def":"A single-character code, 1 to 7, distinguishing intact, step and blended couple families with and without other children present, plus other couple families with other children only, and @ not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Blending (FBLF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter32202016","lim":"A family that moves from intact in 2011 to step in 2016 has not necessarily re-partnered. The code is rebuilt from scratch at each Census around a family reference person, so a different reference person, a new child, or a child leaving home can shift the category on its own.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":75},{"n":"FBLF_P_21","d":"Whether the sampled person's couple family at the 2021 Census was intact, step or blended.","full":"Whether the sampled person's couple family at the 2021 Census was intact, step or blended. The 2021 Census Dictionary tightens the wording to \"classifies couple families with children living in private dwellings, based on the parent-child relationships within them\" and states that \"No changes have been made for 2021\", so the categories match 2016 and 2011. One 2021-specific fault matters: the ABS has identified an overcount of step children for some states and territories, caused by the form's handling of couples with a temporarily absent spouse.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Family blending (FBLF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/family-blending-fblf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Family Blending","t":"categorical","k":"Census family blending code","def":"A single-character code, 1 to 7, over intact, step and blended couple families, each with and without other children present, plus other couple family with other children only and @ not applicable for one-parent families, childless couples and non-family households.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Family blending (FBLF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/family-blending-fblf","lim":"The 2021 step and blended counts are inflated in some states and territories by the documented step-child overcount, so a rise in step families between 2016 and 2021 in this dataset may be a processing artefact rather than a change in family formation. The restriction to private dwellings also means people in non-private dwellings such as aged care are outside the frame entirely.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":75},{"n":"FIDF_P_11","d":"A flag saying how usable the sampled person's 2011 family income figure is, not an income itself.","full":"A flag saying how usable the sampled person's 2011 family income figure is, not an income itself. The 2011 Census Dictionary describes it as the variable that \"allows family income to be derived based on any of the following conditions\", and it crosses three things: whether a family member aged 15 or over was temporarily absent, whether any income was left unstated, and whether any member reported a negative income. It is the column that says whether FINF_P_11 and FINASF_P_11 on the same row can be taken at face value.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Income Derivation Indicator (FIDF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3502011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Family Income Derivation Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census family income derivation indicator code","def":"A single character over eight numbered categories formed by crossing absence, non-response and negative income, plus @ for not applicable. Categories 1 to 4 cover families with nobody aged 15 or over absent; 5 to 8 cover families where someone was.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Income Derivation Indicator (FIDF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3502011","lim":"It measures the completeness of the income record, not the family's circumstances. A family flagged as having an income not stated is not a low-income family, and a family flagged with a negative income is usually a business or investment loss rather than poverty, so filtering on this column selects on reporting behaviour and can bias an income distribution.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":76},{"n":"FIDF_P_16","d":"A flag saying how usable the sampled person's 2016 family income figure is.","full":"A flag saying how usable the sampled person's 2016 family income figure is. The 2016 Census Dictionary repeats the 2011 wording, that the variable \"allows family income to be derived based on any of the following conditions\", over the same eight numbered categories plus not applicable, so the two waves can be compared code for code. Because it is built during processing from the family composition and personal income variables, it carries no non-response rate of its own.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Income Derivation Indicator (FIDF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3502016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Family Income Derivation Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census family income derivation indicator code","def":"A single character over eight categories crossing temporary absence of a member aged 15 or over, incomes not stated and negative incomes, with @ for non-family households, unoccupied dwellings and non-private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Income Derivation Indicator (FIDF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3502016","lim":"A stable code between 2011 and 2016 is not evidence of a stable family. The flag responds to who happened to be home and who answered the income question on one night, so it moves with enumeration conditions, and the ACLD user who conditions on category 1 in both waves has selected a fully responding subsample rather than a representative one.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":76},{"n":"FIDF_P_21","d":"A flag saying how usable the sampled person's 2021 family income figure is.","full":"A flag saying how usable the sampled person's 2021 family income figure is. The 2021 Census Dictionary states that the variable identifies families where a member was \"temporarily absent, did not state their income or stated a negative income\", and that \"No changes have been made for 2021\", so the eight-plus-one category frame matches 2016 and 2011. It is derived from Family composition (FMCF) and Total personal income (INCP) together with the counts of persons and dependent children temporarily absent.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Family income derivation indicator (FIDF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/family-income-derivation-indicator-fidf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Family Income Derivation Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census family income derivation indicator code","def":"A single character over eight numbered categories, split first by whether a member aged 15 or over was temporarily absent, then by whether incomes were stated and whether any were negative, with @ for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Family income derivation indicator (FIDF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/family-income-derivation-indicator-fidf","lim":"It cannot say how much income is missing. A family with one absent adult and a family with three unstated incomes can share a category, and the flag gives no way to bound the gap between the stated total in FINASF_P_21 and the family's true income, so it supports excluding cases rather than correcting them.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":77},{"n":"FINASF_P_11","d":"The sampled person's 2011 family income, added up from whatever income the family actually reported.","full":"The sampled person's 2011 family income, added up from whatever income the family actually reported. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as \"Calculated by summing the personal incomes reported by all family members aged 15 years and over\", and its whole point is that it still produces a figure when someone did not answer the income question or was away on Census Night. FINF_P_11 on the same row refuses to produce a figure in those cases, so the two columns are the same sum under different rules and FIDF_P_11 says which situation applies.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Total Family Income as Stated (weekly) (FINASF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3602011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Family Income as Stated (Weekly)","t":"categorical","k":"Census weekly family income range (as stated)","def":"A banded weekly dollar range rather than a dollar amount: seventeen 2011 bands running from negative income to $5,000 or more, plus && all incomes not stated and @@ not applicable, built by assigning each member's personal income band a median value and summing those medians.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Total Family Income as Stated (weekly) (FINASF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3602011","lim":"The figure is biased low wherever the family was not fully reported, because a missing member contributes nothing rather than being imputed. Comparing a FINASF value against a FINF value for the same family therefore measures how complete the reporting was, not how much the family earned.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":78},{"n":"FINASF_P_16","d":"The sampled person's 2016 family income, summed from the incomes the family actually stated.","full":"The sampled person's 2016 family income, summed from the incomes the family actually stated. The 2016 Census Dictionary keeps the 2011 definition, \"Calculated by summing the personal incomes reported by all family members aged 15 years and over\", but the dollar ranges were redrawn for the 2016 Census: the 2011 classification carried seventeen bands topping out at $5,000 or more, and the 2016 one carries twenty-two topping out at $8,000 or more. The codes therefore do not line up with FINASF_P_11, and the two waves have to be matched on dollar ranges rather than on code values.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Total Family Income as Stated (weekly) (FINASF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3602016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Family Income as Stated (Weekly)","t":"categorical","k":"Census weekly family income range (as stated)","def":"A banded weekly range from negative income through to $8,000 or more, twenty-two bands in all, plus && all incomes not stated and @@ not applicable, so twenty-four categories. Each member's personal income band is converted to a median dollar value before summing.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Total Family Income as Stated (weekly) (FINASF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3602016","lim":"Two separate things break a raw 2011-to-2016 transition matrix on this column. The bands were redrawn for 2016, so a given code does not cover the same dollars in both waves, and the boundaries are nominal in any case, so a family that moves up the scale may have gone backwards in real terms.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":79},{"n":"FINASF_P_21","d":"The sampled person's 2021 family income, summed from the incomes actually stated by family members present.","full":"The sampled person's 2021 family income, summed from the incomes actually stated by family members present. The 2021 Census Dictionary defines it as \"the total family income by summing the Total personal income (weekly) (INCP) of each family member aged 15 years and over present in the household on Census Night\", and notes that it \"includes families where one or more family member's income details were not stated or they were away from the dwelling on Census Night\". The ABS revised the family income ranges for the 2016 Census and made no further change for 2021, so the bands match 2016 but not 2011.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total family income as stated (weekly) (FINASF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-family-income-stated-weekly-finasf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Family Income as Stated (Weekly)","t":"categorical","k":"Census weekly family income range (as stated)","def":"A banded weekly dollar range, twenty-two bands from negative income to $8,000 or more plus && all incomes not stated and @@ not applicable, derived by giving each personal income band its median value from the Survey of Income and Housing and adding those values across members aged 15 and over.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total family income as stated (weekly) (FINASF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-family-income-stated-weekly-finasf","lim":"The 2021 Census was taken during COVID-19 lockdowns in the two largest states, when JobKeeper and the COVID-19 disaster payment were flowing and many households were split across dwellings. A 2016-to-2021 change in this column mixes that with any real income change, and the as-stated rule means a family separated by border closures is measured on the members who were home.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":79},{"n":"FINF_P_11","d":"The sampled person's 2011 family income, calculated only where every adult in the family was present and answered.","full":"The sampled person's 2011 family income, calculated only where every adult in the family was present and answered. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as \"calculated by summing the personal incomes reported by all family members aged 15 years and over\", and where that is not possible the family is sent to the Partial income stated or All incomes not stated codes instead of receiving a dollar band. FINASF_P_11 beside it takes the opposite approach and reports the stated total anyway.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Total Family Income (weekly) (FINF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3702011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Family Income (Weekly)","t":"categorical","k":"Census weekly family income range","def":"A banded weekly dollar range over seventeen 2011 bands from negative income to $5,000 or more, plus three further codes: 18 Partial income stated, && All incomes not stated and @@ Not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Total Family Income (weekly) (FINF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3702011","lim":"Partial income stated is not a low income and must not be dropped silently. Families with an absent or non-responding adult are systematically different from those without one, so treating those codes as missing at random and analysing only the banded cases removes larger, more mobile and more disadvantaged families from the sample.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":80},{"n":"FINF_P_16","d":"The sampled person's 2016 family income, left uncalculated when the family was not fully reported.","full":"The sampled person's 2016 family income, left uncalculated when the family was not fully reported. The 2016 Census Dictionary states the rule directly: \"Total Family Income (weekly) is not calculated where a family member aged 15 years and over did not state their income, or was temporarily absent.\" The Partial income stated and All incomes not stated codes work as they did in 2011, but the dollar bands do not: the ABS redrew the family income ranges for 2016, taking FINF from seventeen bands with a $5,000-or-more top band to twenty-two topping out at $8,000 or more.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Total Family Income (weekly) (FINF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3702016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Family Income (Weekly)","t":"categorical","k":"Census weekly family income range","def":"A banded weekly range with twenty-two dollar bands from negative income to $8,000 or more, built by giving each member's personal income band its Survey of Income and Housing median before summing, plus 23 Partial income stated, && All incomes not stated and @@ Not applicable, so twenty-five categories.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Total Family Income (weekly) (FINF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3702016","lim":"The banding, not just the missingness, limits what can be done with it. Because each member contributes an assigned median rather than a reported dollar figure, family totals cannot support inequality measures that depend on the shape of the distribution within a band, and a small real change will often not move a family across a boundary at all.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":81},{"n":"FINF_P_21","d":"The sampled person's 2021 family income, calculated only for fully reported families.","full":"The sampled person's 2021 family income, calculated only for fully reported families. The 2021 Census Dictionary defines it as recording \"the total family income by summing the Total personal income (weekly) (INCP) of each family member aged 15 years and over present in the household on Census Night\", with families missing an adult's income sent to Partial income stated. The ABS revised the family income ranges for 2016 and made no further change for 2021, so the twenty-two dollar bands match 2016 but not the seventeen bands used in 2011.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total family income (weekly) (FINF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-family-income-weekly-finf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Family Income (Weekly)","t":"categorical","k":"Census weekly family income range","def":"A banded weekly range from negative income through to $8,000 or more, with Nil income, Partial income stated, All incomes not stated and not applicable as separate codes. Band midpoints come from Survey of Income and Housing medians.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total family income (weekly) (FINF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-family-income-weekly-finf","lim":"Family income here is bounded by the dwelling. Support flowing between households, such as child support, a parent paying a student's rent or remittances sent overseas, is invisible, so this column measures the resources of the people who happened to be under one roof on 10 August 2021 rather than a family's economic position.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":81},{"n":"FMCF_P_11","d":"The type of family the sampled person belonged to at the 2011 Census: couple with or without children, one parent, or other family.","full":"The type of family the sampled person belonged to at the 2011 Census: couple with or without children, one parent, or other family. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as classifying \"families into different types\", and adds that \"information about temporarily absent family members is used\" when the type is worked out, so a child away on Census Night still counts. The detail levels split couple and one-parent families by whether children under 15, dependent students or non-dependent children are present.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Composition (FMCF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3802011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Family Composition","t":"categorical","k":"Census family composition code","def":"A hierarchical numeric code with two-, three- and four-digit levels: four broad family types opening out to seventeen four-digit categories, plus a not applicable code for non-family households, unoccupied dwellings and non-private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Composition (FMCF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3802011","lim":"A family here is a set of related people in one dwelling, so it cannot see a family spread across two. Separated parents and their children form two families in different households, shared-care children appear in only one of them, and an adult living alone is not a one-person family but a non-family household coded not applicable.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":82},{"n":"FMCF_P_16","d":"The type of family the sampled person belonged to at the 2016 Census.","full":"The type of family the sampled person belonged to at the 2016 Census. The 2016 Census Dictionary states the mechanism plainly: \"Families are classified in terms of the relationships that exist between a single family reference person and each other member of that family.\" The category structure is unchanged from 2011, so the codes are directly comparable, but the reference person is chosen afresh at each Census and the classification depends on who that is.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Composition (FMCF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter32302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Family Composition","t":"categorical","k":"Census family composition code","def":"A hierarchical numeric code over couple family with no children, couple family with children, one parent family and other family, subdivided by the ages and dependency of the children, with a not applicable code for non-family households and unoccupied dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Composition (FMCF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter32302016","lim":"Movement between the 2011 and 2016 codes is not a clean measure of family change. The 2021 Census Dictionary defines it as classifying \"families into different family types\" and says it \"uses a single family reference person and classifies each member around that person\", with \"No changes have been made for 2021\". It is also the input to several other columns in this dataset: FIDF_P_21 is derived from it and Total personal income, and HCFMD combines it with household composition at the dwelling level.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Family composition (FMCF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/family-composition-fmcf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Family Composition","t":"categorical","k":"Census family composition code","def":"A hierarchical numeric code with six two-digit, ten three-digit and seventeen four-digit categories across couple families with and without children, one parent families and other families, plus a not applicable code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Family composition (FMCF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/family-composition-fmcf","lim":"The 2021 count was taken under COVID-19 restrictions, when students had returned home, borders separated couples and some people were enumerated away from their usual household. A 2016-to-2021 transition in this column can therefore record where people were on one night in August 2021 rather than a durable change in family type.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":82},{"n":"FMGF_P_11","d":"An alternative family type for the sampled person at the 2011 Census, built to make grandparent-headed families visible.","full":"An alternative family type for the sampled person at the 2011 Census, built to make grandparent-headed families visible. It is the same family the standard FMCF_P_11 code describes, read through grandparent-grandchild links instead of parent-child ones.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Grandparent Families (FMGF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3902011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Grandparent Families","t":"categorical","k":"Census grandparent family type code","def":"A two-level numeric code: couple family with grandchildren and lone grandparent family, each split three ways by whether grandchildren under 15, dependent student grandchildren aged 15 to 24, or only non-dependent grandchildren are present, plus a not applicable code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Grandparent Families (FMGF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3902011","lim":"It counts only families where no parent is present. Because it is an alternative to FMCF_P_16 rather than an addition to it, the two columns describe one family two ways and their counts must not be added together.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Grandparent Families (FMGF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3902016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Grandparent Families","t":"categorical","k":"Census grandparent family type code","def":"A two-level numeric code covering couple families with grandchildren and lone grandparent families, each split by whether grandchildren under 15, dependent student grandchildren or only non-dependent grandchildren are present, with a not applicable code for all other families.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Grandparent Families (FMGF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter3902016","lim":"It has to be paired with the grandchild-aware relationship and child-type variables. Crossing FMGF with the ordinary Relationship in household or Child type columns produces cells that contradict each other, because those columns treat a grandchild as a related individual rather than as a child of the family.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":83},{"n":"FMGF_P_21","d":"An alternative 2021 family type for the sampled person, recognising grandparent-grandchild relationships.","full":"An alternative 2021 family type for the sampled person, recognising grandparent-grandchild relationships. The mnemonic FTPP is the 2016 form of the name; the ABS renamed the same variable FTCP in the 2021 microdata products, noting that \"the variable is otherwise unchanged, that is the codes and categories for this variable remain the same\".","dsrc":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Census of Population and Housing, form type variable note","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/census-population-and-housing","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Form Type in 2016","t":"categorical","k":"Census form type code","def":"A small code set distinguishing a personal or household paper form, a personal or household eform completed online, and other form types used for special enumeration.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Census of Population and Housing, form type variable note","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/census-population-and-housing","lim":"It describes the channel, not the respondent. The _21 suffix marks the Census year, and the 2021 Census Dictionary defines the variable as one that \"indicates the type of form a person used to submit their 2021 Census responses\", published under the renamed mnemonic FTCP with \"no changes made to this variable\" since 2016. Online completion rose sharply in 2021, so the paper and eform split is not comparable in level with FTPP_16 even though the codes are identical.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Form type (FTCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/form-type-ftcp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Form Type in 2016","t":"categorical","k":"Census form type code","def":"A small code set over personal or household paper form, personal or household eform, and other form types, identical to the 2016 codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Form type (FTCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/form-type-ftcp","lim":"The custodian's own description for this column says 'Form Type in 2016', which is a label carried over from the previous wave, so a reader who trusts the description rather than the suffix will attribute a 2021 attribute to the 2016 Census. The 2011 Census Dictionary explains the derivation: \"The employer's business name and the workplace address of the employed person is used to classify employed persons into the public or private sector.\" Nobody answered a question about sector, so this is an ABS coding decision made from written employer details, and it splits the public sector into national, state or territory, and local government.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Public/Private Employer Indicator (GNGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Public/Private Employer Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census public/private sector code","def":"A single character: 1 National Government, 2 State/Territory Government, 3 Local Government, 4 Private sector, & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor. Not applicable covers the unemployed, people not in the labour force, labour force status not stated and people aged under 15.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Public/Private Employer Indicator (GNGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4202011","lim":"The private sector code is the residual. The 2016 Census Dictionary repeats the 2011 derivation word for word, that \"the employer's business name and the workplace address of the employed person is used to classify employed persons into the public or private sector\", over the same four sector codes. Read it with the industry and occupation columns for the same year, because sector and industry are coded from the same written employer description and can disagree.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Public/Private Employer Indicator (GNGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4202016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Public/Private Employer Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census public/private sector code","def":"A single character over National Government, State/Territory Government, Local Government and Private sector, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Public/Private Employer Indicator (GNGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4202016","lim":"A move from public to private between 2011 and 2016 need not be a job change. The 2021 Census Dictionary publishes it as Public/private sector, the title the 2016 dictionary also used, and defines it as classifying \"employed people according to whether they are employed in the government (public) or non-government (private) sector\", with \"No changes have been made for 2021\". The mnemonic and the code list are unchanged, so the ACLD's older Public/Private Employer Indicator label is a naming difference only and GNGP_21 remains comparable with GNGP_16 and GNGP_11.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Public/private sector (GNGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/publicprivate-sector-gngp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Public/Private Employer Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census public/private sector code","def":"A single character over National Government, State/Territory Government, Local Government and Private sector, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor. It is derived during processing rather than answered, so it has no non-response rate of its own.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Public/private sector (GNGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/publicprivate-sector-gngp","lim":"Sector at the 2021 Census reflects where a person was working during COVID-19 restrictions, not necessarily their usual employer. People stood down, on JobKeeper, or working in a temporary public health or logistics role were coded from what they wrote in August 2021, so a one-wave shift into or out of government is weak evidence of a lasting move.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":86},{"n":"GNGP_FP_11","d":"The female parent's employment sector at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's record.","full":"The female parent's employment sector at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's record. Paired with GNGP_MP_11 it gives a child's parental employment context, and paired with ENGP_FP_11 and the family income columns it describes the household a child grew up in at that Census.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Public/Private Employer Indicator (GNGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Public/Private Employer Indicator for Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census public/private sector code","def":"A single character over National Government, State/Territory Government, Local Government and Private sector, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Public/Private Employer Indicator (GNGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4202011","lim":"Not applicable does two jobs here and they cannot be separated: there was no female parent in the family, or there was one and she was not employed. The 2016 Census Dictionary keeps the derivation unchanged, classifying from \"the employer's business name and the workplace address of the employed person\", so the codes match GNGP_FP_11 exactly. Women are more likely than men to be employed in the state and territory government category, through health and education, which is why the parent columns often differ in composition rather than just in level.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Public/Private Employer Indicator (GNGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4202016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Public/Private Employer Indicator for Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census public/private sector code","def":"A single character over the three government levels and the private sector, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor, identical to the 2011 code list.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Public/Private Employer Indicator (GNGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4202016","lim":"It cannot follow one woman's career. The 2021 Census Dictionary publishes the base variable as Public/private sector, the title it also carried in 2016, and defines it as classifying \"employed people according to whether they are employed in the government (public) or non-government (private) sector\", with the codes unchanged. The parent link is weaker at this wave: the 2021 Census Dictionary's Parent indicator page reports an error that moved 97,359 parents in couple families to Not applicable when all their children were away on Census Night.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Public/private sector (GNGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/publicprivate-sector-gngp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Public/Private Employer Indicator for Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census public/private sector code","def":"A single character over National Government, State/Territory Government, Local Government and Private sector, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor, unchanged from 2011 and 2016.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Public/private sector (GNGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/publicprivate-sector-gngp","lim":"A rise in Not applicable between 2016 and 2021 is not evidence that mothers left work. The male parent is whoever the Census identified in that role in the family on Census Night, so a resident stepfather can supply the value and a non-resident father never does.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Public/Private Employer Indicator (GNGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Public/Private Employer Indicator for Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census public/private sector code","def":"A single character over National Government, State/Territory Government, Local Government and Private sector, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Public/Private Employer Indicator (GNGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4202011","lim":"The default-to-private coding rule bites harder on this column than on a person's own. Fathers' employer details are written by whoever completed the household form, often a partner, and a vague or misspelt employer name is coded private rather than not stated, so paternal public sector employment is understated.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":86},{"n":"GNGP_MP_16","d":"The male parent's employment sector at the 2016 Census, attached to the sampled person's record.","full":"The male parent's employment sector at the 2016 Census, attached to the sampled person's record. Together with GNGP_FP_16 it supports questions about whether children of public sector parents follow them into the sector, since the person's own GNGP is on the same record at later waves.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Public/Private Employer Indicator (GNGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4202016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Public/Private Employer Indicator for Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census public/private sector code","def":"A single character over the three levels of government and the private sector, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes, unchanged from 2011.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. no. 2901.0), Public/Private Employer Indicator (GNGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4202016","lim":"It is a snapshot of one employer on one night, not a working life. The 2021 Census Dictionary publishes the base variable as Public/private sector, the title it also carried in 2016, and defines it as classifying \"employed people according to whether they are employed in the government (public) or non-government (private) sector\", with no change to the codes. Male parents are identified less often than female parents in every wave, and the 2021 Census Dictionary's corrected counts, 3,062,913 male against 3,788,471 female parents, show the size of that gap.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Public/private sector (GNGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/publicprivate-sector-gngp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Public/Private Employer Indicator for Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census public/private sector code","def":"A single character over National Government, State/Territory Government, Local Government and Private sector, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor, unchanged from the earlier waves.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Public/private sector (GNGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/publicprivate-sector-gngp","lim":"The column is not a sample of fathers. The partner still has to be enumerated in the same dwelling, which the 2021 border closures and lockdowns made less likely than at earlier Censuses.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Public/private sector (GNGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/publicprivate-sector-gngp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Public/Private Employer Indicator for Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census public/private sector code","def":"A single character over National Government, State/Territory Government, Local Government and Private sector, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor, identical to the 2011 and 2016 code lists.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Public/private sector (GNGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/publicprivate-sector-gngp","lim":"A partner missing in 2021 who was present in 2016 is not necessarily a separation. It sits above FMCF_P_11, which describes the person's own family: this column says whether that family shared the dwelling with one or two others, or whether the dwelling was a lone person or group household instead.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Household Composition (Dwelling) (HCFMD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4252011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Household Family Composition","t":"categorical","k":"Census family household composition (dwelling) code","def":"A two-digit code in three blocks: 11 to 14 for one family households by family type, 21 to 28 for two-family and three-or-more-family households, and 31 to 34 for lone person, group, visitors only and other non-classifiable households, plus @@ for unoccupied and non-private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Family Household Composition (Dwelling) (HCFMD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4252011","lim":"In a multiple family household only the primary family's type shows through, so the second and third families in the dwelling are counted but not described. HCFMD was new in 2011 and the ABS made no changes for 2016, so the 2016 and 2011 columns use the same 17 categories. The neighbouring HHCD_P_16 answers a coarser question, whether any family is present at all.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Family Household Composition (Dwelling) (HCFMD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4252016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Household Family Composition","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 family household composition code (HCFMD)","def":"A two-digit code from the 17-category family household composition classification, grouped as one family household, two-family and three-or-more-family households, and lone person, group, visitors-only and other non-classifiable households, plus a not-applicable code for unoccupied and non-private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Family Household Composition (Dwelling) (HCFMD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4252016","lim":"It does not describe the person's own family. The 2016 dictionary attaches a note that in multiple family households only the composition of the primary family is recorded, so anyone who belongs to a secondary family is described by a code that was set by someone else's family. It is a family-level maximum over the person-level HEAP variable, which the ABS derives from highest year of school completed and level of highest non-school qualification. HEAH_P_11 does the same job over the household rather than the family.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202011","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Level of Highest Educational Attainment Completed by Any Family Member","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A code from the Census level of highest educational attainment classification, running from postgraduate degree down through secondary education and certificate levels, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202011","lim":"It names a level, not a person. It cannot say which family member holds the attainment, whether that person is still in the family at the next wave, or whether the family had only one adult, so it is a poor proxy for a child's own parents' education in a multi-generation family. Members under 15 are outside the scope of HEAP and so contribute nothing.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":89},{"n":"HEAF_P_16","d":"The highest education level reached by any member of the family the person was enumerated in at the 2016 Census.","full":"The highest education level reached by any member of the family the person was enumerated in at the 2016 Census.
