Compare it against HEAP_16 to see whether the person is the most educated member of their own family.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Level of Highest Educational Attainment Completed by Any Family Member","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A code from the 2016 Census level of highest educational attainment classification: postgraduate degree, graduate diploma and graduate certificate, bachelor degree, advanced diploma and diploma, certificate levels, secondary education, plus supplementary codes for not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202016","lim":"A rise between waves does not mean anyone studied. One classification change matters for 2021: undergraduate certificates were new and are coded to '420 Diploma level, nfd', a category nothing was coded to in earlier Censuses, so a family maximum can sit at 420 in 2021 for a reason that could not arise in 2016. The household-wide version is HEAH_P_21.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Level of highest educational attainment (HEAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/level-highest-educational-attainment-heap","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Level of Highest Educational Attainment Completed by Any Family Member","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A three-digit code from the 2021 Census level of highest educational attainment classification, ordered from postgraduate degree level down to certificate I and II level, with codes for inadequately described, no educational attainment and not stated.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Level of highest educational attainment (HEAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/level-highest-educational-attainment-heap","lim":"It cannot be compared with 2016 at the diploma level without care, because the new undergraduate certificate lands in a category that was previously empty. It takes the maximum of the person-level HEAP variable over everyone in the dwelling, including people the respondent is not related to, which is what separates it from the family version HEAF_P_11. The custodian's 'as stated' qualifier means a member who left the education questions blank is passed over rather than imputed. In 2011 the ABS released HEAP on request only, so this wave rests on a variable that was not a standard Census output.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202011","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Level of Highest Educational Attainment Completed by Any Household Member (as Stated)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A code from the Census level of highest educational attainment classification, from postgraduate degree through to certificate levels and secondary education, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202011","lim":"A boarder or a flatmate can set the value. Because it maximises over the whole dwelling rather than the family, a highly qualified unrelated resident lifts the household figure without telling you anything about the respondent's family, so it should not be used as a proxy for parental education in group households.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":89},{"n":"HEAH_P_16","d":"The highest education level stated by any member of the household the person was enumerated in at the 2016 Census.","full":"The highest education level stated by any member of the household the person was enumerated in at the 2016 Census. It is the household-wide maximum of HEAP and so covers unrelated residents as well as family, which HEAF_P_16 does not. HEAP was a standard output in 2016 after being available on request in 2011, so the 2016 household value rests on more complete underlying data than the 2011 one. The 'as stated' wording means members whose attainment was not stated do not contribute.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Level of Highest Educational Attainment Completed by Any Household Member (as Stated)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A code from the 2016 Census level of highest educational attainment classification, covering postgraduate through certificate and secondary levels, with separate codes for inadequately described and not stated responses.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202016","lim":"It cannot separate a household where nobody holds a qualification from one where nobody answered. Both push the maximum toward the low or not-stated end, so this column overstates the number of genuinely low-attainment households in dwellings with poor response.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":89},{"n":"HEAH_P_21","d":"The highest education level stated by any member of the household the person was enumerated in at the 2021 Census.","full":"The highest education level stated by any member of the household the person was enumerated in at the 2021 Census. It maximises HEAP, which the ABS says applies to \"Persons aged 15 years and over\", across the whole dwelling rather than the family. The 2021 classification change carries through: undergraduate certificates, new in 2021, are coded to '420 Diploma level, nfd', so a 2021 household maximum can sit in a category that was empty in 2016. HEAF_P_21 gives the same measure restricted to the person's family.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Level of highest educational attainment (HEAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/level-highest-educational-attainment-heap","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Level of Highest Educational Attainment Completed by Any Household Member (as Stated)","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A three-digit code from the 2021 Census level of highest educational attainment classification, ranging from postgraduate degree level to certificate I and II level, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, no attainment and not stated.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Level of highest educational attainment (HEAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/level-highest-educational-attainment-heap","lim":"It cannot support a claim about change over time on its own. Between 2016 and 2021 the household maximum can move because the household changed, because the respondent moved, or because of the new undergraduate certificate coding, and this column distinguishes none of the three.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":89},{"n":"HEAP_11","d":"The person's own highest educational attainment at the 2011 Census.","full":"The person's own highest educational attainment at the 2011 Census. The ABS derives it rather than asking it: \"HEAP is derived from information on the highest year of school completed and level of highest non-school qualification regardless of the particular field of study or the type of institution in which the study was undertaken.\" The 2011 dictionary also records that for this variable in 2011 data was available on request, so HEAP_11 comes from a variable the ABS did not publish as a standard output that year. The family and household maxima on the same row, HEAF_P_11 and HEAH_P_11, describe other people.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Level of Highest Educational Attainment","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 level of highest educational attainment code (HEAP)","def":"A code from the Census level of highest educational attainment classification, which ranks school and non-school attainment on one scale from postgraduate degree down to certificate I and II and secondary education, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202011","lim":"It hides the field of study and the institution, so it cannot separate a trade certificate from a business certificate at the same level. The ranking is also not a simple ordering of years: the ABS decision table puts some secondary education above some certificate attainments, which breaks any attempt to treat the code as a numeric scale.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":90},{"n":"HEAP_16","d":"The person's own highest educational attainment at the 2016 Census, applicable to people aged 15 and over.","full":"The person's own highest educational attainment at the 2016 Census, applicable to people aged 15 and over. The ABS combines the school and non-school answers through a decision table, and notes that \"in some cases secondary education is regarded as higher than some Certificate level attainments\". Unlike 2011, when HEAP was released on request, the 2016 variable was a standard Census output. Reading HEAP_11 and HEAP_16 side by side on one ACLD row gives a five-year change in attainment for the same person.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Level of Highest Educational Attainment","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 level of highest educational attainment code (HEAP)","def":"A code from the 2016 Census level of highest educational attainment classification, covering postgraduate degree, graduate diploma and certificate, bachelor degree, advanced diploma and diploma, certificate levels and secondary education, plus supplementary codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202016","lim":"A fall between 2011 and 2016 is not evidence of lost education. One change matters for comparison with HEAP_16 on the same row: undergraduate certificates are new in 2021 and are coded to '420 Diploma level, nfd', a category nothing was coded to before.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Level of highest educational attainment (HEAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/level-highest-educational-attainment-heap","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Level of Highest Educational Attainment","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 level of highest educational attainment code (HEAP)","def":"A three-digit code from the 2021 classification, ordered postgraduate degree, graduate diploma and graduate certificate, bachelor degree, advanced diploma and diploma, certificate III and IV, secondary education, certificate I and II, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, no attainment and not stated.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Level of highest educational attainment (HEAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/level-highest-educational-attainment-heap","lim":"The 2021 diploma band is not equivalent to the 2016 one. It is the same person-level attainment code as HEAP_11, drawn from a different family member, and it exists so a child's record can carry the mother's education without a household join. In 2011 the ABS released HEAP on request rather than as a standard output, so this wave rests on a variable that was not routinely published. HEAP_MP_11 does the same for the male parent and HEAP_SP_11 for a spouse or partner.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202011","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Level of Highest Educational Attainment by Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A code from the Census level of highest educational attainment classification, identical in form to HEAP, with a not-applicable code where the family has no female parent.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202011","lim":"The column is defined by the parent's sex, so it cannot describe both parents in a same-sex couple family, and in a male lone-parent family it is empty rather than zero. Because the family is the one recorded on Census Night, a child enumerated away from home carries no parent value at all. HEAP_21 on the same row is the respondent's own attainment.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Level of highest educational attainment (HEAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/level-highest-educational-attainment-heap","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Level of Highest Educational Attainment by Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A three-digit code from the 2021 Census level of highest educational attainment classification, plus a not-applicable code where the enumerated family has no female parent.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Level of highest educational attainment (HEAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/level-highest-educational-attainment-heap","lim":"It cannot be used to track one mother across waves. Pairing it with HEAP_FP_16 gives the two-parent education profile of the family as enumerated in 2016, and with HEAP_SP_16 where the respondent is themselves a partner rather than a child.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Level of Highest Educational Attainment by Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A code from the 2016 Census level of highest educational attainment classification, with a not-applicable code where the enumerated family has no male parent.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Level of Highest Educational Attainment (HEAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter39202016","lim":"It says nothing about the father of a child living with their mother alone, because the value reflects the family enumerated in the dwelling and not parentage. The 2021 coding change reaches this column: a partner holding a new undergraduate certificate is coded to '420 Diploma level, nfd', which carried nothing in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Level of highest educational attainment (HEAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/level-highest-educational-attainment-heap","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Level of Highest Educational Attainment by Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A three-digit code from the 2021 Census level of highest educational attainment classification, with a not-applicable code where no co-resident spouse or partner was recorded in the family.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Level of highest educational attainment (HEAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/level-highest-educational-attainment-heap","lim":"It cannot be used to measure whether partners are becoming better matched on education without holding the classification fixed, because the 2021 diploma band absorbs a qualification type that did not exist in 2016. Household composition indicates whether a family is present or not and whether or not other unrelated household members are present.\" It is coarser than HCFMD, which counts the family types inside a family household. The 2016 wording is unchanged from 2011: the variable \"describes the type of household within a dwelling. Household composition indicates whether a family is present or not and whether or not other unrelated household members are present.\" Because the categories are stable across 2011, 2016 and 2021, a transition table built from HHCD_P_11 and HHCD_P_16 is comparing like with like. HCFMD_P_16 on the same row gives the finer family breakdown.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Household Composition (HHCD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter35002016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Household Composition of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 household composition code (HHCD)","def":"A one- or two-digit code covering one family, multiple family, non-family and non-classifiable households, with a not-applicable code for unoccupied private dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory or offshore areas.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Household Composition (HHCD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter35002016","lim":"It cannot identify people living in non-private dwellings, which fall entirely into the not-applicable code. A person in a nursing home, a prison or student accommodation at one Census and a private dwelling at the next will show a transition that is an artefact of scope rather than a change of household type.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":91},{"n":"HHCD_P_21","d":"The type of household the person was enumerated in at the 2021 Census.","full":"The type of household the person was enumerated in at the 2021 Census. The ABS 2021 wording is \"This variable describes the type of household within a dwelling. It indicates if a family is present on Census Night and if other unrelated household members are present.\" The dictionary records that no changes were made for 2021, so the codes match HHCD_P_16 and HHCD_P_11 exactly. It applies to occupied private dwellings only.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Household composition (HHCD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/household-composition-hhcd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Household Composition of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 household composition code (HHCD)","def":"A one- or two-digit code: 1 one family household (11 family members only, 12 with non-family members), 2 multiple family household (21 two family, 22 three or more), 3 non-family household (31 lone person, 32 group), 4 non-classifiable (41 visitors only, 42 other).","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Household composition (HHCD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/household-composition-hhcd","lim":"A large block of households is labelled rather than measured. The ABS reports that the 'Other non-classifiable' category consists mainly of occupied dwellings where a form was not received, 3.8% of all occupied private dwellings in 2021, so a person can shift household code between ACLD waves because a form went missing at one Census and not because their living arrangements changed.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":91},{"n":"HIDD_P_11","d":"A quality flag for the 2011 household income figures on the same row, saying why they can or cannot be trusted.","full":"A quality flag for the 2011 household income figures on the same row, saying why they can or cannot be trusted. The 2011 dictionary describes HIDD as a variable that \"Allows household income to be derived based on any of the following conditions\" and then crosses two conditions: whether any member aged 15 and over was temporarily absent, and whether all incomes were stated and whether any were negative. The ABS advises using it with total personal income to rebuild household income on different assumptions. The 2011 dictionary records that the codes were amended for the 2011 Census, so 2011 codes are not the same values as 2006.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Household Income Derivation Indicator (HIDD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Household Income Derivation Indicator of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 household income derivation indicator code (HIDD)","def":"A single-digit code 1 to 8: codes 1 to 4 where no member aged 15 and over was temporarily absent, codes 5 to 8 where one or more were, each pair splitting on whether all incomes were stated and whether any negative income was stated, plus @ for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Household Income Derivation Indicator (HIDD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It does not measure income and it does not say how large the gap is. A household with one absent member and one with four absent members share a code, so the flag identifies affected households without indicating how far HIND_P_11 falls short of the true total.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":92},{"n":"HIDD_P_16","d":"A quality flag for the 2016 household income figures on the same row.","full":"A quality flag for the 2016 household income figures on the same row. The ABS says the 2016 variable \"identifies households where people were temporarily absent, did not state their income, or stated a negative income\", and that it is a derived dwelling variable created during Census processing for use alongside total personal income. Its purpose is to let a user rebuild household income under different assumptions rather than accept the ABS default. Read it before comparing HIND_P_16 with HIND_P_11 or HIND_P_21.","dsrc":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. no. 2900.0), Household Income Derivation Indicator (HIDD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~HIDD%20Household%20Income%20Derivation%20Indicator~10119","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Household Income Derivation Indicator of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 household income derivation indicator code (HIDD)","def":"A single-digit code crossing two conditions, presence of members aged 15 and over on Census Night and income reporting status, with codes for all incomes stated, one or more not stated, and whether any negative income was reported, plus a not-applicable code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. no. 2900.0), Household Income Derivation Indicator (HIDD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~HIDD%20Household%20Income%20Derivation%20Indicator~10119","lim":"It flags the household, not the person. The ACLD row belongs to one member, and the flag can be triggered by a different member's non-response, so filtering on it removes complete respondents as well as incomplete ones.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":92},{"n":"HIDD_P_21","d":"A quality flag for the 2021 household income figures on the same row.","full":"A quality flag for the 2021 household income figures on the same row. The 2021 definition is that it \"identifies households where people were absent from the dwelling on Census Night, did not state their income, or stated a negative income\", and the dictionary records that no changes were made for 2021. That stability means HIDD_P_16 and HIDD_P_21 can be compared directly, which matters because household income comparability across ACLD waves usually turns on the same non-response conditions. It applies to occupied private dwellings.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Household income derivation indicator (HIDD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/household-income-derivation-indicator-hidd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Household Income Derivation Indicator of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 household income derivation indicator code (HIDD)","def":"Nine categories: codes 1 to 8 for occupied private dwellings, formed by crossing whether members aged 15 and over were present on Census Night with whether incomes were stated and whether any were negative, plus @ for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Household income derivation indicator (HIDD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/household-income-derivation-indicator-hidd","lim":"It cannot repair the income figure. Knowing that one member did not state income tells you the household total is understated but not by how much, and the ACLD carries no imputed replacement, so an analyst must either drop the household or model the missing amount.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":92},{"n":"HIED_P_11","d":"The 2011 household income of the person's household after adjusting for household size and composition.","full":"The 2011 household income of the person's household after adjusting for household size and composition. The ABS defines it as \"total household income adjusted by the application of an equivalence scale to facilitate comparison of income levels between households of differing size and composition. The 'modified OECD' equivalence scale is used.\" The 2011 dictionary records that the variable was renamed from Household Income - Equivalised (weekly) and that its categories were revised and some codes amended for 2011, so the 2011 bands do not line up with 2006. Children absent on Census Night are included in the equivalence factor while visitors are excluded, and HIED is not calculated for visitor-only households.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Equivalised Total Household Income (weekly) (HIED)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Equivalised Total Household Income (Weekly) of Household in Which Person as Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 equivalised total household income, weekly dollar range code (HIED)","def":"A two-digit code for a weekly dollar range of equivalised income, derived by summing the personal incomes of members aged 15 and over and dividing by an equivalence factor of 1 point for the first adult, 0.5 for each further person aged 15 and over and 0.3 for each child under 15.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Equivalised Total Household Income (weekly) (HIED)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It is a standardised figure, not money anyone received. For a household of more than one person the value is the income a lone person would need to reach the same standard of living, so it should never be reported as the household's actual weekly income, which is HIND_P_11.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":93},{"n":"HIED_P_16","d":"The 2016 household income of the person's household after adjusting for household size and composition.","full":"The 2016 household income of the person's household after adjusting for household size and composition. The ABS 2016 definition is that \"Equivalised Total Household Income is total household income adjusted by the application of an equivalence scale to facilitate comparison of income levels between households of differing size and composition\", using the modified OECD scale of 1 point for the first adult, 0.5 for each further person aged 15 and over and 0.3 for each child. The ABS also notes that for 2016 the categories for annual income dollar ranges were revised, so the 2016 bands differ from the 2011 ones on the same row. HIDD_P_16 says whether the underlying income was complete.","dsrc":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. no. 2900.0), Equivalised Total Household Income (HIED)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~HIED%20Equivalised%20Total%20Household%20Income%20(weekly)~10120","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Equivalised Total Household Income (Weekly) of Household in Which Person as Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 equivalised total household income, weekly dollar range code (HIED)","def":"A two-digit code for a weekly dollar range of equivalised income, with the annual equivalent shown in brackets in the ABS category labels, plus codes for partial income stated, all incomes not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. no. 2900.0), Equivalised Total Household Income (HIED)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~HIED%20Equivalised%20Total%20Household%20Income%20(weekly)~10120","lim":"It cannot be differenced against HIED_P_11 to get a real income change, because the dollar ranges were redrawn for 2016 and nominal incomes rose between the two Censuses. A household can move up a band without any change in its purchasing power.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":94},{"n":"HIED_P_21","d":"The 2021 household income of the person's household after adjusting for household size and composition.","full":"The 2021 household income of the person's household after adjusting for household size and composition. The ABS says \"Equivalised total household income is household income adjusted by the application of an equivalence scale to facilitate comparison of income levels between households of differing size and composition.\" For 2021 the top of the scale was split: the former '$3,000 or more' category became '$3,000-$3,499 ($156,000-$181,999)' and '$3,500 or more ($182,000 or more)', so the 2021 column has finer detail at the top than HIED_P_16. It applies to family, lone person and group households.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Equivalised total household income (weekly) (HIED)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/equivalised-total-household-income-weekly-hied","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Equivalised Total Household Income (Weekly) of Household in Which Person as Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 equivalised total household income, weekly dollar range code (HIED)","def":"Codes 01 to 16 for weekly equivalised income ranges from nil income to $3,500 or more, plus code 17 partial income stated, && all incomes not stated and @@ not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Equivalised total household income (weekly) (HIED)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/equivalised-total-household-income-weekly-hied","lim":"The top band is not a ceiling on income. Everything above $3,500 equivalised per week sits in one code, so this column cannot rank high-income households against each other and will flatten any measure of top-end inequality in the ACLD.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":95},{"n":"HINASD_P_11","d":"The 2011 weekly income of the person's household, added up from whatever incomes were actually reported.","full":"The 2011 weekly income of the person's household, added up from whatever incomes were actually reported. The ABS explains the difference from HIND: \"The income ranges for Total Household Income as Stated (weekly) (HINASD) include households where one or more household members aged 15 years and over did not state their income, or were temporarily absent. In the variable Total Household Income (weekly) (HIND), these households would be excluded from the household income calculation.\" Income is collected in ranges, so a median dollar amount from the Survey of Income and Housing is allocated to each person before summing. The 2011 dictionary records that the variable was renamed and its dollar ranges revised for 2011.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Total Household Income as Stated (weekly) (HINASD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Household Income as Stated (Weekly) of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 total household income as stated, weekly dollar range code (HINASD)","def":"A two-digit code, 19 categories in 2011, running 01 negative income, 02 nil income, then weekly bands up to 17 '$5,000 or more ($260,000 or more)', with && all incomes not stated and @@ not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Total Household Income as Stated (weekly) (HINASD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It reads low for incomplete households rather than marking them. Because partially reported households are kept in the range distribution rather than set aside, a household with one non-responding member appears poorer than it is, and only HIDD_P_11 reveals which households those are.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":96},{"n":"HINASD_P_16","d":"The 2016 weekly income of the person's household, added up from whatever incomes were actually reported.","full":"The 2016 weekly income of the person's household, added up from whatever incomes were actually reported. The ABS defines it as \"The total weekly income of a private household based on the reported personal incomes of all members that are aged 15 years or older. It includes households where only partial income details have been stated.\" That inclusion is the whole point of the column: HIND_P_16 sends the same households to a 'Partial income stated' code instead. The dollar ranges were redrawn between 2011 and 2016 and then held fixed for 2021, so HINASD_P_16 and HINASD_P_21 share a band structure that HINASD_P_11 does not.","dsrc":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. no. 2900.0), Total Household Income as Stated (weekly) (HINASD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~HINASD%20Total%20Household%20Income%20as%20Stated%20(weekly)~10121","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Household Income as Stated (Weekly) of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 total household income as stated, weekly dollar range code (HINASD)","def":"A two-digit code for a weekly dollar range with the annual equivalent in brackets, extending to $8,000 or more from 2016, plus codes for all incomes not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. no. 2900.0), Total Household Income as Stated (weekly) (HINASD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~HINASD%20Total%20Household%20Income%20as%20Stated%20(weekly)~10121","lim":"It is not the sum of what households earn. Personal income is collected in ranges and each respondent is assigned the median of their range before summing, so the household total is an estimate whose error grows with the number of earners.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":97},{"n":"HINASD_P_21","d":"The 2021 weekly income of the person's household, added up from whatever incomes were actually reported.","full":"The 2021 weekly income of the person's household, added up from whatever incomes were actually reported. The ABS says it \"provides the total weekly income of a private household based on the reported personal incomes of all members that are aged 15 years or older\", and unlike HIND_P_21 it retains households where a member did not report. The dictionary records that no changes were made to the household income categories for 2021, so the bands match HINASD_P_16 exactly and only nominal income growth separates them. It applies to occupied private dwellings.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total household income as stated (weekly) (HINASD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-household-income-stated-weekly-hinasd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Household Income as Stated (Weekly) of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 total household income as stated, weekly dollar range code (HINASD)","def":"Twenty-four categories spanning negative income and nil income through weekly bands to $8,000 or more ($416,000 or more), plus all incomes not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total household income as stated (weekly) (HINASD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-household-income-stated-weekly-hinasd","lim":"Unchanged bands do not mean comparable real income. Between 2016 and 2021 the categories were held fixed while wages and prices rose, so a household moving up a band across ACLD waves may be no better off, and any level comparison needs deflating.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":97},{"n":"HIND_P_11","d":"The 2011 weekly income of the person's household, calculated only where every member aged 15 and over reported.","full":"The 2011 weekly income of the person's household, calculated only where every member aged 15 and over reported. The ABS is explicit about the exclusion: \"Household income is not calculated where a household member aged 15 years and over did not state their income, or was temporarily absent. These households are coded to the 'Partial income stated' category.\" Incomes are collected in ranges, so a median value from the Survey of Income and Housing is allocated to each person before summing. The 2011 dictionary records that the variable was renamed from Household Income (weekly) and its dollar ranges revised for 2011.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Total Household Income (weekly) (HIND)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Household Income (Weekly) of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 total household income, weekly dollar range code (HIND)","def":"A two-digit code for a weekly dollar range, from 01 negative income and 02 nil income up to '$5,000 or more ($260,000 or more)' in 2011, plus a partial income stated code, all incomes not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. no. 2901.0), Total Household Income (weekly) (HIND)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"It is missing not at random. Households with an absent or non-responding member are pushed into 'Partial income stated', and those households differ systematically from the rest, so restricting an ACLD analysis to complete HIND_P_11 values is a selection, not a clean sample.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":80},{"n":"HIND_P_16","d":"The 2016 weekly income of the person's household, calculated only where every member aged 15 and over reported.","full":"The 2016 weekly income of the person's household, calculated only where every member aged 15 and over reported. The ABS 2016 definition is that it is \"Calculated by summing the personal incomes reported by all household members aged 15 years and over\", after a median dollar amount from the Survey of Income and Housing is allocated to each person's reported range. The dollar bands were redrawn between 2011 and 2016, with the top category rising from $5,000 or more per week to $8,000 or more, so HIND_P_11 and HIND_P_16 are not on the same scale. HIDD_P_16 tells you which households were excluded.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Total Household Income (weekly) (HIND)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4902016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Household Income (Weekly) of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 total household income, weekly dollar range code (HIND)","def":"A two-digit code for a weekly dollar range with the annual equivalent in brackets, running to $8,000 or more ($416,000 or more), plus partial income stated, all incomes not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Total Household Income (weekly) (HIND)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter4902016","lim":"It cannot be treated as a continuous dollar figure. Each household sits in a band built from banded personal incomes, so a mean computed from band midpoints inherits two layers of approximation and will be wrong for households with several earners.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":98},{"n":"HIND_P_21","d":"The 2021 weekly income of the person's household, calculated only where every member aged 15 and over reported.","full":"The 2021 weekly income of the person's household, calculated only where every member aged 15 and over reported. The ABS defines it as \"the sum of Total personal income (weekly) (INCP) of each resident aged 15 years or older who was present in the household on Census Night\", with median incomes from the Survey of Income and Housing standing in for each reported range. No changes were made to the household income categories for 2021, so HIND_P_16 and HIND_P_21 share a band structure. HINASD_P_21 is the version that keeps partially reporting households.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total household income (weekly) (HIND)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-household-income-weekly-hind","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Household Income (Weekly) of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 total household income, weekly dollar range code (HIND)","def":"Twenty-five categories from negative income through nil income and weekly bands to $8,000 or more ($416,000 or more), plus partial income stated and all incomes not stated, and not applicable for non-private, unoccupied and non-classifiable dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total household income (weekly) (HIND)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-household-income-weekly-hind","lim":"It counts only residents present on Census Night, so a household with a member away for work or study is coded to partial income stated rather than measured. That makes the column weakest exactly for the mobile households an ACLD user is most likely to be following.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":98},{"n":"HLTHP_P_21","d":"Whether the person reported at least one long-term health condition at the 2021 Census.","full":"Whether the person reported at least one long-term health condition at the 2021 Census. The ABS says it \"identifies the population who has at least one long-term health condition (including any other long-term health conditions) and the population who reported they did not have a long-term health condition.\" The long-term health condition question was new in the 2021 Census, which is why this column has no 2011 or 2016 counterpart in the ACLD and why it cannot support any within-person change over the earlier waves. It summarises a single Census question listing ten named conditions, from arthritis and asthma to mental health condition and stroke, plus an 'any other long-term health condition(s)' option.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has one or more long-term health condition(s) (HLTHP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-one-or-more-long-term-health-conditions-hlthp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Whether Has One or More Long-term Health Condition(s)","k":"Census 2021 long-term health condition indicator code (HLTHP)","def":"A three-character code: 121 does not have a long-term health condition, 122 has one or more long-term health condition(s), &&& not stated and VVV overseas visitor. It applies to all persons.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has one or more long-term health condition(s) (HLTHP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-one-or-more-long-term-health-conditions-hlthp","lim":"It is self-reported and undiagnosed conditions are invisible. The question was also asked for the first time in 2021, so a positive value cannot be dated: it says the condition was present at the 2021 Census, not that it began after 2016, and any onset analysis using earlier ACLD waves is unsupported.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"HRSP_11","d":"The number of hours the person worked in the week before the 2011 Census, as a count rather than a band.","full":"The number of hours the person worked in the week before the 2011 Census, as a count rather than a band. The ABS defines HRSP in 2011 as a variable that \"records the number of hours worked in all jobs held during the week before Census Night, by employed people aged 15 years and over\". A separate banded variable, Hours Worked (ranges) (HRWRP), was new in the 2011 dictionary and is what standard Census products publish; the ACLD carries the continuous version. For Census purposes 35 hours or more in all jobs counts as full-time.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Hours Worked (HRSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter34702011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Hours Worked (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 hours worked, continuous whole hours (HRSP)","def":"A whole number of hours from 0 to 99 covering all jobs in the reference week, with separate codes for not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Hours Worked (HRSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter34702011","lim":"It measures one week, not usual hours. Leave, illness, school holidays and a short first week in a new job all show as low hours, so a change between ACLD waves can reflect the reference week rather than any change in the person's working arrangements.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":99},{"n":"HRSP_16","d":"The number of hours the person worked in the week before the 2016 Census, as a count rather than a band.","full":"The number of hours the person worked in the week before the 2016 Census, as a count rather than a band. The ABS 2016 definition is that it \"Indicates the number of hours worked by the employed person in all jobs during the week prior to Census night\", recorded from 0 to 99. The continuous form is stable across 2011, 2016 and 2021, so HRSP_11, HRSP_16 and HRSP_21 can be differenced directly, which the banded hours variables cannot. Only employed people aged 15 and over have a value.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Hours Worked (HRSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5002016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Hours Worked (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 hours worked, continuous whole hours (HRSP)","def":"A whole number of hours from 0 to 99 across all jobs in the reference week, with && not stated, @@ not applicable and VV overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Hours Worked (HRSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5002016","lim":"Zero and not applicable mean different things. A zero is an employed person who worked no hours in the reference week, while the not-applicable code covers the unemployed and people not in the labour force, so treating blanks as zero hours will mix non-employment into the hours distribution.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":99},{"n":"HRSP_21","d":"The number of hours the person worked in the week before the 2021 Census, as a count rather than a band.","full":"The number of hours the person worked in the week before the 2021 Census, as a count rather than a band. The ABS says it \"indicates the number of hours worked by the employed person in all jobs during the week prior to Census night\" and records that no changes were made for 2021. That stability matters because the banded companion variable HRWRP was re-cut for 2021 to align with the Standards for labour force statistics, 2018, while the continuous HRSP was not. The 2021 reference week fell during COVID-19 restrictions in parts of Australia.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (HRSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-hrsp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Hours Worked (Continuous)","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 hours worked, continuous whole hours (HRSP)","def":"A whole number of hours from 0 to 99 across all jobs in the reference week, with && not stated, @@ not applicable for people not employed or aged under 15, and VV overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (HRSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-hrsp","lim":"The 2021 reference week is not a normal week everywhere. Lockdowns and stand-downs in some states depressed hours worked without any change in employment status, so a fall from HRSP_16 to HRSP_21 in the ACLD cannot be read as a labour supply change without accounting for where the person lived.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":99},{"n":"HRWF_P_11","d":"The combined hours worked by everyone employed in the person's family at the 2011 Census, reported in bands.","full":"The combined hours worked by everyone employed in the person's family at the 2011 Census, reported in bands. It rolls up the person-level hours worked measure, which counts hours in all jobs during the week before Census Night, over the family the person was enumerated in. The banded person-level variable HRWRP was itself new in the 2011 Census Dictionary, so 2011 is the first ACLD wave at which a family hours band is available. HRWH_P_11 is the same measure taken over the whole household.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Hours Worked (Ranges) in All Jobs by All Employed Persons in Family","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A code for a band of total weekly hours worked across all employed family members, with separate codes for families with no employed members and for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","lim":"It cannot distinguish one full-time worker from two part-time workers. A family total of 40 hours can be one person at 40 or two at 20, so this column is unusable for questions about work intensity per person, which need HRSP_11 on the individual rows.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":100},{"n":"HRWF_P_16","d":"The combined hours worked by everyone employed in the person's family at the 2016 Census, reported in bands.","full":"The combined hours worked by everyone employed in the person's family at the 2016 Census, reported in bands. It aggregates hours worked in all jobs in the week before Census Night across employed family members aged 15 and over. The banding of the underlying person-level variable was unchanged between 2011 and 2016 but was re-cut for 2021 to align with the Standards for labour force statistics, 2018, so HRWF_P_11 and HRWF_P_16 sit on a common scale that HRWF_P_21 may not share. HRWH_P_16 covers the household instead of the family.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Hours Worked (Ranges) in All Jobs by All Employed Persons in Family","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A code for a band of total weekly hours worked across all employed family members, with codes for no employed family members and for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","lim":"It does not identify who works. A family band cannot say whether the ACLD respondent is one of the employed members, so it must not be used as a labour force measure for the person on the row.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":100},{"n":"HRWF_P_21","d":"The combined hours worked by everyone employed in the person's family at the 2021 Census, reported in bands.","full":"The combined hours worked by everyone employed in the person's family at the 2021 Census, reported in bands. The person-level banded variable it builds on had its categories redrawn for 2021, which the ABS states plainly: \"For 2021, the output categories (ranges) for this variable have been updated to align with the Standards for labour force statistics, 2018.\" The 2021 reference week also fell during COVID-19 restrictions in several states, which cut hours without changing employment. HRWH_P_21 gives the household equivalent.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Hours Worked (Ranges) in All Jobs by All Employed Persons in Family","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A code for a band of total weekly hours worked across all employed family members, drawing on the 2021 person-level ranges of 0, 1-9, 10-19, 20-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-59, 60-69 and 70 or more hours.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","lim":"It cannot be compared band for band with HRWF_P_16, because the underlying ranges were re-cut for 2021 and more categories were added. A family that appears to shift bands between waves may only have been reclassified.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":100},{"n":"HRWH_P_11","d":"The combined hours worked by everyone employed in the person's household at the 2011 Census, reported in bands.","full":"The combined hours worked by everyone employed in the person's household at the 2011 Census, reported in bands. It differs from the family version HRWF_P_11 by counting unrelated residents such as boarders and flatmates as well as family members. The person-level banded hours variable HRWRP was new in the 2011 Census Dictionary, so 2011 is the earliest ACLD wave with a household hours band. Household membership is fixed at Census Night, so people temporarily away do not contribute.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Hours Worked (Ranges) in All Jobs by All Employed Persons in Household","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A code for a band of total weekly hours worked across all employed household members aged 15 and over, with codes for households with no employed members and for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","lim":"It rises with household size, not with effort. A group household of five part-time workers records more hours than a couple both working full-time, so the band cannot be read as a measure of how hard the household works without dividing by the number of adults.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":100},{"n":"HRWH_P_16","d":"The combined hours worked by everyone employed in the person's household at the 2016 Census, reported in bands.","full":"The combined hours worked by everyone employed in the person's household at the 2016 Census, reported in bands. It counts hours in all jobs in the week before Census Night across every employed resident, related or not, which is what separates it from HRWF_P_16. The underlying banded ranges were the same in 2011 and 2016 but were redrawn for 2021, so the 2011 and 2016 household bands are the pair that can be compared safely. Non-private dwellings are outside the household scope entirely.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Hours Worked (Ranges) in All Jobs by All Employed Persons in Household","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A code for a band of total weekly hours worked across all employed household members aged 15 and over, with codes for no employed members and for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","lim":"A low band does not mean a low-income household. Retired and self-funded households record few or no hours while still having substantial income, so this column should not stand in for household economic resources, which HIND_P_16 and HIED_P_16 measure directly.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":100},{"n":"HRWH_P_21","d":"The combined hours worked by everyone employed in the person's household at the 2021 Census, reported in bands.","full":"The combined hours worked by everyone employed in the person's household at the 2021 Census, reported in bands. The person-level ranges behind it were re-cut for 2021 to align with the Standards for labour force statistics, 2018, adding categories that did not exist in 2016. The 2021 Census reference week also coincided with COVID-19 restrictions in parts of Australia, so household hours fell in some places without any change in who was employed. HRWF_P_21 restricts the same measure to the person's family.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Number of Hours Worked (Ranges) in All Jobs by All Employed Persons in Household","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A code for a band of total weekly hours worked across all employed household members, drawing on the 2021 person-level ranges of 0, 1-9, 10-19, 20-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-59, 60-69 and 70 or more hours.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","lim":"It cannot be differenced against HRWH_P_16 to measure a change in household work. The band boundaries moved for 2021 and the reference week was disrupted, so both the scale and the level shifted at the same time and the two effects cannot be separated from this column alone.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":100},{"n":"HRWRP_11","d":"Banded hours worked in all jobs in the week before the 2011 Census, for employed people aged 15 and over.","full":"Banded hours worked in all jobs in the week before the 2011 Census, for employed people aged 15 and over. The 2011 Census Dictionary says the variable \"Indicates the number of hours worked in ranges by the employed person in all jobs during the week prior to Census Night\", and the ranges variable was first introduced for the 2011 Census; the exact hour count, collected at earlier Censuses as well, is kept separately as HRSP. On the ABS Census definition a person working 35 hours or more is full-time, so the full-time boundary falls at the start of the 35 to 39 band rather than between two bands.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Hours Worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5102011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Hours Worked (Ranges)","t":"categorical","k":"Census hours worked, eight ranges","def":"A single-digit code: 0 none, 1 for 1 to 15 hours, 2 for 16 to 24, 3 for 25 to 34, 4 for 35 to 39, 5 for exactly 40, 6 for 41 to 48, and 7 for 49 hours and over. The ACLD adds 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Hours Worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5102011","lim":"It measures one reference week, so it cannot stand for usual hours: leave, illness or a burst of overtime in early August 2011 moves a person between bands without any change in their job. A 0 here is an employed person who worked no hours that week, not a person out of work, and 98 bundles the unemployed, people not in the labour force, people whose labour force status was not stated and everyone under 15 into one code.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":101},{"n":"HRWRP_16","d":"The same banded hours-worked measure taken at the 2016 Census, for employed people aged 15 and over.","full":"The same banded hours-worked measure taken at the 2016 Census, for employed people aged 15 and over. The 2016 Census Dictionary repeats the 2011 wording, that the variable \"Indicates the number of hours worked in ranges by the employed person in all jobs during the week prior to Census night\", and lists the identical eight bands, so a move between HRWRP_11 and HRWRP_16 is a real change in hours rather than a change in how the ABS grouped them. The exact hour count for 2016 sits in HRSP_16, and LFHRP_16 is where an employed person with hours not stated can still be identified.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Hours Worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5102016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Hours Worked (Ranges)","t":"categorical","k":"Census hours worked, eight ranges","def":"A single-digit code: 0 none, 1 for 1 to 15 hours, 2 for 16 to 24, 3 for 25 to 34, 4 for 35 to 39, 5 for exactly 40, 6 for 41 to 48, and 7 for 49 hours and over. The ACLD adds 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Hours Worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5102016","lim":"The band boundaries hide movements that matter: a person going from 25 hours to 34 hours stays in band 3, while one hour more takes them to band 4 and across the ABS full-time line. The 2021 Census Dictionary warns that \"For 2021, the output categories (ranges) for this variable have been updated to align with the Standards for labour force statistics, 2018. There are now more categories available\", but the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list still publishes the older eight-band set for 2021, so the finer 2021 ranges are not available in this file. The same page reports that \"The non-response rate for Hours worked (HRSP) was 1.7% in 2021\", which is the underlying variable these bands are cut from.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Hours Worked (Ranges)","t":"categorical","k":"Census hours worked, eight ranges","def":"A single-digit code: 0 none, 1 for 1 to 15 hours, 2 for 16 to 24, 3 for 25 to 34, 4 for 35 to 39, 5 for exactly 40, 6 for 41 to 48, and 7 for 49 hours and over. The ACLD adds 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Hours worked (ranges) (HRWRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/hours-worked-ranges-hrwrp","lim":"A reader coming from standard 2021 Census products will expect the eleven finer ranges published there and will not find them here, so counts built from this column cannot be reconciled row for row with a 2021 TableBuilder table on the same variable. It applies only to people whose relationship in household is a child under 15, a dependent student or a non-dependent child, which is why it is empty for most adults.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Female Parent Related Data Items","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Hours Worked (Ranges) by Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census hours worked, eight ranges","def":"A single-digit code: 0 none, 1 for 1 to 15 hours, 2 for 16 to 24, 3 for 25 to 34, 4 for 35 to 39, 5 for exactly 40, 6 for 41 to 48, and 7 for 49 hours and over, plus 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Female Parent Related Data Items","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"A 98 cannot be read as the mother not working. From 2016 the file also carries EETP_FP, which reports whether the female parent was engaged in work or study at all.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Female Parent Related Data Items","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Hours Worked (Ranges) by Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census hours worked, eight ranges","def":"A single-digit code: 0 none, 1 for 1 to 15 hours, 2 for 16 to 24, 3 for 25 to 34, 4 for 35 to 39, 5 for exactly 40, 6 for 41 to 48, and 7 for 49 hours and over, plus 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 detailed microdata data item list, Female Parent Related Data Items","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"The column follows the sampled child, not the mother, so a change between 2011 and 2016 can mean the child moved household or aged out of the child relationship categories rather than that the mother's hours changed. The ACLD supplies Indigenous Regions and Indigenous Areas only; Indigenous Locations, the finest level of the Indigenous Structure, are not released on the ACLD.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 to June 2026, Indigenous Structure","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/indigenous-structure","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indigenous Areas (Usual Residence)","k":"ASGS Indigenous Area code, six digits","def":"A six-digit Indigenous Area code from the ASGS Indigenous Structure, with 9999999 reserved for an unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 to June 2026, Indigenous Structure","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/indigenous-structure","lim":"It is a place, not a person: everyone with a usual address inside an Indigenous Area carries the code, whether or not they are Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander, so it is no substitute for INGP_21. Indigenous Structure boundaries are also rebuilt for each ASGS edition, so a 2021 code cannot be matched to the 2011 or 2016 column without a concordance.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"IEO_UR_11","d":"The SEIFA Index of Education and Occupation decile of the area where the sampled person usually lived, from the 2011 Census.","full":"The SEIFA Index of Education and Occupation decile of the area where the sampled person usually lived, from the 2011 Census. The ABS says the index \"is designed to reflect the educational and occupational level of communities\", using qualifications and current study together with ANZSCO occupation groups and unemployment, and notes that \"This index does not include any income variables\", which is what separates it from IER and IRSAD. The ACLD carries IEO for 2011 and 2016 only; the 2011-2016-2021 data item list has no IEO column under a 2021 name.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA), Australia, 2011, IEO","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2033.0.55.001main+features100072011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Index of Education and Occupation","t":"categorical","k":"SEIFA decile, 1 to 10","def":"A whole number 1 to 10, decile 1 the most disadvantaged and decile 10 the least, with 0 for an area that has no SEIFA score and 999 for an unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA), Australia, 2011, IEO","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2033.0.55.001main+features100072011","lim":"It describes an area, not the person on the row, so using it as a personal measure of education or occupation is an ecological inference; the person's own schooling is in HSCP_11 and their occupation in OCCP_11. The ABS also advises against comparing SEIFA scores over time, so a decile move between 2011 and 2016 is not evidence that an area changed.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":104},{"n":"IEO_UR_16","d":"The SEIFA Index of Education and Occupation decile of the area where the sampled person usually lived, from the 2016 Census.","full":"The SEIFA Index of Education and Occupation decile of the area where the sampled person usually lived, from the 2016 Census. The ABS repeats the 2011 definition, that the index \"is designed to reflect the educational and occupational level of communities\", with the occupation inputs classified to ANZSCO major groups and skill levels and no income variables included. This is the last wave for which the ACLD carries IEO: the 2011-2016-2021 data item list shows no IEO column for 2021, even though SEIFA 2021 publishes the index.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA), Australia, 2016, IEO","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2033.0.55.001~2016~Main%20Features~IEO~22","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Index of Education and Occupation","t":"categorical","k":"SEIFA decile, 1 to 10","def":"A whole number 1 to 10, decile 1 the most disadvantaged and decile 10 the least, with 0 for an area that has no SEIFA score and 999 for an unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA), Australia, 2016, IEO","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2033.0.55.001~2016~Main%20Features~IEO~22","lim":"A decile is a rank within the 2016 distribution, so an area can hold decile 5 in both 2016 and 2011 while its absolute education and occupation profile has shifted, and the ABS recommends against reading movement between releases as change. Areas with too few people to score are coded 0 rather than left empty.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":104},{"n":"IEO_UR_21","d":"Index of Education and Occupation","vp":"official","od":"Index of Education and Occupation","k":"seifa_index_of_education_and_occupation_decile","def":"The source publishes this value domain.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset 2016-21 detailed microdata data item list, codeframe ACLD119 ('Geographical Areas' sheet)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202016_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"The source defines the value domain. Frequency information is not included.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":104},{"n":"IER_UR_11","d":"The SEIFA Index of Economic Resources decile of the area where the sampled person usually lived, from the 2011 Census.","full":"The SEIFA Index of Economic Resources decile of the area where the sampled person usually lived, from the 2011 Census. The ABS defines it as an index that \"focuses on the financial aspects of relative socio-economic advantage and disadvantage, by summarising variables related to income and wealth\", and notes that it \"excludes education and occupation variables because they are not direct measures of economic resources\" and misses assets such as savings and equities \"because this information was not collected in the 2011 Census\". IEO_UR_11 is the companion index built from education and occupation instead.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA), Australia, 2011, IER","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2033.0.55.001main+features100062011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Index of Economic Resources","t":"categorical","k":"SEIFA decile, 1 to 10","def":"A whole number 1 to 10, decile 1 the most disadvantaged and decile 10 the most advantaged, with 0 for an area that has no SEIFA score and 999 for an unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA), Australia, 2011, IER","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2033.0.55.001main+features100062011","lim":"It measures both ends of the distribution at once, so a low decile cannot be read as a measure of disadvantage on its own; IRSD is the index built only from disadvantage indicators.
