It also cannot be used alongside household income from the same file without double counting, because income is one of its inputs.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":105},{"n":"IER_UR_16","d":"The SEIFA Index of Economic Resources decile of the area where the sampled person usually lived, from the 2016 Census.","full":"The SEIFA Index of Economic Resources decile of the area where the sampled person usually lived, from the 2016 Census. The ABS keeps the 2011 wording, that the index \"focuses on the financial aspects of relative socio-economic advantage and disadvantage, by summarising variables related to income and wealth\", with savings and equities again absent because they were \"not collected in the 2016 Census\". Unlike IEO, IER is carried in the ACLD for all three waves, so 2016 sits between IER_UR_11 and IER_UR_21.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA), Australia, 2016, IER","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2033.0.55.001~2016~Main%20Features~IER~21","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Index of Economic Resources","t":"categorical","k":"SEIFA decile, 1 to 10","def":"A whole number 1 to 10, decile 1 the most disadvantaged and decile 10 the most advantaged, with 0 for an area that has no SEIFA score and 999 for an unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA), Australia, 2016, IER","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2033.0.55.001~2016~Main%20Features~IER~21","lim":"The deciles are recalculated from scratch for each release against that Census's own distribution, and area boundaries change between Censuses, so the same physical neighbourhood can shift decile without any change in its households.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":105},{"n":"IER_UR_21","d":"The SEIFA Index of Economic Resources decile of the area where the sampled person usually lived, from the 2021 Census.","full":"The SEIFA Index of Economic Resources decile of the area where the sampled person usually lived, from the 2021 Census. The 2021 release restates the index as one that \"focuses on the financial aspects of relative socio-economic advantage and disadvantage, by summarising variables related to income and housing\", where the 2011 and 2016 releases said income and wealth, and the indexes are constructed at Statistical Area Level 1 with larger areas taken as population-weighted averages of SA1 scores. It is the only one of the two SEIFA indexes in this slice that the ACLD carries for 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA), Australia, 2021","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/people-and-communities/socio-economic-indexes-areas-seifa-australia/2021","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Index of Economic Resources","t":"categorical","k":"SEIFA decile, 1 to 10","def":"A whole number 1 to 10, decile 1 the most disadvantaged and decile 10 the most advantaged, with 0 for an area that has no SEIFA score and 999 for an unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Socio-Economic Indexes for Areas (SEIFA), Australia, 2021","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/people-and-communities/socio-economic-indexes-areas-seifa-australia/2021","lim":"The 2021 inputs were collected during COVID-19, when incomes in many areas were supported by temporary payments, so the 2021 ranking reflects conditions in August 2021 rather than a settled state. The ACLD data item list does not name the geography the decile is assigned at, so the level should be confirmed against the geography columns on the same row before assuming SA1.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":105},{"n":"IFAGEP_11","d":"Whether the sampled person's age at the 2011 Census was imputed rather than reported.","full":"Whether the sampled person's age at the 2011 Census was imputed rather than reported. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it in one line, that the variable \"Indicates if a person's age was imputed\", and applies it to all persons. The 2011 form allowed either age or date of birth; where neither was given, the ABS imputed age from other information on the form and from the population age distribution, so AGEP_11 on the same row is a modelled value wherever this flag is 2.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Imputation Flag for Age (IFAGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Age","t":"categorical","k":"Imputation flag, imputed or not imputed","def":"A code 1 age not imputed or 2 age imputed, with 99 for an unlinked record; there is no not-applicable code, because the flag applies to every person.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Imputation Flag for Age (IFAGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5302011","lim":"It says that age was imputed, not how far the imputed value might be from the truth, and it carries no uncertainty measure. It also cannot explain an age that moves oddly between waves; the CFAGEP_11_16 consistency flag is the column that measures that.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":106},{"n":"IFAGEP_16","d":"Whether the sampled person's age at the 2016 Census was imputed rather than reported.","full":"Whether the sampled person's age at the 2016 Census was imputed rather than reported. The 2016 Census Dictionary keeps the 2011 wording, that the variable \"Indicates if a person's age was imputed\", applied to all persons, so the flag means the same thing in both waves. The 2021 Census Dictionary entry for the same variable puts the 2016 non-response rate for age at 5.6 per cent, which is the share of 2016 records this flag marks as imputed.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Imputation Flag for Age (IFAGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Age","t":"categorical","k":"Imputation flag, imputed or not imputed","def":"A code 1 age not imputed or 2 age imputed, with 99 for an unlinked record; there is no not-applicable code, because the flag applies to every person.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Imputation Flag for Age (IFAGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5302016","lim":"Age is imputed independently at each Census, so a person can be flagged in 2016 and not in 2011 without anything about them having changed, and filtering the panel to unimputed records in every wave removes a different, non-random group each time.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":106},{"n":"IFAGEP_21","d":"Whether the sampled person's age at the 2021 Census was imputed rather than reported.","full":"Whether the sampled person's age at the 2021 Census was imputed rather than reported. The 2021 Census Dictionary expands the earlier one-line definition: the variable \"indicates if a person's age was imputed\", where \"Imputation is a statistical process for predicting values where no response was provided to a question and a response could not be derived\". Non-response for age was 4.4 per cent in 2021, down from 5.6 per cent in 2016, so the imputed share of the 2021 column is smaller than in either earlier wave.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for age (IFAGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/imputation-flag-age-ifagep","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Age","t":"categorical","k":"Imputation flag, imputed or not imputed","def":"A code 1 age not imputed or 2 age imputed, with 99 for an unlinked record; there is no not-applicable code, because the flag applies to every person.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for age (IFAGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/imputation-flag-age-ifagep","lim":"It flags age only. A record with a stated age can still have an imputed sex, place of usual residence, workplace or marital status, each of which has its own flag, so this column is not a general quality indicator for the person.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":106},{"n":"IFMSTP_11","d":"Whether the sampled person's registered marital status at the 2011 Census was imputed rather than reported.","full":"Whether the sampled person's registered marital status at the 2011 Census was imputed rather than reported. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as a variable that \"Indicates if a person's registered marital status was imputed\", applicable to persons aged 15 years and over. Where the flag is 2, MSTP_11 on the same row is a modelled value, and everyone under 15 is coded not applicable.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Imputation Flag for Registered Marital Status (IFMSTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5402011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Registered Marital Status","t":"categorical","k":"Imputation flag, imputed or not imputed","def":"A code 1 marital status not imputed or 2 marital status imputed, with 98 not applicable for people under 15 and 99 for an unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Imputation Flag for Registered Marital Status (IFMSTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5402011","lim":"It covers registered marital status only, not social marital status. MDCP is derived from relationships within the household, so a person with an imputed registered status can still have a directly observed de facto relationship, and the two measures disagree for reasons this flag does not explain.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":107},{"n":"IFMSTP_16","d":"Whether the sampled person's registered marital status at the 2016 Census was imputed rather than reported.","full":"Whether the sampled person's registered marital status at the 2016 Census was imputed rather than reported. The 2016 Census Dictionary keeps the 2011 wording, that the variable \"Indicates if a person's registered marital status was imputed\", but widens the applicable population: it now covers all responding persons aged 15 and over, all imputed persons in private dwellings, and imputed persons aged 15 and over in non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping areas. Non-response for registered marital status was 6.9 per cent in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Imputation Flag for Registered Marital Status (IFMSTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5402016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Registered Marital Status","t":"categorical","k":"Imputation flag, imputed or not imputed","def":"A code 1 marital status not imputed or 2 marital status imputed, with 98 not applicable for people under 15 and 99 for an unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Imputation Flag for Registered Marital Status (IFMSTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5402016","lim":"The 2016 population change means the count of records eligible for the flag is not the same as in 2011, so comparing the imputed share across the two waves compares slightly different denominators rather than a pure change in response quality.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":107},{"n":"IFMSTP_21","d":"Whether the sampled person's registered marital status at the 2021 Census was imputed rather than reported.","full":"Whether the sampled person's registered marital status at the 2021 Census was imputed rather than reported. The 2021 Census Dictionary defines it as a variable that \"indicates if a person's Registered marital status (MSTP) was imputed\", and reports non-response of 5.5 per cent in 2021, down from 6.9 per cent in 2016. Imputation is done by hotdecking, taking a donor record matched on sex, relationship in household, age and dwelling type and as geographically close as possible within the same capital city or balance of state.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for registered marital status (IFMSTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/imputation-flag-registered-marital-status-ifmstp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Registered Marital Status","t":"categorical","k":"Imputation flag, imputed or not imputed","def":"A code 1 marital status not imputed or 2 marital status imputed, with 98 not applicable for people under 15 and 99 for an unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for registered marital status (IFMSTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/imputation-flag-registered-marital-status-ifmstp","lim":"Because the donor is matched on age, sex, relationship and area, an imputed status looks plausible for the person and cannot be spotted from MSTP_21 itself, so any analysis of marital transitions between waves has to read this flag rather than assume the recorded status was reported.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":107},{"n":"IFNMFD_P_11","d":"Whether the people in this person's occupied private dwelling were counted or imputed at the 2011 Census.","full":"Whether the people in this person's occupied private dwelling were counted or imputed at the 2011 Census. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines the flag as one that \"Indicates whether the number of males and females could be established for an occupied private dwelling, or needed to be imputed\", and 2011 is the last Census with a middle category, because a collector could still obtain a count from a resident, a building manager or a neighbour when no form came back. The ACLD carries this dwelling attribute on the person record, so it describes the household the sampled person lived in rather than the answers that person gave.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Imputation Flag for Number of Males and Females in Dwelling (IFNMFD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Imputation Flag for Number of Males and Females in Dwelling","k":"Census 2011 dwelling imputation flag (3 categories)","def":"Three substantive codes in the ACLD: 1 not imputed with a form returned, 2 not imputed with no form but a count obtained by the collector, and 3 imputed with neither. 98 is not applicable, covering unoccupied private dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping areas, and 99 marks a record not linked to the 2011 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Imputation Flag for Number of Males and Females in Dwelling (IFNMFD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"Treating code 3 as the imputation rate and comparing it with 2016 overstates the increase, because the 2016 item folds the old codes 1 and 2 into a single not-imputed category. The flag also does not say which people in the dwelling were imputed or how many, and a person imputed into a dwelling still carries values for age, sex, registered marital status and usual residence that nobody reported.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"IFNMFD_P_16","d":"Whether people were imputed into this person's occupied private dwelling at the 2016 Census, on a two-way flag that replaced the 2011 three-way one.","full":"Whether people were imputed into this person's occupied private dwelling at the 2016 Census, on a two-way flag that replaced the 2011 three-way one. ABS states that \"categories for this item were changed for 2016 due to the changes in dwelling enumeration\": field officers no longer collected the number of males and females at non-responding dwellings, so imputation became the only option and the old collector-count category disappeared. ABS reports the number of males and females was imputed for 4.9% of occupied private dwellings in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), IFNMFD Imputation Flag for Number of Males and Females in Dwelling","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~IFNMFD%20Imputation%20Flag%20for%20Number%20of%20Males%20and%20Females%20in%20Dwelling~10124","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Imputation Flag for Number of Males and Females in Dwelling","k":"Census 2016 dwelling imputation flag (2 categories)","def":"Two substantive codes, 1 persons not imputed into dwelling and 2 persons imputed into dwelling, with 98 not applicable for unoccupied private dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping areas, and 99 for a record not linked to the 2016 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), IFNMFD Imputation Flag for Number of Males and Females in Dwelling","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~IFNMFD%20Imputation%20Flag%20for%20Number%20of%20Males%20and%20Females%20in%20Dwelling~10124","lim":"The 2016 code 1 is not the same population as the 2011 code 1, so a like-for-like series has to add the 2011 codes 1 and 2 together first. The flag is also not a form response rate: a dwelling can return a form and still leave individual items blank, and those blanks are picked up by the item-level flags rather than here.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"IFNMFD_P_21","d":"Whether people were imputed into this person's occupied private dwelling at the 2021 Census.","full":"Whether people were imputed into this person's occupied private dwelling at the 2021 Census. ABS defines it as a variable that \"indicates whether the number of males and females were counted for an occupied private dwelling or were imputed\", and the two categories are unchanged from 2016. When persons are imputed into a dwelling the ABS imputes sex, age, registered marital status and place of usual residence and sets every other variable to not stated or not applicable, which is why an imputed person's other 2021 columns look empty.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for number of males and females in dwelling (IFNMFD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/imputation-flag-number-males-and-females-dwelling-ifnmfd","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Imputation Flag for Number of Males and Females in Dwelling","k":"Census 2021 dwelling imputation flag (2 categories)","def":"Two substantive codes, 1 persons not imputed into dwelling and 2 persons imputed into dwelling, with 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record in the ACLD recode of the Census not-applicable symbol.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for number of males and females in dwelling (IFNMFD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/imputation-flag-number-males-and-females-dwelling-ifnmfd","lim":"It is a dwelling property attached to a person, so it does not say whether this individual's own answers were imputed; IFSEXP_21 and IFPURP_21 answer that for sex and usual residence. Nor is it a measure of 2021 field disruption, because a dwelling that responded late or online still counts as not imputed.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"IFPOWP_16","d":"Whether the workplace address a person gave for the week before the 2016 Census was imputed, and at what geographic level.","full":"Whether the workplace address a person gave for the week before the 2016 Census was imputed, and at what geographic level. ABS created the flag that year: \"The variable Imputation Flag for Place of Work (IFPOWP) has been introduced to identify the geographic level at which imputation was required.\" The ACLD data item list prints Not available in the 2011 column for that reason, so 2016 is the first wave at which workplace imputation can be identified at all. Workplace address is coded to a Destination Zone, and the five substantive codes rank how much of the address the respondent supplied.","dsrc":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), POWP Place of Work","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~POWP%20Place%20of%20Work~10069","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Workplace Address","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 workplace address imputation flag (5 levels)","def":"Codes 1 to 5 running from not imputed, through imputed with the SA2, the capital city or the state and territory stated, to imputed with nothing stated. 98 is not applicable for people who were not employed or were under 15, and 99 marks a record not linked to the 2016 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), POWP Place of Work","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~POWP%20Place%20of%20Work~10069","lim":"The flag grades the address, not the job. A record coded 1 can still put a worker in the wrong place, because home-based, mobile and multi-site workers are coded to whatever address was written on the form. There is also no 2011 counterpart, so a change in workplace geography quality between the first two ACLD waves cannot be measured.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":108},{"n":"IFPOWP_21","d":"Whether the workplace address a person gave for the week before the 2021 Census was imputed, and at what geographic level.","full":"Whether the workplace address a person gave for the week before the 2021 Census was imputed, and at what geographic level. ABS defines it as a variable that \"indicates if a person's place of work in the week before Census Night was imputed, and to what geographic level\", with the same five substantive codes as 2016. The place of work non-response rate rose to 11.1% in 2021 from 10.0% in 2016, and the 2021 Census added guidance for respondents whose usual workplace was affected by COVID-19 restrictions.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for place of work (IFPOWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/imputation-flag-place-work-ifpowp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Workplace Address","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 workplace address imputation flag (5 levels)","def":"Codes 1 to 5 ordered by how much of the workplace address survived, from not imputed to imputed with nothing stated, then 98 not applicable for people not employed at the 2021 Census and 99 for a record not linked to that Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for place of work (IFPOWP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/imputation-flag-place-work-ifpowp","lim":"A 2021 workplace is not a normal-year workplace. Sydney and Melbourne were in lockdown on Census night 2021 and many people answered with a home address, so a code of 1 is evidence that an address was complete, not that the person travelled there. The flag also cannot separate a workplace that moved from one that was reported differently.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":108},{"n":"IFPURP_11","d":"Whether the person's place of usual residence had to be imputed at the 2011 Census, and at which geographic level.","full":"Whether the person's place of usual residence had to be imputed at the 2011 Census, and at which geographic level. The 2011 Census Dictionary says the flag \"Provides information on the level of response a person provided to the 'place of usual residence' question\", and for 2011 the categories were rewritten onto the new SA1 and SA2 geography in place of the Collection District and Statistical Local Area wording used in 2006. The ACLD data item list still prints the older SLA and CD labels for all three waves, so ACLD code 2 should be read as the finest level imputed rather than literally as a Collection District.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Imputation Flag for Place of Usual Residence (IFPURP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Place of Usual Residence","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 usual residence imputation flag (geographic level)","def":"Five ordered codes in the ACLD, from 1 not imputed through to 5 with state or territory and every lower level imputed, plus 99 for a record not linked to the 2011 Census. The Census itself publishes four, because it merges the capital-city and state-only cases into one code. There is no not-applicable code, since the item applies to all persons.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Imputation Flag for Place of Usual Residence (IFPURP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Main%20Features802011/$FILE/2011%20Census%20Dictionary%2027102011.pdf","lim":"An imputed usual residence is still a usable geography, so people coded 2 to 5 sit inside SA1 and SA2 counts like anyone else; the flag marks them but does not exclude them. It also grades address completeness, not movement, so it must not be read beside PUR1P or PUR5P as evidence that a person did or did not move.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":109},{"n":"IFPURP_16","d":"Whether the person's place of usual residence had to be imputed at the 2016 Census, and at which geographic level.","full":"Whether the person's place of usual residence had to be imputed at the 2016 Census, and at which geographic level. ABS puts it as follows: \"The variable Imputation Flag for Place of Usual Residence (IFPURP) indicates if a person's place of usual residence was imputed in the Census, and to what level.\" The concept is unchanged from 2011 but the incidence is not: ABS reports the 2016 non-response rate for place of usual residence at 5.3% for SA2 and 5.4% for SA1, against 3.8% and 3.9% in 2011.","dsrc":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), place of usual residence (PURP, IFPURP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features100722016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Place of Usual Residence","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 usual residence imputation flag (geographic level)","def":"The same five ordered ACLD codes as the other waves, from 1 not imputed to 5 with every geographic level imputed, plus 99 unlinked record. The published Census categories run 01 to 04, because the capital-city and state-only cases share one code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), place of usual residence (PURP, IFPURP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features100722016","lim":"The rise in imputation between 2011 and 2016 reflects the move to a digital-first Census and lower form response, not a change in how well people knew their address, so using the flag as a quality weight across waves confounds the two. The flag also grades only what was written down, so a complete address that was out of date on Census night is coded as not imputed.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":109},{"n":"IFPURP_21","d":"Whether the person's place of usual residence had to be imputed at the 2021 Census, and at which geographic level.","full":"Whether the person's place of usual residence had to be imputed at the 2021 Census, and at which geographic level. ABS defines it as a variable that \"indicates if a person's place of usual residence was imputed in the Census, and to what geographic level\", and reports no change to the variable for 2021. Imputation fell back: the 2021 non-response rate for place of usual residence was 4.3% at SA2 and 4.4% at SA1, down from 5.4% and 5.5% in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for place of usual residence (IFPURP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/imputation-flag-place-usual-residence-ifpurp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Place of Usual Residence","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 usual residence imputation flag (geographic level)","def":"Five ordered ACLD codes from 1 not imputed to 5 with every level imputed, plus 99 unlinked record; the 2021 Census Dictionary publishes the same information as four categories coded 01 to 04 in SA1 and SA2 terms.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for place of usual residence (IFPURP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/imputation-flag-place-usual-residence-ifpurp","lim":"Because the ACLD prints the same SLA and Collection District labels for 2011, 2016 and 2021, the labels cannot be read as the geography actually imputed in 2021, which was SA1 and SA2. The flag is also silent about the addresses held at other waves, so it cannot decide which of two conflicting usual residences in a person's panel record to believe.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":109},{"n":"IFSEXP_16","d":"Whether the person's sex was imputed at the 2016 Census, the first Census for which this flag exists.","full":"Whether the person's sex was imputed at the 2016 Census, the first Census for which this flag exists. The 2016 Census Dictionary puts it plainly: \"The variable Imputation Flag for Sex (IFSEXP) is used to indicate if a person's sex has been imputed for the Census.\" The ACLD data item list prints Not available in the 2011 column for that reason, and ABS reports the 2016 non-response rate for sex, measured with this flag, at 5.8%.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Sex (SEXP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter52402016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Sex","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 sex imputation flag (2 categories)","def":"Two substantive codes, 1 sex not imputed and 2 sex imputed, with 99 for a record not linked to the 2016 Census. There is no not-applicable code, because a sex is output for every person counted.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Sex (SEXP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter52402016","lim":"A 5.8% imputation rate reads like a question people refused, but most of it comes from whole dwellings that returned no form and had their occupants created; IFNMFD_P_16 identifies those dwellings. The flag also cannot tell you whether an imputed sex is right, only that it was assigned.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":110},{"n":"IFSEXP_21","d":"Whether the person's binary sex was imputed at the 2021 Census.","full":"Whether the person's binary sex was imputed at the 2021 Census. ABS defines it as a variable that \"indicates if a person's binary sex was imputed\", unchanged from the 2016 version, and reports the non-response rate for sex falling to 4.7% in 2021 from 5.8% in 2016. With no 2011 column in the ACLD, this flag and IFSEXP_16 give a two-point series rather than a trend across the panel.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for sex (IFSEXP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/imputation-flag-sex-ifsexp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Sex","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 sex imputation flag (2 categories)","def":"Two substantive codes, 1 sex not imputed and 2 sex imputed, with 99 for a record not linked to the 2021 Census; every person counted receives one of the two substantive codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for sex (IFSEXP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/imputation-flag-sex-ifsexp","lim":"The 2021 wording is deliberate about binary sex, so the flag says nothing about how a non-binary answer to the sex question was handled, and it is not a statement about gender. It also does not record which imputation route produced the value, so code 2 cannot be split between people created inside a non-responding dwelling and people who left the question blank on a returned form.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":110},{"n":"INCP_11","d":"Total weekly personal income reported at the 2011 Census, in twelve ranges topping out at $2,000 or more a week.","full":"Total weekly personal income reported at the 2011 Census, in twelve ranges topping out at $2,000 or more a week. The ABS definition is that the variable \"Indicates the total income that the person usually receives each week. Equivalent annual amounts appear in brackets.\" 2011 is the Census at which ABS renamed the item from Individual Income to Total Personal Income and widened the dollar ranges in line with income growth, so the bottom band is $1 to $199 rather than the $1 to $149 used from 2016. Income covers wages, business and rental income net of expenses, investment income, superannuation and government payments before tax.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Personal Income (Weekly)","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 weekly personal income band (12 ranges)","def":"Codes 1 to 12: negative income, nil income, then ten dollar ranges from $1-$199 to $2,000 or more a week with the annual equivalent in brackets. 997 is not stated, 998 not applicable for people under 15, and 999 a record not linked to the 2011 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702011","lim":"It is a band, not an amount, so any mean or median depends on the midpoint you assume and the open top band has no midpoint at all. The bands are also nominal: a person in band 9 in 2011 and band 9 in 2016 has had a real income fall, and because the band edges moved the two years do not line up code for code.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":111},{"n":"INCP_16","d":"Total weekly personal income reported at the 2016 Census, in fifteen ranges topping out at $3,000 or more a week.","full":"Total weekly personal income reported at the 2016 Census, in fifteen ranges topping out at $3,000 or more a week. ABS defines the item as one that \"Indicates the total income that the person usually receives each week\", and 2016 is the Census at which the ranges were updated: the twelve 2011 bands become fifteen, with new cuts at $150, $500, $650, $1,750 and $3,000. The ranges are the mark boxes on the form, so the question people answered changed with them; the break between 2011 and 2016 is in what was asked, not only in how the answers were output.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Personal Income (Weekly)","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 weekly personal income band (15 ranges)","def":"Codes 1 to 15: negative income, nil income and thirteen dollar ranges from $1-$149 to $3,000 or more a week. 997 is not stated, 998 not applicable, and 999 a record not linked to the 2016 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702016","lim":"The 2016 bands cannot be mapped one to one onto 2011, because the 2011 band 3 of $1-$199 straddles the 2016 bands 3 and 4, so a person whose income did not change can appear to move. A transition analysis needs both years collapsed onto a coarse common grid, and even then the bands are in nominal dollars.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":112},{"n":"INCP_21","d":"Total weekly personal income reported at the 2021 Census, in sixteen ranges after the old top band was split.","full":"Total weekly personal income reported at the 2021 Census, in sixteen ranges after the old top band was split. ABS defines it as a variable that \"indicates the total income (in ranges) that a person usually receives each week\", asked of people aged 15 years and over. For 2021 the 2016 top category of $3,000 or more was split into $3,000-$3,499 and $3,500 or more; every band below $3,000 is unchanged, which makes 2016 to 2021 the one clean income comparison in this file once codes 15 and 16 are added back together.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total personal income (weekly) (INCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-personal-income-weekly-incp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Personal Income (Weekly)","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 weekly personal income band (16 ranges)","def":"Codes 1 to 16: negative income, nil income and fourteen dollar ranges from $1-$149 up to $3,500 or more a week, with the annual equivalent in brackets. 997 is not stated, 998 not applicable for people under 15, and 999 a record not linked to the 2021 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total personal income (weekly) (INCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-personal-income-weekly-incp","lim":"Census income is self-reported in ranges, and ABS warns it is not directly comparable with income from its own surveys or from administrative sources because scope, reference period and method differ. The column also cannot be decomposed: wages, business income, rent and government payments all sit in the one band, so a fall between waves cannot be attributed to a source.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":113},{"n":"INCP_FP_11","d":"The 2011 weekly income band of the sampled person's female parent, carried on the person's own record.","full":"The 2011 weekly income band of the sampled person's female parent, carried on the person's own record. The ACLD builds every family item at the person level, so this is the 2011 Census item INCP as reported by the female parent in the same family, defined by ABS as the variable that \"Indicates the total income that the person usually receives each week\". The bands are the twelve-category 2011 scale, the same one used by INCP_11.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Personal Income (Weekly) of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 weekly personal income band of the female parent","def":"The twelve 2011 income bands, 1 negative income to 12 $2,000 or more a week, with the ACLD supplementary codes 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. The male parent version of the same item uses 997, 998 and 999 instead.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702011","lim":"It is neither household income nor a mother's income in general. A female parent who was not counted in the dwelling, or a person who did not live with a parent, falls into not applicable, so the column goes missing by family structure rather than at random and cannot be treated as data missing by chance.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":114},{"n":"INCP_FP_16","d":"The 2016 weekly income band of the sampled person's female parent, on the revised fifteen-band scale introduced that year.","full":"The 2016 weekly income band of the sampled person's female parent, on the revised fifteen-band scale introduced that year. The underlying item is the 2016 Census INCP, which ABS defines as the variable that \"Indicates the total income that the person usually receives each week\", copied from the female parent in the same family onto the person's record. Because the ranges were recut in 2016, this column is not comparable band for band with INCP_FP_11.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Personal Income (Weekly) of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 weekly personal income band of the female parent","def":"The fifteen 2016 income bands, 1 negative income to 15 $3,000 or more a week, with the ACLD supplementary codes 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702016","lim":"The value moves when the family changes, not only when the parent's income does. A person who lived with a low-income mother in 2011 and with no parent in 2016 shows a drop to not applicable, so a difference between the two columns is a change in who they lived with at least as often as a change in income.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":115},{"n":"INCP_FP_21","d":"The 2021 weekly income band of the sampled person's female parent, on the sixteen-band scale.","full":"The 2021 weekly income band of the sampled person's female parent, on the sixteen-band scale. The underlying item is the 2021 Census INCP, which ABS defines as the variable that \"indicates the total income (in ranges) that a person usually receives each week\", with the old $3,000 or more category split into $3,000-$3,499 and $3,500 or more. The ACLD data item list also widens the supplementary codes for this column to three digits, unlike the two-digit codes printed for 2011 and 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total personal income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-personal-income-weekly-incp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Personal Income (Weekly) of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 weekly personal income band of the female parent","def":"The sixteen 2021 income bands, 1 negative income to 16 $3,500 or more a week, with 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total personal income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-personal-income-weekly-incp","lim":"Reading the three female parent income columns as one series needs the missing value codes handled per year, because they are 97, 98 and 99 in 2011 and 2016 but 997, 998 and 999 in 2021, and a single recode rule applied to all three will mislabel them. A parent's band is also only a household resource if the income was shared, and the ACLD records no transfers between family members.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":116},{"n":"INCP_MP_11","d":"The 2011 weekly income band of the sampled person's male parent, carried on the person's own record.","full":"The 2011 weekly income band of the sampled person's male parent, carried on the person's own record. It is the 2011 Census item INCP, which ABS defines as the variable that \"Indicates the total income that the person usually receives each week\", taken from the male parent enumerated in the same family. The twelve-band 2011 scale applies, so the top band is $2,000 or more a week.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Personal Income (Weekly) of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 weekly personal income band of the male parent","def":"The twelve 2011 income bands, 1 negative income to 12 $2,000 or more a week, with 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record throughout all three waves of this item.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702011","lim":"The male parent column is absent far more often than the female parent one, because sole parent families are mostly mother-headed, so a comparison of the two parents' bands is taken over a selected set of families rather than over all children. Absence is coded 98 and cannot be distinguished from a father who was present but did not answer, which is coded 97.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":111},{"n":"INCP_MP_16","d":"The 2016 weekly income band of the sampled person's male parent, on the fifteen-band scale introduced that year.","full":"The 2016 weekly income band of the sampled person's male parent, on the fifteen-band scale introduced that year. The item is the 2016 Census INCP, which ABS defines as the variable that \"Indicates the total income that the person usually receives each week\", copied from the male parent in the same family. The recut ranges mean the same code number carries a different dollar range from the one it carried in 2011.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Personal Income (Weekly) of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 weekly personal income band of the male parent","def":"The fifteen 2016 income bands, 1 negative income to 15 $3,000 or more a week, with 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702016","lim":"A parent's income band is attached to the child only while they live together, so this column empties out as the sampled person ages through the panel; by 2016 a person who was 15 in 2011 may simply have left home. Rising rates of not applicable across waves are therefore a life-course artefact, not a data quality problem.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":112},{"n":"INCP_MP_21","d":"The 2021 weekly income band of the sampled person's male parent, on the sixteen-band scale.","full":"The 2021 weekly income band of the sampled person's male parent, on the sixteen-band scale. It is the 2021 Census item INCP, which ABS defines as the variable that \"indicates the total income (in ranges) that a person usually receives each week\", taken from the male parent in the same family. Only the top of the scale changed from 2016, where $3,000 or more became $3,000-$3,499 and $3,500 or more.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total personal income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-personal-income-weekly-incp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Personal Income (Weekly) of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 weekly personal income band of the male parent","def":"The sixteen 2021 income bands, 1 negative income to 16 $3,500 or more a week, with 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total personal income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-personal-income-weekly-incp","lim":"The split top band matters more for fathers than for the population, because men are over-represented in the highest income category, so a 2016 to 2021 comparison that leaves codes 15 and 16 apart will show a spurious fall in the share of fathers at the top. The column also says nothing about whether the father was in paid work, which needs LFSP for the same year.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":116},{"n":"INCP_SP_11","d":"The 2011 weekly income band of the sampled person's spouse or partner, carried on the person's own record.","full":"The 2011 weekly income band of the sampled person's spouse or partner, carried on the person's own record. The item is the 2011 Census INCP, defined by ABS as the variable that \"Indicates the total income that the person usually receives each week\", read off the partner identified from the Census relationship questions in the same dwelling. The twelve-band 2011 scale applies, with a top band of $2,000 or more a week.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Personal Income (Weekly) of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 weekly personal income band of the spouse or partner","def":"The twelve 2011 income bands, 1 negative income to 12 $2,000 or more a week, with 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702011","lim":"A partner is only recognised if the couple were enumerated in the same dwelling on Census night, so people in living-apart-together relationships, fly-in fly-out couples and partners away that night all fall into not applicable. Adding this band to INCP_11 also does not give couple income, because both are bands and their sum is only defined up to the width of each.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":111},{"n":"INCP_SP_16","d":"The 2016 weekly income band of the sampled person's spouse or partner, on the fifteen-band scale introduced that year.","full":"The 2016 weekly income band of the sampled person's spouse or partner, on the fifteen-band scale introduced that year. The underlying item is the 2016 Census INCP, which ABS defines as the variable that \"Indicates the total income that the person usually receives each week\". The ACLD data item list prints two-digit supplementary codes for this 2016 column, where the 2011 and 2021 columns of the same item use three digits.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Personal Income (Weekly) of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 weekly personal income band of the spouse or partner","def":"The fifteen 2016 income bands, 1 negative income to 15 $3,000 or more a week, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Total Personal Income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter5702016","lim":"A change in this column between waves is usually a change of partner or of household, not a change in one person's earnings, and nothing in the ACLD identifies the partner, so the 2011 and 2016 values cannot be assumed to describe the same individual. The band scale also changed in 2016, so the code numbers themselves are not continuous with the 2011 column.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":112},{"n":"INCP_SP_21","d":"The 2021 weekly income band of the sampled person's spouse or partner, on the sixteen-band scale.","full":"The 2021 weekly income band of the sampled person's spouse or partner, on the sixteen-band scale. It is the 2021 Census item INCP, defined by ABS as the variable that \"indicates the total income (in ranges) that a person usually receives each week\", taken from the partner enumerated in the same dwelling. Only the top category differs from 2016, where $3,000 or more was split at $3,500.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total personal income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-personal-income-weekly-incp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Personal Income (Weekly) of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 weekly personal income band of the spouse or partner","def":"The sixteen 2021 income bands, 1 negative income to 16 $3,500 or more a week, with 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total personal income (weekly) (INCP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-personal-income-weekly-incp","lim":"The 2021 partner's band is a stated usual income, not the income of that week: ABS told people in lockdown to report their income as it was before the lockdown began, and a partner on the COVID-19 Disaster Payment records that payment like any other income. Supplementary codes also revert to three digits here after two digits in the 2016 column of the same item.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":116},{"n":"INDP_11","d":"The industry of the sampled person's main job at the 2011 Census, as a four-digit ANZSIC class.","full":"The industry of the sampled person's main job at the 2011 Census, as a four-digit ANZSIC class. ABS defines the item as one that \"describes the industries in which employed people aged 15 years and over work\", coded for 2011 to the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification (ANZSIC) 2006 (Revision 1.0). 2011 is also the Census at which the mnemonic changed from IND06P to INDP. The code comes from the description of the business and of the main goods produced or services provided, which in 2011 was still asked partly as a mark box, and the ABS warns that coding from a person's occupation instead gives a very different result.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Industry of Employment","k":"ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 1.0) four-digit industry class, 2011 Census","def":"A four-digit ANZSIC class code, with the ACLD supplementary codes 99997 not stated, 99998 not applicable for people who were not employed or were under 15, and 99999 for a record not linked to the 2011 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","lim":"Industry is the employer's activity, not the person's job: a payroll clerk at a mine is Mining, and a fitter employed by a labour hire firm is Administrative and Support Services. The column also covers the main job only, so a second job or self-employment alongside it is invisible.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"INDP_16","d":"The industry of the sampled person's main job at the 2016 Census, as a four-digit ANZSIC class.","full":"The industry of the sampled person's main job at the 2016 Census, as a four-digit ANZSIC class. ABS defines the item as one that \"describes the industries in which employed people aged 15 years and over work\", and 2016 is the wave at which two things changed: the classification moved to ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), and the industry question moved from a mark box list to a write-in backed by targeted supplementary questions in the online form for hard-to-code answers such as construction. The 2013 revision clarified and corrected the classification without adding or removing industries, so class-level comparability with 2011 is close.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Industry of Employment","k":"ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0) four-digit industry class, 2016 Census","def":"A four-digit ANZSIC class code drawn from 721 classes, with 99997 not stated, 99998 not applicable and 99999 for a record not linked to the 2016 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","lim":"The question change is a larger break than the classification change. The write-in plus supplementary questions pushed more answers into a codable class, so a fall in vague or unclassified industry answers between 2011 and 2016 is a collection artefact rather than a real change in where people worked.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"INDP_1DIG_11","d":"The ANZSIC division of the sampled person's main job at the 2011 Census, the one-digit level of INDP_11.","full":"The ANZSIC division of the sampled person's main job at the 2011 Census, the one-digit level of INDP_11. It is the four-digit ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 1.0) class collapsed to its division, giving nineteen industry divisions from Agriculture, Forestry and Fishing through to Other Services, plus a residual category for inadequately described answers. The ACLD data item list points to the 2011 Census Dictionary for the codes and spells them out only on the parent and spouse versions of the item, where they run 0 to 18 with 19 for inadequately described.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Industry of Employment (1dig)","k":"ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 1.0) industry division, 2011 Census","def":"A one-digit ANZSIC division code with a residual category for inadequately described answers, plus the ACLD supplementary codes 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","lim":"Division is too coarse for most industry questions. A move from a mine to a mining services contractor crosses from Mining to Administrative and Support Services, while a move between two quite different manufacturing industries does not change the code at all, so division transitions over- and under-count real industry change at the same time.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"INDP_1DIG_16","d":"The ANZSIC division of the sampled person's main job at the 2016 Census, the one-digit level of INDP_16.","full":"The ANZSIC division of the sampled person's main job at the 2016 Census, the one-digit level of INDP_16. The underlying class is coded to ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), the edition first used in 2016, and the division level collapses it to nineteen industry divisions plus a residual for inadequately described answers. Because the revision added and removed no industries, division totals are close to comparable with 2011 even though the underlying class codes were revised.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Industry of Employment (1dig)","k":"ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0) industry division, 2016 Census","def":"A one-digit ANZSIC division code with a residual category for inadequately described answers, plus 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 for a record not linked to the 2016 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","lim":"Division counts are still not a clean 2011 to 2016 series, because the 2016 write-in question changed which answers could be coded at all. The effect concentrates in the residual inadequately described category rather than spreading evenly, so a division-share table looks stable while the residual moves underneath it.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"INDP_1DIG_21","d":"The ANZSIC division of the sampled person's main job at the 2021 Census, the one-digit level of INDP_21.","full":"The ANZSIC division of the sampled person's main job at the 2021 Census, the one-digit level of INDP_21. ABS documents the one-digit level of the classification as twenty categories, being the nineteen industry divisions plus a residual, sitting above 106 subdivisions, 293 groups and 721 classes. The classification is ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), unchanged from 2016, so 2016 to 2021 is the cleanest division comparison in this file.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Industry of Employment (1dig)","k":"ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0) industry division, 2021 Census","def":"A one-digit ANZSIC division code with a residual category for inadequately described answers, plus 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 for a record not linked to the 2021 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","lim":"The 2021 divisions are shaped by when the Census was taken. People who were employed but away from work on Census night keep their industry code, so division totals through the 2021 lockdowns describe attachment to an industry rather than activity in it, and a division that shut down is not visible here.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"INDP_21","d":"The industry of the sampled person's main job at the 2021 Census, as a four-digit ANZSIC class.","full":"The industry of the sampled person's main job at the 2021 Census, as a four-digit ANZSIC class. ABS defines it as the variable that \"describes the industry of the main job held by the employed person in the week prior to Census night\", coded to ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), the same edition used in 2016. The 2021 non-response rate was 1.3%, up slightly from 1.2% in 2016, and the targeted supplementary questions were reworded rather than replaced.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Industry of Employment","k":"ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0) four-digit industry class, 2021 Census","def":"A four-digit ANZSIC class code drawn from 721 classes, which aggregate to 293 groups, 106 subdivisions and 20 one-digit categories, with 99997 not stated, 99998 not applicable and 99999 for a record not linked to the 2021 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","lim":"The reference week is the week before Census night 2021, when Sydney and Melbourne were locked down, so people stood down but still employed keep their industry while people who lost work drop out to not applicable. An industry distribution built from this column is therefore not the 2021 employment structure, and it cannot be compared with a normal-year survey estimate without that caveat.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"INDP_2DIG_11","d":"The ANZSIC subdivision of the sampled person's main job at the 2011 Census, the two-digit level of INDP_11.","full":"The ANZSIC subdivision of the sampled person's main job at the 2011 Census, the two-digit level of INDP_11. It is the four-digit ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 1.0) class truncated to its subdivision, the level between division and group, and it is provided so that industry can be analysed at a middle level without releasing the full class code. The same subdivision structure carries through 2016 and 2021, where the classification moves to Revision 2.0.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Industry of Employment (2dig)","k":"ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 1.0) industry subdivision, 2011 Census","def":"A two-digit ANZSIC subdivision code, plus the ACLD supplementary codes 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 for a record not linked to the 2011 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","lim":"The ACLD is a 5% sample, and ABS publishes 106 subdivisions, so a subdivision by state or by year cell is often too small to estimate and will be suppressed or unstable in a longitudinal table. Subdivision is a level for classifying, not for counting small populations.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"INDP_2DIG_16","d":"The ANZSIC subdivision of the sampled person's main job at the 2016 Census, the two-digit level of INDP_16.","full":"The ANZSIC subdivision of the sampled person's main job at the 2016 Census, the two-digit level of INDP_16. The class beneath it is coded to ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), first used in 2016, and the subdivision level groups those classes into the 106 categories the ABS publishes at this level. The revision corrected and clarified class definitions without adding or removing industries, so the subdivision frame itself is the same one used in 2011.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Industry of Employment (2dig)","k":"ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0) industry subdivision, 2016 Census","def":"A two-digit ANZSIC subdivision code, plus 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 for a record not linked to the 2016 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","lim":"A change of subdivision between waves is not evidence of a change of employer. The code comes from the respondent's own description of the business, so different wording at two Censuses can move the code with no change of job, and the 2016 shift to a write-in question makes that more likely between 2011 and 2016 than between 2016 and 2021.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"INDP_2DIG_21","d":"The ANZSIC subdivision of the sampled person's main job at the 2021 Census, the two-digit level of INDP_21.","full":"The ANZSIC subdivision of the sampled person's main job at the 2021 Census, the two-digit level of INDP_21. ABS documents the two-digit level as 106 categories, sitting between the 20 one-digit categories and the 293 groups, and 2021 uses the same ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0) edition as 2016. It is the level most industry analysis of the ACLD can actually support, because the class level is too fine for a 5% sample and the division level is too coarse.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Industry of Employment (2dig)","k":"ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0) industry subdivision, 2021 Census","def":"A two-digit ANZSIC subdivision code, plus 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 for a record not linked to the 2021 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","lim":"Do not derive the division by truncating this code. The ACLD publishes the division as a separate column, INDP_1DIG_21, numbered 0 to 19 rather than by the ANZSIC division letter, so the first digit of the subdivision code does not correspond to it.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"INDP_3DIG_11","d":"The ANZSIC group of the sampled person's main job at the 2011 Census, the three-digit level of INDP_11.","full":"The ANZSIC group of the sampled person's main job at the 2011 Census, the three-digit level of INDP_11. It is the ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 1.0) four-digit class collapsed one level, which is the finest industry detail most users of the ACLD will release. The 2011 wave is the first in this file, so there is no earlier group code to compare it with inside the 2011-2016-2021 dataset.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Industry of Employment (3dig)","k":"ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 1.0) industry group, 2011 Census","def":"A three-digit ANZSIC group code, plus the ACLD supplementary codes 9997 not stated, 9998 not applicable and 9999 for a record not linked to the 2011 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","lim":"In a 5% sample most of the ANZSIC groups have too few people to support an estimate, particularly once the table is cut by state or by age, so the level is there to classify a person rather than to count a population. Confidentiality rules will suppress many of the resulting cells before a rate can be formed.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"INDP_3DIG_16","d":"The ANZSIC group of the sampled person's main job at the 2016 Census, the three-digit level of INDP_16.","full":"The ANZSIC group of the sampled person's main job at the 2016 Census, the three-digit level of INDP_16. The class beneath it is coded to ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), and ABS states that the 2013 revision involved clarifications and corrections with no industries added or removed, so group totals should line up with 2011. Groups are the level at which the effect of the 2016 write-in question is easiest to see, because a vaguer answer is coded up to a broader category rather than left blank.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Industry of Employment (3dig)","k":"ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0) industry group, 2016 Census","def":"A three-digit ANZSIC group code, plus 9997 not stated, 9998 not applicable and 9999 for a record not linked to the 2016 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","lim":"Comparability at group level is close but not guaranteed. Revision 2.0 reassigned some activities between classes even though it created no new industries, so a transition matrix between the 2011 and 2016 group codes should be checked against the ANZSIC correspondence before any movement is called a real industry change.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"INDP_3DIG_21","d":"The ANZSIC group of the sampled person's main job at the 2021 Census, the three-digit level of INDP_21.","full":"The ANZSIC group of the sampled person's main job at the 2021 Census, the three-digit level of INDP_21. ABS documents the three-digit level as 293 categories, immediately above the 721 four-digit classes, and 2021 keeps the ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0) edition used in 2016. Group codes are stable between those two waves, so a 2016 to 2021 transition needs no concordance.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Industry of Employment (3dig)","k":"ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0) industry group, 2021 Census","def":"A three-digit ANZSIC group code drawn from 293 categories, plus 9997 not stated, 9998 not applicable and 9999 for a record not linked to the 2021 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","lim":"A group code says nothing about the size or the location of the employer. Workplace geography lives in the place of work columns, and IFPOWP_21 says whether that address was imputed, so an industry-by-region table built from this column alone places people where they live, not where they work.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"INDP_FP_11","d":"The industry division of the female parent's main job at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's record.","full":"The industry division of the female parent's main job at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's record. The underlying item is the 2011 Census INDP, which ABS defines as the variable that \"describes the industries in which employed people aged 15 years and over work\", coded to ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 1.0). The parent version is published at division level only, so it is a nineteen-way split rather than the four-digit class held for the person themselves.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Industry of Employment of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ANZSIC industry division of the female parent, 2011 Census","def":"Codes 0 to 18 for the ANZSIC divisions from Agriculture, Forestry and Fishing to Other Services, 19 for inadequately described, then 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 for a record not linked to the 2011 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","lim":"The parent's industry cannot be compared like for like with the person's own INDP_11, which is a four-digit class; the person's column has to be collapsed to division first, and even then the division numbering here is the ACLD's 0 to 19 rather than the ANZSIC letter.
