Code 19, inadequately described, is a real answer rather than a missing value and should not be dropped with 997 to 999.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":117},{"n":"INDP_FP_16","d":"The industry division of the female parent's main job at the 2016 Census, carried on the sampled person's record.","full":"The industry division of the female parent's main job at the 2016 Census, carried on the sampled person's record. The underlying item is the 2016 Census INDP, which ABS defines as the variable that \"describes the industries in which employed people aged 15 years and over work\", coded for the first time to ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0) and collected by write-in rather than mark box. Division labels and numbering are unchanged from the 2011 column of the same item.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Industry of Employment of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ANZSIC industry division of the female parent, 2016 Census","def":"Codes 0 to 18 for the ANZSIC divisions, 19 for inadequately described, and 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 for a record not linked to the 2016 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","lim":"A mother recorded in Health Care and Social Assistance in both 2011 and 2016 need not have kept the same job, and one who changes division need not have changed employer, because the division follows how the business was described on each form. The division categories are the same nineteen plus a residual used at the earlier waves.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Industry of Employment of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ANZSIC industry division of the female parent, 2021 Census","def":"Codes 0 to 18 for the ANZSIC divisions, 19 for inadequately described, and 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 for a record not linked to the 2021 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","lim":"Because the 2021 reference week fell during lockdowns, a mother stood down from Accommodation and Food Services still shows that division, so the column cannot be used to identify parents whose work stopped. It also carries no hours or earnings, so a division alone says nothing about how much the parent worked.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":117},{"n":"INDP_MP_11","d":"The industry division of the male parent's main job at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's record.","full":"The industry division of the male parent's main job at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's record. It is the 2011 Census item INDP, which ABS defines as the variable that \"describes the industries in which employed people aged 15 years and over work\", coded to ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 1.0) and published for parents at division level only. The 2011 wave is the earliest in this ACLD file, so it fixes the starting industry for any father-to-child analysis.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Industry of Employment of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ANZSIC industry division of the male parent, 2011 Census","def":"Codes 0 to 18 for the ANZSIC divisions, 19 for inadequately described, and 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 for a record not linked to the 2011 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","lim":"Fathers are missing from this column much more often than mothers are from the female parent column, because most sole parent families are mother-headed, so an intergenerational industry analysis built on it is conditioned on family type. The division categories match the 2011 and 2021 columns of the same item exactly.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Industry of Employment of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ANZSIC industry division of the male parent, 2016 Census","def":"Codes 0 to 18 for the ANZSIC divisions, 19 for inadequately described, and 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 for a record not linked to the 2016 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","lim":"The 2016 write-in question was introduced partly to fix vague answers such as construction, which is exactly where fathers concentrate, so a drop in the inadequately described category between 2011 and 2016 for male parents reflects better coding rather than a change of industry.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":117},{"n":"INDP_MP_21","d":"The industry division of the male parent's main job at the 2021 Census, carried on the sampled person's record.","full":"The industry division of the male parent's main job at the 2021 Census, carried on the sampled person's record. Because the classification did not change between 2016 and 2021, those two columns can be compared directly while 2011 sits on Revision 1.0.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Industry of Employment of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ANZSIC industry division of the male parent, 2021 Census","def":"Codes 0 to 18 for the ANZSIC divisions, 19 for inadequately described, and 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 for a record not linked to the 2021 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","lim":"By 2021 most people sampled in 2011 are old enough to have left home, so the not applicable share of this column is dominated by household composition rather than by fathers' employment. Any trend in the division distribution across the three waves is therefore taken over a shrinking and increasingly young subgroup.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":117},{"n":"INDP_SP_11","d":"The industry division of the spouse or partner's main job at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's record.","full":"The industry division of the spouse or partner's main job at the 2011 Census, carried on the sampled person's record. Partners are published at division level, not at the four-digit class held for the person themselves.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Industry of Employment of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"ANZSIC industry division of the spouse or partner, 2011 Census","def":"Codes 0 to 18 for the ANZSIC divisions, 19 for inadequately described, and 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 for a record not linked to the 2011 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302011","lim":"Not applicable covers both people without a partner and people whose partner was not employed, so the column cannot be used to measure how many partnered people had a working spouse. It is the 2016 Census INDP, which ABS defines as the variable that \"describes the industries in which employed people aged 15 years and over work\", coded to ANZSIC 2006 (Revision 2.0), the first Census to use that revision. The partner is whoever was recorded as the person's husband, wife or partner in the same dwelling on Census night.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Industry of Employment of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"ANZSIC industry division of the spouse or partner, 2016 Census","def":"Codes 0 to 18 for the ANZSIC divisions, 19 for inadequately described, and 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 for a record not linked to the 2016 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Industry of Employment (INDP), with the ACLD codes from the ACLD 2011-2016-2021 data item list","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37302016","lim":"Pairing this column with the person's own INDP_16 to study assortative matching requires the person's four-digit class to be collapsed to division first, and even then couples who were apart on Census night drop out. resident was an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander person.\" The ACLD labels it the Indigenous Dwelling Indicator and phrases the categories from the person's point of view, so code 1 reads as a person usually resident in a household with one or more Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander persons.","full":"Whether the sampled person usually lived in a household with at least one Aboriginal one usual resident was an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander person.\" The ACLD labels it the Indigenous Dwelling Indicator and phrases the categories from the person's point of view, so code 1 reads as a person usually resident in a household with one or more Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander persons.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Indigenous Household Indicator 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Indigenous Household Indicator ABS defines the 2016 item as one that \"Indicates households who have at least one person who identified as being Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander who is usually resident at that dwelling and was present on Census night\", and notes minor changes to the wording of the categories from 2011. It is derived from Indigenous status, the usual address indicator and household composition, and counts only people who were home on Census night.","dsrc":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), Indigenous household Indicator (INGDWTD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features101252016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Indigenous Dwelling Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 Indigenous household indicator (2 categories)","def":"Two substantive codes with the same ACLD labels as the 2011 column, 1 for a person usually resident in a household with one or more Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander persons and 2 for a person usually resident in other households, plus 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), Indigenous household Indicator (INGDWTD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features101252016","lim":"Because only usual residents present on Census night count, a household whose one Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander member was away that night is coded 2, so the indicator is sensitive to travel and to visitor-only households. Comparing 2011 with 2016 therefore mixes a change in household composition with a change in who happened to be home.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":118},{"n":"INGDWTD_P_21","d":"Whether the household this person usually lived in at the 2021 Census contained at least one Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander person.","full":"Whether the household this person usually lived in at the 2021 Census contained at least one Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander person. The ABS defines it as \"This variable indicates households which have at least one person who identified as being Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander\", counting only people who were usual residents and present on Census Night. It is a household attribute carried on the person record, so every usual resident of the dwelling gets the same code; ISPH_P_21 on the same row splits the same household five ways instead of two. The ACLD relabelled the categories at 2021: the 2011 and 2016 columns read \"Person usually resident in household with 1 or more Aboriginal and/ or Torres Strait Islander persons\", the 2021 column reads \"Household with Aboriginal and/ or Torres Strait Islander person(s)\".","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Indigenous household indicator (INGDWTD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/indigenous-household-indicator-ingdwtd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Indigenous Dwelling Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 Indigenous household indicator (2 categories)","def":"Two substantive codes, 1 for a household with one or more Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander persons and 2 for other households, plus 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. The ABS gives the not applicable category as visitor only households, other non-classifiable households, unoccupied private dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping SA1s.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Indigenous household indicator (INGDWTD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/indigenous-household-indicator-ingdwtd","lim":"It cannot tell you whether this person is the Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander member. The ABS data item list defines the column as \"This variable records the response of persons who identified themselves as being of Australian Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin in the Census\", which makes it a record of an answer given in 2011 rather than a fixed attribute. INGP_16 and INGP_21 hold the same question at the later Censuses, and the consistency flag CFINGP records whether a linked person answered the same way twice.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item INGP_11","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Indigenous Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 Indigenous status (4 categories)","def":"Codes 1 non-Indigenous, 2 Aboriginal, 3 Torres Strait Islander and 4 both Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, with 97 not stated and 99 unlinked record. The same four substantive categories are used at all three Censuses on this file.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item INGP_11","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"It cannot be differenced across waves as though it were a fixed trait. Identification changes between Censuses, so a person coded 1 in 2011 and 2 in 2016 may simply have answered differently, and the ABS reports non-response of 6.0% at 2016 and 4.9% at 2021 sitting in code 97.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":120},{"n":"INGP_16","d":"Indigenous status as reported at the 2016 Census, the middle wave of the ACLD 2011 panel.","full":"Indigenous status as reported at the 2016 Census, the middle wave of the ACLD 2011 panel. The 2016 Census Dictionary says \"The Indigenous status of a person is determined by their response to the ABS Standard Indigenous Question, which asks whether each person is of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin\", the same standard question used in 2011 and 2021. The question and the four output categories did not change between 2011 and 2016, so INGP_11 and INGP_16 are directly comparable in wording even though the answers move.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Indigenous Status (INGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter37202016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Indigenous Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 Indigenous status (4 categories)","def":"Codes 1 non-Indigenous, 2 Aboriginal, 3 Torres Strait Islander and 4 both, plus 97 not stated and 99 unlinked record. Nothing changed in the question for 2021, but response improved: the ABS puts INGP non-response at 4.9% in 2021 against 6.0% in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Indigenous status (INGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/indigenous-status-ingp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Indigenous Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 Indigenous status (4 categories)","def":"Codes 1 non-Indigenous, 2 Aboriginal, 3 Torres Strait Islander and 4 both, with 97 not stated and 99 unlinked record. A Census form is often completed by one household member for everybody, so a child's or an absent adult's Indigenous status can be another person's report of it, and that reporting can differ from the answer the same person gives at the next Census.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":120},{"n":"INGP_FP_11","d":"The Indigenous status the person's female parent reported at the 2011 Census, attached to the child's record.","full":"The Indigenous status the person's female parent reported at the 2011 Census, attached to the child's record. This includes the female parent of nominal children.\" Because it is built from the relationship coded within the dwelling, it empties out as the panel ages: a person aged 4 in 2011 has a female parent recorded, the same person at 24 in 2021 usually does not.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item INGP_FP_11","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Indigenous Status of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ACLD 2011 Indigenous status of female parent (2 categories)","def":"Two substantive codes at 2011, 1 non-Indigenous and 2 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. Code 99998 covers both people with no partner in the dwelling and people whose partner was temporarily absent on Census Night.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item LANP_SP_21","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"It cannot tell you which language the couple uses with each other. Each partner answers about their own home language use, so a mixed pair of codes describes two individual answers rather than a household practice.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"LEVEL","d":"An undocumented level indicator on the ACLD tables, with no matching data item in the ABS documentation.","full":"An undocumented level indicator on the ACLD tables, with no matching data item in the ABS documentation. It is the only column on the ACLD tables that carries no Census year suffix, and no item called LEVEL appears in the ABS data item list for the 2011-2016-2021 file, so what it distinguishes cannot be confirmed from published sources. The ABS states that every ACLD data item is held at the person level, including family, household and dwelling characteristics, so it is not a unit-of-analysis switch between person and household rows.","dsrc":"ABS Microdata and TableBuilder, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Level","k":"ACLD record level indicator (not documented by the ABS)","def":"The PLIDA metadata publishes no value list for this column and the ABS data item list does not describe it, so neither its type nor its categories can be stated.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Microdata and TableBuilder, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","lim":"It cannot be used to subset or weight the file. Because no published document defines the column, any filter on it risks dropping records for a reason the analyst cannot state, and it should not be confused with the education and occupation items whose names contain the word level, such as HEAP or OCSKP.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"LFDIF_P_11","d":"A quality flag saying how complete the 2011 family labour force information behind LFSF_P_11 is.","full":"A quality flag saying how complete the 2011 family labour force information behind LFSF_P_11 is. The ABS describes it as the variable that \"allows family labour force status to be derived based on following conditions\", the conditions being whether all family members stated labour force status and whether anyone aged 15 or over was temporarily absent on Census Night. It is a family attribute carried on the person record, so every family member takes the same code.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item LFDIF_P_11","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Family Labour Force Status Derivation Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"ACLD 2011 family labour force status derivation indicator (4 categories)","def":"Four substantive codes crossing two 2011 conditions: 1 all members stated labour force status and nobody aged 15 or over was temporarily absent, 2 one or more did not state, 3 one or more aged 15 or over was absent, 4 both. Code 98 is not applicable and 99 unlinked record; the item has no not stated code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item LFDIF_P_11","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"It is not a labour force measure. It says nothing about whether anyone in the family was employed, only whether the family's labour force information is complete, and it does not identify which member was missing or absent.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":123},{"n":"LFDIF_P_16","d":"A quality flag on the completeness of the 2016 family labour force information, carried on every member of the family.","full":"A quality flag on the completeness of the 2016 family labour force information, carried on every member of the family. Codes 2 and 4 mark families where at least one member did not state labour force status, and codes 3 and 4 mark families with a person aged 15 or over temporarily absent on Census Night. Use it to decide whether a 2016 family labour force category built from LFSF_P_16 rests on complete reporting.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item LFDIF_P_16","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Family Labour Force Status Derivation Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"ACLD 2016 family labour force status derivation indicator (4 categories)","def":"The same four codes at 2016: 1 complete reporting and nobody absent, 2 one or more members did not state labour force status, 3 one or more persons aged 15 or over temporarily absent, 4 both problems together, plus 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item LFDIF_P_16","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"It cannot be compared across waves as a family-level history. The family is defined afresh within each Census dwelling, so a person whose flag changes between 2011 and 2016 may be in a different family rather than in a family that reported differently.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":123},{"n":"LFDIF_P_21","d":"A quality flag on the completeness of the 2021 family labour force information behind LFSF_P_21.","full":"A quality flag on the completeness of the 2021 family labour force information behind LFSF_P_21. The ABS gives the not applicable category as visitors to the dwelling, unrelated persons living in family households, persons in non-family or non-classifiable households, persons in non-private dwellings and persons in migratory, off-shore and shipping SA1s. The categories are unchanged from 2011 and 2016, so the flag is directly comparable across the three waves even though the family is not.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item LFDIF_P_21","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Family Labour Force Status Derivation Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"ACLD 2021 family labour force status derivation indicator (4 categories)","def":"Four substantive codes at 2021, unchanged from 2011 and 2016, crossing whether every family member stated labour force status against whether anyone aged 15 or over was temporarily absent, plus 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. The 98 group is set by household type, not by how the family reported.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item LFDIF_P_21","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"A clean code 1 does not mean the family labour force category is right. It means everyone answered and nobody was away, not that the answers are accurate, and it does not flag imputed person records in the household.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":123},{"n":"LFHRP_11","d":"Labour force status in the week before the 2011 Census, with employed people who did not state their hours kept in a category of their own.","full":"Labour force status in the week before the 2011 Census, with employed people who did not state their hours kept in a category of their own. The ABS defines it as the variable that \"combines Labour Force Status (LFSP) with the 'Not stated' category from the Hours Worked (HRSP) variable to provide more detailed information on employed persons\" and notes that it \"is available in the ACLD from 2011\", so there is no 2006 column. LFSP_11 on the same row is the same classification with those people folded back into full-time, part-time or away from work.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item LFHRP_11","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status and Hours Worked Not Stated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 labour force status with hours not stated (7 categories)","def":"Codes 1 employed worked full-time, 2 employed worked part-time, 3 employed away from work, 4 employed hours of work not stated, 5 unemployed looking for full-time work, 6 unemployed looking for part-time work and 7 not in the labour force, plus 97 labour force status not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. The ABS gives not applicable as persons aged under 15 years, and 2011 is the first Census at which the item exists.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item LFHRP_11","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"It cannot be used as a full-time or part-time split without a decision about code 4. Employed people with hours not stated are excluded from both, so a full-time share computed over employed people will differ depending on whether code 4 sits in the denominator.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":124},{"n":"LFHRP_16","d":"Labour force status in the week before the 2016 Census, with employed people whose hours were not stated held separately.","full":"Labour force status in the week before the 2016 Census, with employed people whose hours were not stated held separately. The 2016 Census Dictionary puts it as \"The 'Not stated' category from the Hours Worked (HRSP) variable is added to Labour Force Status (LFSP) to provide more detailed information on employed persons in LFHRP\". The classification is unchanged from 2011, but the labour force status underneath it is not: from 2016 participants in the Community Development Programme are no longer automatically counted as employed, where 2011 counted Community Development Employment Projects participants that way.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Labour Force Status and Hours Worked Not Stated (LFHRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter38702016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status and Hours Worked Not Stated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 labour force status with hours not stated (7 categories)","def":"The same seven substantive codes at 2016, with 97 labour force status not stated, 98 not applicable for persons aged under 15 and 99 unlinked record. Code 4 is what separates this item from LFSP_16, which folds employed people with hours not stated back into away from work.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Labour Force Status and Hours Worked Not Stated (LFHRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter38702016","lim":"A change from employed in 2011 to not in the labour force in 2016 in a remote community can be the CDEP to CDP treatment change rather than a change in the person's work. The column gives no flag for which records are affected.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":124},{"n":"LFHRP_21","d":"Labour force status in the week before the 2021 Census, with employed people whose hours were not stated kept in their own category.","full":"Labour force status in the week before the 2021 Census, with employed people whose hours were not stated kept in their own category. The ABS defines it as \"This variable combines Labour force status (LFSP) with the 'Not stated' category from the Hours worked (HRSP) variable to provide more detailed information on employed persons\" and records that no changes were made for 2021. The reference week is the week before Census Night, Tuesday 10 August 2021, which for many people fell inside COVID-19 restrictions.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status and hours worked not stated (LFHRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-and-hours-worked-not-stated-lfhrp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status and Hours Worked Not Stated","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 labour force status with hours not stated (7 categories)","def":"Seven substantive codes at 2021 with no change from 2016: 1 employed full-time, 2 employed part-time, 3 employed away from work, 4 employed hours not stated, 5 unemployed seeking full-time work, 6 unemployed seeking part-time work and 7 not in the labour force, plus 97 labour force status not stated, 98 not applicable for persons aged under 15 and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status and hours worked not stated (LFHRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-and-hours-worked-not-stated-lfhrp","lim":"The 2021 reading is not a normal week. Lockdowns in several states over the reference week pushed people into away from work and reduced hours, so a 2016 to 2021 transition on this column mixes labour market change with the conditions of that particular week.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":124},{"n":"LFSF_P_11","d":"The combined labour force status of the parents or partners in the person's 2011 family, carried on every family member's record.","full":"The combined labour force status of the parents or partners in the person's 2011 family, carried on every family member's record. The ABS defines it as \"This variable records the labour force status of parents/partners in couple and lone parent families\", built from each parent's LFSP and hours worked. LFDIF_P_11 on the same row says whether every member stated a labour force status, which is what separates a genuine not stated category from a complete one.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item LFSF_P_11","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status of Parents/Partners in Families","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 labour force status of parents and partners in families (28 categories)","def":"Twenty-eight substantive categories at 2011: 1 to 21 for couple families, covering every pairing of full-time, part-time, away from work, unemployed, not in the labour force and not stated; 22 to 27 for one parent families; 28 other family. Code 998 is not applicable and 999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item LFSF_P_11","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"It cannot say which partner holds which status. Code 2, one employed full-time and the other part-time, does not identify the full-time earner, so it cannot be used for questions about mothers' or fathers' work without the separate parent columns.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":125},{"n":"LFSF_P_16","d":"The combined labour force status of the parents or partners in the person's 2016 family.","full":"The combined labour force status of the parents or partners in the person's 2016 family. The 2016 Census Dictionary defines LFSF as \"This variable records the labour force status of parents/partners in couple and lone parent families\", derived by taking family composition from FMCF and then each parent's labour force status and hours worked. The ABS data item list for the 2011-2016-2021 file names the 2016 column LFSFS_P_16 rather than LFSF_P_16, with the same 28 categories as the 2011 column.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Labour Force Status of Parents/Partners in Families (LFSF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter38802016","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Labour Force Status of Parents/Partners in Families","k":"Census 2016 labour force status of parents and partners in families (28 categories)","def":"The same 28 categories at 2016, with the three-digit missing codes 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record. The ABS records minor changes to LFSF at the 2016 Census, and the ACLD data item list names this column LFSFS_P_16.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Labour Force Status of Parents/Partners in Families (LFSF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter38802016","lim":"The category is only as good as the underlying labour force answers, and the 2016 shift away from counting Community Development Programme participants as employed moves some families between categories without anyone's work changing. LFDIF_P_16 flags incomplete reporting but not this.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"LFSF_P_21","d":"The combined labour force status of the parents or partners in the person's 2021 family.","full":"The combined labour force status of the parents or partners in the person's 2021 family. The ABS defines it as \"This variable records the labour force status of parents/partners in couple and lone parent families\" and records that no changes were made for 2021, so the categories match the 2011 and 2016 columns; the ABS data item list names this column LFSFS_P_21. Away from work covers parents who worked zero hours or did not state hours in the reference week, which in 2021 was the week before Tuesday 10 August.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status of parents/partners in families (LFSF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-parentspartners-families-lfsf","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Labour Force Status of Parents/Partners in Families","k":"Census 2021 labour force status of parents and partners in families (28 categories)","def":"Twenty-eight categories at 2021 with no change from 2016: 1 to 21 couple families, 22 to 27 one parent families, 28 other family, plus 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record. Away from work inside these categories covers a parent who worked no hours or did not state hours in the reference week.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status of parents/partners in families (LFSF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-parentspartners-families-lfsf","lim":"It describes the family, not the person whose row it sits on. A 20-year-old non-dependent child living at home carries their parents' combined status here, so treating the column as the person's own employment will misclassify every adult child and every dependent student.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"LFSP_11","d":"The person's labour force status in the week before the 2011 Census.","full":"The person's labour force status in the week before the 2011 Census. The ABS defines it as \"This variable records a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night\", derived from the work, hours, job search and availability questions and asked only of people aged 15 and over. In 2011 participants in the Community Development Employment Projects were counted as employed; the 2016 Census Dictionary records that Community Development Programme participants are no longer automatically classified that way, so LFSP_11 and LFSP_16 are not fully comparable in remote communities.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item LFSP_11","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 labour force status (6 categories)","def":"Codes 1 employed worked full-time, 2 employed worked part-time, 3 employed away from work, 4 unemployed looking for full-time work, 5 unemployed looking for part-time work and 6 not in the labour force, plus 97 not stated, 98 not applicable for people under 15 and 99 unlinked record. Full-time means 35 hours or more across all jobs.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item LFSP_11","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"It is a one-week snapshot, not a description of the year. A seasonal worker between contracts in August 2011 is not in the labour force here, and someone who worked one hour is employed, so the column cannot support statements about attachment to work over the period between Censuses.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":126},{"n":"LFSP_16","d":"The person's labour force status at the 2016 Census, for the week before Census Night.","full":"The person's labour force status at the 2016 Census, for the week before Census Night. The 2016 Census Dictionary calls it \"a derived variable applicable to all people aged 15 years and over. It classifies people as employed working full-time, part-time or away from work, unemployed looking for full-time work, looking for part-time work, or not in the labour force.\" It is built from the answers on full-time or part-time work, whether a job was held last week, hours worked, looking for work and availability to start, rather than from one question. The break with 2011 is remote employment programmes: participants in the Community Development Employment Projects were counted as employed in 2011, while for 2016 \"People participating only in this programme are not considered to be employed for the 2016 Census.\"","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Labour Force Status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter38602016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 labour force status (LFSP) code","def":"One code from the LFSP classification: employed working full-time, employed working part-time, employed away from work, unemployed looking for full-time work, unemployed looking for part-time work, or not in the labour force, with separate not stated and not applicable codes. Not applicable covers people aged under 15.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Labour Force Status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter38602016","lim":"It cannot be differenced against the 2011 column without allowing for the move from CDEP to the Community Development Programme, which shifted remote programme participants out of employment on definition alone. It also describes one week, so someone coded not in the labour force may have worked for most of the five years since the previous Census.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":126},{"n":"LFSP_21","d":"Whether the person was employed, unemployed or out of the labour force in the week before the 2021 Census.","full":"Whether the person was employed, unemployed or out of the labour force in the week before the 2021 Census. The ABS defines it as follows: \"This variable records a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night.\" The categories are unchanged from 2016, but 2021 added COVID-19 guidance: a person who could not work because of a lockdown yet had worked in the previous four weeks was told to report as absent from work rather than not employed, which moves people between the employed away from work and not in the labour force categories. Non-response fell to 5.8% in 2021 from 6.7% in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 labour force status (LFSP) code","def":"One code from the 2021 LFSP classification: employed worked full-time, employed worked part-time, employed away from work, unemployed looking for full-time work, unemployed looking for part-time work, not in the labour force, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes. Full-time means 35 hours or more across all jobs.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","lim":"The 2021 count was taken during lockdowns in Greater Sydney, Victoria and the ACT, so 'employed, away from work' in 2021 does not describe the same population as in 2016 and any transition built from LFSP_16 to LFSP_21 mixes labour market movement with the lockdown reporting instruction. Nor does the column say anything about the four intervening years.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":126},{"n":"LFSP_FP_11","d":"The labour force status of the person's female parent at the 2011 Census, read off the parent's own Census record.","full":"The labour force status of the person's female parent at the 2011 Census, read off the parent's own Census record. The underlying variable is LFSP, which the ABS describes as follows: \"This variable records a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night. The variable classifies people aged 15 years and over as employed working full-time, part-time or away from work; unemployed looking for full-time work; looking for part-time work; or not in the labour force.\" The ACLD attaches it to the child's record only where the female parent was enumerated in the same family in the same dwelling, so it describes a co-resident parent rather than a mother in general. At 2011 a participant in the Community Development Employment Projects was classified as employed, which the 2016 wave no longer does.","dsrc":"ABS 2011 Census, Labour Force Status (LFSP) statement","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementspersonlfsp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 labour force status (LFSP) code, female parent","def":"The same six-category LFSP classification used for the person, applied to the female parent: employed full-time, part-time or away from work, unemployed looking for full-time or part-time work, or not in the labour force, with not stated and not applicable codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS 2011 Census, Labour Force Status (LFSP) statement","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementspersonlfsp","lim":"Not applicable does not mean the person has no mother. A young adult who has moved out, a child whose mother was interstate on Census Night and a person in a non-private dwelling all take the same code, so the column measures whether a female parent was counted in the same family, not whether one exists.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":126},{"n":"LFSP_FP_16","d":"The labour force status of the person's female parent at the 2016 Census, where that parent was counted in the same family.","full":"The labour force status of the person's female parent at the 2016 Census, where that parent was counted in the same family. The base variable is LFSP, which the 2016 Census Dictionary calls \"a derived variable applicable to all people aged 15 years and over. It classifies people as employed working full-time, part-time or away from work, unemployed looking for full-time work, looking for part-time work, or not in the labour force.\" Against the 2011 column on the same row, the 2016 wave stopped treating remote employment programme participation as employment, so a mother in a remote community can move from employed to not in the labour force with no change in what she does. Read it with LFSP_MP_16 to describe both parents.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Labour Force Status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter38602016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 labour force status (LFSP) code, female parent","def":"The LFSP classification carried on the mother's record: employed working full-time, part-time or away from work, unemployed looking for full-time or part-time work, not in the labour force, plus not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Labour Force Status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter38602016","lim":"It cannot support a mother's employment trajectory on its own, because a child who leaves home between waves loses the parent columns and the record then looks like a mother who stopped working. Movement between LFSP_FP_11 and LFSP_FP_16 therefore confounds household change, definitional change and real labour market change.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":126},{"n":"LFSP_FP_21","d":"The labour force status of the person's female parent at the 2021 Census, taken from the parent's record in the same family.","full":"The labour force status of the person's female parent at the 2021 Census, taken from the parent's record in the same family. The base variable is defined by the ABS as follows: \"This variable records a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night.\" Because the 2021 Census fell during lockdowns, mothers who could not work but had worked in the previous four weeks were directed to report as absent from work, so the employed away from work category is unusually large in this wave. Non-response on the underlying LFSP variable was 5.8% in 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 labour force status (LFSP) code, female parent","def":"The 2021 LFSP classification applied to the female parent: employed worked full-time, employed worked part-time, employed away from work, unemployed looking for full-time work, unemployed looking for part-time work, not in the labour force, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","lim":"A mother recorded as employed away from work in 2021 may have had no work at all that week, so counting her as employed and comparing with 2016 overstates parental employment stability. The column also disappears once the child no longer lives with her, which is common by 2021 for a panel that started in 2011.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":126},{"n":"LFSP_MP_11","d":"The labour force status of the person's male parent at the 2011 Census, copied from the father's own Census record.","full":"The labour force status of the person's male parent at the 2011 Census, copied from the father's own Census record. The ABS defines the base variable as follows: \"This variable records a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night. The variable classifies people aged 15 years and over as employed working full-time, part-time or away from work; unemployed looking for full-time work; looking for part-time work; or not in the labour force.\" It is present only where the male parent was counted in the same family in the same dwelling on 2011 Census Night, so a father living elsewhere after separation leaves the column not applicable. At 2011 participation in the Community Development Employment Projects still counted as employment.","dsrc":"ABS 2011 Census, Labour Force Status (LFSP) statement","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementspersonlfsp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 labour force status (LFSP) code, male parent","def":"The LFSP classification carried on the father's record: employed full-time, part-time or away from work, unemployed looking for full-time or part-time work, or not in the labour force, plus not stated and not applicable codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS 2011 Census, Labour Force Status (LFSP) statement","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementspersonlfsp","lim":"It cannot distinguish a father who was absent from the household from a father who has no recorded labour force status, because both fall to not applicable. Pairing it with LFSP_FP_11 to build a two-parent employment measure therefore drops single-parent and separated families rather than describing them.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":126},{"n":"LFSP_MP_16","d":"The labour force status of the person's male parent at the 2016 Census, where the father was enumerated in the same family.","full":"The labour force status of the person's male parent at the 2016 Census, where the father was enumerated in the same family. The 2016 Census Dictionary defines the base variable as \"a derived variable applicable to all people aged 15 years and over. It classifies people as employed working full-time, part-time or away from work, unemployed looking for full-time work, looking for part-time work, or not in the labour force.\" The 2016 wave differs from 2011 in one respect that matters for remote communities: \"People participating only in this programme are not considered to be employed for the 2016 Census\", whereas the CDEP participants the Community Development Programme replaced were counted as employed in 2011. Non-response on the underlying LFSP variable was 6.7% in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Labour Force Status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter38602016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 labour force status (LFSP) code, male parent","def":"The LFSP classification applied to the male parent: employed working full-time, part-time or away from work, unemployed looking for full-time or part-time work, not in the labour force, plus not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Labour Force Status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter38602016","lim":"A change from employed at 2011 to not in the labour force at 2016 for a father in a remote community is likely to be the programme reclassification rather than a job loss, so the column should not be used untreated in intercensal transition tables. The ABS defines the base variable as follows: \"This variable records a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night.\" In 2021 a father stood down or unable to work under a COVID-19 lockdown, but who had worked within the previous four weeks, was directed to report as absent from work, so employed away from work absorbs people who would previously have reported no job. LFSP_FP_21 is the matching column for the female parent.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 labour force status (LFSP) code, male parent","def":"The 2021 LFSP classification applied to the male parent, including the employed away from work category and the not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes. Reading a 2016 to 2021 change as recovery or loss of parental employment therefore attributes a reporting instruction to the labour market.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":126},{"n":"LFSP_SP_11","d":"The labour force status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census, copied from the partner's own record.","full":"The labour force status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census, copied from the partner's own record. The ABS describes the base variable as follows: \"This variable records a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night. The variable classifies people aged 15 years and over as employed working full-time, part-time or away from work; unemployed looking for full-time work; looking for part-time work; or not in the labour force.\" The ACLD fills it only where a spouse or partner was counted in the same household on Census Night, covering both registered and de facto partners. It supports household joint labour supply measures when read against the person's own LFSP.","dsrc":"ABS 2011 Census, Labour Force Status (LFSP) statement","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementspersonlfsp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 labour force status (LFSP) code, spouse or partner","def":"The LFSP classification carried on the partner's record: employed full-time, part-time or away from work, unemployed looking for full-time or part-time work, or not in the labour force, plus not stated and not applicable codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS 2011 Census, Labour Force Status (LFSP) statement","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementspersonlfsp","lim":"A partner who lives at another address, was away on Census Night, or is in a relationship not reported on the household form leaves this column not applicable, so it cannot be used to identify who has a partner. The 2016 Census Dictionary calls the base variable \"a derived variable applicable to all people aged 15 years and over. It classifies people as employed working full-time, part-time or away from work, unemployed looking for full-time work, looking for part-time work, or not in the labour force.\" As for every 2016 labour force column, participation in the Community Development Programme is not employment, unlike CDEP at 2011. A partner present in 2011 but not in 2016 produces a not applicable value rather than a partner who left the labour force.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Labour Force Status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter38602016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 labour force status (LFSP) code, spouse or partner","def":"The LFSP classification applied to the spouse or partner: employed working full-time, part-time or away from work, unemployed looking for full-time or part-time work, not in the labour force, plus not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Labour Force Status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter38602016","lim":"It cannot tell a partnership that ended from a partner who simply was not enumerated, so a not applicable value in 2016 after a valid 2011 value is not evidence of separation. The ABS defines the base variable as follows: \"This variable records a person's labour force status for the week prior to Census Night.\" In 2021 partners stood down under COVID-19 restrictions were told to report as absent from work if they had worked in the previous four weeks, so the employed away from work category is larger in this wave than in 2016. Since the December 2017 Marriage Act amendment, same-sex partners appear here on the same footing as any other spouse.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Labour Force Status of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 labour force status (LFSP) code, spouse or partner","def":"The 2021 LFSP classification applied to the spouse or partner, including employed away from work and the not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Labour force status (LFSP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/labour-force-status-lfsp","lim":"A household with both members coded employed away from work in 2021 may have had no earnings that week, so this column cannot be used to infer household income continuity through the lockdowns. The ABS explains that \"Local Government Areas (LGAs) are an ABS approximation of officially gazetted LGAs as defined by each state and territory's Local Government Department. The LGA boundaries are approximated using MBs.\" Usual residence is where the person lives, which is not always where they were counted on Census Night. Unincorporated areas, including the ACT, northern South Australia and the Other Territories, have no council and are identified separately rather than left blank.","dsrc":"ABS 2011 Census fact sheet, Non-ABS structures","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/factsheetsnas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Local Government Areas (Usual Residence)","k":"ASGS 2011 Local Government Area code (usual residence)","def":"A numeric ASGS 2011 Local Government Area code with an accompanying name, built by allocating whole Mesh Blocks to each council area. Codes and names are only meaningful together, because a code can be reused across editions.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS 2011 Census fact sheet, Non-ABS structures","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/factsheetsnas","lim":"A different LGA in 2016 or 2021 is not proof that the person moved. Council amalgamations, the 2016 New South Wales mergers and routine annual boundary revisions all change the code for a person who never left the house, so intercensal mobility needs an ABS geographic correspondence rather than a straight comparison of LGA_UR_11 with the later columns.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"LGA_UR_16","d":"The Local Government Area of the person's usual residence at the 2016 Census, on the ASGS July 2016 boundaries.","full":"The Local Government Area of the person's usual residence at the 2016 Census, on the ASGS July 2016 boundaries. The ABS builds them from the smallest statistical units: Local Government Areas \"have been constructed by allocating whole Mesh Blocks\", because \"The relatively small size of Mesh Blocks and common boundary elements tend to allow Mesh Blocks to match these regions closely.\" The July 2016 edition is the one that carries the New South Wales council amalgamations, so many 2011 codes have no counterpart here. Usual residence, not place of enumeration, is what this column geocodes.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 3 - Non ABS Structures, July 2016, Methodology","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/1270.0.55.003~July%202016~Main%20Features~Methodology~5","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Local Government Areas (Usual Residence)","k":"ASGS 2016 Local Government Area code (usual residence)","def":"A numeric ASGS July 2016 Local Government Area code with its name, formed from whole Mesh Blocks so that it nests within state and territory but not within the ABS main structure above SA1.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 3 - Non ABS Structures, July 2016, Methodology","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/1270.0.55.003~July%202016~Main%20Features~Methodology~5","lim":"Comparing this column with LGA_UR_11 counts boundary change as migration, most visibly in New South Wales where amalgamated councils replaced dozens of former LGAs between the two Censuses. The ABS defines them as follows: \"Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory.\" Edition 3 has 567 Local Government Areas covering the whole of Australia, including unincorporated areas, without gaps or overlaps. The ABS warns that these \"approximations of administrative boundaries do not match official legal boundaries and should only be used for statistical purposes.\"","dsrc":"ABS Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Local Government Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/non-abs-structures/local-government-areas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Local Government Areas (Usual Residence)","k":"ASGS Edition 3 Local Government Area code (usual residence)","def":"A numeric ASGS Edition 3 Local Government Area code with its name, built by allocating whole Mesh Blocks primarily on where the population sits. It is the gate on every column ending in _16, because the ABS states that \"Where records are not linked to a future Census cycle all variables for the unlinked period will be set to 'Unlinked record'.\" The flag exists because linkage is probabilistic, not administrative: the ABS reports that 76.0% of the 2011 panel linked forward to 2016. Filter on it before analysing any 2016 variable, or the unlinked code will be read as a real Census response.","dsrc":"ABS Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Record Linked Flag","t":"categorical","k":"ACLD record linkage indicator, 2011 record to 2016 Census","def":"A two-state indicator distinguishing records linked to the 2016 Census from records not linked. The flag also says nothing about the quality of the base-year record, only about the forward match.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":127},{"n":"LINKFLAG_21","d":"Whether the person's base Census record in this ACLD panel was linked forward to a 2021 Census record.","full":"Whether the person's base Census record in this ACLD panel was linked forward to a 2021 Census record. It governs every column ending in _21, since the ABS states that \"Where records are not linked to a future Census cycle all variables for the unlinked period will be set to 'Unlinked record'.\" Linkage thins with distance: the ABS reports 76.0% of the 2011 panel linked to 2016 but only about 67% linked across 2011, 2016 and 2021 together. LINKFLAG_16 is the matching flag for the intermediate wave, and the two have to be read together for a three-wave analysis.","dsrc":"ABS Microdata and TableBuilder: Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Record Linked Flag","t":"categorical","k":"ACLD record linkage indicator, base record to 2021 Census","def":"A two-state indicator separating records linked to the 2021 Census from records not linked. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines the variable as one that \"Records the landlord type of rented dwellings-as classified in Tenure Type (TEND).\" It applies only to occupied private dwellings being rented, including those occupied rent free, so an owner-occupier or a resident of a non-private dwelling takes a not applicable code. The 2016 Census Dictionary defines the variable as one that \"Records the landlord type of rented dwellings as classified in Tenure Type (TEND)\", applicable to \"Occupied private dwellings being rented (including being occupied rent free)\", which was 29.4% of occupied private dwellings in 2016. The 2016 categories are unchanged from 2011 and still carry code 60 for a housing co-operative, community or church group as distinct from code 20 for a state or territory housing authority. The ABS defines it as follows: \"This variable records the landlord type of rented dwellings. It is the finest geography in this table and every coarser 2021 usual residence column, including LGA_UR_21, aggregates from it.
