The 2011 Census Dictionary says the variable \"Reports responses to two questions: 'What is the person's relationship to Person 1/Person 2?' and 'What is the person's present marital status?'\" At 2011 a person is classified as married in a registered marriage only where a husband or wife relationship answer is matched by a married response to the marital status question; a husband or wife answer with any other marital status response gives a de facto marriage. It applies only to people usually resident and present in the household on Census Night, so people in non-private dwellings are out of scope.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Social Marital Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 social marital status (MDCP) code","def":"One of three output categories, married in a registered marriage, married in a de facto marriage, or not married, plus not applicable. De facto covers responses reported as de facto, partner, common law husband, wife or spouse, lover, boyfriend or girlfriend.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402011","lim":"It cannot see a partner who lives elsewhere or was away on Census Night, so a married person whose spouse was interstate is coded not married here while MSTP_11 on the same row still shows married. The registered and de facto split also turns on two answers agreeing, so a couple who called themselves husband and wife but did not report a registered marital status of married is counted here as de facto married.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":131},{"n":"MDCP_16","d":"The person's living arrangement at the 2016 Census: registered marriage, de facto marriage, or not married.","full":"The person's living arrangement at the 2016 Census: registered marriage, de facto marriage, or not married. The 2016 Census Dictionary describes it as a variable that \"Reports responses to two questions: 'What is the person's relationship to Person 1/Person 2?' and 'What is the person's present marital status?'\" A registered marriage requires both a husband or wife relationship answer and a married response to the marital status question, and a husband or wife answer with any other marital status response gives a de facto marriage. The 2011 Census Dictionary states the same rule, so the 2011 and 2016 columns draw the registered and de facto line in the same place, although the 2021 dictionary instead dates this alignment with the ABS family standards to 2016. It is \"Only applicable to those usually resident and present in the household on Census night (i.e. not applicable to those in non-private dwellings)\".","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Social Marital Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 social marital status (MDCP) code","def":"One of three output categories, married in a registered marriage, married in a de facto marriage, or not married, plus not applicable for people out of scope. There is no not stated code, because the variable is derived during processing rather than answered.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402016","lim":"A couple whose two answers disagree falls into de facto marriage rather than registered marriage, so the registered category undercounts legally married couples where a partner reported some other marital status, and a change between MDCP_11 and MDCP_16 can come from a different answer rather than a different relationship. The column also cannot describe a relationship with a partner at another address.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":131},{"n":"MDCP_21","d":"The person's living arrangement at the 2021 Census: registered marriage, de facto marriage, or not married.","full":"The person's living arrangement at the 2021 Census: registered marriage, de facto marriage, or not married. The ABS defines it as follows: \"This variable records a person's relationship status based on their current living arrangements. It identifies whether they form a couple relationship with another person living in the same usual residence, and the nature of that relationship.\" It is derived from Relationship in household (RLHP) and Registered marital status (MSTP), not asked directly. Processing changed for 2021 because all couples can now be in registered marriages after the December 2017 Marriage Act amendment, which moves same-sex couples out of de facto marriage and into registered marriage.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Social marital status (MDCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/social-marital-status-mdcp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Social Marital Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 social marital status (MDCP) code","def":"One of three output categories, married in a registered marriage, married in a de facto marriage, or not married, plus not applicable and overseas visitor. It applies to people aged 15 and over who were usually resident and present in the household on Census Night.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Social marital status (MDCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/social-marital-status-mdcp","lim":"A fall in de facto marriages between MDCP_16 and MDCP_21 is partly the marriage equality reclassification rather than couples changing status, so the series should not be read as a shift in relationship preferences. The column also cannot detect a partner living at a different address, which MSTP_21 on the same row may still show as married.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":131},{"n":"MDCP_FP_11","d":"The living arrangement of the person's female parent at the 2011 Census: registered marriage, de facto marriage, or not married.","full":"The living arrangement of the person's female parent at the 2011 Census: registered marriage, de facto marriage, or not married. The base variable \"Reports responses to two questions: 'What is the person's relationship to Person 1/Person 2?' and 'What is the person's present marital status?'\", and the ACLD copies the mother's own value onto the child's record where she was counted in the same family. For a child living with both parents the value effectively describes the parents' relationship to each other. At 2011 the parents count as registered married only where the husband or wife relationship answer is matched by a married response to the marital status question.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Social Marital Status of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 social marital status (MDCP) code, female parent","def":"The three-category MDCP classification carried on the female parent's record, married in a registered marriage, married in a de facto marriage or not married, plus not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402011","lim":"A mother coded not married is not necessarily a single parent, because MDCP only sees a partner who lives in the same household, and a partner at another address or away on Census Night does not count. Nor can the column be used to identify step-families, since the value says nothing about whether the mother's partner is the child's parent.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":131},{"n":"MDCP_FP_16","d":"The living arrangement of the person's female parent at the 2016 Census, copied from the mother's record in the same family.","full":"The living arrangement of the person's female parent at the 2016 Census, copied from the mother's record in the same family. The base variable \"Reports responses to two questions: 'What is the person's relationship to Person 1/Person 2?' and 'What is the person's present marital status?'\", and a registered marriage requires both answers to agree, which is the same rule the 2011 Census Dictionary sets out. It is \"Only applicable to those usually resident and present in the household on Census night (i.e. not applicable to those in non-private dwellings)\", so the column is empty for a mother in a nursing home or other non-private dwelling. MDCP_MP_16 is the matching column for the male parent.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Social Marital Status of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 social marital status (MDCP) code, female parent","def":"The three-category MDCP classification applied to the female parent, married in a registered marriage, married in a de facto marriage or not married, with a not applicable code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402016","lim":"A shift from registered to de facto marriage between MDCP_FP_11 and MDCP_FP_16 can come from the mother answering the marital status question differently rather than from any change in her relationship, because the registered category needs both of her answers to agree in each wave. It also cannot distinguish a mother who was not in the household from a mother out of scope.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":131},{"n":"MDCP_FP_21","d":"The living arrangement of the person's female parent at the 2021 Census, taken from the mother's record in the same family.","full":"The living arrangement of the person's female parent at the 2021 Census, taken from the mother's record in the same family. The ABS defines the base variable as follows: \"This variable records a person's relationship status based on their current living arrangements.\" It is derived from Relationship in household (RLHP) and Registered marital status (MSTP), so it depends on how the household form described who lives with whom. From 2021 all couples can be in registered marriages, so a mother in a same-sex couple who appeared as de facto married in 2016 can appear as registered married here.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Social marital status (MDCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/social-marital-status-mdcp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Social Marital Status of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 social marital status (MDCP) code, female parent","def":"The three-category MDCP classification applied to the female parent, married in a registered marriage, married in a de facto marriage or not married, plus not applicable and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Social marital status (MDCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/social-marital-status-mdcp","lim":"By 2021 an ACLD member who started the panel as a child is often an adult living away from home, so this column falls to not applicable for reasons that have nothing to do with the mother's relationship. Reading the not applicable share as growth in single parenthood therefore measures the panel ageing, not family formation.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":131},{"n":"MDCP_MP_11","d":"The living arrangement of the person's male parent at the 2011 Census, copied from the father's record in the same family.","full":"The living arrangement of the person's male parent at the 2011 Census, copied from the father's record in the same family. The base variable \"Reports responses to two questions: 'What is the person's relationship to Person 1/Person 2?' and 'What is the person's present marital status?'\", and at 2011 a husband or wife relationship answer counts as a registered marriage only where the marital status answer is also married, otherwise the couple is recorded as de facto married. Because it is a household variable, a father counted at a different address on Census Night leaves the column not applicable even where he is on the child's birth record.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Social Marital Status of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 social marital status (MDCP) code, male parent","def":"The three-category MDCP classification carried on the male parent's record, married in a registered marriage, married in a de facto marriage or not married, plus not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402011","lim":"Where both MDCP_FP_11 and MDCP_MP_11 are present they usually repeat each other, because they describe the two sides of the same parental couple, so treating them as two independent measures double counts one relationship. Fathers in non-private dwellings are out of scope, since the variable is \"Only applicable to those usually resident and present in the household on Census night\". Non-response does not arise, because the variable is created in processing rather than reported.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Social Marital Status of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 social marital status (MDCP) code, male parent","def":"The three-category MDCP classification applied to the male parent, married in a registered marriage, married in a de facto marriage or not married, with a not applicable code for people out of scope.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402016","lim":"It cannot separate a de facto stepfather from a de facto biological father, because the category describes the parents' relationship rather than the child's relationship to the man. The ABS defines the base variable as follows: \"It identifies whether they form a couple relationship with another person living in the same usual residence, and the nature of that relationship.\" It is derived from Relationship in household (RLHP) and Registered marital status (MSTP). Since the December 2017 Marriage Act amendment all couples can be in registered marriages, so a father in a same-sex couple can move from de facto in 2016 to registered marriage in 2021 with no change in the household.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Social marital status (MDCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/social-marital-status-mdcp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Social Marital Status of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 social marital status (MDCP) code, male parent","def":"The three-category MDCP classification applied to the male parent, married in a registered marriage, married in a de facto marriage or not married, plus not applicable and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Social marital status (MDCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/social-marital-status-mdcp","lim":"It cannot be used to count fathers, only fathers who were enumerated in the same family, and shared-care arrangements put a child in one parent's household on Census Night and not the other's. It is present only where a spouse or partner was counted in the same household, and it is not applicable in non-private dwellings.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Social Marital Status of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 social marital status (MDCP) code, spouse or partner","def":"The three-category MDCP classification carried on the partner's record, married in a registered marriage, married in a de facto marriage or not married, plus not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402011","lim":"It carries almost no information beyond MDCP_11 on the same row, because both values describe one couple and are derived from the same household relationship answer; they differ only where the two partners gave inconsistent marital status responses. The 2016 Census Dictionary describes the base variable as one that \"Reports responses to two questions: 'What is the person's relationship to Person 1/Person 2?' and 'What is the person's present marital status?'\", and both answers must agree for a registered marriage, as they did at 2011. The rule applies to each partner separately, so a couple can split between registered and de facto across the person's column and the partner's column.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Social Marital Status of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 social marital status (MDCP) code, spouse or partner","def":"The three-category MDCP classification applied to the spouse or partner, married in a registered marriage, married in a de facto marriage or not married, with a not applicable code for people with no co-resident partner.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Social Marital Status (MDCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter40402016","lim":"A disagreement between MDCP_16 and MDCP_SP_16 is a reporting inconsistency inside the couple, not evidence of two different relationships, so treating the pair as two separate relationship states misreads a processing rule. The column also cannot identify which household member the partner is.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":131},{"n":"MDCP_SP_21","d":"The social marital status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2021 Census, taken from the partner's record in the same household.","full":"The social marital status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2021 Census, taken from the partner's record in the same household. The ABS defines the base variable as follows: \"This variable records a person's relationship status based on their current living arrangements.\" From 2021 all couples can be in registered marriages after the December 2017 Marriage Act amendment, so a partner recorded as de facto married in 2016 may appear as registered married here without the relationship changing. MDCP_21 on the same row is the person's own value.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Social marital status (MDCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/social-marital-status-mdcp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Social Marital Status of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 social marital status (MDCP) code, spouse or partner","def":"The three-category MDCP classification applied to the spouse or partner, married in a registered marriage, married in a de facto marriage or not married, plus not applicable and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Social marital status (MDCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/social-marital-status-mdcp","lim":"It cannot be used to identify a couple's legal status, because the category describes living arrangements; a partner who is legally married to someone else and living de facto here is recorded as de facto married, and their registered status appears only in the MSTP columns. The column is also empty for a partner who lives at a different address.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":131},{"n":"MRERD_P_11","d":"The monthly mortgage repayment band for the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2011 Census.","full":"The monthly mortgage repayment band for the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2011 Census. It is the banded form of the dollar-value variable MRED, which the 2011 Census Dictionary defines as \"Derived from responses to a number of questions and records the amount of money spent monthly on mortgage repayments.\" 2011 was the first Census to record a nil repayment as $0 and to give it its own 'Nil repayments' range, where earlier Censuses coded a nil response as not stated. It applies to occupied private dwellings being purchased, so renters and outright owners take a not applicable code.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Mortgage Repayments (monthly) Dollar Values (MRED)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter6632011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Mortgage Repayments (Monthly) Ranges","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 monthly mortgage repayment range (MRERD)","def":"A single band from the MRERD range set, running from nil repayments through dollar intervals to a top open-ended category, expressed in nominal dollars per month. It is derived by banding the dollar-value variable MRED rather than collected as a range.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Mortgage Repayments (monthly) Dollar Values (MRED)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter6632011","lim":"The nil repayments change means a 2011 count of households with no mortgage repayment is not comparable with Censuses before 2011, where those households sat in not stated. Non-response on the underlying dollar values was 5.3% in 2011, and a not stated band cannot be read as a low repayment.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":132},{"n":"MRERD_P_16","d":"The monthly mortgage repayment band for the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2016 Census.","full":"The monthly mortgage repayment band for the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2016 Census. The ABS says these variables \"record the mortgage repayments being paid by a household to purchase the dwelling in which they were enumerated on Census night\", covering the 32.4% of occupied private dwellings being purchased in 2016. Since 2011 a nil repayment has been reported as $0 in the dollar variable and as a separate 'Nil repayments' category here, so the 2011 and 2016 bands line up on that point. Non-response was 4.2% in 2016, down from 5.3% in 2011.","dsrc":"ABS 2900.0 Understanding the Census and Census Data, Australia 2016, Mortgage Repayments","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features101272016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Mortgage Repayments (Monthly) Ranges","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 monthly mortgage repayment range (MRERD)","def":"A single band from the 2016 MRERD range set, in nominal dollars per month, derived by banding the dollar-value variable MRED. Standard Census products recode the dollar values into a fixed number of ranges.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS 2900.0 Understanding the Census and Census Data, Australia 2016, Mortgage Repayments","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features101272016","lim":"The bands are nominal, so a household moving up a band between 2011 and 2016 may be paying the same real amount, and comparison across waves needs deflating or a common banding rather than a straight code comparison. The column also covers repayments on this dwelling only, and says nothing about the loan balance, an offset account or an investment property loan.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":132},{"n":"MRERD_P_21","d":"The monthly mortgage repayment band for the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2021 Census.","full":"The monthly mortgage repayment band for the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2021 Census. The ABS defines it as follows: \"This variable records the mortgage repayments being paid by a household in ranges. It is applicable to occupied private dwellings on Census Night.\" The ABS states that \"No changes have been made for 2021\", so the concept matches 2016, but non-response on the underlying dollar variable MRED rose to 6.0% in 2021 from 4.2% in 2016. It applies to dwellings owned with a mortgage, including those bought under shared equity schemes.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Mortgage repayments (monthly) ranges (MRERD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/mortgage-repayments-monthly-ranges-mrerd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Mortgage Repayments (Monthly) Ranges","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 monthly mortgage repayment range (MRERD)","def":"One of 23 categories running from nil repayments through dollar intervals such as $1 to $149 and $150 to $299 up to $5,000 and over, plus not stated and not applicable codes. The bands are banded from the dollar-value variable MRED.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Mortgage repayments (monthly) ranges (MRERD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/mortgage-repayments-monthly-ranges-mrerd","lim":"It describes the dwelling, so every ACLD member in the household repeats the same band and none of them is identified as the borrower. Repayments in 2021 also fell during a period of mortgage deferrals and record low interest rates, so a lower band than 2016 can reflect a rate change or a deferral rather than a smaller loan.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":133},{"n":"MSTP_11","d":"The person's registered marital status at the 2011 Census.","full":"The person's registered marital status at the 2011 Census. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as a variable that \"records an individual's current status in regard to a registered marriage, i.e. whether he/she is widowed, divorced, separated, married or has never married.\" It is not left blank when unanswered: \"Registered Marital Status (MSTP) is coded from Question 6 and is imputed if no response is provided. The variable Imputation Flag for Registered Marital Status (IFMSTP) is used to indicate if a person's marital status has been imputed for the Census.\" At 2011 only opposite-sex marriages could be registered in Australia, so 'married' has a narrower meaning here than in 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Registered Marital Status (MSTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48902011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Registered Marital Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 registered marital status (MSTP) code","def":"One of five categories, never married, married, separated but not divorced, divorced or widowed, plus a not applicable code for people aged under 15. Marital status applies to people aged 15 years and over.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Registered Marital Status (MSTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48902011","lim":"There is no missing category, because non-response is imputed, so an apparent change between MSTP_11 and a later wave can be an imputed value on one side rather than a real event; IFMSTP is the flag that identifies those records. The column also records registration, not living arrangements, so a separated person living with a new partner still reads as separated while MDCP_11 shows a de facto marriage.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":134},{"n":"MSTP_16","d":"The person's registered marital status at the 2016 Census.","full":"The person's registered marital status at the 2016 Census. The 2016 Census Dictionary defines the variable as one that \"records an individual's current status in regard to a registered marriage, i.e. whether he/she is widowed, divorced, separated, married or has never married\", noting that a question on registered marital status \"has been asked in all Australian censuses\" and that the categories have been stable since 1986. The 2016 Census fell before marriage equality commenced in December 2017, so a same-sex couple could not be recorded as married here even if married overseas. Where the question was unanswered the value is imputed, flagged by IFMSTP.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Registered Marital Status (MSTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48902016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Registered Marital Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 registered marital status (MSTP) code","def":"One of five categories, never married, married, separated but not divorced, divorced or widowed, with a not applicable code for people under 15. The category set has been unchanged since the 1986 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Registered Marital Status (MSTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48902016","lim":"A move from never married or divorced in 2016 to married in 2021 can be the legal recognition of an existing same-sex relationship rather than a new marriage, so the 2016 to 2021 transition overstates new marriages for those couples. Non-response was 6.9% in 2016 and those records were imputed, not dropped.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":134},{"n":"MSTP_21","d":"The person's registered marital status at the 2021 Census.","full":"The person's registered marital status at the 2021 Census. The ABS defines it as follows: \"This variable records a person's formal registered marital status. If registered marital status is not stated, it is imputed.\" The question was unchanged for 2021, but processing was amended to reflect the December 2017 changes to the Marriage Act 1961, so 'married' now covers same-sex registered marriages as well as opposite-sex ones. Non-response was 5.5% in 2021, down from 6.9% in 2016, and every non-responding record carries an imputed value.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Registered marital status (MSTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/registered-marital-status-mstp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Registered Marital Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 registered marital status (MSTP) code","def":"One of five categories, never married, widowed, divorced, separated or married, plus a not applicable code for people aged under 15. It applies to persons aged 15 years and over.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Registered marital status (MSTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/registered-marital-status-mstp","lim":"Growth in the married category between 2016 and 2021 partly reflects the widening of what can be registered, so it cannot be read as a rise in the marriage rate for the panel. The base variable \"records an individual's current status in regard to a registered marriage, i.e. whether he/she is widowed, divorced, separated, married or has never married\", and it \"is imputed if no response is provided\". The ACLD attaches it only where the mother was counted in the same family, so it is a characteristic of a co-resident parent. Unlike MDCP_FP_11, it survives a spouse living elsewhere, because it records registration rather than household composition.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Registered Marital Status (MSTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48902011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Registered Marital Status of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 registered marital status (MSTP) code, female parent","def":"The five-category MSTP classification carried on the female parent's record, never married, married, separated but not divorced, divorced or widowed, plus a not applicable code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Registered Marital Status (MSTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48902011","lim":"A mother recorded as married is not necessarily living with the person's father, and a mother recorded as never married may still live with a de facto partner, so this column cannot be used to classify family type; MDCP_FP_11 is the column for that. Imputation also means a value is present even where the mother left the question blank.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":135},{"n":"MSTP_FP_16","d":"The registered marital status of the person's female parent at the 2016 Census, where the mother was counted in the same family.","full":"The registered marital status of the person's female parent at the 2016 Census, where the mother was counted in the same family. The 2016 Census Dictionary defines the base variable as one that \"records an individual's current status in regard to a registered marriage, i.e. whether he/she is widowed, divorced, separated, married or has never married\", and notes the categories have applied \"In all censuses since 1986\". Because 2016 preceded marriage equality, a mother in a same-sex relationship could not be recorded as married in this wave. Non-response was 6.9% in 2016 and those records were imputed.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Registered Marital Status (MSTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48902016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Registered Marital Status of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 registered marital status (MSTP) code, female parent","def":"The five-category MSTP classification applied to the female parent, never married, married, separated but not divorced, divorced or widowed, with a not applicable code for people under 15 and for parents not enumerated in the same family.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Registered Marital Status (MSTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48902016","lim":"It cannot be used to detect a parental separation between waves, because a mother recorded as married in 2011 and separated in 2016 may simply have answered differently, and imputation can move the value without any event. The ABS defines the base variable as follows: \"This variable records a person's formal registered marital status. Non-response on the base variable was 5.5% in 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Registered marital status (MSTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/registered-marital-status-mstp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Registered Marital Status of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 registered marital status (MSTP) code, female parent","def":"The five-category MSTP classification applied to the female parent, never married, widowed, divorced, separated or married, plus a not applicable code where the mother was under 15 or was not enumerated in the same family.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Registered marital status (MSTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/registered-marital-status-mstp","lim":"By 2021 many ACLD members no longer live with a parent, so the column empties for panel reasons rather than family reasons and cannot be used to track a mother's marital history across the three waves. The value appears only where the father was enumerated in the same family, so a non-resident father contributes nothing. At 2011 only opposite-sex marriages could be registered in Australia.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Registered Marital Status (MSTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48902011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Registered Marital Status of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 registered marital status (MSTP) code, male parent","def":"The five-category MSTP classification carried on the male parent's record, never married, married, separated but not divorced, divorced or widowed, plus a not applicable code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Registered Marital Status (MSTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48902011","lim":"Where both parents are present this column and MSTP_FP_11 usually agree, since they describe two members of the same registered marriage, so the pair is not two independent observations. The 2016 wave predates marriage equality, so a father in a same-sex relationship appears as never married, divorced or widowed rather than married.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Registered Marital Status (MSTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48902016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Registered Marital Status of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 registered marital status (MSTP) code, male parent","def":"The five-category MSTP classification applied to the male parent, never married, married, separated but not divorced, divorced or widowed, with a not applicable code for men under 15 and for fathers not enumerated in the same family.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Registered Marital Status (MSTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter48902016","lim":"It cannot identify de facto parents, so a father living with the person's mother without a registered marriage is grouped with fathers who live alone; MDCP_MP_16 is the column that separates them. The 2021 Census Dictionary says of the underlying variable that \"This variable records a person's formal registered marital status. If registered marital status is not stated, it is imputed.\" The 2021 question was unchanged, but responses were processed differently after the 2017 Marriage Act amendments, so a same-sex partner can be coded married here where the same couple could not be in 2011 or 2016. Non-response fell to 5.5% in 2021 from 6.9% in 2016 and the imputed cases are flagged by IFMSTP.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Registered marital status (MSTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/registered-marital-status-mstp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Registered Marital Status of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census registered marital status code (MSTP), 2021","def":"A single code from the Census registered marital status classification: 1 never married, 2 widowed, 3 divorced, 4 separated, 5 married, with @ for not applicable, which in 2021 covers people under 15 and people with no spouse or partner in the dwelling.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Registered marital status (MSTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/registered-marital-status-mstp","lim":"It cannot be read as evidence that the couple is not in a de facto relationship, because a de facto partner keeps their registered status of never married, divorced or widowed. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as recording \"up to three methods, or means, of travel to work on the day of the Census, for each person aged 15 years and over who was employed during the week before the Census\". Question 45 allowed more than one mode for a single trip, except for walked only, worked at home and did not go to work, which are recorded on their own.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Method of Travel to Work (MTWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter41002011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Method of Travel to Work","t":"categorical","k":"Census method of travel to work code (MTWP), 2011","def":"A code standing for one, two or three travel modes used on the one journey, drawn from the Census method of travel to work classification, plus separate codes for walked only, worked at home, did not go to work, not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Method of Travel to Work (MTWP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter41002011","lim":"It describes one day, not a commuting habit. A person on leave, on a rest day or between jobs on 9 August 2011 is coded did not go to work even though they were employed that week, and someone who usually drives but caught a train that morning is counted as a train user. It also says nothing about trip length or how far the journey was, which are separate variables.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":136},{"n":"MTWP_16","d":"How the person travelled to work on 2016 Census day, 9 August 2016.","full":"How the person travelled to work on 2016 Census day, 9 August 2016. The 2016 Census Dictionary keeps the 2011 concept, defining the variable as \"up to three methods, or means, of travel to work on the day of the Census, for each person aged 15 years and over who was employed during the week before the Census\", and warns that a person's job and journey on Census day may not be the one they usually make. The response categories were unchanged from 2011; the renaming of taxi and tram options came later, in 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Method of Travel to Work (MTWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter41002016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Method of Travel to Work","t":"categorical","k":"Census method of travel to work code (MTWP), 2016","def":"A code standing for one, two or three travel modes used on the one journey, drawn from the Census method of travel to work classification, plus separate codes for walked only, worked at home, did not go to work, not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Method of Travel to Work (MTWP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter41002016","lim":"The 2016 code is a snapshot of a Tuesday in August, so it understates modes used on other days and cannot be compared with a person's 2011 or 2021 code as though it measured a settled commuting pattern. Non-response was 1.0% in 2016, twice the 2021 rate, so blanks are more common in this wave than in the next one.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":136},{"n":"MTWP_21","d":"How the person travelled to work on 2021 Census day, 10 August 2021.","full":"How the person travelled to work on 2021 Census day, 10 August 2021. The 2021 Census Dictionary defines it as \"up to three methods, or means, of travel to work on the day of the Census\" for employed people aged 15 and over. Two response labels changed for 2021, taxi becoming taxi or ride-share service and tram becoming tram or light rail, and non-response fell to 0.5% from 1.0% in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Method of travel to work (MTWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/transport/method-travel-work-mtwp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Method of Travel to Work","t":"categorical","k":"Census method of travel to work code (MTWP), 2021","def":"One of 237 codes. Single modes have their own codes and combinations of two or three modes have their own, for example 012 for train and bus and 067 for train, bus and ferry; walked only, worked at home, did not go to work, not stated and not applicable override any other selection.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Method of travel to work (MTWP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/transport/method-travel-work-mtwp","lim":"The 2021 figure cannot be read as normal commuting. Census night fell during COVID-19 lockdowns and stay-at-home orders in Greater Sydney and elsewhere, which pushed the worked at home and did not go to work categories far above their usual share, so a 2011 to 2021 comparison of public transport or car use on this column measures the pandemic as much as any change in travel behaviour.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":137},{"n":"MV1D_P_11","d":"Whether all, some or none of the household this person was counted in at the 2011 Census had moved in the previous year.","full":"Whether all, some or none of the household this person was counted in at the 2011 Census had moved in the previous year. The ABS says the variable \"combines data from questions 8 and 9 on the Census Household Form asking for a person's place of usual residence on Census Night and one year ago\", so it is derived from address answers rather than asked directly. Non-response was 1.9% in 2011, well below the 6.2% recorded in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS 2011 Census, Data Quality Statement: Household One Year Mobility Indicator (MV1D)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementsdwellingmv1d","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Household One Year Mobility Indicator of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census household one year mobility indicator code (MV1D), 2011","def":"A single household-level code: all residents aged one year and over had a different address a year ago, some did, or none did, with separate codes for at least one resident not stating an address and for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS 2011 Census, Data Quality Statement: Household One Year Mobility Indicator (MV1D)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementsdwellingmv1d","lim":"It is a property of the household, not of this person. Because the household is the one the person was counted in at that Census, the same person's indicator at two Censuses can describe two different households.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":138},{"n":"MV1D_P_16","d":"Whether all, some or none of the household this person was counted in at the 2016 Census had moved in the previous year.","full":"Whether all, some or none of the household this person was counted in at the 2016 Census had moved in the previous year. The ABS describes the 2016 variable as indicating whether \"all, some, or none of the residents of a household have changed address in the previous year\". Non-response jumped to 6.2% in 2016 from 1.9% in 2011 because the indicator is set to not stated whenever any one resident left the address question blank, so the 2016 column has far more missing households than either neighbouring wave.","dsrc":"ABS Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), Household One Year Mobility Indicator (MV1D)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features101282016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Household One Year Mobility Indicator of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census household one year mobility indicator code (MV1D), 2016","def":"A single household-level code: all residents aged one year and over had a different address a year ago, some did, or none did, with separate codes for at least one resident not stating an address and for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), Household One Year Mobility Indicator (MV1D)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features101282016","lim":"It is a household attribute attached to a person, so it cannot tell you whether this person moved, only what the household did as a group. In 2016 the high not stated rate also means an apparent fall in mobility between 2011 and 2016 on this column may be missing data rather than fewer moves.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":138},{"n":"MV1D_P_21","d":"Whether all, some or none of the household this person was counted in at the 2021 Census had moved in the previous year.","full":"Whether all, some or none of the household this person was counted in at the 2021 Census had moved in the previous year. The Census Dictionary defines it as a derived variable that \"indicates if all, some, or none of the usual residents of a household on 10 August 2021 have a different usual address compared to one year earlier\", excluding visitors and people temporarily absent. For 2021 the not stated label was rewritten as at least one resident did not state an address one year ago, and non-response fell back to 1.9% from 6.2% in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Household one year mobility indicator (MV1D)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/household-one-year-mobility-indicator-mv1d","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Household One Year Mobility Indicator of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census household one year mobility indicator code (MV1D), 2021","def":"A single household-level code: 1 all residents aged one year and over had a different address one year ago, 2 some did, 3 none did, & at least one resident did not state an address, and @ not applicable. It applies to family, group and lone person households.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Household one year mobility indicator (MV1D)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/household-one-year-mobility-indicator-mv1d","lim":"It is a property of the household, not of this person. It does not say whether this particular person moved, only whether all, some or none of the household did, so a mover in a household of stayers is coded some rather than identified. Because the household is the one the person was counted in at that Census, the same person's indicator at two Censuses can describe two different households.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":138},{"n":"MV5D_P_11","d":"Whether all, some or none of the household this person was counted in at the 2011 Census had moved in the previous five years.","full":"Whether all, some or none of the household this person was counted in at the 2011 Census had moved in the previous five years. The ABS says the variable \"combines data from questions 8, 9 and 10 on the Census Household Form asking for a person's place of usual residence on Census Night, one year ago and five years ago\", so it rests on a recalled 2006 address. Non-response was 2.9% in 2011.","dsrc":"ABS 2011 Census, Data Quality Statement: Household Five Years Mobility Indicator (MV5D)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementsdwellingmv5d","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Household Five Years Mobility Indicator of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census household five year mobility indicator code (MV5D), 2011","def":"A single household-level code: all residents aged five years and over had a different address five years ago, some did, or none did, with separate codes for at least one resident not stating an address and for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS 2011 Census, Data Quality Statement: Household Five Years Mobility Indicator (MV5D)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementsdwellingmv5d","lim":"A five-year window hides everything inside it: a household that moved twice and returned is coded the same as one that never moved, and this column cannot be differenced against MV1D_P_11 to count moves. The ABS describes the 2016 variable as one that \"indicates if all, some, or none of the residents of a household have changed address in the previous five years\". Non-response held at 2.9% in 2016, the same as 2011, so unlike the one-year indicator this column is stable in quality across those two waves.","dsrc":"ABS Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), Household Five Year Mobility Indicator (MV5D)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features101292016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Household Five Years Mobility Indicator of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census household five year mobility indicator code (MV5D), 2016","def":"A single household-level code: all residents aged five years and over had a different address five years ago, some did, or none did, with separate codes for at least one resident not stating an address and for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), Household Five Year Mobility Indicator (MV5D)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features101292016","lim":"It is set from the household as a group, so it cannot identify which member moved, and it is not a linkage variable: an ACLD person whose 2011 and 2016 records are linked has their own address change available directly, which this column neither confirms nor contradicts.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":139},{"n":"MV5D_P_21","d":"Whether all, some or none of the household this person was counted in at the 2021 Census had moved since 2016.","full":"Whether all, some or none of the household this person was counted in at the 2021 Census had moved since 2016. The Census Dictionary defines it as a derived variable that \"indicates if all, some, or none of the usual residents of a household on 10 August 2021 have a different usual address compared to five years earlier\". For 2021 the output category labels were rewritten to be easier to read and non-response fell to 2.5% from 2.9% in 2016; visitors and people temporarily absent are excluded.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Household five year mobility indicator (MV5D)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/household-five-year-mobility-indicator-mv5d","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Household Five Years Mobility Indicator of Household in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Census household five year mobility indicator code (MV5D), 2021","def":"A single household-level code: 1 all residents aged five years and over had a different address five years ago, 2 some did, 3 none did, & at least one resident did not state an address five years ago, and @ not applicable for visitor-only households, unoccupied dwellings and non-private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Household five year mobility indicator (MV5D)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/household-five-year-mobility-indicator-mv5d","lim":"The 2021 five-year window spans the COVID-19 period, so a household coded as having moved may have done so for reasons peculiar to 2020 and 2021. The 2011 Census Dictionary defines it as a variable that \"records whether a dwelling has an Internet connection, regardless of whether or not it is paid for by the household\", adding that where there is more than one connection the most frequently used type is reported and only one is recorded. This is a connection-type question; by 2016 the same mnemonic had been changed into a yes or no question about internet access, and it was dropped from the 2021 Census.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Internet Connection (NEDD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter7302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Internet Connection / Dwelling Internet Connection","t":"categorical","k":"Census type of internet connection code (NEDD), 2011","def":"One code per dwelling from a short list: no internet connection, broadband connection, dial-up connection or other connection, plus not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Internet Connection (NEDD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter7302011","lim":"It cannot be lined up with NEDD_P_16 as a time series. The 2011 codes distinguish broadband from dial-up at the dwelling, while the 2016 column only records whether anyone in the household accessed the internet from the dwelling at all, so a fall or rise between the two waves is a change of question rather than a change in connectivity. It also says nothing about mobile internet used away from the dwelling.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":140},{"n":"NEDD_P_16","d":"Whether anyone in the household accessed the internet from the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2016 Census.","full":"Whether anyone in the household accessed the internet from the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2016 Census. This includes accessing the internet through a desktop/laptop computer, mobile or smart phone, tablet, music or video player, gaming console, smart TV or any other devices.\" The 2011 column of the same name recorded the type of connection instead, and there is no 2021 column because the internet question was not asked in the 2021 Census.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Internet Connection (NEDD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter7302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Internet Connection / Dwelling Internet Connection","t":"categorical","k":"Census dwelling internet connection code (NEDD), 2016","def":"One code per dwelling: internet accessed from dwelling, internet not accessed from dwelling, not stated, or not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Internet Connection (NEDD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter7302016","lim":"A yes here does not mean a fixed connection. It is a quality and coverage flag, not a labour force measure: the household's actual employment picture is carried by the labour force status variables themselves.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD) microdata and data item lists","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Household Labour Force Status Derivation Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A small integer code standing for a combination of conditions in the household: whether any member aged 15 and over was temporarily absent on Census night and whether any member's labour force status was not stated. Someone in hospital, in student accommodation or in a hotel on that one night carries that code, so the column cannot be read as institutional residence, and it is not applicable for everyone counted in a private dwelling, which is most of the sample.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":143},{"n":"NPDD_P_16","d":"The kind of non-private dwelling the person was counted in on 2016 Census night.","full":"The kind of non-private dwelling the person was counted in on 2016 Census night. The 2016 Census Dictionary explains that \"non-private dwellings are establishments which provide a communal type of accommodation\", listing hotels, boarding houses, hospitals and child care institutions among them. The change at this Census was in how the type was obtained rather than in the categories: in mail-out areas ABS address canvassing officers recorded it while building the Address Register before Census night, and field officers corrected it during enumeration elsewhere. That makes the 2016 codes dependent on register quality in a way the 2011 codes were not.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Non-Private Dwelling (NPDD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter57102016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Non-Private Dwelling","t":"categorical","k":"Census type of non-private dwelling code (NPDD), 2016","def":"A two-digit code for the establishment type, covering hotels and motels, staff and nurses' quarters, boarding houses, boarding schools and residential colleges, hospitals, nursing homes and aged accommodation, welfare institutions and refuges, prisons and detention centres, religious institutions, and other or non-classifiable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Non-Private Dwelling (NPDD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter57102016","lim":"Because the 2016 type came from the Address Register rather than from the establishment on the night, an establishment that had changed use since it was canvassed can carry the wrong type. The column also cannot be used as a homelessness measure: it names the accommodation, not the person's circumstances, and the ABS homelessness estimates combine it with other variables.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":143},{"n":"NPDD_P_21","d":"The kind of non-private dwelling the person was counted in on 2021 Census night.","full":"The kind of non-private dwelling the person was counted in on 2021 Census night. The Census Dictionary says the variable \"classifies the Type of non-private dwelling in which people were counted on Census Night\". The 20 output categories are unchanged from 2016, but counts in the other welfare institution category rose because more complete address lists for homelessness accommodation were obtained from state and territory governments and non-government organisations.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Type of non-private dwelling (NPDD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/type-non-private-dwelling-npdd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Non-Private Dwelling","t":"categorical","k":"Census type of non-private dwelling code (NPDD), 2021","def":"One of 20 codes: 1 hotel, motel, bed and breakfast; 2 nurses' quarters; 3 staff quarters; 4 boarding house or private hotel; 5 boarding school; 6 residential college or hall of residence; 7 to 9 public, private and psychiatric hospitals; 10 hostel for the disabled; 11 nursing home; 12 accommodation for the retired or aged; 13 hostel for homeless, night shelter or refuge; 14 to 17 child care and corrective institutions and other welfare institutions; 18 immigration detention centre; 19 convent or monastery; 20 other and non-classifiable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Type of non-private dwelling (NPDD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/type-non-private-dwelling-npdd","lim":"The rise in welfare institution counts in 2021 reflects better address coverage, so a 2016 to 2021 increase on those codes is partly a coverage effect and not evidence that more people were in supported accommodation. As in earlier waves the code records the establishment a person was counted in on the night, not their usual living arrangement.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":143},{"n":"NPRD_P_11","d":"How many people usually lived in the private dwelling this person was counted in at the 2011 Census.","full":"How many people usually lived in the private dwelling this person was counted in at the 2011 Census. The ABS says the variable \"combines Relationship in Household (RLHP) and Count of Persons Temporarily Absent from Household (CPAD) to determine the number of persons usually resident in an occupied private dwelling\", so it is built during processing from questions 5 and 53 rather than asked. 2011 was the first Census to carry it in this form, and it was unchanged in 2016 and 2021.","dsrc":"ABS 2011 Census, Data Quality Statement: Number of Persons Usually Resident in Dwelling (NPRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementsdwellingnprd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Usual Residents in Dwelling in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Count of usual residents in dwelling, 1 to 8 or more (NPRD), 2011","def":"An integer from 1 to 8, where 8 means eight or more persons, plus a not applicable code for visitor-only households, unoccupied dwellings and non-private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS 2011 Census, Data Quality Statement: Number of Persons Usually Resident in Dwelling (NPRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementsdwellingnprd","lim":"It counts usual residents, not people present, so it will not match a headcount of the household's Census records when someone was away or a visitor was staying. Only up to three temporarily absent residents can be added back, so a household with four members away is undercounted.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":144},{"n":"NPRD_P_16","d":"How many people usually lived in the private dwelling this person was counted in at the 2016 Census.","full":"How many people usually lived in the private dwelling this person was counted in at the 2016 Census. The ABS defines it as a variable that \"counts the number of persons usually resident in an occupied private dwelling. It includes up to three residents who were temporarily absent from the household on Census night.\" It is derived during processing, so the ABS reports no non-response rate for it, unlike most 2016 household variables.","dsrc":"ABS Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), Number of Persons Usually Resident in Dwelling (NPRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features101322016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Usual Residents in Dwelling in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Count of usual residents in dwelling, 1 to 8 or more (NPRD), 2016","def":"An integer from 1 to 8, where 8 means eight or more persons, plus a not applicable code for visitor-only households, unoccupied dwellings and non-private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016 (cat. 2900.0), Number of Persons Usually Resident in Dwelling (NPRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features101322016","lim":"Because it is derived rather than reported, a blank means the dwelling was out of scope rather than that anyone failed to answer, so treating blanks as missing data biases household size downwards. Eight or more residents share one code, so average household size computed from this column is understated in the largest households.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":144},{"n":"NPRD_P_21","d":"How many people usually lived in the private dwelling this person was counted in at the 2021 Census.","full":"How many people usually lived in the private dwelling this person was counted in at the 2021 Census. The Census Dictionary defines it as a variable that \"counts the number of people who usually reside in an occupied private dwelling. It includes up to three residents who were temporarily absent from the household on Census Night.\" No change was made to the variable for 2021, so the 2011, 2016 and 2021 columns are on the same basis and can be compared directly.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of persons usually resident in dwelling (NPRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/number-persons-usually-resident-dwelling-nprd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Usual Residents in Dwelling in Which Person Was Enumerated","t":"categorical","k":"Count of usual residents in dwelling, 1 to 8 or more (NPRD), 2021","def":"Codes 1 to 8, where 1 to 7 are exact counts and 8 means eight or more persons, plus @ for not applicable, which covers visitor-only households, unoccupied dwellings and non-private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of persons usually resident in dwelling (NPRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/number-persons-usually-resident-dwelling-nprd","lim":"It is a count of the dwelling, not of the family, so a dwelling holding two families gives every member the same total and the column cannot be used as family size. The ABS defines the variable as follows: \"This variable describes the occupation or main job held by employed people aged 15 years and over in the week prior to Census Night.\" Occupations were coded to the six-digit level of ANZSCO First Edition Revision 1, which added 24 occupations and removed or merged eight against the first edition, and non-response was 0.8%, the same as 2006.","dsrc":"ABS 2011 Census, Data Quality Statement: Occupation (OCCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementspersonoccp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Occupation code","k":"ANZSCO occupation code, 2011 Census (ANZSCO First Edition Revision 1)","def":"A numeric ANZSCO code, up to six digits, from the Australian and New Zealand Standard Classification of Occupations First Edition Revision 1, with separate codes for inadequately described, not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS 2011 Census, Data Quality Statement: Occupation (OCCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/websitedbs/censushome.nsf/home/statementspersonoccp","lim":"It covers the main job only, so second jobs are invisible and a person's reported occupation can be the smaller half of their working week. It is also not applicable for anyone not employed in the week before that Census, so a blank means outside the labour force or unemployed rather than an unknown occupation. Comparing the 2011 code with another wave's is not safe at fine levels, because the ANZSCO edition differs between the 2011, 2016 and 2021 columns.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"OCCP_16","d":"The occupation of the person's main job at the 2016 Census, coded to ANZSCO Version 1.2.","full":"The occupation of the person's main job at the 2016 Census, coded to ANZSCO Version 1.2. Comparing the 2021 code with another wave's is not safe at fine levels, because the ANZSCO edition differs between the 2011, 2016 and 2021 columns.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"OCCP_FP_11","d":"The occupation of the person's coresident female parent at the 2011 Census, coded to ANZSCO First Edition Revision 1.","full":"The occupation of the person's coresident female parent at the 2011 Census, coded to ANZSCO First Edition Revision 1.
