POWP_SA2_21 on the same row is this same workplace rolled up to Statistical Area Level 2, which is the level most Census outputs use.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-work-powp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Destination Zone (Place of Work)","k":"2021 Census destination zone (place of work)","def":"A destination zone code from the 2021 Australian Statistical Geography Standard, the finest unit of the place of work hierarchy, which aggregates to SA2, SA3, SA4, greater capital city statistical area and state or territory.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-work-powp","lim":"Destination zone codes cannot be lined up with the 2011 or 2016 codes on neighbouring ACLD columns. The ABS states that boundaries and code structure both changed between Censuses, so a person whose zone code differs across waves has not necessarily moved workplace; local government area is the ABS recommendation for a time series. Non-response was 11.1 per cent in 2021, up from 10.0 per cent in 2016.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"POWP_SA2_11","d":"The SA2 the person worked in during the week before 2011 Census Night.","full":"The SA2 the person worked in during the week before 2011 Census Night. The ABS states that \"the address of the person's workplace in the week prior to Census Night is coded to a Destination Zone using an index provided by the State Transport Authorities\", and this column is that zone rolled up to SA2. The 2011 Census was the first to use the Australian Statistical Geography Standard for place of work, so the SA2 codes here belong to the 2011 edition of the ASGS and not to the 2016 or 2021 editions used by the later waves.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Place of Work (POWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter47402011","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 2 (Place of Work)","k":"ASGS 2011 Statistical Area Level 2 code (place of work)","def":"A nine digit ASGS 2011 SA2 code, obtained by aggregating the destination zone rather than by coding the workplace address to SA2 directly. Destination zones do not align with SA1 but do aggregate cleanly to SA2.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Place of Work (POWP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter47402011","lim":"It is the SA2 of one workplace, not of an employer. A person with two jobs is coded to the main job only, and an employee of a large firm is coded where they attended, so this column cannot count jobs by employer location. SA2 boundaries were also redrawn for 2016 and again for 2021, so comparing this column with POWP_SA2_16 needs a correspondence rather than a code match.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"POWP_SA2_16","d":"The SA2 the person worked in during the week before 2016 Census Night.","full":"The SA2 the person worked in during the week before 2016 Census Night. The ABS notes that for 2016 \"Destination Zones do not concord with Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s) but they do aggregate to Statistical Areas Level 2 (SA2s)\", and this column is the workplace destination zone taken up to that level. The 2016 destination zones were rebuilt from 2016 mesh blocks, so both the zones underneath this column and the SA2 codes themselves differ from the 2011 wave.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Place of Work (POWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter47402016","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 2 (Place of Work)","k":"ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 2 code (place of work)","def":"A nine digit ASGS 2016 SA2 code for the workplace, derived by aggregating the 2016 destination zone. Records with partial or missing workplace details carry an imputed zone, flagged in the Census by IFPOWP.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Place of Work (POWP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter47402016","lim":"It does not tell you whether the value was reported or imputed, because the ACLD carries the SA2 and not the imputation flag that the Census uses to mark made up workplaces. It also says nothing about the commute: pairing it with the same wave's usual residence gives a straight line, not the journey, and people who worked from home are coded to their home zone.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"POWP_SA2_21","d":"The SA2 the person worked in during the week before 2021 Census Night.","full":"The SA2 the person worked in during the week before 2021 Census Night. The ABS defines the parent variable as one that \"records the geographic area in which a person worked in the week before Census Night\", coded to a destination zone and released at SA2 and above. It is the comparable form of POWP_21 on the same row, because SA2 has a published correspondence between ASGS editions while the destination zone codes do not.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-work-powp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 2 (Place of Work)","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code (place of work)","def":"A nine digit ASGS 2021 SA2 code for the workplace, aggregated up from the 2021 destination zone, which in turn is built from 2021 mesh blocks.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-work-powp","lim":"The 2021 value is heavily affected by COVID-19 restrictions on 10 August 2021, when Greater Sydney and other areas were in lockdown, so people who normally travelled to an office were recorded at home. A shift in this column between 2016 and 2021 can therefore be a lockdown artefact rather than a change of job. Non-response was 11.1 per cent, the highest of the three waves.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"PUR1P_16","d":"Where the person usually lived at 9 August 2015, as reported at the 2016 Census.","full":"Where the person usually lived at 9 August 2015, as reported at the 2016 Census. The ABS defines it as the variable that \"records the geographic area in which a person usually lived one year ago (i.e. at August 9, 2015)\", output at SA2 and coded from the 2016 edition of the ASGS. For the 76.4 per cent of people whose address had not changed it was derived automatically from their 2016 place of usual residence rather than written on the form.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Place of Usual Residence One Year Ago (PUR1P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~PUR1P%20Place%20of%20Usual%20Residence%20One%20Year%20Ago~10070","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Place of Usual Residence One Year Ago","t":"categorical","k":"ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 2 code (usual residence one year earlier)","def":"An ASGS 2016 SA2 code, with supplementary categories for capital city undefined, state undefined, overseas, no usual address and not stated. It does not apply to children under one year of age.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Place of Usual Residence One Year Ago (PUR1P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~PUR1P%20Place%20of%20Usual%20Residence%20One%20Year%20Ago~10070","lim":"It records two points a year apart and misses everything in between, so a person who moved twice and returned looks like a person who never moved. Non-response rose sharply to 8.6 per cent in 2016 from 5.3 per cent in 2011, which means an apparent fall in mobility between those waves can be a reporting effect.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":149},{"n":"PUR1P_21","d":"Where the person usually lived at 10 August 2020, as reported at the 2021 Census.","full":"Where the person usually lived at 10 August 2020, as reported at the 2021 Census. The ABS defines it as the variable that \"records the geographic area in which a person usually lived one year before the Census\", output at SA2 on the 2021 ASGS. Two things changed from 2016: non-response fell to 6.0 per cent from 8.6 per cent, and the supplementary code once labelled Undefined state became State/Territory nfd.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence one year ago (PUR1P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-one-year-ago-pur1p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Place of Usual Residence One Year Ago","t":"categorical","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code (usual residence one year earlier)","def":"An ASGS 2021 SA2 code, with supplementary categories for Capital city nfd, State/Territory nfd, overseas, no usual address, migratory, off shore and shipping, not stated (&&&&) and not applicable (@@@@).","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence one year ago (PUR1P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-one-year-ago-pur1p","lim":"The year it covers, August 2020 to August 2021, sits inside the pandemic, when international borders were shut and internal moves were interrupted by lockdowns, so it is a poor guide to normal one year mobility. It also cannot be compared code for code with PUR1P_16, because SA2 boundaries were redrawn between the 2016 and 2021 editions of the ASGS.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":149},{"n":"PUR5P_16","d":"Where the person usually lived at 9 August 2011, as reported at the 2016 Census.","full":"Where the person usually lived at 9 August 2011, as reported at the 2016 Census. The ABS defines it as the variable that \"records the geographic area in which a person usually lived five years ago (i.e. at August 9, 2011)\", output at SA2 on the 2016 ASGS and covering usual residents aged five and over. In 2016, 52.4 per cent reported the same address as on Census Night, 33.9 per cent another Australian address and 6.3 per cent an overseas address.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Place of Usual Residence Five Years Ago (PUR5P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~PUR5P%20Place%20of%20Usual%20Residence%20Five%20Years%20Ago~10071","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Place of Usual Residence Five Years Ago","t":"categorical","k":"ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 2 code (usual residence five years earlier)","def":"An ASGS 2016 SA2 code, with categories for capital city undefined, state undefined, overseas, no usual address and not stated. It is not applicable to children under five years of age.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Place of Usual Residence Five Years Ago (PUR5P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~PUR5P%20Place%20of%20Usual%20Residence%20Five%20Years%20Ago~10071","lim":"In the ACLD it is a self report about 2011 that can disagree with the person's own linked 2011 Census record, which gives the address they actually stated at the time. Where the two disagree, the linked record is the better evidence and this column measures recall. Non-response was 8.0 per cent in 2016, up from 6.5 per cent in 2011.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":149},{"n":"PUR5P_21","d":"Where the person usually lived at 10 August 2016, as reported at the 2021 Census.","full":"Where the person usually lived at 10 August 2016, as reported at the 2021 Census. The ABS defines it as the variable that \"records the geographic area in which a person usually lived five years before the Census\", output at SA2 on the 2021 ASGS for people aged five and over. Non-response fell to 6.9 per cent from 8.0 per cent in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence five years ago (PUR5P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-five-years-ago-pur5p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Place of Usual Residence Five Years Ago","t":"categorical","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code (usual residence five years earlier)","def":"An ASGS 2021 SA2 code, with supplementary categories for Capital city nfd, State/Territory nfd, overseas, no usual residence, migratory, off shore and shipping, not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence five years ago (PUR5P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-five-years-ago-pur5p","lim":"It is a recalled address, and the ACLD already holds the person's stated 2016 address in the linked 2016 record, so treating this column as a second measurement rather than the truth avoids double counting a move. The five year gap also hides return moves entirely, and the 2016 to 2021 window includes closed international borders, which suppresses the overseas category.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":149},{"n":"QALFP_11","d":"The subject area of the person's highest completed non-school qualification at the 2011 Census.","full":"The subject area of the person's highest completed non-school qualification at the 2011 Census. The ABS says the variable \"describes the field of study of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", coded to the Australian Standard Classification of Education field of education classification and applicable to people aged 15 and over who stated a completed qualification. QALLP_11 on the same row gives the level of that same qualification, so the pair describes one credential and not two.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8152011","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-School Qualification: Field of Study","k":"ASCED 2001 field of education code","def":"A six digit ASCED field of education code, nested inside 12 broad two digit fields running from Natural and Physical Sciences to Mixed Field Programmes, with 435 categories at the six digit level. Supplementary codes cover inadequately described, not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8152011","lim":"It describes the highest qualification only, so a person with an engineering degree and a later graduate diploma in management appears under management and their engineering training disappears. Non-response was 16.7 per cent in 2011, and the not applicable code lumps together people with no qualification, people still studying and people under 15.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"QALFP_16","d":"The subject area of the person's highest completed non-school qualification at the 2016 Census.","full":"The subject area of the person's highest completed non-school qualification at the 2016 Census. The ABS defines it as the variable that \"describes the field of study of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", coded to ASCED 2001 and applicable to people aged 15 and over who stated a completed qualification. The ABS records that \"no changes were made for 2016\", so this wave is directly comparable in concept with QALFP_11, and non-response improved to 15.1 per cent from 16.7 per cent.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~QALFP%20Non-School%20Qualification%20Field%20of%20Study~10073","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-School Qualification: Field of Study","k":"ASCED 2001 field of education code","def":"A six digit ASCED 2001 field of education code within 12 broad fields, with 83 narrow four digit categories and 435 detailed six digit categories. Supplementary codes mark inadequately described, not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor responses.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~QALFP%20Non-School%20Qualification%20Field%20of%20Study~10073","lim":"It cannot be read as a count of graduates in a field. Among people who ticked yes to holding a qualification the field was still unstated for 2.0 per cent, and anyone whose highest qualification is in a different field from their working life is coded to the qualification, not the job, so it is not a proxy for the industry or occupation columns beside it.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"QALFP_21","d":"The subject area of the person's highest completed non-school qualification at the 2021 Census.","full":"The subject area of the person's highest completed non-school qualification at the 2021 Census. The ABS defines it as the variable that \"describes the field of study of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", still coded to ASCED 2001. For 2021 the ABS made \"minor instructional text changes to the main field of study question ... to provide guidance for people with double degrees\" and refreshed the examples, and overall non-response fell to 12.3 per cent from 15.1 per cent in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: field of study (QALFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-field-study-qalfp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Non-School Qualification: Field of Study","k":"ASCED 2001 field of education code","def":"A six digit ASCED 2001 field of education code within 12 broad fields, with supplementary codes 00 for inadequately described, && for not stated, @@ for not applicable and VV for overseas visitors.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: field of study (QALFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-field-study-qalfp","lim":"A person with a double degree still gets one field, so the 2021 guidance changed which of the two is reported rather than allowing both, and a shift between 2016 and 2021 in a field's share can come from that instruction rather than from study patterns. The improvement in overall non-response also does not carry through: among people who reported holding a qualification, non-response was 2.3 per cent in 2021 against 2.0 per cent in 2016.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"QALFP_FP_11","d":"The field of study of the highest non-school qualification held by the person's female parent at the 2011 Census.","full":"The field of study of the highest non-school qualification held by the person's female parent at the 2011 Census. The base variable \"describes the field of study of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", coded to the ASCED field of education classification; this column copies that value across from the record of the person coded as female parent in the same family. It is one of the parental background columns the ACLD attaches so that a child's later outcomes can be read against the household they grew up in.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8152011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Field of Study for Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 field of education code","def":"A six digit ASCED field of education code taken from the female parent's record, inside 12 broad fields and 435 six digit categories, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8152011","lim":"It exists only where a female parent was enumerated in the same household on 2011 Census Night and coded into the same family, so an absent, deceased or separately living mother reads as not applicable rather than as unknown. Female parent is a family coding role, not a biological relationship, so a stepmother or an adoptive mother fills the same column.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":150},{"n":"QALFP_FP_16","d":"The field of study of the highest non-school qualification held by the person's female parent at the 2016 Census.","full":"The field of study of the highest non-school qualification held by the person's female parent at the 2016 Census. The ABS definition of the base variable is unchanged from 2011, since \"no changes were made for 2016\", so the mother's field at this wave lines up conceptually with QALFP_FP_11. The value is her own 2016 Census response, carried onto the child's record for people living with her on Census Night.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~QALFP%20Non-School%20Qualification%20Field%20of%20Study~10073","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Field of Study for Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 field of education code","def":"A six digit ASCED 2001 field of education code from the female parent's 2016 record, inside 12 broad fields, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~QALFP%20Non-School%20Qualification%20Field%20of%20Study~10073","lim":"Comparing this column with QALFP_FP_11 for the same child does not track the mother's study, because the child may be living with a different female parent, or with none, at the two waves. Overall non-response on the underlying question was 15.1 per cent in 2016, and that missingness lands on the child's record without any flag distinguishing it from having no mother present.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":150},{"n":"QALFP_FP_21","d":"The field of study of the highest non-school qualification held by the person's female parent at the 2021 Census.","full":"The field of study of the highest non-school qualification held by the person's female parent at the 2021 Census. The base variable \"describes the field of study of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\" and is still coded to ASCED 2001, but the 2021 question added guidance for people with double degrees, which can change which field a mother with two degrees is coded to. Non-response on the underlying question improved to 12.3 per cent.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: field of study (QALFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-field-study-qalfp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Field of Study for Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 field of education code","def":"A six digit ASCED 2001 field of education code from the female parent's 2021 record, with supplementary codes 00 inadequately described, && not stated, @@ not applicable and VV overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: field of study (QALFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-field-study-qalfp","lim":"By 2021 most people sampled in 2011 are adults living away from their parents, so this column is empty for the majority of the panel and is not a fixed measure of family background that can be carried across waves. The base variable \"describes the field of study of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", coded to the ASCED field of education classification, and this column carries the value from the record of the person coded as male parent in the same family. Read it beside QALFP_FP_11 to get both parents, and beside QALLP_MP_11 for the level of the same qualification.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8152011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Field of Study for Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 field of education code","def":"A six digit ASCED field of education code taken from the male parent's 2011 record, within 12 broad two digit fields and 435 six digit categories, plus supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8152011","lim":"Fathers are missing from this column more often than mothers, because it depends on the male parent being enumerated in the same household, and children in sole mother families have no male parent record at all. The ABS confirms that \"no changes were made for 2016\" to the field of study question, so the father's field at this wave is measured on the same basis as at 2011 and the two can be compared. The value is his own 2016 response, attached to the child's record where they were enumerated in the same family.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~QALFP%20Non-School%20Qualification%20Field%20of%20Study~10073","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Field of Study for Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 field of education code","def":"A six digit ASCED 2001 field of education code from the male parent's 2016 record, within 12 broad fields, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~QALFP%20Non-School%20Qualification%20Field%20of%20Study~10073","lim":"It cannot separate a father who reported no qualification from one who did not answer or was not present: all three arrive as an unusable value on the child's row. The base variable \"describes the field of study of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", coded to ASCED 2001, with 2021 adding instructions for double degrees and refreshed field examples drawn from 2016 prevalence. Only people still living with a male parent in 2021 carry a value.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: field of study (QALFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-field-study-qalfp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Field of Study for Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 field of education code","def":"A six digit ASCED 2001 field of education code from the male parent's 2021 record, within 12 broad fields and with supplementary codes 00, &&, @@ and VV.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: field of study (QALFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-field-study-qalfp","lim":"The 2021 field examples printed on the form were rewritten, and examples shift what people write, so a change in the distribution of fathers' fields between 2016 and 2021 is not safely read as a change in what fathers studied. The column also cannot identify a father who lives elsewhere but is still involved, since Census family coding works on the household enumerated on Census Night.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":150},{"n":"QALFP_SP_11","d":"The field of study of the highest non-school qualification held by the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census.","full":"The field of study of the highest non-school qualification held by the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census. The base variable \"describes the field of study of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", coded to the ASCED field of education classification, and this column copies the partner's own answer onto the respondent's row. Paired with the person's own QALFP_11 it supports work on educational assortative matching within couples.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8152011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Field of Study for Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 field of education code","def":"A six digit ASCED field of education code from the partner's 2011 record, inside 12 broad two digit fields, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8152011","lim":"It covers registered marriages and de facto partners living in the same dwelling only, so a partner living apart leaves it empty and a person can be partnered without appearing so. It also gives no marriage or relationship start date, so it cannot say whether the qualification predates the partnership.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":150},{"n":"QALFP_SP_16","d":"The field of study of the highest non-school qualification held by the person's spouse or partner at the 2016 Census.","full":"The field of study of the highest non-school qualification held by the person's spouse or partner at the 2016 Census. The underlying question was unchanged for 2016, since the ABS records that \"no changes were made for 2016\", so the partner's field is measured the same way as at 2011. It comes from the partner's own 2016 form, attached to the respondent because both were enumerated in the same dwelling.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~QALFP%20Non-School%20Qualification%20Field%20of%20Study~10073","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Field of Study for Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 field of education code","def":"A six digit ASCED 2001 field of education code from the partner's 2016 record, inside 12 broad fields, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Non-School Qualification: Field of Study (QALFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~QALFP%20Non-School%20Qualification%20Field%20of%20Study~10073","lim":"A different value at 2016 from 2011 usually means a different partner rather than new study, and the ACLD carries no partner identifier that would let you tell the two apart. The base variable \"describes the field of study of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\" and remains on ASCED 2001, with 2021 adding guidance for double degrees that can change which field a partner with two degrees is coded to. Non-response on the question fell to 12.3 per cent from 15.1 per cent.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: field of study (QALFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-field-study-qalfp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Field of Study for Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 field of education code","def":"A six digit ASCED 2001 field of education code from the partner's 2021 record, within 12 broad fields, with supplementary codes 00 inadequately described, && not stated, @@ not applicable and VV overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: field of study (QALFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-field-study-qalfp","lim":"It says what the partner studied, not what the couple does, so pairing it with the household income columns without also holding occupation and hours will attribute earnings to a field of study that neither person works in. The 2021 double degree instruction also breaks a strict field for field comparison with the 2016 column.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":150},{"n":"QALLP_11","d":"How high the person's highest completed non-school qualification reached at the 2011 Census.","full":"How high the person's highest completed non-school qualification reached at the 2011 Census. The ABS entry \"describes the level of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", coded to the Australian Standard Classification of Education level of education classification, for people aged 15 and over who stated a completed qualification. QALFP_11 beside it gives the subject of that same qualification, and HEAP combines this with school attainment where a reader wants a single ranking.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Level of Education (QALLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Level of Education","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 level of education code","def":"A three digit ASCED level of education code running from Postgraduate Degree Level through to Certificate I and II Level, with 5 one digit, 13 two digit and 11 three digit categories in the 2011 structure, plus 011 inadequately described, &&& not stated and @@@ not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Level of Education (QALLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8202011","lim":"It cannot be used to count qualification holders, because the not applicable code covers people with no qualification, people still studying and people under 15 all at once, and non-response was 17.1 per cent. A person's level can also fall between waves if they report a different qualification, which is a reporting change and not a lost credential.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":151},{"n":"QALLP_16","d":"How high the person's highest completed non-school qualification reached at the 2016 Census.","full":"How high the person's highest completed non-school qualification reached at the 2016 Census. The ABS defines it as \"the level of a person's highest completed non-school qualification. Non-school qualifications are educational attainments other than those of a pre-primary, primary or secondary education level\", coded to ASCED. The question was unchanged from 2011, and non-response improved to 16.0 per cent from 17.1 per cent, so QALLP_11 and this column can be compared directly.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Non-School Qualification: Level of Education (QALLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features100742016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Level of Education","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 level of education code","def":"A three digit ASCED 2001 level of education code, from 1 Postgraduate Degree Level down to 5 Certificate Level, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor. The ABS defines it as the variable that \"describes the level of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", coded to ASCED 2001. The change from 2016 is that undergraduate certificates, a new short credential, are coded to 420 Diploma Level nfd rather than given a level of their own, and non-response fell to 12.4 per cent from 16.0 per cent.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: level of education (QALLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-level-education-qallp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Level of Education","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 level of education code","def":"A three digit ASCED 2001 level of education code from Postgraduate Degree Level through Certificate Level, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor. It is mainly coded from the written level and field responses, with the qualification indicator, year of school completion and pre-1998 completion date used to resolve the rest.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: level of education (QALLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-level-education-qallp","lim":"The 2021 treatment of undergraduate certificates places a sub-diploma credential inside Diploma Level nfd, so a small rise in diploma counts between 2016 and 2021 can be a coding decision rather than more diplomas. The base variable \"describes the level of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", coded to ASCED, and this column carries that value from the record of the person coded as female parent in the same family. It is the usual measure of maternal education in ACLD work on intergenerational mobility.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Level of Education (QALLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Level of Education for Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 level of education code","def":"A three digit ASCED level of education code from the female parent's 2011 record, running from Postgraduate Degree Level to Certificate I and II Level, with 011 inadequately described, &&& not stated and @@@ not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Level of Education (QALLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8202011","lim":"It is not a lifetime measure of maternal education, because it captures where the mother had reached in 2011 and mothers do complete qualifications later. The ABS defines the base variable as \"the level of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\" and made no change to the question for 2016, so a mother's level at this wave sits on the same scale as at 2011. The value is her own 2016 response, attached to people enumerated with her on Census Night.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Non-School Qualification: Level of Education (QALLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features100742016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Level of Education for Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 level of education code","def":"A three digit ASCED 2001 level of education code from the female parent's 2016 record, from Postgraduate Degree Level down to Certificate Level, with the standard supplementary codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Non-School Qualification: Level of Education (QALLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features100742016","lim":"A rise between QALLP_FP_11 and this column does not prove the mother studied further, since the child may be living with a different female parent at the two waves and the ACLD supplies no parent identifier to check. The base variable \"describes the level of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", coded to ASCED 2001, with 2021 folding the new undergraduate certificate into 420 Diploma Level nfd. Coverage is thin at this wave because most of the original 2011 sample no longer lives with a parent.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: level of education (QALLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-level-education-qallp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Level of Education for Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 level of education code","def":"A three digit ASCED 2001 level of education code from the female parent's 2021 record, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: level of education (QALLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-level-education-qallp","lim":"For an adult respondent still living with their mother in 2021, the column is present for a reason, and that reason is correlated with the outcomes people study, so treating a non-missing value as random maternal education selects on co-residence. With QALLP_FP_11 it gives the pair of parental education levels most studies use as family background.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Level of Education (QALLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Level of Education for Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 level of education code","def":"A three digit ASCED level of education code from the male parent's 2011 record, spanning Postgraduate Degree Level to Certificate I and II Level, with codes 011, &&& and @@@ for inadequately described, not stated and not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Non-School Qualification: Level of Education (QALLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8202011","lim":"Taking the higher of the two parental values as a household measure quietly penalises sole parent families, where only one column can ever be filled. The base variable \"describes the level of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", coded to ASCED 2001, and in 2021 undergraduate certificates are coded to 420 Diploma Level nfd. Non-response on the question dropped to 12.4 per cent, so more partners carry a usable level at this wave than at 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: level of education (QALLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-level-education-qallp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Level of Education for Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 level of education code","def":"A three digit ASCED 2001 level of education code from the partner's 2021 record, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: level of education (QALLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-level-education-qallp","lim":"The improvement in non-response between 2016 and 2021 means more partners have a stated level, so an apparent rise in partner education across waves partly reflects better reporting rather than more study. The column also holds only the highest qualification, so a partner who added a certificate to an existing degree shows no change at all.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":151},{"n":"RA_UR_11","d":"Remoteness Areas (Usual residence)","vp":"official","od":"Remoteness Areas (Usual residence)","k":"asgs_remoteness_area_2011","def":"The source publishes this value domain.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS ASGS 2011 Remoteness Areas (geo.abs.gov.au ASGS2011/RA), with the unlinked code from the ABS ACLD 2011-16-21 detailed microdata data item list (codeframe ACLD191)","url":"https://geo.abs.gov.au/arcgis/rest/services/ASGS2011/RA/MapServer/0/query?where=1%3D1&outFields=ra_code,ra_name,state_code&returnGeometry=false&f=json","lim":"The source defines the value domain. Frequency information is not included.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":152},{"n":"RA_UR_16","d":"Remoteness Areas (Usual residence)","vp":"official","od":"Remoteness Areas (Usual residence)","k":"asgs_remoteness_area_2016","def":"The source publishes this value domain.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Statistical Geography Standard 2016 Remoteness Areas, with the unlinked-record code from the ABS ACLD detailed microdata data item list","url":"https://geo.abs.gov.au/arcgis/rest/services/ASGS2016/RA/MapServer","lim":"The source defines the value domain. Frequency information is not included.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":152},{"n":"RA_UR_21","d":"The remoteness class of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census.","full":"The remoteness class of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census. The ABS defines the structure so that \"Remoteness Areas (RA) divide Australia into five classes of remoteness which are characterised by a measure of relative geographic access to services\", built by grouping SA1s on their average ARIA+ score. The UR suffix marks it as usual residence rather than place of enumeration, so it is where the person lived and not necessarily where they spent Census Night.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Remoteness Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/remoteness-structure/remoteness-areas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Remoteness Areas (Usual residence)","k":"ASGS 2021 Remoteness Area","def":"A single digit under ASGS Edition 3: 0 Major Cities of Australia, 1 Inner Regional Australia, 2 Outer Regional Australia, 3 Remote Australia and 4 Very Remote Australia. ARIA+ scores are produced by the Australian Centre for Housing Research and rest on road distance from populated places to service centres.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Remoteness Areas","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/remoteness-structure/remoteness-areas","lim":"The classes were re-derived for the 2021 edition using 2021 population and urban centre boundaries, so places changed class without moving: parts of the Sunshine Coast and Wollongong shifted from Inner Regional to Major Cities, while Mount Gambier and Devonport went from Inner Regional to Outer Regional. A person coded differently at 2016 and 2021 may not have moved at all. Remoteness also measures road access to services, not disadvantage, and is not a substitute for a SEIFA index.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"RELP_11","d":"The religion the person reported at the 2011 Census.","full":"The religion the person reported at the 2011 Census. The ABS says the variable \"records a person's religious affiliation\" and that \"answering this Census question is optional\", coded to the Australian Standard Classification of Religious Groups, Second Edition, Revision 1. In 2011 the form still listed the named religions before the no religion option, which is the ordering the ABS changed for 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Religious Affiliation","t":"categorical","k":"ASCRG religious group code","def":"A four digit ASCRG code, with 137 categories at the four digit level in the Second Edition Revision 1 arranged under broad groups, plus supplementary codes for not stated, not defined and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8302011","lim":"It records affiliation as stated on a form, not belief, practice or attendance, so it cannot distinguish an active member of a congregation from someone recording a family tradition. Because the question is optional, 8.6 per cent left it blank in 2011, and a blank is not evidence of having no religion, which is its own separate category.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":153},{"n":"RELP_16","d":"The religion the person reported at the 2016 Census.","full":"The religion the person reported at the 2016 Census. The ABS states that the variable \"records a person's religious affiliation and is applicable to all persons\", and 2016 brought two changes at once: the classification was revised to ASCRG 2016, taking four digit religious groups from 137 to 151, and no religion was moved to the first response option on the form. Non-response rose to 9.1 per cent from 8.6 per cent in 2011.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features100752016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Religious Affiliation","t":"categorical","k":"ASCRG religious group code","def":"A four digit ASCRG 2016 code within broad groups covering Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, Other Religions and Secular Beliefs and Other Spiritual Beliefs and No Religious Affiliation, with supplementary codes for not stated and inadequately described.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features100752016","lim":"The jump in no religion between 2011 and 2016 is confounded by the form change, because putting the option first raises the share who select it, so a person switching from a religion at 2011 to no religion at 2016 in the ACLD is not clean evidence of a change in belief. The classification revision also regrouped some four digit categories, so a code for code match against RELP_11 will misplace a small number of people.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":154},{"n":"RELP_21","d":"The religion the person reported at the 2021 Census.","full":"The religion the person reported at the 2021 Census. The ABS defines it as the variable that \"records a person's religious affiliation. Answering this Census question is optional\", still coded to ASCRG 2016, so the classification matches RELP_16 and only the form changed. The 2021 mark boxes were reordered on 2016 prevalence, with Islam moving from seventh to fifth and Presbyterian from fifth to seventh, while no religion stayed first, and non-response fell to 6.9 per cent.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Religious affiliation (RELP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/religious-affiliation-relp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Religious Affiliation","t":"categorical","k":"ASCRG religious group code","def":"A four digit ASCRG 2016 code, 151 categories at the four digit level, grouped under Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, Other Religions and Secular Beliefs and Other Spiritual Beliefs and No Religious Affiliation.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Religious affiliation (RELP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/religious-affiliation-relp","lim":"Reordering the mark boxes changes how often a religion is selected, so a shift in the shares of Islam or Presbyterian between 2016 and 2021 is partly an artefact of where they sat on the form. The column also records one affiliation per person, so it cannot represent someone with more than one, and it says nothing about how strongly the affiliation is held.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":154},{"n":"RELP_FP_11","d":"The religion reported by the person's female parent at the 2011 Census.","full":"The religion reported by the person's female parent at the 2011 Census. The base variable \"records a person's religious affiliation\" and is coded to ASCRG Second Edition Revision 1; this column carries the answer given by the person coded as female parent in the same family. It lets a child's own religion at a later wave be compared with the mother's at 2011.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Religious Affiliation of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCRG religious group code","def":"A four digit ASCRG Second Edition Revision 1 code from the female parent's 2011 record, drawn from 137 four digit categories, with supplementary codes for not stated, not defined and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8302011","lim":"The religion question is optional, so a mother who declined leaves the child's row blank in exactly the same way as a mother who was not enumerated in the household, and the two cannot be separated. A parent's stated religion is also often the one recorded for the whole household by whoever filled in the form, so it may not be her own independent answer.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":155},{"n":"RELP_FP_16","d":"The religion reported by the person's female parent at the 2016 Census.","full":"The religion reported by the person's female parent at the 2016 Census. The ABS notes the base variable \"records a person's religious affiliation and is applicable to all persons\", and for 2016 the classification became ASCRG 2016 and no religion moved to the first response option. Both changes apply to the mother's answer here, so it is not on the same footing as RELP_FP_11.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features100752016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Religious Affiliation of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCRG religious group code","def":"A four digit ASCRG 2016 code from the female parent's 2016 record, drawn from 151 four digit categories under the broad religious and secular groups, with supplementary codes for not stated and inadequately described.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features100752016","lim":"A mother recorded with a religion at 2011 and none at 2016 is the pattern the 2016 form change manufactures, so this column should not be used on its own to show mothers leaving religion. Non-response on the question rose to 9.1 per cent in 2016, and that missingness is silent on the child's record.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":156},{"n":"RELP_FP_21","d":"The religion reported by the person's female parent at the 2021 Census.","full":"The religion reported by the person's female parent at the 2021 Census. The base variable \"records a person's religious affiliation\" and remains on ASCRG 2016, so codes line up with RELP_FP_16 even though the mark boxes were reordered for 2021. Few people in the ACLD panel still live with a parent by 2021, so this column is sparse.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Religious affiliation (RELP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/religious-affiliation-relp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Religious Affiliation of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCRG religious group code","def":"A four digit ASCRG 2016 code from the female parent's 2021 record, 151 categories at the four digit level, with supplementary codes for not stated and inadequately described.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Religious affiliation (RELP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/religious-affiliation-relp","lim":"The people who still have a value here in 2021 are mostly young adults living at home or older people living with an elderly parent, so the column describes an unusual slice of households rather than family background in general. It also cannot show whether the respondent was raised in that religion, since it is the mother's affiliation in 2021 and not at the respondent's childhood.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":156},{"n":"RELP_MP_11","d":"The religion reported by the person's male parent at the 2011 Census.","full":"The religion reported by the person's male parent at the 2011 Census. The base variable \"records a person's religious affiliation\", coded to ASCRG Second Edition Revision 1, and this column carries the answer from the person coded as male parent in the same family. With RELP_FP_11 it shows whether both parents in a household reported the same religion.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Religious Affiliation of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCRG religious group code","def":"A four digit ASCRG Second Edition Revision 1 code from the male parent's 2011 record, from 137 four digit categories, with supplementary codes for not stated, not defined and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8302011","lim":"Disagreement between this column and the mother's is weak evidence of a mixed religion household, because one household form is usually completed by one person and the entries can reflect that person's assumptions about the others. Sole mother households leave it permanently empty, so households where it is populated are not a random selection.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":157},{"n":"RELP_MP_16","d":"The religion reported by the person's male parent at the 2016 Census.","full":"The religion reported by the person's male parent at the 2016 Census. The ABS records that the base variable \"records a person's religious affiliation and is applicable to all persons\", and the 2016 Census both revised the classification to ASCRG 2016 and moved no religion to the top of the response list. The father's 2016 answer therefore sits on a different form design from his 2011 one.","dsrc":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features100752016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Religious Affiliation of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCRG religious group code","def":"A four digit ASCRG 2016 code from the male parent's 2016 record, drawn from 151 four digit categories across the broad religious and secular groups, with supplementary codes for not stated and inadequately described.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2900.0main+features100752016","lim":"It cannot support a claim that fathers became less religious between 2011 and 2016, because the response option order changed in a direction that raises no religion. The 9.1 per cent non-response in 2016 also arrives on the child's row indistinguishably from having no male parent in the household.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":158},{"n":"RELP_MP_21","d":"The religion reported by the person's male parent at the 2021 Census.","full":"The religion reported by the person's male parent at the 2021 Census. The base variable \"records a person's religious affiliation\", still coded to ASCRG 2016, so a code here is directly comparable with RELP_MP_16 even though the order of the mark boxes changed. Non-response on the question fell to 6.9 per cent in 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Religious affiliation (RELP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/religious-affiliation-relp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Religious Affiliation of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"ASCRG religious group code","def":"A four digit ASCRG 2016 code from the male parent's 2021 record, 151 categories at the four digit level, with supplementary codes for not stated and inadequately described.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Religious affiliation (RELP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/religious-affiliation-relp","lim":"The fall in non-response between waves means a father who is blank in 2016 and coded in 2021 may simply have answered the second time, so a first appearance of a religion is not a conversion. The column is also empty for the large majority of the 2021 panel, who no longer live with a father, and that emptiness carries no information about his religion.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":158},{"n":"RELP_SP_11","d":"The religion reported by the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census.","full":"The religion reported by the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census. The base variable \"records a person's religious affiliation\" and \"answering this Census question is optional\", coded to ASCRG Second Edition Revision 1; this column carries the partner's own answer onto the respondent's row. Set against the person's own RELP_11 it is the standard way to identify religiously matched and mixed couples in the 2011 wave.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Religious Affiliation of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"ASCRG religious group code","def":"A four digit ASCRG Second Edition Revision 1 code from the partner's 2011 record, from 137 four digit categories, with supplementary codes for not stated, not defined and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Religious Affiliation (RELP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter8302011","lim":"Matching on this column identifies couples who reported the same religion on one household form, which is not the same as couples who share a faith, since one person often completes the form for both. It also requires the partner to be enumerated in the same dwelling, so couples living apart never appear as matched or mixed.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":157},{"n":"RELP_SP_16","d":"The religion reported at the 2016 Census by the person's spouse or partner, carried onto this record from the partner's own answer.","full":"The religion reported at the 2016 Census by the person's spouse or partner, carried onto this record from the partner's own answer. The ABS defines the source variable as one that \"records a person's religious affiliation\" and states that \"Answering this Census question is optional\"; non-response was 9.1% in 2016. The column is filled only where a spouse or partner was enumerated in the same family on Census Night 2016, and it sits beside RELP_16 for the person's own answer and RELP_FP_16 and RELP_MP_16 for a parent's.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Religious affiliation (RELP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/religious-affiliation-relp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Religious Affiliation of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"ASCRG religious group code (spouse or partner)","def":"A code from the Australian Standard Classification of Religious Groups, the same code set as the person's own religion column, with a separate 'No religion' code and an 'Inadequately described' code for written answers that cannot be classified.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Religious affiliation (RELP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/religious-affiliation-relp","lim":"A blank does not mean the partner has no religion. 'No religion' is a code in its own right, so an empty cell means no partner in the family, a partner who was not enumerated, or a partner who left the optional question blank, and those three cases cannot be told apart here.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":158},{"n":"RELP_SP_21","d":"The religion reported at the 2021 Census by the person's spouse or partner, carried onto this record from the partner's own answer.","full":"The religion reported at the 2021 Census by the person's spouse or partner, carried onto this record from the partner's own answer. The ABS codes the source variable to the \"Australian Standard Classification of Religious Groups (ASCRG), 2016\" and reports non-response of 6.9% in 2021, down from 9.1% in 2016. For 2021 the order of the mark-box categories on the form was updated on 2016 frequency data, so a small shift between waves can reflect the form rather than the household.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Religious affiliation (RELP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/religious-affiliation-relp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Religious Affiliation of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"ASCRG 2016 religious group code (spouse or partner)","def":"A code from the Australian Standard Classification of Religious Groups, 2016 edition, the same code set as the person's own RELP_21 column, including a 'No religion' code and 'Inadequately described' for written answers that cannot be classified.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Religious affiliation (RELP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/religious-affiliation-relp","lim":"It cannot stand in for the household's religion. The column describes one other person, so in a dwelling with several couples or with adult children it says nothing about anyone but the partner, and where no partner was enumerated the cell is empty for a reason that has nothing to do with belief.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":158},{"n":"RLGP_11","d":"Each person's relationship to their family reference person at the 2011 Census, on the variant that keeps grandchildren separate.","full":"Each person's relationship to their family reference person at the 2011 Census, on the variant that keeps grandchildren separate. The ABS says RLGP \"has an extra grandchild type, being 'Dependent student grandchild'\" and \"classifies lone grandparents (with no parent-child relationship present in the household) as 'Lone parent'\", which is what distinguishes it from RLHP_11 on the same row. It applies to people present in an occupied private dwelling, so anyone counted in a hospital, hostel or hotel in 2011 has no code here.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Relationship in household (including grandchildren) (RLGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/relationship-household-including-grandchildren-rlgp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Relationship in Household (including grandchildren)","t":"categorical","k":"Census household relationship code (grandchildren separated)","def":"A relationship code on the ABS household relationship classification, grouped as husband, wife or partner; lone parent; child under 15; dependent student; non-dependent child; grandchild types; other related individual; and non-family member, plus non-classifiable, not applicable and overseas visitor codes. The variable is derived in processing and carries no not stated code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Relationship in household (including grandchildren) (RLGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/relationship-household-including-grandchildren-rlgp","lim":"It gives a role, not a pairing. Two people coded as husband, wife or partner in a dwelling holding two couples cannot be matched to each other from this column, and 'Other related individual' covers cousins, in-laws and siblings alike without saying which.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":159},{"n":"RLGP_16","d":"Each person's relationship to their family reference person at the 2016 Census, on the variant that keeps grandchildren separate.","full":"Each person's relationship to their family reference person at the 2016 Census, on the variant that keeps grandchildren separate. The ABS states of RLGP that \"No changes have been made for 2021\", so the 2016 and 2021 category sets line up and a family can be followed across those two waves on like categories. It is applicable to \"Persons present in an occupied private dwelling on Census Night\", which excludes anyone counted in a nursing home, prison or hotel in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Relationship in household (including grandchildren) (RLGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/relationship-household-including-grandchildren-rlgp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Relationship in Household (including grandchildren)","t":"categorical","k":"Census household relationship code (grandchildren separated)","def":"A relationship code on the ABS household relationship classification, with a 'Dependent student grandchild' type and a 'Non-dependent grandchild' type that RLHP_16 does not carry, and lone grandparents coded as 'Lone parent', plus non-classifiable, not applicable and overseas visitor codes rather than a not stated code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Relationship in household (including grandchildren) (RLGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/relationship-household-including-grandchildren-rlgp","lim":"It is a Census Night snapshot of who was in the dwelling, not of who normally lives there. A student away from home or a worker on a shift roster is missing from their own family's structure in 2016 and appears in whichever dwelling counted them, and nothing in the ACLD reconciles the two.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":159},{"n":"RLGP_21","d":"Each person's relationship to their family reference person at the 2021 Census, on the variant that keeps grandchildren separate.","full":"Each person's relationship to their family reference person at the 2021 Census, on the variant that keeps grandchildren separate. The ABS defines the variable as one that \"describes the relationship of each person in a family to the family reference person\", and records \"No changes have been made for 2021\", so it is directly comparable with RLGP_16. It applies to people present in an occupied private dwelling on Census Night 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Relationship in household (including grandchildren) (RLGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/relationship-household-including-grandchildren-rlgp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Relationship in Household (including grandchildren)","t":"categorical","k":"Census household relationship code (grandchildren separated)","def":"A code in the 31-category classification for 2021, including a 'Dependent student grandchild' type and lone grandparents coded as 'Lone parent', with two non-classifiable codes for visitors from within Australia and other unresolved relationships, plus not applicable and overseas visitor. Being derived in processing, it has no not stated code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Relationship in household (including grandchildren) (RLGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/relationship-household-including-grandchildren-rlgp","lim":"It does not identify a grandparent-headed household on its own. The grandchild codes sit on the child's record, so counting such households means reading the column across every person in the dwelling rather than off any one row, and a grandchild who lives with a parent as well as a grandparent codes to the parent relationship.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":159},{"n":"RLHP_11","d":"Each person's relationship to their family reference person at the 2011 Census, without the extra grandchild detail RLGP_11 carries.","full":"Each person's relationship to their family reference person at the 2011 Census, without the extra grandchild detail RLGP_11 carries. The ABS derives it from the \"relationship in household, sex, age and full-time/part-time student questions\", using sex to separate opposite-sex from same-sex couples and using age and student status to split children into under 15, dependent student and non-dependent. In 2011 a registered marriage was one undivided category, because the Marriage Act 1961 amendments that allowed same-sex marriage did not commence until 9 December 2017.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Relationship in household (RLHP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/relationship-household-rlhp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Relationship in Household","t":"categorical","k":"Census household relationship code","def":"A relationship code on the ABS household relationship classification, grouped as husband, wife or partner; lone parent; child under 15; dependent student; non-dependent child; other related individual; and non-family member, plus non-classifiable and supplementary codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Relationship in household (RLHP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/relationship-household-rlhp","lim":"The relationship is to the reference person, not to everyone else in the dwelling.
