'Other related individual' collapses cousins, in-laws, grandparents and siblings into one code, so a specific tie between two named people cannot be recovered.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":160},{"n":"RLHP_16","d":"Each person's relationship to their family reference person at the 2016 Census, without the extra grandchild detail RLGP_16 carries.","full":"Each person's relationship to their family reference person at the 2016 Census, without the extra grandchild detail RLGP_16 carries. The 2016 classification still held a single registered marriage category: the ABS records that for 2021 \"the category '11 Registered marriage' has been replaced with three categories\" separating opposite-sex couples, male same-sex couples and female same-sex couples. A married couple recorded in 2016 therefore cannot be split by couple type the way RLHP_21 can.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Relationship in household (RLHP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/relationship-household-rlhp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Relationship in Household","t":"categorical","k":"Census household relationship code","def":"A relationship code on the ABS household relationship classification as it stood for 2016, with one registered marriage category rather than the three used from 2021, alongside de facto, lone parent, child, other related individual and non-family member groups.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Relationship in household (RLHP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/relationship-household-rlhp","lim":"A change in this column between 2016 and 2021 need not be a change in the household. The couple categories were recut for 2021, so a same-sex de facto couple that later married moves category for reasons that mix a real event with a classification change.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":160},{"n":"RLHP_21","d":"Each person's relationship to their family reference person at the 2021 Census, without the extra grandchild detail RLGP_21 carries.","full":"Each person's relationship to their family reference person at the 2021 Census, without the extra grandchild detail RLGP_21 carries. The ABS defines it as describing \"the relationship of each person in a family to the family reference person\" and adds that \"Where a person is not part of a family, that person's relationship to the household reference person is captured\". For 2021 registered marriage was split into opposite-sex, male same-sex and female same-sex couples, giving 34 categories in all.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Relationship in household (RLHP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/relationship-household-rlhp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Relationship in Household","t":"categorical","k":"Census household relationship code","def":"A code in the 34-category ABS household relationship classification for 2021, grouped as husband, wife or partner (6 codes), lone parent (1), child under 15 (6), dependent student (3), non-dependent child (3), other related individual (8), non-family member (3), plus two non-classifiable codes and the not applicable and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Relationship in household (RLHP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/relationship-household-rlhp","lim":"It is not a partner identifier. The column says a person is a husband, wife or partner within the family, but two such people in a dwelling holding more than one couple cannot be paired from it, and the split of registered marriage by sex is derived from SEXP_21 rather than reported by the couple.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":160},{"n":"RLNP_11","d":"Residential status in a non-private dwelling at the 2011 Census: whether the person was staff, an owner, or a guest, patient, inmate or other resident.","full":"Residential status in a non-private dwelling at the 2011 Census: whether the person was staff, an owner, or a guest, patient, inmate or other resident. It is filled only for people counted in a non-private dwelling such as a hotel, hostel, boarding house, hospital, nursing home or staff quarters on Census Night 2011, and only where a Personal Form was completed. The ABS puts the 2011 non-response rate at 18.3%, which is the lowest of the three waves the ACLD carries.","dsrc":"ABS, Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Residential Status in a Non-Private Dwelling (RLNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~RLNP%20Residential%20Status%20in%20a%20Non-Private%20Dwelling~10079","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Residential Status in a Non-private Dwelling","t":"categorical","k":"Census non-private dwelling residential status code","def":"A two-way output code as it stood for 2011, separating owner, proprietor, staff and their family from guest, patient, inmate and other resident, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes alongside. Eight mark box options on the form collapse into those two output categories.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Residential Status in a Non-Private Dwelling (RLNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~RLNP%20Residential%20Status%20in%20a%20Non-Private%20Dwelling~10079","lim":"It does not say what kind of institution the person was in. A prisoner, a nursing home resident and a backpacker all fall in the resident category, the dwelling type is a separate column, and a blank here means a private dwelling rather than an unknown status.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":161},{"n":"RLNP_16","d":"Residential status in a non-private dwelling at the 2016 Census, separating staff and proprietors from guests, patients and other residents.","full":"Residential status in a non-private dwelling at the 2016 Census, separating staff and proprietors from guests, patients and other residents. For 2016 the ABS revised the questions on the online personal form relating to this classification to improve clarity and sequencing, and non-response rose from 18.3% in 2011 to 27.6% in 2016. It is filled only for people counted in a non-private dwelling on Census Night 2016 who completed a Personal Form.","dsrc":"ABS, Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Residential Status in a Non-Private Dwelling (RLNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~RLNP%20Residential%20Status%20in%20a%20Non-Private%20Dwelling~10079","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Residential Status in a Non-private Dwelling","t":"categorical","k":"Census non-private dwelling residential status code","def":"The same two output categories as 2011, owner, proprietor, staff and family against guest, patient, inmate and other resident, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes. For 2016 the wording and sequencing of the online form questions feeding these categories were revised.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Census of Population and Housing: Understanding the Census and Census Data 2016, Residential Status in a Non-Private Dwelling (RLNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/by%20Subject/2900.0~2016~Main%20Features~RLNP%20Residential%20Status%20in%20a%20Non-Private%20Dwelling~10079","lim":"For more than a quarter of the people it applies to it cannot tell staff from residents. With 27.6% not stated in 2016, a count of institutional residents built from this column understates them by an unknown margin, and the not-stated share is not spread evenly across dwelling types.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":161},{"n":"RLNP_21","d":"Residential status in a non-private dwelling at the 2021 Census: whether the person was staff, an owner, a guest, a patient, an inmate or another resident.","full":"Residential status in a non-private dwelling at the 2021 Census: whether the person was staff, an owner, a guest, a patient, an inmate or another resident. The ABS defines it as a variable that \"describes the residential status of each person in a non-private dwelling\", applicable to \"All persons in a non-private dwelling on Census Night\", and records that \"No changes have been made for 2021\". Non-response reached 42.0%, up from 27.6% in 2016, which the ABS links to COVID-19 restrictions on enumerating non-private dwellings, the shift to the online form and a new pathway to complete a form without mailed material.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Residential status in a non-private dwelling (RLNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/residential-status-non-private-dwelling-rlnp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Residential Status in a Non-private Dwelling","t":"categorical","k":"Census non-private dwelling residential status code","def":"Five output categories: owner, proprietor, staff or family of either; guest, patient, inmate or other resident; not stated; not applicable; and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Residential status in a non-private dwelling (RLNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/residential-status-non-private-dwelling-rlnp","lim":"In 2021 it is close to unusable as a population split. Two of every five in-scope people are not stated, so a 2016 to 2021 comparison of staff against residents mostly measures the collapse in response rather than a change in who was living in institutions.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":161},{"n":"RNTRD_P_11","d":"The weekly rent range for the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2011 Census, carried onto the person record.","full":"The weekly rent range for the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2011 Census, carried onto the person record. The ABS derives the rent variable \"from the Tenure type and Household payments questions on the Census form\", converting fortnightly and monthly amounts to a weekly figure, and applies it to occupied private dwellings being rented. The 2011 bands are in 2011 dollars and were recut for 2021, so the code cannot be read on the same scale as RNTRD_P_21.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Rent (weekly) ranges (RNTRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/rent-weekly-ranges-rntrd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Rent (weekly) Ranges","t":"categorical","k":"Census weekly rent range code","def":"An ordered range code for weekly rent in whole dollars, running from the lowest band to an open-ended top band, with not stated and not applicable codes. The ABS lists no overseas visitor code for this variable. The band boundaries are nominal dollars fixed for the 2011 Census.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Rent (weekly) ranges (RNTRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/rent-weekly-ranges-rntrd","lim":"The bands are never adjusted for inflation, so the same code buys less housing at each later wave. It is also the whole dwelling's rent rather than the person's share, so every member of a share house carries the same figure and a per-person rent cannot be recovered.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":162},{"n":"RNTRD_P_16","d":"The weekly rent range for the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2016 Census, carried onto the person record.","full":"The weekly rent range for the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2016 Census, carried onto the person record. In 2016 the variable had 25 output categories; for 2021 the ABS split category 18 into four $25 intervals, \"increasing the number of categories from 25 in 2016 to 27 in 2021\". Dwellings occupied rent free were also treated differently in 2016 from 2021, when they moved into the not applicable category.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Rent (weekly) ranges (RNTRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/rent-weekly-ranges-rntrd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Rent (weekly) Ranges","t":"categorical","k":"Census weekly rent range code","def":"An ordered range code with 25 categories in total for the 2016 Census, comprising weekly rent bands in nominal dollars from the lowest band to an open-ended top band, plus not stated and not applicable. There is no overseas visitor code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Rent (weekly) ranges (RNTRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/rent-weekly-ranges-rntrd","lim":"A code number means a different dollar band in 2016 than in 2021. Treating RNTRD_P_16 and RNTRD_P_21 as one scale moves households up or down the distribution for no reason other than the recut, and the rent-free change alters which dwellings are in scope at all.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":163},{"n":"RNTRD_P_21","d":"The weekly rent range for the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2021 Census, carried onto the person record.","full":"The weekly rent range for the dwelling the person was counted in at the 2021 Census, carried onto the person record. The ABS defines the source variable as one that \"records the rent paid for a dwelling on a weekly basis in ranges\", applicable to \"Occupied private dwellings being rented\", with 27 categories running from $1 - $74 up to $950 and over. For 2021 the scope changed so that \"dwellings with the Tenure type of 'Occupied rent free' are included in the Not applicable category and the 01 category starts at $1\".","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Rent (weekly) ranges (RNTRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/rent-weekly-ranges-rntrd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Rent (weekly) Ranges","t":"categorical","k":"Census weekly rent range code","def":"An ordered range code with 27 categories for the 2021 Census: 25 nominal weekly dollar bands from $1 - $74 up to $950 and over, plus not stated and not applicable. There is no overseas visitor code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Rent (weekly) ranges (RNTRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/rent-weekly-ranges-rntrd","lim":"The top band is open-ended, so no mean rent can be computed from this column and no distinction is possible above $950 a week. The Census holds the exact figure in Rent (weekly) dollar values, but this column keeps only the band.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":164},{"n":"SA1UCD_11","d":"The Statistical Area Level 1 the person was counted in on Census Night 2011, which is where they were rather than where they usually live.","full":"The Statistical Area Level 1 the person was counted in on Census Night 2011, which is where they were rather than where they usually live. It is coded on the first edition of the ASGS; the ABS describes the next edition as \"the second edition of the ASGS, which updates the first edition (introduced in 2011) for growth and change in Australia's population, economy and infrastructure\", so 2011 SA1s are not the same areas as 2016 or 2021 SA1s. SA1UCP_11 on the same row holds the usual residence version instead.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 1 (Enumeration)","k":"ASGS 2011 Statistical Area Level 1 code","def":"An 11-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Statistical Area Level 1 code on 2011 boundaries. SA1s are built from whole Mesh Blocks and generally hold 200 to 800 people, averaging about 400.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","lim":"A person away from home on Census Night codes to wherever they slept, so a hospital, a caravan park or a relative's house can stand in for a home address. The ACLD supplies concorded SA2 columns but no SA1 concordance, so a 2011 SA1 cannot be put onto later boundaries from within the dataset.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"SA1UCD_16","d":"The Statistical Area Level 1 the person was counted in on Census Night 2016, coded on the second edition of the ASGS.","full":"The Statistical Area Level 1 the person was counted in on Census Night 2016, coded on the second edition of the ASGS. That edition \"updates the first edition (introduced in 2011) for growth and change in Australia's population, economy and infrastructure\", retiring and renumbering SA1s that changed, so a code equal to SA1UCD_11 does not guarantee the same ground. Enumeration geography records where the person was that night, while SA1UCP_16 records usual residence.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 1 (Enumeration)","k":"ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 1 code","def":"An 11-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Statistical Area Level 1 code on 2016 boundaries. SA1s are built from whole Mesh Blocks and generally hold 200 to 800 people.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","lim":"Comparing SA1UCD_11 with SA1UCD_16 measures boundary change as well as movement. With no SA1 correspondence in the ACLD, a change in code cannot be separated into the part caused by the person moving and the part caused by the ABS redrawing the area.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"SA1UCD_21","d":"The Statistical Area Level 1 the person was counted in on Census Night 2021, coded on the third edition of the ASGS.","full":"The Statistical Area Level 1 the person was counted in on Census Night 2021, coded on the third edition of the ASGS. The ABS defines SA1s as areas \"built from whole Mesh Blocks\" and reports \"61,845 SA1 regions covering the whole of Australia without gaps or overlaps\", each carrying \"an 11-digit fully hierarchical code\". SA1UCP_21 on the same row is the usual residence version, and the two differ for anyone counted away from home.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 1","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-1","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 1 (Enumeration)","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 1 code","def":"An 11-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Edition 3 Statistical Area Level 1 code, one of 61,845 areas, each generally holding 200 to 800 people and averaging about 400.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 1","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-1","lim":"An area of about 400 people is small enough that ABS confidentiality treatments bite, and counts at this level within a 5% longitudinal sample are very thin. The code identifies a small area, not a dwelling or a household, so two people sharing an SA1 are not neighbours in any usable sense.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"SA1UCP_11","d":"The Statistical Area Level 1 of the person's usual residence at the 2011 Census, which need not be where they were counted.","full":"The Statistical Area Level 1 of the person's usual residence at the 2011 Census, which need not be where they were counted. Usual residence is the address a person has lived at, or intends to live at, for a total of six months or more in the Census year, and for people at home on Census Night it is derived from the enumeration address. It is coded on the first edition of the ASGS, so it is not on the same boundaries as SA1UCP_16 or SA1UCP_21.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 1 (Usual Residence)","k":"ASGS 2011 Statistical Area Level 1 code (usual residence)","def":"An 11-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Statistical Area Level 1 code on 2011 boundaries, built up from the mesh block the usual address falls in. SA1s generally hold 200 to 800 people.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","lim":"Usual residence is imputed where the reported address could not be coded, so a value is not always an address the person gave. The column is also a single point in time: it says where a person lived in August 2011 and nothing about moves before or after.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"SA1UCP_16","d":"The Statistical Area Level 1 of the person's usual residence at the 2016 Census, coded on the second edition of the ASGS.","full":"The Statistical Area Level 1 of the person's usual residence at the 2016 Census, coded on the second edition of the ASGS. It differs from SA1UCD_16 for anyone counted away from home, because usual residence is the address a person has lived at, or intends to live at, for six months or more, rather than where they slept on Census Night. The 2016 SA1 boundaries replace the 2011 ones, so the code cannot be read against SA1UCP_11 as a like-for-like area.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 1 (Usual Residence)","k":"ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 1 code (usual residence)","def":"An 11-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Statistical Area Level 1 code on 2016 boundaries, aggregated from the mesh block containing the usual address. SA1s generally hold 200 to 800 people.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","lim":"It cannot date a move. Different SA1s in 2011 and 2016 show only that the person lived somewhere else at the two Census dates, with no indication of when they moved, how often, or whether they returned in between.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"SA1UCP_21","d":"The Statistical Area Level 1 of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census, coded on the third edition of the ASGS.","full":"The Statistical Area Level 1 of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census, coded on the third edition of the ASGS. The ABS defines the underlying Census variable as one that \"records the geographic area in which a person usually lives\", where \"'Usually live' means the address at which the person has lived, or intends to live, for a total of six months or more in 2021\". It can differ from SA1UCD_21, which records where the person was counted on Census Night.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 1 (Usual Residence)","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 1 code (usual residence)","def":"An 11-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Edition 3 Statistical Area Level 1 code, aggregated from the mesh block containing the usual address, one of 61,845 such areas.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","lim":"A usual residence SA1 is not a household. Members of the same family carry different codes if one of them usually lives elsewhere, and a person with two homes is assigned a single address by the six-month rule rather than being split between them.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"SA2_MOVE_1YR_16","d":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2016 Census was in the same Statistical Area Level 2, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas.","full":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2016 Census was in the same Statistical Area Level 2, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas. It resolves the Census usual address one year ago question to SA2, so a move within the same SA2 does not register at all. The ACLD carries this indicator only from the 2016 wave on; there is no 2011 counterpart column in either ACLD table.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address one year ago indicator (UAI1P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-one-year-ago-indicator-uai1p","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address One Year Ago Indicator for SA2","t":"categorical","k":"One-year usual address mobility indicator at SA2","def":"A short indicator code separating the same area as at the Census, elsewhere in Australia, and overseas one year earlier, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes. It applies to people aged one year and over.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address one year ago indicator (UAI1P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-one-year-ago-indicator-uai1p","lim":"It undercounts moves by design. A household that moved across the street stays in the same SA2 and reads as no move, while a short move across an SA2 boundary reads as one, so the column measures crossing a boundary rather than changing address.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":165},{"n":"SA2_MOVE_1YR_21","d":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2021 Census was in the same Statistical Area Level 2, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas.","full":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2021 Census was in the same Statistical Area Level 2, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas. The Census indicator behind it \"indicates whether a person: lived in the same address one year ago as their current usual residence, lived elsewhere in Australia one year ago, usually lived in another country one year ago\", and applies to \"All persons aged one year and over\". Non-response on that question was 5.5% in 2021, down from 8.3% in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address one year ago indicator (UAI1P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-one-year-ago-indicator-uai1p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address One Year Ago Indicator for SA2","t":"categorical","k":"One-year usual address mobility indicator at SA2","def":"A short indicator code separating the same area as in 2021, elsewhere in Australia, and overseas in 2020, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address one year ago indicator (UAI1P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-one-year-ago-indicator-uai1p","lim":"A no-move reading is not evidence of a settled year. The reference period runs from August 2020 to August 2021, inside the pandemic, when interstate borders were shut for long stretches and moves were suppressed, so this column and its 2016 version answer the same question under very different conditions.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":166},{"n":"SA2_MOVE_5YR_16","d":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2016 Census, that is in 2011, was in the same Statistical Area Level 2.","full":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2016 Census, that is in 2011, was in the same Statistical Area Level 2. It rests on the Census five-years-ago question, which applies to people aged five years and over and had a non-response rate of 7.3% in 2016. The five-year window lines up with the ACLD's own 2011 wave, so the answer can be checked against SA2UCP_11 on the same row.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address five years ago indicator (UAI5P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-five-years-ago-indicator-uai5p","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address Five Years Ago Indicator for SA2","t":"categorical","k":"Five-year usual address mobility indicator at SA2","def":"A short indicator code separating the same area as at the Census, elsewhere in Australia, and overseas five years earlier, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address five years ago indicator (UAI5P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-five-years-ago-indicator-uai5p","lim":"It is the respondent's recall of an address five years earlier, not a record of it. Where this column and the linked 2011 geography disagree, the indicator is the weaker of the two, because a person can misremember a date or answer for another household member.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":167},{"n":"SA2_MOVE_5YR_21","d":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2021 Census, that is in 2016, was in the same Statistical Area Level 2.","full":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2021 Census, that is in 2016, was in the same Statistical Area Level 2. The Census question behind it \"indicates whether a person: lived in the same address five years ago as their current usual residence, lived elsewhere in Australia five years ago, usually lived in another country five years ago\", and covers \"All persons aged five years and over\". Its non-response rate was 6.0% in 2021, down from 7.3% in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address five years ago indicator (UAI5P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-five-years-ago-indicator-uai5p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address Five Years Ago Indicator for SA2","t":"categorical","k":"Five-year usual address mobility indicator at SA2","def":"A short indicator code separating the same area as in 2021, elsewhere in Australia, and overseas in 2016, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address five years ago indicator (UAI5P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-five-years-ago-indicator-uai5p","lim":"It compares two dates and hides everything between them. A person who left an SA2 in 2017 and returned by 2021 reads as never having moved, so the column cannot be used to count moves or to date them.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":168},{"n":"SA2UCD_11","d":"The Statistical Area Level 2 the person was counted in on Census Night 2011, coded on the first edition of the ASGS.","full":"The Statistical Area Level 2 the person was counted in on Census Night 2011, coded on the first edition of the ASGS. The ABS describes the following edition as \"the second edition of the ASGS, which updates the first edition (introduced in 2011) for growth and change in Australia's population, economy and infrastructure\", which is why the ACLD also ships SA2UCD_11_ASGS16 and SA2UCD_11_ASGS21. Enumeration geography records where the person was that night; SA2UCP_11 records usual residence.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 2 (Enumeration)","k":"ASGS 2011 Statistical Area Level 2 code (enumeration)","def":"A 9-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Statistical Area Level 2 code on 2011 boundaries. SA2s are built from whole SA1s and generally hold between 3,000 and 25,000 people.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","lim":"A raw 2011 code cannot be tabulated against a 2021 code. Some SA2 identifiers were retired and reissued between editions, so matching on the number alone can place a person in an area they never lived in, which is exactly what the ASGS-suffixed columns exist to avoid.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"SA2UCD_11_ASGS16","d":"The 2011 enumeration Statistical Area Level 2 restated on 2016 ASGS boundaries, so the 2011 and 2016 waves can be tabulated on one geography.","full":"The 2011 enumeration Statistical Area Level 2 restated on 2016 ASGS boundaries, so the 2011 and 2016 waves can be tabulated on one geography. It is a concordance rather than a fresh coding: the ABS publishes correspondence files \"to help users to mathematically convert statistical data to and from geographic regions\", weighted on modelled residential population. SA2UCD_11 holds the original 2011 code and SA2UCD_11_ASGS21 the same 2011 area expressed on 2021 boundaries.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Correspondences","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/access-and-downloads/correspondences","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical area level 2 concordance 2011 to asgs 2016 (enumeration)","k":"ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 2 code, concorded from 2011 (enumeration)","def":"A 9-digit ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 2 code assigned to an area originally coded in 2011. The underlying correspondences carry a ratio between 0 and 1 describing how much of a source region is donated to each destination region.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Correspondences","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/access-and-downloads/correspondences","lim":"A concorded code is a mapping between boundary sets, not a fresh geocode of the person's address. Where a 2011 SA2 was split across several 2016 areas the assignment is a best allocation rather than a fact, and the ABS rates the quality of individual correspondences on a scale that runs down to poor.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"SA2UCD_11_ASGS21","d":"The 2011 enumeration Statistical Area Level 2 restated on 2021 ASGS boundaries, so that all three ACLD waves can be tabulated on the newest geography.","full":"The 2011 enumeration Statistical Area Level 2 restated on 2021 ASGS boundaries, so that all three ACLD waves can be tabulated on the newest geography. It is built from ABS correspondence files, whose weighting the ABS describes as \"calculated on the location of the population\" using population modelled to residential address locations. SA2UCD_11 is the original 2011 code and SA2UCD_11_ASGS16 is the same area on 2016 boundaries.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Correspondences","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/access-and-downloads/correspondences","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical area level 2 concordance 2011 to asgs 2021 (enumeration)","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code, concorded from 2011 (enumeration)","def":"A 9-digit ASGS Edition 3 Statistical Area Level 2 code assigned to an area originally coded in 2011, one of 2,473 SA2s. The correspondence ratios that produce it run between 0 and 1.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Correspondences","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/access-and-downloads/correspondences","lim":"It spans two boundary revisions, 2011 to 2016 and 2016 to 2021, so the approximation compounds. Agreement between this column and SA2UCD_21 is therefore weaker evidence that a person stayed put than agreement between two codes originally coded on the same edition.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"SA2UCD_16","d":"The Statistical Area Level 2 the person was counted in on Census Night 2016, coded on the second edition of the ASGS.","full":"The Statistical Area Level 2 the person was counted in on Census Night 2016, coded on the second edition of the ASGS. That edition \"updates the first edition (introduced in 2011) for growth and change in Australia's population, economy and infrastructure\", so 2016 SA2s are not 2011 SA2s, and the ACLD ships SA2UCD_16_ASGS21 to bring them onto 2021 boundaries. It records where the person was counted, not where they usually live.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 2 (Enumeration)","k":"ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 2 code (enumeration)","def":"A 9-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Statistical Area Level 2 code on 2016 boundaries. SA2s are built from whole SA1s and generally hold between 3,000 and 25,000 people.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS): Volume 1 - Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas, July 2016","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/mf/1270.0.55.001","lim":"Enumeration SA2 follows the person on one night of the year. A grey nomad, a worker on site, or anyone on holiday in August 2016 codes to the holiday area, so reading this column as a residence history manufactures moves that never happened.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"SA2UCD_16_ASGS21","d":"The 2016 enumeration Statistical Area Level 2 restated on 2021 ASGS boundaries, so the 2016 and 2021 waves sit on one geography.","full":"The 2016 enumeration Statistical Area Level 2 restated on 2021 ASGS boundaries, so the 2016 and 2021 waves sit on one geography. It comes from the published 2016 to 2021 correspondence files, which carry a \"RATIO_FROM_TO\" field describing \"the Ratio of the FROM region that is being donated to the TO region\". SA2UCD_16 holds the original 2016 code, and the same treatment is applied to usual residence in SA2UCP_16_ASGS21.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Correspondences","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/access-and-downloads/correspondences","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical area level 2 concordance 2016 to asgs 2021 (enumeration)","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code, concorded from 2016 (enumeration)","def":"A 9-digit ASGS Edition 3 Statistical Area Level 2 code assigned to an area originally coded in 2016, produced by a population-weighted correspondence whose ratios lie between 0 and 1.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Correspondences","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/access-and-downloads/correspondences","lim":"The mapping is population-weighted, so it is least reliable exactly where population changed most. New housing areas are where SA2s were split between 2016 and 2021, and they are where a concorded code is most likely to place a person in the wrong new area.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"SA2UCD_21","d":"The Statistical Area Level 2 the person was counted in on Census Night 2021, coded on the third edition of the ASGS.","full":"The Statistical Area Level 2 the person was counted in on Census Night 2021, coded on the third edition of the ASGS. The ABS defines SA2s as \"medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s)\", and reports \"2,473 SA2s covering the whole of Australia without gaps or overlaps\". SA2UCP_21 is the usual residence version, and the two differ for anyone counted away from home.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-2","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 2 (Enumeration)","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code (enumeration)","def":"A 9-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Edition 3 Statistical Area Level 2 code, one of 2,473 areas, each generally holding between 3,000 and 25,000 people and averaging about 10,000.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-2","lim":"An SA2 is a statistical area, not a suburb or a council. Its name often matches a suburb but its boundary need not, so joining this column to local government areas, postcodes or suburb names needs a correspondence rather than a name match.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"SA2UCP_11","d":"The Statistical Area Level 2 of the person's usual residence at the 2011 Census, coded on the first edition of the ASGS.","full":"The Statistical Area Level 2 of the person's usual residence at the 2011 Census, coded on the first edition of the ASGS. Usual residence is the address the person had lived at, or intended to live at, for six months or more, so it can differ from the enumeration column SA2UCD_11 on the same row. The ACLD also ships SA2UCP_11_ASGS16 and SA2UCP_11_ASGS21 for comparison with the later waves.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 2 (Usual Residence)","k":"ASGS 2011 Statistical Area Level 2 code (usual residence)","def":"A 9-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Statistical Area Level 2 code on 2011 boundaries, aggregated from the mesh block containing the usual address. SA2s generally hold between 3,000 and 25,000 people.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","lim":"A usual residence code is assigned to a person, not to a dwelling, and where the address could not be coded the ABS imputes it. A 2011 value can therefore be an imputation rather than a report, and the imputation flag that would say so is a separate Census variable.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"SA2UCP_11_ASGS16","d":"The 2011 usual residence Statistical Area Level 2 restated on 2016 ASGS boundaries, so the 2011 and 2016 home areas sit on one set of areas.","full":"The 2011 usual residence Statistical Area Level 2 restated on 2016 ASGS boundaries, so the 2011 and 2016 home areas sit on one set of areas. It is produced from ABS correspondence files, which exist \"to help users to mathematically convert statistical data to and from geographic regions\" and are weighted on modelled residential population. SA2UCP_11 holds the original 2011 code, and SA2UCD_11_ASGS16 does the same job for the enumeration geography.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Correspondences","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/access-and-downloads/correspondences","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical area level 2 concordance 2011 to asgs 2016 (usual residence)","k":"ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 2 code, concorded from 2011 (usual residence)","def":"A 9-digit ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 2 code assigned to a usual residence originally coded in 2011, produced by a correspondence whose ratios lie between 0 and 1.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Correspondences","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/access-and-downloads/correspondences","lim":"Equality between this column and SA2UCP_16 is not proof that the person did not move. Both sides carry mapping error, and a person who moved to a neighbouring area that the correspondence folds into the same destination reads as having stayed.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"SA2UCP_11_ASGS21","d":"The 2011 usual residence Statistical Area Level 2 restated on 2021 ASGS boundaries, giving a single home-area series across all three ACLD waves.","full":"The 2011 usual residence Statistical Area Level 2 restated on 2021 ASGS boundaries, giving a single home-area series across all three ACLD waves. The ABS builds these mappings with a weighting \"calculated on the location of the population\", using population modelled to residential address locations. SA2UCP_11 is the original 2011 code and SA2UCP_11_ASGS16 is the same area on 2016 boundaries.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Correspondences","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/access-and-downloads/correspondences","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical area level 2 concordance 2011 to asgs 2021 (usual residence)","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code, concorded from 2011 (usual residence)","def":"A 9-digit ASGS Edition 3 Statistical Area Level 2 code assigned to a usual residence originally coded in 2011, one of 2,473 SA2s, produced by chained population-weighted correspondences.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Correspondences","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/access-and-downloads/correspondences","lim":"It carries the error of two boundary revisions rather than one, so it is the least precise of the 2011 geography columns. A ten-year mobility rate built on this column against SA2UCP_21 will differ from one built on the raw codes, and neither is exact.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"SA2UCP_16","d":"The Statistical Area Level 2 of the person's usual residence at the 2016 Census, coded on the second edition of the ASGS.","full":"The Statistical Area Level 2 of the person's usual residence at the 2016 Census, coded on the second edition of the ASGS. The ABS defines the Census variable behind it as one that \"records the geographic area in which a person usually lives\", built up from the mesh block containing that address, and notes it \"may or may not be the place where the person was counted on Census Night\". SA2UCP_16_ASGS21 restates the same area on 2021 boundaries.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 2 (Usual Residence)","k":"ASGS 2016 Statistical Area Level 2 code (usual residence)","def":"A 9-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Statistical Area Level 2 code on 2016 boundaries, aggregated from the mesh block containing the usual address. SA2s generally hold between 3,000 and 25,000 people.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","lim":"An SA2 is coarse enough to hide most residential mobility. With an average of about 10,000 residents, a household can move several suburbs within a city and keep the same code, so this column is a regional locator rather than a mobility measure.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"SA2UCP_16_ASGS21","d":"The 2016 usual residence Statistical Area Level 2 restated on 2021 ASGS boundaries, so a person's home area can be compared directly with SA2UCP_21.","full":"The 2016 usual residence Statistical Area Level 2 restated on 2021 ASGS boundaries, so a person's home area can be compared directly with SA2UCP_21. It comes from the published 2016 to 2021 correspondences, whose \"RATIO_FROM_TO\" field gives \"the Ratio of the FROM region that is being donated to the TO region\", a figure between 0 and 1. SA2UCP_16 keeps the original 2016 code for anyone who needs the geography as coded.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Correspondences","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/access-and-downloads/correspondences","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical area level 2 concordance 2016 to asgs 2021 (usual residence)","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code, concorded from 2016 (usual residence)","def":"A 9-digit ASGS Edition 3 Statistical Area Level 2 code assigned to a usual residence originally coded in 2016, one of 2,473 SA2s, produced by a population-weighted correspondence.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Correspondences","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/access-and-downloads/correspondences","lim":"Where a 2016 SA2 maps to more than one 2021 area, the person is placed in one of them rather than divided between them, so an individual record can be assigned an area their address was never in even where the aggregate conversion is sound.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"SA2UCP_21","d":"The Statistical Area Level 2 of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census, coded on the third edition of the ASGS.","full":"The Statistical Area Level 2 of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census, coded on the third edition of the ASGS. The ABS defines the Census variable as one that \"records the geographic area in which a person usually lives\", where \"'Usually live' means the address at which the person has lived, or intends to live, for a total of six months or more in 2021\". It can differ from SA2UCD_21, which is where the person was counted on Census Night.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Statistical Area Level 2 (Usual Residence)","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code (usual residence)","def":"A 9-digit fully hierarchical ASGS Edition 3 Statistical Area Level 2 code, aggregated from the mesh block containing the usual address, one of 2,473 such areas averaging about 10,000 people.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","lim":"A person with more than one home is assigned a single area by the six-month rule, so shared care arrangements, fly-in fly-out work and student terms away all resolve to one code with nothing recording the other place.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"SEXP_11","d":"The person's sex as recorded at the 2011 Census, output as male or female only.","full":"The person's sex as recorded at the 2011 Census, output as male or female only. The 2011 form carried no third input option, so a person who did not identify as male or female had no way to say so within the standard question. SEXP_16 and SEXP_21 record the same concept at the later waves, and the three columns need not agree for the same person.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Sex (SEXP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/sex-sexp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Sex","t":"categorical","k":"Census sex code (male, female)","def":"A two-category code: 1 Male, 2 Female. No third output category exists at any Census wave carried in this dataset.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Sex (SEXP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/sex-sexp","lim":"It records sex, not gender, and cannot identify transgender or non-binary people at all. Where sex was not reported the ABS imputes it, so a value is not always an answer the person gave.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":169},{"n":"SEXP_16","d":"The person's sex as recorded at the 2016 Census, output as male or female only.","full":"The person's sex as recorded at the 2016 Census, output as male or female only. In 2016 a respondent wanting to report a sex other than male or female had to follow a special procedure or use an alternate form, and the output still carried two categories. SEXP_21 records the same two categories after a non-binary option was added to the form as an input.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Sex (SEXP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/sex-sexp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Sex","t":"categorical","k":"Census sex code (male, female)","def":"A two-category code: 1 Male, 2 Female, captured from mark box responses so that processing error is minimal.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Sex (SEXP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/sex-sexp","lim":"Where a person's sex differs between the 2011, 2016 and 2021 columns of the ACLD, imputation at one wave is a more likely explanation than any change in the person, and this column carries no flag to tell an imputed value from a reported one.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":169},{"n":"SEXP_21","d":"The person's sex as recorded at the 2021 Census, output as male or female.","full":"The person's sex as recorded at the 2021 Census, output as male or female. The ABS defines it as a variable that \"records each person's sex\", where \"A person's sex is based on their sex characteristics, such as their chromosomes, hormones and reproductive organs\", and notes that \"In 2021, a 'non-binary sex' option was added as an input category to the standard question, however the output categories for this variable are unchanged for 2021\". Using the imputation flag, the ABS puts 2021 non-response at 4.7%.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Sex (SEXP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/sex-sexp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Sex","t":"categorical","k":"Census sex code (male, female)","def":"A two-category code: 1 Male, 2 Female, captured from mark box responses on the form.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Sex (SEXP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/sex-sexp","lim":"Non-binary responses cannot be recovered from this column. They were collected in 2021 but coded away in output, so a tally of male and female here is not a tally of how people answered the question.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":169},{"n":"SIEMP_11","d":"The person's status in employment in their main job in the week before Census Night 2011: employee, owner manager, or contributing family worker.","full":"The person's status in employment in their main job in the week before Census Night 2011: employee, owner manager, or contributing family worker. It applies to employed people aged 15 and over, so everyone not working carries a not applicable code rather than a missing one. SIEMP_16 and SIEMP_21 hold the same concept at the later waves, and SIEMP_FP_11, SIEMP_MP_11 and SIEMP_SP_11 hold it for a female parent, a male parent and a spouse.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Status in Employment","t":"categorical","k":"Census status in employment code","def":"A code distinguishing employee; owner manager of an incorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, and employees not stated; owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, and employees not stated; and contributing family worker, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes. The not applicable code carries everyone under 15, the unemployed and people not in the labour force.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"It describes the main job only. A person who is an employee in one job and runs a business in another shows only the main one, and the not applicable code covers the unemployed and people outside the labour force alike, so this column cannot be read as a labour force status.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":170},{"n":"SIEMP_16","d":"The person's status in employment in their main job in the week before Census Night 2016.","full":"The person's status in employment in their main job in the week before Census Night 2016. The ABS puts the non-response rate at 1.0% in 2016, falling to 0.6% in 2021, and states that \"No changes have been made for 2021\", so SIEMP_16 and SIEMP_21 are directly comparable. It applies only to employed people aged 15 and over.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Status in Employment","t":"categorical","k":"Census status in employment code","def":"An 11-category code: employee; owner manager of an incorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, and employees not stated; owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, and employees not stated; and contributing family worker, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes. Two of the six owner manager codes exist only because the respondent did not say whether the business had employees.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"It says nothing about job security or contract type. A casual and a permanent worker both code to employee, and a labour hire worker is an employee of the agency, so precarious work cannot be identified from this column at any wave.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":170},{"n":"SIEMP_21","d":"The person's status in employment in their main job in the week before Census Night 2021.","full":"The person's status in employment in their main job in the week before Census Night 2021. The ABS defines it as a variable that \"defines a person's employment status for the main job held in the week prior to Census Night\", applicable to \"Employed persons aged 15 years and over\", with a non-response rate of 0.6%. \"No changes have been made for 2021\", so it sits on the same categories as SIEMP_16 on the same row.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Status in Employment","t":"categorical","k":"Census status in employment code","def":"An 11-category code: employee; owner manager of an incorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, and employees not stated; owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, and employees not stated; and contributing family worker, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes. The category set is unchanged from 2016.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"Owner manager status here is a self-report about the person's own job, not a company record. It cannot be reconciled with an ABN or a business register entry, and an owner manager of an incorporated enterprise is also an employee of that company in tax data, which this column does not show.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":170},{"n":"SIEMP_FP_11","d":"The status in employment of the female parent in the person's family at the 2011 Census, carried onto this record.","full":"The status in employment of the female parent in the person's family at the 2011 Census, carried onto this record. It is that parent's own SIEMP value for her main job in the week before Census Night, so it exists only where a female parent was in the same family in the dwelling in 2011. SIEMP_11 holds the person's own status, SIEMP_MP_11 the male parent's and SIEMP_SP_11 the spouse or partner's.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Status in Employment of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census status in employment code (female parent)","def":"The female parent's own code on the status in employment classification: employee; owner manager of an incorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, and employees not stated; owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, and employees not stated; and contributing family worker, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"A blank does not mean the mother was not working. It means no female parent was enumerated in the same family on Census Night 2011, which covers a non-resident parent, a parent counted elsewhere and a family with no female parent, and this column cannot separate those cases from a genuine not stated.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":170},{"n":"SIEMP_FP_16","d":"The status in employment of the female parent in the person's family at the 2016 Census, carried onto this record.","full":"The status in employment of the female parent in the person's family at the 2016 Census, carried onto this record. Because the ABS records \"No changes have been made for 2021\" to the underlying variable, the female parent's status is on the same categories in 2016 and 2021, so a child's family circumstances can be followed across those two waves. It is populated only where a female parent was enumerated in the same family in the dwelling in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Status in Employment of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census status in employment code (female parent)","def":"The female parent's own code from the 11-category 2016 classification: employee; owner manager of an incorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, and employees not stated; owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, and employees not stated; and contributing family worker, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"A parent's employment status attaches to the family in the dwelling, not to the parent-child relationship. A child who moved between parents between waves picks up a different adult's record with no flag saying so, and the column cannot show that the female parent changed.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":170},{"n":"SIEMP_FP_21","d":"The status in employment of the female parent in the person's family at the 2021 Census, carried onto this record.","full":"The status in employment of the female parent in the person's family at the 2021 Census, carried onto this record. It is that parent's own value for a variable the ABS defines as one that \"defines a person's employment status for the main job held in the week prior to Census Night\", applicable to \"Employed persons aged 15 years and over\". The person's own status is in SIEMP_21, and the male parent's and the spouse's in SIEMP_MP_21 and SIEMP_SP_21.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Status in Employment of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census status in employment code (female parent)","def":"The female parent's own code from the 11-category 2021 classification: employee; owner manager of an incorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, and employees not stated; owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, and employees not stated; and contributing family worker, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes. A not applicable value here means the parent was not employed, not that no parent was present.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"One column cannot carry two mothers. In a couple family with two female parents, which 2021 was the first Census able to record as married, this field holds a single status, so the household's second parent is either invisible here or must be read off the male parent column that does not apply.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":170},{"n":"SIEMP_MP_11","d":"The male parent's status in employment at the 2011 Census, taken from his own Census record and carried onto the sampled person's row.","full":"The male parent's status in employment at the 2011 Census, taken from his own Census record and carried onto the sampled person's row. The 2011 Census had no SIEMP variable at all, because the ABS introduced that classification for 2016, so the 2011 wave rests on Employment type (EMTP), which the dictionary defines as a variable that \"Employment Type classifies all employed people, to either employees, owner manager of incorporated enterprises, owner manager of unincorporated enterprises, or contributing family workers.\" SIEMP_SP_11 gives the same measure for a spouse or partner, and STUP_MP_11 and TYPP_MP_11 give the same man's study.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Employment Type (EMTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter31202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Status in Employment of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 employment type code, male parent","def":"One code for one employed person: employee, owner manager of an incorporated enterprise, owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise, or contributing family worker, with not stated and not applicable codes alongside. The 2011 frame carries no with-employees or without-employees split.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Employment Type (EMTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter31202011","lim":"It will not line up category for category with SIEMP_MP_16 or SIEMP_MP_21, because the 2016 classification splits each owner manager group by whether the business had employees; a transition table built on the raw codes shows movement that is classification change rather than job change. The column is also empty wherever no male parent was enumerated in the person's family on Census night, so a blank means no parent on the form, not a parent out of work.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":170},{"n":"SIEMP_MP_16","d":"The male parent's status in employment at the 2016 Census, the first Census at which the ABS collected SIEMP.","full":"The male parent's status in employment at the 2016 Census, the first Census at which the ABS collected SIEMP. The dictionary defines the underlying variable as one that, \"For employed persons, defines their status in employment for the main job held in the week prior to Census night.\" and the ACLD copies the male parent's value onto the sampled person's row. 2016 is where the owner manager frame starts, so this is the earliest wave that separates an owner manager with employees from one without.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Status in Employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9152016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Status in Employment of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 status in employment (SIEMP) code, male parent","def":"A single code from eight substantive categories: employee; owner manager of an incorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, or employees not stated; the same three for an unincorporated enterprise; and contributing family worker. The residual codes are & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Status in Employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9152016","lim":"It describes the main job only, so a father who ran a business alongside a wage job is recorded as an employee and the self-employment does not appear. Not applicable also covers two quite different situations, no male parent enumerated in the family and a male parent who was not employed, so this column cannot be counted as parents out of work.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":170},{"n":"SIEMP_MP_21","d":"The male parent's status in employment at the 2021 Census, on the same eight-category frame the ABS introduced in 2016.","full":"The male parent's status in employment at the 2021 Census, on the same eight-category frame the ABS introduced in 2016. The 2021 dictionary defines the underlying variable as one where \"This variable defines a person's employment status for the main job held in the week prior to Census Night.\" and records no change to it for 2021, so this column and SIEMP_MP_16 can be compared code for code while SIEMP_MP_11 cannot. The value is the father's own, not a household summary.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Status in Employment of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 status in employment (SIEMP) code, male parent","def":"The same eight-category owner manager frame the ABS built for 2016, coded one character per person, with & for not stated, @ for not applicable and V for an overseas visitor. Employee is the modal category; the six owner manager codes split on incorporation and on whether the business had employees.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"August 2021 fell inside extended lockdowns in New South Wales, Victoria and the Australian Capital Territory, and the Census told people stood down by a lockdown to report themselves as employed if they had worked at all in the four weeks before it, and as not having a job if they had not. The line between an employed owner manager and a not applicable code therefore fell in a different place in 2021, and reading a shift between 2016 and 2021 as business exit risks reading a lockdown rule as a structural change.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":170},{"n":"SIEMP_SP_11","d":"The employment status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census, read off the partner's own form.","full":"The employment status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census, read off the partner's own form. Because SIEMP did not exist until the 2016 Census, the 2011 wave sits on Employment type (EMTP), a variable that \"Employment Type classifies all employed people, to either employees, owner manager of incorporated enterprises, owner manager of unincorporated enterprises, or contributing family workers.\" A value appears only where a spouse or partner was enumerated in the same household, so a partner counted elsewhere on Census night leaves it empty.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Employment Type (EMTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter31202011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Status in Employment of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 employment type code, spouse or partner","def":"One code covering employee, owner manager of an incorporated enterprise, owner manager of an unincorporated enterprise and contributing family worker, plus not stated and not applicable. The 2011 classification stops there and does not record whether the business had employees.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Employment Type (EMTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter31202011","lim":"It cannot be lined up against SIEMP_SP_16 without a crosswalk, and there is no clean one, since the 2016 categories subdivide the 2011 owner manager groups.
