The column also says nothing about a partner's hours or earnings, so a spouse who worked one hour as an employee and one who worked sixty carry the same code; HRWRP and INCP for the partner are needed for that.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":170},{"n":"SIEMP_SP_16","d":"The employment status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2016 Census, the first Census to use the SIEMP classification.","full":"The employment status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2016 Census, the first Census to use the SIEMP classification. The dictionary's definition is that, \"For employed persons, defines their status in employment for the main job held in the week prior to Census night.\" and the ACLD attaches the partner's value to the sampled person's row. Registered and de facto partners both qualify, since the Census identifies the couple through social marital status rather than marriage registration.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Status in Employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9152016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Status in Employment of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 status in employment (SIEMP) code, spouse or partner","def":"A single code from eight substantive categories: employee; owner manager of an incorporated enterprise with employees, without employees, or employees not stated; the same three for an unincorporated enterprise; and contributing family worker. The residual codes are & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Status in Employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9152016","lim":"The column is filled only for people in a couple relationship recorded in the same household on Census night: a partner working interstate, in hospital or overseas that night is a spouse in life but not in this column. A blank therefore mixes single people, people whose partner was absent, and people whose partner was not employed, and none of the three can be told apart here.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":170},{"n":"SIEMP_SP_21","d":"The employment status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2021 Census, unchanged in classification from 2016.","full":"The employment status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2021 Census, unchanged in classification from 2016. The 2021 dictionary defines the variable as one that \"This variable defines a person's employment status for the main job held in the week prior to Census Night.\" and reports no change to it for 2021, so SIEMP_SP_16 and this column form a comparable pair across two waves of the ACLD. The value belongs to the partner alone and says nothing about the sampled person's own work.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Status in Employment of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 status in employment (SIEMP) code, spouse or partner","def":"The same eight-category owner manager frame the ABS built for 2016, coded one character per person, with & for not stated, @ for not applicable and V for an overseas visitor. Employee is the modal category; the six owner manager codes split on incorporation and on whether the business had employees.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Status in employment (SIEMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/status-employment-siemp","lim":"It cannot be used to build a couple's joint labour market position on its own, because a partner recorded as an owner manager without employees may be a sole trader with almost no income; pairing it with the partner's income and hours columns is what makes it interpretable. Nor does it identify the same partner across waves, since a person who separated and repartnered between 2016 and 2021 shows a changed code for a changed person.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":170},{"n":"STATE_MOVE_1YR_16","d":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2016 Census, at 9 August 2015, was in the same state or territory as their 2016 address.","full":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2016 Census, at 9 August 2015, was in the same state or territory as their 2016 address. It is the ACLD's state-level reading of the Census item UAI1P, which by itself separates only same address, elsewhere in Australia and overseas; SA2_MOVE_1YR_16 does the same job at SA2 level. The pair of columns appears from the 2016 wave onward, so there is no 2011 counterpart in this table.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Usual Address One Year Ago Indicator (UAI1P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10402016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address One Year Ago Indicator for State","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A short categorical indicator distinguishing no move, a move within the same state or territory, a move between states or territories, and arrival from overseas, with not stated and not applicable residuals. The states and territories are the ASGS state and territory level.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Usual Address One Year Ago Indicator (UAI1P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10402016","lim":"One year is a short window and the indicator is a comparison of two points, so a person who moved interstate in September 2015 and moved home in July 2016 registers as not having moved at all. Children under one year of age are outside the Census question's scope, and the not applicable code covers them rather than marking them as non-movers.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":171},{"n":"STATE_MOVE_1YR_21","d":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2021 Census was in the same state or territory as their 2021 address.","full":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2021 Census was in the same state or territory as their 2021 address. The Census item behind it, UAI1P, indicates whether a person lived at the same address a year earlier, elsewhere in Australia, or in another country, and the ACLD resolves the middle category against the state of usual residence. The one-year reference date falls in August 2020, inside the first year of the COVID-19 border closures.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address one year ago indicator (UAI1P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-one-year-ago-indicator-uai1p","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address One Year Ago Indicator for State","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A categorical indicator of same address, a move within the state or territory, a move across a state or territory border, and arrival from overseas, with residual codes for not stated and not applicable. States and territories follow the ASGS.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address one year ago indicator (UAI1P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-one-year-ago-indicator-uai1p","lim":"The 2020 to 2021 window is not a normal year of Australian mobility: internal borders were closed for long stretches and overseas arrivals were capped, so a low interstate move rate here measures restriction rather than settled behaviour. The indicator also records where a person usually lived, not where they were on Census night, so a fly-in worker stranded interstate is still at their usual address.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":172},{"n":"STATE_MOVE_5YR_16","d":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2016 Census, at 9 August 2011, was in the same state or territory as their 2016 address.","full":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2016 Census, at 9 August 2011, was in the same state or territory as their 2016 address. It is the ACLD's state-level reading of UAI5P, the Census item derived from the mark box answer to the question \"Where did the person usually live five years ago (at 9 August 2011)?\" and it applies to persons aged five years and over. The five-year window lines up with the ACLD's own wave spacing, so it can be checked against the person's linked 2011 record.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Usual Address Five Years Ago Indicator (UAI5P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10502016","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address Five Years Ago Indicator for State","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A categorical indicator separating no change of address, a move within the state or territory, an interstate move, and residence overseas five years earlier, with not stated and not applicable residuals. Geography is the ASGS state and territory level.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Usual Address Five Years Ago Indicator (UAI5P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10502016","lim":"It records only the two endpoints, so a person who left Queensland for Victoria in 2013 and returned in 2015 counts as a non-mover, and someone who moved four times inside one state counts once. Read against the linked 2011 Census record it can also disagree, because the Census item is the respondent's own recollection of where they usually lived in 2011 rather than the address the 2011 form recorded.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":173},{"n":"STATE_MOVE_5YR_21","d":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2021 Census was in the same state or territory as their 2021 address.","full":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2021 Census was in the same state or territory as their 2021 address. The Census item behind it indicates whether a person lived at the same address five years earlier, elsewhere in Australia, or in another country, and the ACLD resolves the middle category to state and territory. The 2021 reference date is 10 August 2016, which is the night of the previous Census, so the question asks about the same point in time that the ACLD's 2016 wave records directly.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address five years ago indicator (UAI5P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-five-years-ago-indicator-uai5p","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address Five Years Ago Indicator for State","t":"categorical","k":"finite source-defined values","def":"A categorical indicator of same address, an intrastate move, an interstate move, and overseas residence five years earlier, with codes for not stated and not applicable. The applicable population is persons aged five years and over, so children born after the reference date are not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address five years ago indicator (UAI5P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-five-years-ago-indicator-uai5p","lim":"The five years to 2021 contain both the pre-pandemic period and the border closures, and the indicator cannot separate them: a move recorded here may have happened in 2017 or in 2021. Comparing this column with STATE_MOVE_5YR_16 also compares two different five-year windows rather than tracking the same people's continuing mobility, which is what the linked 2011 and 2016 addresses are for.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":174},{"n":"STRD_P_11","d":"The structure of the private dwelling the person was counted in at the 2011 Census: separate house, semi-detached, flat or other.","full":"The structure of the private dwelling the person was counted in at the 2011 Census: separate house, semi-detached, flat or other. The 2011 dictionary defines STRD as a variable that \"Records the structure of private dwellings.\" and notes that the Census classification is close to, but not the same as, the ABS standard dwelling classification. It is a dwelling attribute carried on a person's row, so everyone enumerated in the same dwelling shares the value, and TEND_P_11 and TENLLD_P_11 describe that dwelling's tenure.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Structure (STRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9502011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Dwelling Structure","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 dwelling structure (STRD) code","def":"A two-digit code: 11 separate house; 21 and 22 semi-detached, row or terrace and townhouse by storeys; 31 to 34 flat, unit or apartment by block height and by attachment to a house; 91 caravan, cabin or houseboat; 93 improvised home, tent or sleepers out; 94 house or flat attached to a shop or office; && not stated; @@ not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Structure (STRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9502011","lim":"The 2011 codes do not map one to one onto later waves. Caravans sat with cabins and houseboats in a single code 91 until 2016 split them, and 2011 code 33 covers every block of four storeys or more, which 2021 divides in two. Structure is also silent on quality and on ownership: a separate house here may be a rented share house or an owner-occupied family home.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":175},{"n":"STRD_P_16","d":"The structure of the private dwelling the person was counted in at the 2016 Census, the wave at which caravans were separated from cabins and houseboats.","full":"The structure of the private dwelling the person was counted in at the 2016 Census, the wave at which caravans were separated from cabins and houseboats. The dictionary keeps the 2011 definition, a variable that \"Records the structure of private dwellings.\", but code 91 now means a caravan alone and a new code 92 carries cabins and houseboats. The flat categories are unchanged from 2011, so 31 to 34 mean the same thing in both waves.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Structure (STRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9502016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Dwelling Structure","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 dwelling structure (STRD) code","def":"A two-digit code: 11 separate house; 21 and 22 semi-detached, row or terrace and townhouse by storeys; 31, 32 and 33 flat or apartment in a one or two, three, or four or more storey block; 34 flat attached to a house; 91 caravan; 92 cabin or houseboat; 93 improvised home, tent or sleepers out; 94 house or flat attached to a shop or office; && not stated; @@ not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Dwelling Structure (STRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9502016","lim":"Code 33 is the trap between waves. In 2016 it is any block of four storeys or more, while in 2021 the same number means a four to eight storey block and nine or more storeys move to 34, which in 2016 means a flat attached to a house. A 2016 to 2021 comparison on raw codes therefore turns high-rise flats into granny flats without any error being visible.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":175},{"n":"STRD_P_21","d":"The structure of the private dwelling the person was counted in at the 2021 Census, the first with a nine or more storey category.","full":"The structure of the private dwelling the person was counted in at the 2021 Census, the first with a nine or more storey category. The dictionary's definition is that \"This variable records the structure of private dwellings.\", and for 2021 the flat and apartment block was renumbered so that 33 is four to eight storeys, 34 is nine or more and 35 is a flat attached to a house. The 2021 Census also revised what counts as a structurally independent separate house, dropping the earlier half-metre separation rule.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Dwelling structure (STRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/dwelling-structure-strd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Dwelling Structure","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 dwelling structure (STRD) code","def":"A two-digit code: 11 separate house; 21 and 22 semi-detached, row or terrace and townhouse by storeys; 31, 32, 33 and 34 flat or apartment by block height from one or two storeys to nine or more; 35 flat attached to a house; 91 caravan; 92 cabin or houseboat; 93 improvised home, tent or sleepers out; 94 house or flat attached to a shop or office; && not stated; @@ not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Dwelling structure (STRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/dwelling-structure-strd","lim":"Reading the numeric code straight across the ACLD's three waves silently reclassifies dwellings: 34 is a nine or more storey apartment in 2021 but a flat attached to a house in 2011 and 2016, and 35 does not exist before 2021. The revised separate house rule also shifts a small number of dwellings between codes 11 and 21 for reasons that have nothing to do with rebuilding.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":175},{"n":"STUP_11","d":"Whether the person was a full-time student, a part-time student, or not attending an educational institution at the 2011 Census.","full":"Whether the person was a full-time student, a part-time student, or not attending an educational institution at the 2011 Census. The dictionary defines STUP as a variable that \"Describes the full-time or part-time status of students.\", and it applies to all persons rather than only to those of school age. TYPP_11 on the same row says which kind of institution, and the two are meant to be read together.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Full/Part Time Student Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 full-time/part-time student status code","def":"A one-character code: 1 not attending; 2 full-time student; 3 part-time student; 4 institution stated but full-time or part-time status not stated; & both institution and status not stated; V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602011","lim":"Full-time or part-time is meant to follow what the institution considers the person to be, but it is reported by whoever filled in the household form, so it will not reconcile line for line with a provider's own study load records or with a Centrelink student payment assessment. The question also asks about attendance on one night in August, so a person who studied earlier in 2011 and finished before the Census counts as not attending.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":176},{"n":"STUP_16","d":"Whether the person was a full-time student, a part-time student, or not attending an educational institution at the 2016 Census.","full":"Whether the person was a full-time student, a part-time student, or not attending an educational institution at the 2016 Census. The 2016 dictionary keeps the 2011 wording exactly, a variable that \"Describes the full-time or part-time status of students.\", so STUP_11 and STUP_16 are directly comparable. The ABS also publishes TYSTAP, which combines this variable with TYPP and age, and which has been produced since the 2011 Census.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Full/Part Time Student Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 full-time/part-time student status code","def":"A one-character code: 1 not attending; 2 full-time student; 3 part-time student; 4 institution stated but full-time or part-time status not stated; & both institution and status not stated; V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602016","lim":"The non-response rate on this item was 6.8 per cent in 2016 and fell to 5.6 per cent in 2021, so a rise in the student count between the two waves partly reflects better answering rather than more study. The column also does not distinguish a student on leave from one attending, since the question asks about attendance at an educational institution and not about enrolment status.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":176},{"n":"STUP_21","d":"Whether the person was a full-time student, a part-time student, or not attending an educational institution at the 2021 Census.","full":"Whether the person was a full-time student, a part-time student, or not attending an educational institution at the 2021 Census. The dictionary defines it as a variable where \"This variable describes the full-time or part-time status of students.\", and for 2021 the question wording and instructions were refined and a COVID-19 instruction added to the online form. Non-response fell from 6.8 per cent in 2016 to 5.6 per cent in 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Full-time/part-time student status (STUP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/full-timepart-time-student-status-stup","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Full/Part Time Student Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 full-time/part-time student status code","def":"A one-character code running 1 not attending, 2 full-time student, 3 part-time student and 4 institution stated with status not stated, with & where neither institution nor status was given and V for an overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Full-time/part-time student status (STUP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/full-timepart-time-student-status-stup","lim":"A student learning from home during the 2021 lockdowns is still attending an institution, so this column cannot be used to measure disrupted schooling; it records the enrolment relationship, not whether a classroom was open. The added instruction and the improved response rate also mean that part of any 2016 to 2021 increase in students is a reporting effect.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":176},{"n":"STUP_FP_11","d":"The female parent's full-time or part-time student status at the 2011 Census, copied onto the sampled person's row from her own Census record.","full":"The female parent's full-time or part-time student status at the 2011 Census, copied onto the sampled person's row from her own Census record. The underlying variable \"Describes the full-time or part-time status of students.\" and applies to all persons, so a mother studying part-time while working appears here as a part-time student. STUP_MP_11 carries the same measure for the male parent and STUP_SP_11 for a spouse or partner.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Full/Part Time Student Status of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 student status code, female parent","def":"A one-character code: 1 not attending; 2 full-time student; 3 part-time student; 4 institution stated but full-time or part-time status not stated; & both institution and status not stated; V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602011","lim":"It is filled only where a female parent was enumerated in the same family on Census night, so lone father families, adults living apart from parents and household visitors all sit at not applicable for reasons that have nothing to do with study. Combined with the not attending code, that makes a blank and a 1 easy to confuse in a tabulation.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":177},{"n":"STUP_FP_16","d":"The female parent's full-time or part-time student status at the 2016 Census, on a category frame unchanged from 2011.","full":"The female parent's full-time or part-time student status at the 2016 Census, on a category frame unchanged from 2011. The base variable \"Describes the full-time or part-time status of students.\", so this column and STUP_FP_11 measure the same thing five years apart and can be tabulated against each other. Whether the mother was studying at school, TAFE or university is in TYPP_FP_16, not here.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Full/Part Time Student Status of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 student status code, female parent","def":"A one-character code: 1 not attending; 2 full-time student; 3 part-time student; 4 institution stated but full-time or part-time status not stated; & both institution and status not stated; V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602016","lim":"Mature-age study is often part-time and episodic, and a Census-night snapshot five years apart will miss a mother who completed a course in 2013 and another who started in 2017, so this pair of columns understates how many parents studied across the period. It also cannot say what she was studying toward, since level and field of qualification are separate variables.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":177},{"n":"STUP_FP_21","d":"The female parent's full-time or part-time student status at the 2021 Census, after the question was reworded and a COVID-19 instruction added online.","full":"The female parent's full-time or part-time student status at the 2021 Census, after the question was reworded and a COVID-19 instruction added online. The base variable is one where \"This variable describes the full-time or part-time status of students.\", and the ACLD attaches the mother's value to the sampled person's row. The 2021 categories still run not attending, full-time and part-time, so the comparison with 2016 holds at the level of those three.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Full-time/part-time student status (STUP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/full-timepart-time-student-status-stup","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Full/Part Time Student Status of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 student status code, female parent","def":"A one-character code running 1 not attending, 2 full-time student, 3 part-time student and 4 institution stated with status not stated, with & where neither institution nor status was given and V for an overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Full-time/part-time student status (STUP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/full-timepart-time-student-status-stup","lim":"A parent studying online through lockdown counts as attending, so this column will not identify families whose study was interrupted in 2021. The value also belongs to a woman identified as the person's female parent in that Census household, which need not be the same woman as in 2016 where a family reformed between waves.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":177},{"n":"STUP_MP_11","d":"The male parent's full-time or part-time student status at the 2011 Census, read from his own Census record.","full":"The male parent's full-time or part-time student status at the 2011 Census, read from his own Census record. The base variable \"Describes the full-time or part-time status of students.\", and the ACLD holds it against the sampled person rather than against the father, so it is a characteristic of the household the person grew up in. SIEMP_MP_11 on the same row gives his employment status in the same week.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Full/Part Time Student Status of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 student status code, male parent","def":"A one-character code: 1 not attending; 2 full-time student; 3 part-time student; 4 institution stated but full-time or part-time status not stated; & both institution and status not stated; V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602011","lim":"Very few fathers of school-age children are students, so this column is dominated by code 1 and by not applicable, and small cell counts make it fragile for anything except a broad indicator of a studying household. It also cannot separate a father who never studied from one who finished a qualification before Census night; HEAP for the male parent is the variable for attainment.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":177},{"n":"STUP_MP_16","d":"The male parent's full-time or part-time student status at the 2016 Census, on the same categories as 2011.","full":"The male parent's full-time or part-time student status at the 2016 Census, on the same categories as 2011. The dictionary keeps the definition of a variable that \"Describes the full-time or part-time status of students.\", so the 2011 and 2016 male parent columns can be compared directly. The combined TYSTAP variable, produced since 2011, pairs this with type of institution and age, but the ACLD carries the two separately.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Full/Part Time Student Status of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 student status code, male parent","def":"A one-character code: 1 not attending; 2 full-time student; 3 part-time student; 4 institution stated but full-time or part-time status not stated; & both institution and status not stated; V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602016","lim":"The column is only present where a male parent was enumerated in the person's family, so it is missing for most lone mother families and for adults living independently, and a comparison of studying fathers between waves partly tracks changes in who was living with whom. Non-response on the item was 6.8 per cent in 2016, which lands in code 4 or the & code rather than being imputed.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":177},{"n":"STUP_MP_21","d":"The male parent's full-time or part-time student status at the 2021 Census, after the 2021 question refinements.","full":"The male parent's full-time or part-time student status at the 2021 Census, after the 2021 question refinements. The base variable is one where \"This variable describes the full-time or part-time status of students.\", and the value here belongs to the father identified in the person's 2021 Census family. Non-response on the item improved to 5.6 per cent in 2021 from 6.8 per cent in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Full-time/part-time student status (STUP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/full-timepart-time-student-status-stup","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Full/Part Time Student Status of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 student status code, male parent","def":"A one-character code running 1 not attending, 2 full-time student, 3 part-time student and 4 institution stated with status not stated, with & where neither institution nor status was given and V for an overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Full-time/part-time student status (STUP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/full-timepart-time-student-status-stup","lim":"Better answering in 2021 means a small part of any measured rise in studying fathers between 2016 and 2021 is a change in reporting, not in behaviour. The column also carries no start or end date, so it cannot say whether a father shown as a part-time student in 2021 had been studying since 2016 or enrolled the month before Census night.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":177},{"n":"STUP_SP_11","d":"The student status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census, taken from the partner's own form.","full":"The student status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2011 Census, taken from the partner's own form. The base variable \"Describes the full-time or part-time status of students.\", so a partner enrolled at university appears as a full-time or part-time student and a partner not enrolled at anything appears as not attending. A value exists only where a spouse or partner was enumerated in the same household on Census night.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Full/Part Time Student Status of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 student status code, spouse or partner","def":"A one-character code: 1 not attending; 2 full-time student; 3 part-time student; 4 institution stated but full-time or part-time status not stated; & both institution and status not stated; V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602011","lim":"It cannot be used to identify student couples on its own, because the sampled person's own status is in STUP_11 and the two have to be crossed; a blank here is not evidence that the partner was not studying. De facto and registered partners are both in scope, but a partner living elsewhere for work or study, which is common precisely among students, is out of scope entirely.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":177},{"n":"STUP_SP_16","d":"The student status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2016 Census, on categories unchanged from 2011.","full":"The student status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2016 Census, on categories unchanged from 2011. The dictionary defines the base variable as one that \"Describes the full-time or part-time status of students.\", and the ACLD copies the partner's value across. Read with SIEMP_SP_16 it separates a partner who was studying from one who was working, and it will show both where the partner did each.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Full/Part Time Student Status of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 student status code, spouse or partner","def":"A one-character code: 1 not attending; 2 full-time student; 3 part-time student; 4 institution stated but full-time or part-time status not stated; & both institution and status not stated; V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Full/Part-Time Student Status (STUP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9602016","lim":"The column identifies the partner in the 2016 household, so where a person separated and repartnered between waves a change from full-time student to not attending is a change of partner, not a change in anyone's study. It also stops at status and does not say whether the partner's course was a degree, a certificate or secondary school.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":177},{"n":"STUP_SP_21","d":"The student status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2021 Census, after the question was reworded and a COVID-19 instruction was added online.","full":"The student status of the person's spouse or partner at the 2021 Census, after the question was reworded and a COVID-19 instruction was added online. The base variable is one where \"This variable describes the full-time or part-time status of students.\", so the partner is placed in not attending, full-time or part-time study. The three substantive categories match 2016 and 2011, which is what makes the ACLD's three waves comparable at that level.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Full-time/part-time student status (STUP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/full-timepart-time-student-status-stup","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Full/Part Time Student Status of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 student status code, spouse or partner","def":"A one-character code running 1 not attending, 2 full-time student, 3 part-time student and 4 institution stated with status not stated, with & where neither institution nor status was given and V for an overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Full-time/part-time student status (STUP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/full-timepart-time-student-status-stup","lim":"The 2021 wave was taken while many campuses were closed and international students were offshore, so a partner enrolled but stranded overseas is not in the household and is absent from this column altogether. That absence is not a fall in student partners; it is a fall in partners who were counted.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":177},{"n":"SYNTHETIC_AEUID","d":"The person key for the ACLD row, identifying one sampled person and joining their Census history to the rest of PLIDA.","full":"The person key for the ACLD row, identifying one sampled person and joining their Census history to the rest of PLIDA. In the real asset the ACLD is a five per cent random sample of people counted on Census night, carried forward using \"a mix of deterministic and probabilistic linkage methodologies\", with the 2016 and 2021 Censuses also linked to the ABS person linkage spine. In fplida the value is generated rather than derived from anyone, but it behaves like the real key: one value per sampled person, stable across every column on the row.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD), microdata and TableBuilder","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Synthetic person ID for ACLD record","k":"PLIDA person linkage key (synthetic)","def":"An opaque identifier with no meaning in its digits. It is not a Census form number, not a household number, and not decodable back to a person, so it can be matched but not read.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD), microdata and TableBuilder","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","lim":"It does not tell you whether the person linked at every wave. A row exists for each sampled person, and a wave where linkage failed looks in the data exactly like a wave where the person had died, left the country or was missed by the Census, so missing 2021 columns must not be read as attrition from Australia. It is also a person key and not a family key: two members of one couple sampled independently carry unrelated values and nothing here shows they lived together.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"TEND_P_11","d":"Whether the private dwelling the person lived in at the 2011 Census was owned outright, owned with a mortgage, rented or held some other way.","full":"Whether the private dwelling the person lived in at the 2011 Census was owned outright, owned with a mortgage, rented or held some other way. The dictionary's definition is that the variable \"Describes whether a dwelling is owned, being purchased or rented. Dwellings occupied under a life tenure scheme can be considered as being owned.\" It is an attribute of the dwelling carried on the person's row, and TENLLD_P_11 breaks the rented category down by landlord.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Tenure Type (TEND)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9702011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Tenure Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 tenure type (TEND) code","def":"A one-character code: 1 owned outright; 2 owned with a mortgage; 3 being purchased under a rent/buy scheme; 4 rented; 5 being occupied rent-free; 6 being occupied under a life tenure scheme; 7 other tenure type; & not stated; @ not applicable. The population is occupied private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Tenure Type (TEND)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9702011","lim":"Code 3 reads as a rent/buy scheme in 2011 and a shared equity scheme from 2016; the ABS treats this as a relabel of the same category, so the wording changes between waves but the group does not. Tenure belongs to the dwelling and not to the person: a boarder or an adult child in an owner-occupied house carries owned outright, which makes this column a poor proxy for whether the individual is a homeowner.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":178},{"n":"TEND_P_16","d":"Whether the private dwelling the person lived in at the 2016 Census was owned outright, owned with a mortgage, rented or held some other way.","full":"Whether the private dwelling the person lived in at the 2016 Census was owned outright, owned with a mortgage, rented or held some other way. The 2016 dictionary shortens the definition to a variable that \"Describes whether a dwelling is owned, being purchased or rented.\" and relabels code 3 from a rent/buy scheme to a shared equity scheme. The remaining categories match 2011, so the ownership and rental splits are comparable across the two waves.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Tenure Type (TEND)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9702016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Tenure Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 tenure type (TEND) code","def":"A one-character code: 1 owned outright; 2 owned with a mortgage; 3 being purchased under a shared equity scheme; 4 rented; 5 being occupied rent-free; 6 being occupied under a life tenure scheme; 7 other tenure type; & not stated; @ not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Tenure Type (TEND)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9702016","lim":"Owned with a mortgage does not measure how much is owed, so a household two years into a loan and one two months from paying it out are the same code, and a shift from 2 to 1 between waves can be a refinance ending as easily as a windfall. Non-response was 7.7 per cent in 2016, high enough that the not stated code has to be reported rather than dropped.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":178},{"n":"TEND_P_21","d":"Whether the private dwelling the person lived in at the 2021 Census was owned outright, owned with a mortgage, rented or held some other way.","full":"Whether the private dwelling the person lived in at the 2021 Census was owned outright, owned with a mortgage, rented or held some other way. The dictionary defines it as a variable where \"This variable describes whether a dwelling is owned, being purchased or rented.\", with only minor category label changes for 2021 and non-response down to 5.4 per cent from 7.7 per cent in 2016. The distinction between owners with and without a mortgage has been in the question since 2006, so it holds across all three ACLD waves.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Tenure type (TEND)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/tenure-type-tend","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Tenure Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 tenure type (TEND) code","def":"A one-character code: 1 owned outright; 2 owned with a mortgage; 3 purchased under a shared equity scheme; 4 rented; 5 occupied rent free; 6 occupied under a life tenure scheme; 7 other; & not stated; @ not applicable. The population is occupied private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Tenure type (TEND)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/tenure-type-tend","lim":"TEND_P_21 and TENLLD_P_21 disagree by design on rent-free dwellings: this column keeps code 5 for occupied rent free while the 2021 tenure and landlord variable folds rent-free houses into other tenure type. A tabulation that uses whichever column is handier will therefore produce two different counts of rent-free housing from the same Census.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":178},{"n":"TENLLD_P_11","d":"Tenure of the person's dwelling at the 2011 Census with the rented category split by who the landlord was.","full":"Tenure of the person's dwelling at the 2011 Census with the rented category split by who the landlord was. The dictionary defines it as a variable that \"Combines Tenure Type (TEND) and Landlord Type (LLDD) to provide more detailed information for rented dwellings.\", so it is a derived combination rather than a separate question. It is the column that separates public housing from a private rental in 2011, which TEND_P_11 on its own cannot do.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Tenure and Landlord Type (TENLLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9802011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Tenure and Landlord Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 tenure and landlord type (TENLLD) code","def":"A one-character code: 1 owned outright; 2 owned with a mortgage; 3 to 8 rented, by real estate agent, state or territory housing authority, person not in the same household, housing co-operative, community or church group, other landlord, and landlord not stated; 9 other tenure type; & tenure not stated; @ not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Tenure and Landlord Type (TENLLD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9802011","lim":"The landlord categories are the respondent's description of who they pay, so a community housing tenancy managed under a head lease from a state authority can land in either code 4 or code 6 depending on who the household thinks the landlord is. That makes the public and community housing split softer than it looks, particularly in states that transferred stock to providers.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":179},{"n":"TENLLD_P_16","d":"Tenure of the person's dwelling at the 2016 Census with the rented category split by landlord, on the same code list as 2011.","full":"Tenure of the person's dwelling at the 2016 Census with the rented category split by landlord, on the same code list as 2011. The dictionary again defines it as a variable that \"Combines Tenure Type (TEND) and Landlord Type (LLDD) to provide more detailed information for rented dwellings.\", and the eleven categories are numbered exactly as they were in 2011. That stability ends at 2021, when the rented codes were reordered.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Tenure and Landlord Type (TENLLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9802016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Tenure and Landlord Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 tenure and landlord type (TENLLD) code","def":"A one-character code: 1 owned outright; 2 owned with a mortgage; 3 rented from a real estate agent; 4 rented from a state or territory housing authority; 5 rented from a person not in the same household; 6 rented from a housing co-operative, community or church group; 7 other landlord; 8 landlord not stated; 9 other tenure type; & tenure not stated; @ not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Tenure and Landlord Type (TENLLD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9802016","lim":"Code 5 means a person not in the same household in 2016 but a community housing provider in 2021, so a raw comparison of the two waves converts private landlords into community housing and back again. The column also cannot identify a boarder within a household, because it describes the dwelling's tenancy and not the arrangement between people inside it.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":179},{"n":"TENLLD_P_21","d":"Tenure of the person's dwelling at the 2021 Census with the rented category split by landlord, on a renumbered code list.","full":"Tenure of the person's dwelling at the 2021 Census with the rented category split by landlord, on a renumbered code list. For 2021 the housing co-operative, community or church group category was reworded to community housing provider and moved to code 5, pushing a person not in the same household to code 6, and the dictionary records that \"'Other tenure type' has been rescoped for 2021 to include houses being occupied rent free.\" That last change is why this column and TEND_P_21 count rent-free housing differently.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Tenure and landlord type (TENLLD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/tenure-and-landlord-type-tenlld","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Tenure and Landlord Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 tenure and landlord type (TENLLD) code","def":"A one-character code: 1 owned outright; 2 owned with a mortgage; 3 rented from a real estate agent; 4 rented from a state or territory housing authority; 5 rented from a community housing provider; 6 rented from a person not in the same household; 7 other landlord; 8 landlord not stated; 9 other tenure type; & tenure not stated; @ not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Tenure and landlord type (TENLLD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/tenure-and-landlord-type-tenlld","lim":"Codes 5 and 6 swap meaning between 2016 and 2021, so a longitudinal table built on the raw values shows a wave of households moving from private to community landlords that never happened. The rescoping of other tenure type also means the 2021 code 9 group is larger than the 2016 one for a definitional reason, not because more households fell outside the usual arrangements.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":180},{"n":"TISP_11","d":"The number of children a woman reported ever having borne, as recorded at the 2011 Census.","full":"The number of children a woman reported ever having borne, as recorded at the 2011 Census. The dictionary defines it as a variable that \"Records the number of children ever born (live births) to each female.\", and the 2011 form still carried the instruction to count live births only, which was removed for 2016. It applies to females aged 15 years and over; TISRP_11 holds the same count in bands.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Number of Children Ever Born (TISP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9902011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Children Ever Born","t":"categorical","k":"Count of children ever born, 00 to 30","def":"A two-digit count from 00 for no children through 29, with 30 standing for thirty or more children. The residual codes are && not stated, @@ not applicable and VV overseas visitor, and not applicable covers males and females under 15 years.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Number of Children Ever Born (TISP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9902011","lim":"It counts births, not the children a woman is raising: an adopted or step child never appears and a child who has died still does. Because the live-births instruction was dropped after 2011, a rise between TISP_11 and TISP_16 for the same woman can reflect the changed instruction rather than another birth, which matters in a longitudinal file where the same person is observed twice.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":181},{"n":"TISP_16","d":"The number of children a woman reported ever having borne, as recorded at the 2016 Census.","full":"The number of children a woman reported ever having borne, as recorded at the 2016 Census. The 2016 definition drops the live births qualifier and reads that the variable \"Records the number of children ever born to each female.\", because the instruction limiting the count to live births was removed for 2016 on question sensitivity grounds. The applicable population is unchanged at females aged 15 years and over.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Number of Children Ever Born (TISP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9902016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Children Ever Born","t":"categorical","k":"Count of children ever born, 00 to 30","def":"A two-digit count: 00 no children, 01 to 29 counted individually, and 30 for thirty or more. Residuals are && not stated, @@ not applicable and VV overseas visitor, with not applicable covering males and females aged under 15.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Number of Children Ever Born (TISP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter9902016","lim":"The variable is asked of women only, so it cannot be used to measure men's fertility or a couple's combined children, and a household's children are better counted from the family composition columns. Non-response was 8.0 per cent in 2016, the highest of the three ACLD waves, so the not stated code cannot be treated as a rounding error.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":181},{"n":"TISP_21","d":"The number of children a woman reported ever having borne, as recorded at the 2021 Census.","full":"The number of children a woman reported ever having borne, as recorded at the 2021 Census. The dictionary defines it as a variable that \"This variable records the number of children ever born to each female aged 15 years and over.\", and states that no change was made for 2021, so TISP_16 and TISP_21 are on the same basis. Non-response fell from 8.0 per cent in 2016 to 6.7 per cent in 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of children ever born (TISP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/number-children-ever-born-tisp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Children Ever Born","t":"categorical","k":"Count of children ever born, 00 to 30","def":"A two-digit count from 00 to 29 with 30 for thirty or more children, and && not stated, @@ not applicable and VV overseas visitor as residuals. Only females aged 15 years and over take a substantive value.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of children ever born (TISP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/number-children-ever-born-tisp","lim":"Because the count is cumulative and the ACLD observes the same women in 2011, 2016 and 2021, a fall between waves is impossible in life but does occur in the data, through misreporting or through a different person answering the household form. Treating any decrease as real fertility rather than as a reporting artefact is the error this column invites.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":181},{"n":"TISRP_11","d":"The banded version of the number of children a woman reported ever having borne at the 2011 Census.","full":"The banded version of the number of children a woman reported ever having borne at the 2011 Census. The dictionary defines it as a variable that \"Records the number of children ever born (live births) to each female in ranges.\", so it is TISP_11 collapsed rather than a separate question, and the 2011 form still asked for live births only. Everything above seven children is grouped into a single top band.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Number of Children Ever Born (ranges) (TISRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10002011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Children Ever Born (Ranges)","t":"categorical","k":"Children ever born, ranges 0 to 8","def":"A one-character code: 0 no children through 7 seven children, then 8 for eight or more children. Residuals are & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor, with not applicable covering males and females under 15 years.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Number of Children Ever Born (ranges) (TISRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10002011","lim":"The top band is closed at eight or more, so an average calculated from these codes understates fertility in the populations where large families are most common, including some Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and some migrant groups. TISP_11 is the column to use whenever a mean or a distribution above seven matters.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":182},{"n":"TISRP_16","d":"The banded version of the number of children a woman reported ever having borne at the 2016 Census.","full":"The banded version of the number of children a woman reported ever having borne at the 2016 Census. The 2016 definition drops the live births qualifier, reading that the variable \"Records the number of children ever born to each female in ranges.\", which follows the removal of that instruction from the form for 2016. The bands themselves are unchanged from 2011.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Number of Children Ever Born (ranges) (TISRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10002016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Children Ever Born (Ranges)","t":"categorical","k":"Children ever born, ranges 0 to 8","def":"A one-character code from 0 for no children to 7 for seven children, with 8 for eight or more. The residual codes are & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor; only females aged 15 years and over take a substantive value.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Number of Children Ever Born (ranges) (TISRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10002016","lim":"The bands are identical across waves but their content is not, because the 2016 instruction change means a woman may report differently in 2016 from 2011 without any birth occurring. A crosstab of TISRP_11 by TISRP_16 will therefore show off-diagonal movement in both directions, and only the upward movement can be a birth.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":182},{"n":"TISRP_21","d":"The banded version of the number of children a woman reported ever having borne at the 2021 Census.","full":"The banded version of the number of children a woman reported ever having borne at the 2021 Census. The dictionary defines it as a variable that \"This variable records the number of children ever born to each female aged 15 years and over in ranges.\" and records no change for 2021, so the bands line up with 2016 and with 2011. It is the column to use where a full count would produce cells too small to release.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of children ever born (ranges) (TISRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/number-children-ever-born-ranges-tisrp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Children Ever Born (Ranges)","t":"categorical","k":"Children ever born, ranges 0 to 8","def":"A one-character code: 0 no children, 1 to 7 for each number of children, and 8 for eight or more. Residuals are & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of children ever born (ranges) (TISRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/number-children-ever-born-ranges-tisrp","lim":"Banding hides the difference between a woman with eight children and one with fifteen, and it also hides the not stated group inside a tabulation unless that code is reported separately, which matters more in 2021 than the 6.7 per cent non-response suggests because the missing women are not spread evenly across ages. Use TISP_21 when the exact count is needed.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":182},{"n":"TYPP_11","d":"The type of educational institution the person was attending at the 2011 Census, from preschool through to university.","full":"The type of educational institution the person was attending at the 2011 Census, from preschool through to university. The dictionary defines TYPP as a variable that \"Records the type of educational institution being attended.\", and it applies only to people attending an institution, so everyone else sits at not applicable. STUP_11 on the same row says whether that attendance was full-time or part-time.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Educational Institution Attending (TYPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10102011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Education Institution Attending","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 type of educational institution (TYPP) code","def":"A two-digit code: 10 preschool; 21 to 23 infants or primary by government, Catholic and other non-government; 31 to 33 the same three sectors for secondary; 40 a technical or further educational institution including TAFE; 50 a university or other tertiary institution; 60 other; && not stated; @@ not applicable; VV overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Educational Institution Attending (TYPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10102011","lim":"The tertiary codes do not survive to 2021: technical study is 40 and university 50 in 2011, whereas 2021 numbers them 41 and 42, so a comparison on raw codes across the ACLD's waves misassigns every tertiary student. The variable also names a sector and not a fee level or a school's performance, so code 23 covers both a low-fee religious school and an expensive independent one.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":183},{"n":"TYPP_16","d":"The type of educational institution the person was attending at the 2016 Census, on the same code list as 2011.","full":"The type of educational institution the person was attending at the 2016 Census, on the same code list as 2011. The dictionary repeats the definition of a variable that \"Records the type of educational institution being attended.\", so TYPP_11 and TYPP_16 can be compared code for code. The ABS also publishes TYSTAP, which combines this variable with student status and age, and which dates from the 2011 Census rather than from 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Educational Institution Attending (TYPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10102016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Education Institution Attending","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 type of educational institution (TYPP) code","def":"A two-digit code: 10 preschool; 21 to 23 infants or primary by government, Catholic and other non-government; 31 to 33 the same three sectors for secondary; 40 a technical or further educational institution including TAFE; 50 a university or other tertiary institution; 60 other; && not stated; @@ not applicable; VV overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Educational Institution Attending (TYPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10102016","lim":"There is no code for the mode of study, so a distance student at a regional university and one living on campus are both 50, and the column cannot support any claim about attendance in person. The dictionary defines it as a variable that \"This variable records the type of education institution being attended by people who are full-time or part-time students.\", and for 2021 the tertiary categories became 41 for vocational education including TAFE and private providers and 42 for university or other higher education. New not further defined codes 29, 39 and 49 were added because the online form asks the question in two parts.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Type of educational institution attending (TYPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/type-educational-institution-attending-typp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Education Institution Attending","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 type of educational institution (TYPP) code","def":"A two-digit code: 10 preschool; 21 to 23 and 29 primary by sector and not further defined; 31 to 33 and 39 secondary on the same pattern; 41 tertiary vocational education including TAFE and private providers; 42 tertiary university or other higher education; 49 tertiary not further defined; 60 other; && not stated; @@ not applicable; VV overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Type of educational institution attending (TYPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/type-educational-institution-attending-typp","lim":"Codes 29, 39 and 49 exist only from 2021 and hold people who answered the first part of the online question and not the second, so a 2016 to 2021 comparison that ignores them loses students rather than reclassifying them. The wider inclusion of private training providers in code 41 also means vocational study looks larger in 2021 than the 2016 code 40 group for a definitional reason.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":184},{"n":"TYPP_FP_11","d":"The type of educational institution the person's female parent was attending at the 2011 Census, taken from her own Census record.","full":"The type of educational institution the person's female parent was attending at the 2011 Census, taken from her own Census record. The base variable \"Records the type of educational institution being attended.\", and it is populated only for people who were attending one, so a mother not studying leaves the column at not applicable. STUP_FP_11 says whether her attendance was full-time or part-time.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Educational Institution Attending (TYPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10102011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Educational Institution Attended by Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 type of educational institution code, female parent","def":"A two-digit code: 10 preschool; 21 to 23 infants or primary by government, Catholic and other non-government; 31 to 33 the same three sectors for secondary; 40 a technical or further educational institution including TAFE; 50 a university or other tertiary institution; 60 other; && not stated; @@ not applicable; VV overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Educational Institution Attending (TYPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10102011","lim":"Two very different situations share the not applicable code here: no female parent was enumerated in the person's family, and a female parent was enumerated but was not studying. The base variable \"Records the type of educational institution being attended.\", so the 2011 and 2016 female parent columns can be tabulated against each other without a crosswalk. Most substantive values fall in 40 or 50, since a parent still at school is rare.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Educational Institution Attending (TYPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10102016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Educational Institution Attended by Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 type of educational institution code, female parent","def":"A two-digit code: 10 preschool; 21 to 23 infants or primary by government, Catholic and other non-government; 31 to 33 the same three sectors for secondary; 40 a technical or further educational institution including TAFE; 50 a university or other tertiary institution; 60 other; && not stated; @@ not applicable; VV overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Educational Institution Attending (TYPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10102016","lim":"Because the tertiary codes are the coarse 40 and 50 pair, this column cannot separate a mother retraining at a private registered training organisation from one at a public TAFE, a distinction the 2021 wording makes explicit and this wave cannot. The base variable \"This variable records the type of education institution being attended by people who are full-time or part-time students.\", and for 2021 vocational study is 41 and university or other higher education is 42, replacing the 40 and 50 pair used at the earlier waves. The not further defined codes 29, 39 and 49 appear here for the first time.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Type of educational institution attending (TYPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/type-educational-institution-attending-typp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Educational Institution Attended by Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 type of educational institution code, female parent","def":"A two-digit code: 10 preschool; 21 to 23 and 29 primary by sector and not further defined; 31 to 33 and 39 secondary on the same pattern; 41 tertiary vocational education including TAFE and private providers; 42 tertiary university or other higher education; 49 tertiary not further defined; 60 other; && not stated; @@ not applicable; VV overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Type of educational institution attending (TYPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/type-educational-institution-attending-typp","lim":"A mother's tertiary study cannot be compared with TYPP_FP_16 by code, because 41 and 42 in 2021 have no counterpart numbers in the earlier list and 40 and 50 no longer exist. The base variable \"Records the type of educational institution being attended.\", and only people attending an institution take a substantive code, so the column is dominated by not applicable. STUP_MP_11 gives his full-time or part-time status and SIEMP_MP_11 his employment in the same week.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Educational Institution Attending (TYPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10102011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Educational Institution Attended by Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 type of educational institution code, male parent","def":"A two-digit code: 10 preschool; 21 to 23 infants or primary by government, Catholic and other non-government; 31 to 33 the same three sectors for secondary; 40 a technical or further educational institution including TAFE; 50 a university or other tertiary institution; 60 other; && not stated; @@ not applicable; VV overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011 (cat. 2901.0), Type of Educational Institution Attending (TYPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter10102011","lim":"Studying fathers are uncommon, so substantive counts here are small and will often be suppressed or unstable once crossed with anything else; treating a zero cell as evidence that no fathers in a group studied is the mistake to avoid. The ABS defines the item as one that \"Records the type of educational institution being attended by the male parent\", including the male parent of nominal children and, in male same-sex couple families, the reference person. It is populated only while the person is enumerated as a child under 15, a dependent student or a non-dependent child in the family, so it thins as the 2011 panel ages, and the column also appears in the 2016-based panel table acld_1621.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item TYPP_MP_16","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Educational Institution Attended by Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 type of education institution attended by the male parent (4 categories)","def":"Four codes: 1 Secondary, 2 Technical or Further Educational Institution (including TAFE colleges), 3 University or other Tertiary Institution and 4 Other, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. It merges a father who is not attending an institution with a person who has no male parent on the record at all, including lone-mother families, female same-sex couple families and a father temporarily absent on Census Night, so the denominator for any share of studying fathers has to be built from the family variables rather than from this column.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":185},{"n":"TYPP_MP_21","d":"The type of education institution the sampled person's male parent was attending at the 2021 Census, on the same four categories used in 2011 and 2016.","full":"The type of education institution the sampled person's male parent was attending at the 2021 Census, on the same four categories used in 2011 and 2016. The person-level TYPP_21 was re-cut for 2021, with 'Infants' dropped from the primary categories and the tertiary categories renamed, but this parent column was not, so it stays comparable back to 2011 while TYPP_21 does not.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item TYPP_MP_21","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Educational Institution Attended by Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 type of education institution attended by the male parent (4 categories)","def":"Four codes: 1 Secondary, 2 Technical or Further Educational Institution (including TAFE colleges), 3 University or other Tertiary Institution and 4 Other, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record.
