Only the 2011-based table acld_1121 carries a 2011 column, so this is the baseline value against which TYPP_SP_16 and TYPP_SP_21 are read.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item TYPP_SP_11","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Educational Institution Attended by Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 type of education institution attended by the spouse or partner (4 categories)","def":"Four codes: 1 Secondary, 2 Technical or Further Educational Institution (including TAFE colleges), 3 University or other Tertiary Institution and 4 Other, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. The ABS defines it as \"This variable records the type of education institution being attended by a person's spouse or partner who is a full-time or part-time student\", and the four categories are unchanged from 2011, so the 2011 and 2016 columns line up exactly. The column sits in both ACLD tables, acld_1121 and acld_1621, so the same 2016 partner is described whichever panel a user starts from.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item TYPP_SP_16","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Educational Institution Attended by Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 type of education institution attended by the spouse or partner (4 categories)","def":"Four codes: 1 Secondary, 2 Technical or Further Educational Institution (including TAFE colleges), 3 University or other Tertiary Institution and 4 Other, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. The parent and partner items use this same four-way collapse in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 columns.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item TYPP_SP_16","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"Code 98 covers three different situations at once: a partner who is not studying, a partner temporarily absent on Census Night, and a person with no registered or de facto partner. The ABS defines it as \"This variable records the type of education institution being attended by a person's spouse or partner who is a full-time or part-time student\", and the four partner categories were left unchanged for 2021 even though the person-level TYPP_21 was renamed and expanded. A partner's study therefore cannot be compared with the person's own study at 2021 without collapsing TYPP_21 back to these four groups.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item TYPP_SP_21","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Educational Institution Attended by Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 type of education institution attended by the spouse or partner (4 categories)","def":"Four codes: 1 Secondary, 2 Technical or Further Educational Institution (including TAFE colleges), 3 University or other Tertiary Institution and 4 Other, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. The ABS describes it as a variable that \"combines Full-Time/Part-Time Student Status (STUP) with age categories and Type of Educational Institution Attending (TYPP) to provide more detailed information on persons attending an educational institution\". 2011 is the first Census for which TYSTAP was created, so the ACLD has no earlier wave of it, and TYPP_11 on the same row holds the institution type on its own.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Educational Institution: Attendee Status (TYSTAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter30302011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Educational Institution: Attendee Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 educational institution attendee status (20 categories)","def":"Twenty substantive codes: 1 preschool, 2 to 4 infants or primary by sector, 5 to 7 secondary by sector, 8 to 12 technical or further education split by full-time and part-time study and by age 15-24 against 25 and over, 13 to 17 university or other tertiary on the same split, and 18 to 20 other; plus 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Educational Institution: Attendee Status (TYSTAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter30302011","lim":"The age split is not an age variable. Because nothing changed between 2011 and 2016, TYSTAP_11 and TYSTAP_16 can be differenced directly; the break comes at 2021. The column also appears in the 2016-based table acld_1621.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Educational Institution: Attendee Status (TYSTAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter30302016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Educational Institution: Attendee Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 educational institution attendee status (20 categories)","def":"Twenty substantive codes: 1 preschool, 2 to 4 infants or primary by sector, 5 to 7 secondary by sector, 8 to 12 technical or further education split by full-time and part-time study and by age 15-24 against 25 and over, 13 to 17 university or other tertiary on the same split, and 18 to 20 other; plus 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Educational Institution: Attendee Status (TYSTAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter30302016","lim":"A move between codes is not evidence of a course change. Ageing past 25 shifts a continuing full-time university student from code 13 to code 14 with nothing else altering, so the age boundary generates transitions in a panel that is followed for five years at a time.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":186},{"n":"TYSTAP_21","d":"Attendee status at the 2021 Census, rebuilt on a wider set of categories than 2011 and 2016.","full":"Attendee status at the 2021 Census, rebuilt on a wider set of categories than 2011 and 2016. The ABS defines it as a variable that \"combines responses from Type of educational institution attending (TYPP), Full-time/part-time student status (STUP) and Age (AGEP) to indicate a person's attendee status at an education institution\". For 2021 the code numbers were realigned with TYPP, 'Infants' was dropped from the primary labels, the tertiary categories were renamed to vocational education and university or other higher education, and not further defined categories were added because the online form asks the institution question in two parts.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Educational institution: attendee status (TYSTAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/educational-institution-attendee-status-tystap","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Educational Institution: Attendee Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 educational institution attendee status (27 categories)","def":"Twenty-seven substantive codes in the ACLD 2021 column: 1 preschool, 2 to 4 primary by sector, 5 to 7 secondary by sector, 8 to 12 tertiary vocational education by study load and age, 13 to 17 tertiary university or other higher education on the same split, 18 to 20 other, 21 and 22 primary and secondary not further defined, and 23 to 27 tertiary not further defined; plus 997 not stated, 998 not applicable and 999 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Educational institution: attendee status (TYSTAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/educational-institution-attendee-status-tystap","lim":"It cannot be differenced against 2016 as though the categories held still. The not further defined codes absorb people who said they were attending but not what kind of institution, so a fall in Catholic or government primary between 2016 and 2021 can be an artefact of the two-part online question rather than a real shift between sectors.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":187},{"n":"UAI1P_11","d":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2011 Census was the same address, another address in Australia, or overseas.","full":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2011 Census was the same address, another address in Australia, or overseas. The ABS says \"The information acquired from the answers to the usual residence questions is recorded in the usual residence indicator variables\", of which this is one, so the reference date here is August 2010 and the overseas category is labelled accordingly. It is asked of people aged one year and over, and UAI5P_11 beside it carries the same question over five years.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Usual residence","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58402011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address One Year Ago Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 usual address one year ago indicator (3 categories)","def":"Three substantive codes: 1 same as in 2011, 2 elsewhere in Australia and 3 overseas in 2010, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable for children under one year and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Usual residence","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58402011","lim":"It says that the address changed, not where from. The ACLD carries no Place of Usual Residence One Year Ago column for 2011 - PUR1P starts at the 2016 wave - so the origin of a move in the year to August 2011 cannot be recovered from this table at all, and a person who moved twice within the year and returned to the same dwelling is coded 1 alongside people who never moved.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":188},{"n":"UAI1P_16","d":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2016 Census was the same address, another address in Australia, or overseas.","full":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2016 Census was the same address, another address in Australia, or overseas. The ABS says \"The information acquired from the answers to the usual residence questions is also used to create the usual residence indicator variables\", and for this wave the anchor dates move on: code 1 reads same as in 2016 and code 3 reads overseas in 2015. Non-response to the question was 8.3% in 2016, the highest of the three ACLD waves, and the column also appears in the 2016-based table acld_1621.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Usual residence","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58402016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address One Year Ago Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 usual address one year ago indicator (3 categories)","def":"Three substantive codes: 1 same as in 2016, 2 elsewhere in Australia and 3 overseas in 2015, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable for children under one year and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Usual residence","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58402016","lim":"The one-year window does not cover the gap between ACLD waves. Someone who moved in 2013 and stayed put is coded 1 here, so stringing UAI1P_11 and UAI1P_16 together counts far fewer movers than the panel actually contains; the five-year item is the one that spans the intercensal period.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":189},{"n":"UAI1P_21","d":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2021 Census was the same address, another address in Australia, or overseas.","full":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the 2021 Census was the same address, another address in Australia, or overseas. The ABS defines it as a variable indicating whether a person \"lived in the same address one year ago as their current usual residence\", lived elsewhere in Australia, or usually lived in another country, here against 10 August 2020. Non-response fell to 5.5% in 2021 from 8.3% in 2016, and the one-year window falls inside the COVID-19 period, so a move recorded here is a 2020 move.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address one year ago indicator (UAI1P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-one-year-ago-indicator-uai1p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address One Year Ago Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 usual address one year ago indicator (3 categories)","def":"Three substantive codes: 1 same as in 2021, 2 elsewhere in Australia and 3 overseas in 2020, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable for children under one year and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address one year ago indicator (UAI1P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-one-year-ago-indicator-uai1p","lim":"Not every value is the person's own answer. Where a person aged under 16 did not respond but their parents did, the ABS sets the child's UAI1P to the parent's value, so child mobility measured from this column is partly a copy of the parents' record rather than an independent observation.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":190},{"n":"UAI1P_SP_11","d":"Whether the sampled person's spouse or partner usually lived at the same address one year before the 2011 Census, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas.","full":"Whether the sampled person's spouse or partner usually lived at the same address one year before the 2011 Census, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas. The ABS notes it \"is derived from the spouse's mark box answer to the question on the Census forms which asks, 'Where did the person usually live one year ago?'\", so it is the partner's own answer copied onto this row rather than anything the sampled person reported. Read against UAI1P_11 it shows whether the couple arrived at the address together.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item UAI1P_SP_11","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address One Year Ago of Spouse or Partner Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 usual address one year ago indicator for the spouse or partner (3 categories)","def":"Three substantive codes: 1 same as in 2011, 2 elsewhere in Australia and 3 overseas in 2010, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. Not applicable covers a temporarily absent partner and any person without a registered or de facto partner.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item UAI1P_SP_11","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"It does not say the couple were together a year earlier. A partner coded 2 may have been living elsewhere because the relationship had not started, so the pair of indicators identifies a joint move only when other relationship variables rule that out.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":188},{"n":"UAI1P_SP_16","d":"Whether the sampled person's spouse or partner usually lived at the same address one year before the 2016 Census, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas.","full":"Whether the sampled person's spouse or partner usually lived at the same address one year before the 2016 Census, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas. The ABS notes it \"is derived from the spouse's mark box answer to the question on the Census forms which asks, 'Where did the person usually live one year ago?'\", and the anchor dates advance with the wave, so code 1 reads same as in 2016 and code 3 reads overseas in 2015. The column appears in both ACLD tables, acld_1121 and acld_1621.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item UAI1P_SP_16","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address One Year Ago of Spouse or Partner Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 usual address one year ago indicator for the spouse or partner (3 categories)","def":"Three substantive codes: 1 same as in 2016, 2 elsewhere in Australia and 3 overseas in 2015, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. Not applicable covers a temporarily absent partner and any person without a registered or de facto partner.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item UAI1P_SP_16","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"The partner behind the 2016 value need not be the partner behind the 2011 value. Because the item is refilled from whoever the partner is at each Census, a difference between UAI1P_SP_11 and UAI1P_SP_16 can reflect a change of partner rather than a move.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":189},{"n":"UAI1P_SP_21","d":"Whether the sampled person's spouse or partner usually lived at the same address one year before the 2021 Census, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas.","full":"Whether the sampled person's spouse or partner usually lived at the same address one year before the 2021 Census, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas. The ABS notes it \"is derived from the spouse's mark box answer to the question on the Census forms which asks, 'Where did the person usually live one year ago?'\", which for this wave means the year to 10 August 2021, a period of closed international and state borders. Code 3, overseas in 2020, is therefore rare by comparison with the earlier waves.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item UAI1P_SP_21","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address One Year Ago of Spouse or Partner Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 usual address one year ago indicator for the spouse or partner (3 categories)","def":"Three substantive codes: 1 same as in 2021, 2 elsewhere in Australia and 3 overseas in 2020, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. Not applicable covers a temporarily absent partner and any person without a registered or de facto partner.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item UAI1P_SP_21","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","lim":"It cannot be used to count partners who were overseas during the pandemic. A partner still living abroad on Census Night 2021 is not on the household form at all and produces a not applicable or absent-partner code, not code 3, which is reserved for partners who have since arrived.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":190},{"n":"UAI5P_11","d":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2011 Census was the same address, another address in Australia, or overseas, measured against 2006.","full":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2011 Census was the same address, another address in Australia, or overseas, measured against 2006. The ABS says that \"Use of usual residence indicators, in conjunction with the other variables relating to usual residence, make it possible to identify the pattern of net movement of people between three dates, i.e. Census Night, one year ago and five years ago\". Its five-year window reaches back to the 2006 Census, which is the base of the earlier ACLD panel, so it is the one mobility item that spans an intercensal gap.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Usual residence","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58402011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address Five Years Ago Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 usual address five years ago indicator (3 categories)","def":"Three substantive codes: 1 same as in 2011, 2 elsewhere in Australia and 3 overseas in 2006, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable for children under five years and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Usual residence","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58402011","lim":"It counts states, not moves. A person who moved three times and came back is coded 1, and a person who moved once is coded 2, so the column measures net displacement over five years rather than residential churn.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":191},{"n":"UAI5P_16","d":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2016 Census was the same address, another address in Australia, or overseas, measured against 2011.","full":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2016 Census was the same address, another address in Australia, or overseas, measured against 2011. The ABS says that \"Use of usual residence indicators, in conjunction with the other variables relating to usual residence, make it possible to identify the pattern of net movement of people between three dates, i.e. Census night, one year ago and five years ago\". Because the window closes exactly on the 2011 Census, this is the column that tells you whether an ACLD panel member moved between the first and second waves; non-response was 7.3% in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Usual residence","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58402016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address Five Years Ago Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 usual address five years ago indicator (3 categories)","def":"Three substantive codes: 1 same as in 2016, 2 elsewhere in Australia and 3 overseas in 2011, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable for children under five years and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Usual residence","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58402016","lim":"Code 1 is not proof that the 2011 and 2016 address records agree. The comparison is made from the respondent's own report of where they lived in 2011, not from the linked 2011 Census record, so it can disagree with the geography columns on the same row without either being wrong.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":192},{"n":"UAI5P_21","d":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2021 Census was the same address, another address in Australia, or overseas.","full":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the 2021 Census was the same address, another address in Australia, or overseas. The ABS defines it as a variable indicating whether a person \"lived in the same address five years ago as their current usual residence\", lived elsewhere in Australia, or usually lived in another country, here against 10 August 2016. Non-response was 6.0% in 2021, down from 7.3% in 2016, and for people aged under 20 who did not answer, the value is set to their parent's.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address five years ago indicator (UAI5P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-five-years-ago-indicator-uai5p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address Five Years Ago Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 usual address five years ago indicator (3 categories)","def":"Three substantive codes: 1 same as in 2021, 2 elsewhere in Australia and 3 overseas in 2016, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable for children under five years and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address five years ago indicator (UAI5P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-five-years-ago-indicator-uai5p","lim":"Category 2 is broader than it looks. Before 2011 the Census had a separate category for people whose five-year and one-year addresses were the same, and the ABS now merges that group into elsewhere in Australia before release, so recent movers and long-settled movers cannot be told apart within code 2.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":193},{"n":"UAI5P_SP_11","d":"Whether the sampled person's spouse or partner usually lived at the same address five years before the 2011 Census, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas.","full":"Whether the sampled person's spouse or partner usually lived at the same address five years before the 2011 Census, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas. The ABS notes it \"is derived from the spouse's mark box answer to the question on the Census forms which asks, 'Where did the person usually live five years ago?'\", so the reference point is 2006 and the answer belongs to the partner. Code 3 is the usual way to identify a partner who arrived in Australia between 2006 and 2011.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item UAI5P_SP_11","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address Five Years Ago of Spouse or Partner Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 usual address five years ago indicator for the spouse or partner (3 categories)","def":"Three substantive codes: 1 same as in 2011, 2 elsewhere in Australia and 3 overseas in 2006, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. Overseas in 2006 tells you where they were on one day five years earlier, not when they arrived, how long they have been here or whether they had lived in Australia before; YARP_SP_11 on the same row is the arrival item.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":191},{"n":"UAI5P_SP_16","d":"Whether the sampled person's spouse or partner usually lived at the same address five years before the 2016 Census, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas.","full":"Whether the sampled person's spouse or partner usually lived at the same address five years before the 2016 Census, elsewhere in Australia, or overseas. The ABS notes it \"is derived from the spouse's mark box answer to the question on the Census forms which asks, 'Where did the person usually live five years ago?'\", and the 2016 window closes on the 2011 Census, so it covers the same interval as the first gap in the ACLD panel. The column appears in both acld_1121 and acld_1621.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item UAI5P_SP_16","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address Five Years Ago of Spouse or Partner Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 usual address five years ago indicator for the spouse or partner (3 categories)","def":"Three substantive codes: 1 same as in 2016, 2 elsewhere in Australia and 3 overseas in 2011, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. The ABS notes it \"is derived from the spouse's mark box answer to the question on the Census forms which asks, 'Where did the person usually live five years ago?'\", which for this wave sets the reference point at 2016. The five years it covers include the closed-border period, so partners coded 3 arrived before March 2020 in almost every case.","dsrc":"ABS Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset, 2011-2016-2021 microdata data item list (data item definitions in cell comments), data item UAI5P_SP_21","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset/ACLD%202011_16_21%20detailed%20microdata.xlsx","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address Five Years Ago of Spouse or Partner Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2021 usual address five years ago indicator for the spouse or partner (3 categories)","def":"Three substantive codes: 1 same as in 2021, 2 elsewhere in Australia and 3 overseas in 2016, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. It exists only where the sampled person had a partner present on Census Night 2021, so partnership formation and dissolution decide who has a value, and analyses restricted to non-missing rows are conditioned on being partnered.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":193},{"n":"UAICP_11","d":"Whether the person was counted at home on Census Night 2011 or somewhere else in Australia.","full":"Whether the person was counted at home on Census Night 2011 or somewhere else in Australia. The ABS says \"Usual residence data provide information on the usually resident population of an area, and on the internal migration patterns at the state and regional levels\", and this indicator is what separates a resident from a visitor in the dwelling where they were enumerated. It is the column that decides whether the enumeration geography and the usual residence geography on the same row refer to the same place.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Usual residence","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58402011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 usual address indicator, Census Night (2 categories)","def":"Two substantive codes only: 1 at home and 2 elsewhere in Australia, with 99 unlinked record. Where usual residence was not stated the ABS imputes it, so some people counted as at home were placed there by the imputation rather than by their own form, and this column does not flag which ones.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":194},{"n":"UAICP_16","d":"Whether the person was counted at home on Census Night 2016 or somewhere else in Australia.","full":"Whether the person was counted at home on Census Night 2016 or somewhere else in Australia. Non-response to the underlying count was 8.4% in 2016, and the column also appears in the 2016-based table acld_1621.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2016, Number of Motor Vehicles (VEHD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter44402016","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Motor Vehicles (Ranges)","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2016 number of motor vehicles at the dwelling, ranges (5 categories)","def":"Five substantive codes: 0 no motor vehicles, 1 one, 2 two, 3 three and 4 four or more, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable and 99 unlinked record. At 2011 the stated exclusions are work that is part of paid employment, work in a family business and work done to qualify for a government benefit such as Newstart Allowance.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Unpaid work","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58002011","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Voluntary Work for an Organisation or Group","t":"categorical","k":"Census 2011 voluntary work for an organisation or group (2 categories)","def":"Two substantive codes, 1 not a volunteer and 2 volunteer, with 97 not stated, 98 not applicable for people aged under 15 years and 99 unlinked record.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2011, Unpaid work","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/ausstats/abs@.nsf/Lookup/2901.0Chapter58002011","lim":"Informal help is invisible here. The question was first asked at the 2006 Census and the ABS made no change to it for 2021. Non-response at the 2016 Census was 8.2 per cent, against 6.4 per cent in 2021. The person's own answer for the same year is VOLWP_16, and the male parent's other 2016 characteristics sit in the matching _MP_16 columns.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Voluntary work for an organisation or group (VOLWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/unpaid-work-and-care/voluntary-work-organisation-or-group-volwp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Voluntary Work Done for an Organisation or Group by Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census volunteer status code (2016)","def":"Two substantive codes, volunteer and not a volunteer, plus separate codes for not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor. The ABS made no change to the question for 2021 and non-response fell to 6.4 per cent, from 8.2 per cent in 2016, so the 2016 and 2021 columns measure the same thing on a slightly better response base. Only help willingly given to a club, organisation, association or group is in scope, so care for a relative and help to a neighbour are never asked about here; the work the ABS explicitly excludes is work done as paid employment, in a family business, to qualify for a government benefit or an educational qualification, or under a community or court order.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":197},{"n":"VOLWP_SP_16","d":"Whether the person's spouse or partner volunteered for an organisation or group in the 12 months before the 2016 Census.","full":"Whether the person's spouse or partner volunteered for an organisation or group in the 12 months before the 2016 Census. The same file carries WEIGHT4_11_16_21 for analyses that run through to 2021, and the ABS directs users to choose on the end point and in-scope population of the research rather than on which variables the table uses.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD), microdata and TableBuilder release","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Acld weightings","k":"ACLD longitudinal person weight, 2011 panel linked to 2016","def":"A positive, non-integer number giving how many people in the in-scope Australian population one linked record stands for. The ABS does not publish relative standard errors for weighted ACLD counts because the effect of linking error on the sample could not be quantified, so a weighted total carries no measure of precision and should not be reported as if it were a survey estimate with a known error.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"WEIGHT4_11_16_21","d":"The weight for analyses that follow the 2011 panel all the way to the 2021 Census.","full":"The weight for analyses that follow the 2011 panel all the way to the 2021 Census. It applies to a narrower group than WEIGHT4_11_16, because a record must have been linked at both 2016 and 2021 to carry it, and it benchmarks that group to the population still in scope in 2021. The ABS built the ACLD weights from a design weight, an undercoverage adjustment, a missed link adjustment and population benchmarking, and asks users to pick the weight by the end point and in-scope population of their research.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD), microdata and TableBuilder release","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Acld weightings","k":"ACLD longitudinal person weight, 2011 panel linked to 2016 and 2021","def":"A positive real number representing persons in the 2021 in-scope population. Records that could not be linked across all three Censuses do not receive a value on this column.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD), microdata and TableBuilder release","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","lim":"It cannot be mixed with the shorter weight in one table. Weighting a 2011-to-2016 transition with this column counts only the people who survived to a 2021 link as well, which drops emigrants and deaths and biases any change measured over the first period.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"WEIGHT4_16_21","d":"The weight for the 2016-2021 file, where the panel is a 5 per cent sample of 2016 Census records followed to 2021.","full":"The weight for the 2016-2021 file, where the panel is a 5 per cent sample of 2016 Census records followed to 2021. It is the only weight on acld_1621, which spans a single five-year step, whereas the 2011 panel file offers a choice of two. The ABS builds every ACLD weight from a design weight, an undercoverage adjustment, a missed link adjustment and benchmarking to the estimated in-scope population by state or territory, age, sex and Indigenous status.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD), microdata and TableBuilder release","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Acld weightings","k":"ACLD longitudinal person weight, 2016 panel linked to 2021","def":"A positive, non-integer expansion factor from the linked 2016 panel record to the in-scope Australian population. No code list applies.","p":"2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Census Longitudinal Dataset (ACLD), microdata and TableBuilder release","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/australian-census-longitudinal-dataset-acld","lim":"It is not comparable with a weight from the 2011 panel. The 2016 panel is a separate 5 per cent sample drawn from a different Census, so stacking weighted counts from acld_1621 and acld_1121 double counts anyone selected into both panels.","where":["madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"YARP_FP_11","d":"The 2011 Census year-of-arrival band for the female parent in the person's family, not for the person.","full":"The 2011 Census year-of-arrival band for the female parent in the person's family, not for the person. The ABS ranges variable \"is applicable to persons born overseas and records the year in ranges when they first arrived in Australia to live for one year or more\"; the 2011 Census collected the underlying year singly, with valid responses in the range 1895 to 2011. Read it with BPLP_FP_11, which gives the same woman's country of birth and decides whether an arrival year applies at all.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Year of Arrival in Australia (Ranges) of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census year of arrival in Australia, in ranges (2011)","def":"Grouped bands of arrival years rather than single years, with separate categories for not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor. Not applicable covers the Australia-born and anyone whose country of birth was not stated.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","lim":"It is not a measure of time spent in Australia. The question records first arrival to live for a year or more, so a woman who arrived, left for a decade and returned is dated by the first arrival, and periods spent overseas since do not reduce the apparent duration of residence.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":198},{"n":"YARP_FP_16","d":"Which band of years the female parent first arrived in Australia in, as recorded at the 2016 Census.","full":"Which band of years the female parent first arrived in Australia in, as recorded at the 2016 Census. The 2016 collection accepted single years from 1900 to 2016, five years later at the top than the 2011 valid range and five years later at the bottom, so the earliest arrivals are grouped differently at the two Censuses. The ACLD carries the parent's value as ranges, which is what the item label means by (Ranges).","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Year of Arrival in Australia (Ranges) of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census year of arrival in Australia, in ranges (2016)","def":"Bands of arrival years, plus not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor. The value is the female parent's, attached to the sampled person's row.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","lim":"The same woman can move between bands across Censuses even though her arrival year cannot change. A not-stated answer at one Census, or a different female parent being enumerated in the dwelling, produces an apparent change in arrival year that is an artefact of the family coding.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":199},{"n":"YARP_FP_21","d":"The female parent's year of first arrival in Australia at the 2021 Census, grouped into ranges rather than single years.","full":"The female parent's year of first arrival in Australia at the 2021 Census, grouped into ranges rather than single years. The 2021 valid range runs from 1905 to 2021, and the ABS notes that the 2021 category covers only arrivals between 1 January and Census Night on 10 August, so the most recent band is a part year. Border closures over 2020 and 2021 also make the last two bands unusually small, which matters when they are compared with the equivalent bands at earlier Censuses.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Year of Arrival in Australia (Ranges) of Female Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census year of arrival in Australia, in ranges (2021)","def":"Nine bands, from 'Arrived 1905 - 1950' through decade groups to 'Arrived 2011 - 2020', closing with 'Arrived 1 January 2021 - 10 August 2021', with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor kept separate. Not applicable is the code for the Australia-born, so it is not a missing value.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","lim":"A part-year top band cannot be annualised. Treating the 2021 band as a full year of arrivals overstates the flow, and comparing it with the 2016 or 2011 top bands compares seven months of arrivals under closed borders with a full year under open ones.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":200},{"n":"YARP_MP_11","d":"The male parent's year of first arrival in Australia, in year bands, as recorded at the 2011 Census.","full":"The male parent's year of first arrival in Australia, in year bands, as recorded at the 2011 Census. The 2011 Census took a single year with a valid range of 1895 to 2011, the earliest lower bound of the three Censuses in the ACLD, and the ACLD groups the parent's answer into ranges. Because the question asks about arrival to live for a year or more, short earlier visits and study trips are not what is dated here.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Year of Arrival in Australia (Ranges) of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census year of arrival in Australia, in ranges (2011)","def":"Banded arrival years for the male parent, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor as separate categories. The bands are ACLD output categories, not the single years the Census collected.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","lim":"It gives no visa or migration stream. Two men who arrived in the same band may be a skilled migrant and a refugee, and nothing on this column or its neighbours separates them, so arrival year cannot stand in for migration pathway.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":198},{"n":"YARP_MP_16","d":"Year-of-arrival ranges for the male parent in the person's family, taken from the 2016 Census.","full":"Year-of-arrival ranges for the male parent in the person's family, taken from the 2016 Census. The valid range at 2016 was 1900 to 2016, so a man who arrived before 1900 could be recorded in 2011 but not in 2016, and the oldest cohorts are handled differently at the two Censuses. The ABS defines the item as first arrival to live for one year or more, and the ACLD attaches the male parent's value to the sampled person rather than storing a separate parent record.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Year of Arrival in Australia (Ranges) of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census year of arrival in Australia, in ranges (2016)","def":"Grouped years of first arrival for the male parent, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor coded separately. Not applicable includes people born in Australia and people whose country of birth was not stated.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","lim":"A filled value does not mean the man was a recent migrant, and an empty one does not mean the information is missing. The column is only defined for the overseas-born male parent enumerated with the person, so the Australia-born, absent parents and households with no male parent all resolve to not applicable.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":199},{"n":"YARP_MP_21","d":"The band of years in which the male parent first arrived in Australia to live, recorded at the 2021 Census.","full":"The band of years in which the male parent first arrived in Australia to live, recorded at the 2021 Census. The 2021 valid range is 1905 to 2021 and the top category stops at Census Night on 10 August, so it is a seven-month band rather than a year. On acld_1121 this column completes a 2011, 2016 and 2021 series for the same relationship, and the three should agree for a man enumerated in all three Censuses.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Year of Arrival in Australia (Ranges) of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"Census year of arrival in Australia, in ranges (2021)","def":"Ranges of first-arrival years attached from the male parent, alongside not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor codes. The 2021 band set opens at 1905 to 1950 and then runs in decades to 2011 to 2020; the single years the Census collected are not exposed here.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","lim":"Disagreement between YARP_MP_11, YARP_MP_16 and YARP_MP_21 for one person is not a data error to be averaged away. It usually means a different man was coded as the male parent at each Census, and reconciling the three requires the relationship and household columns rather than the arrival year alone.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":200},{"n":"YARP_S_11","d":"The year the sampled person first arrived in Australia to live for a year or more, as reported at the 2011 Census.","full":"The year the sampled person first arrived in Australia to live for a year or more, as reported at the 2011 Census. The ABS defines the variable as one that \"is applicable to persons born overseas and records the year they first arrived in Australia to live for one year or more\", and the 2011 Census accepted single years from 1895 to 2011. Unlike the _FP, _MP and _SP versions, which the ACLD labels as ranges, this is the person's own answer, and it pairs with BPLP_11 for country of birth and CITP_11 for citizenship.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (YARP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-yarp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Year of Arrival in Australia","k":"Census year of arrival in Australia (2011)","def":"A four-digit year within the 1895 to 2011 range, with distinct codes for not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor. Not applicable covers the Australia-born and people who did not state a country of birth.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (YARP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-yarp","lim":"It is not a migration record. The Census asks the respondent to recall a first arrival that may be decades earlier, and repeated arrivals, time spent living overseas since, and changes of visa status leave no trace, so it cannot be used to build a residence history.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"]},{"n":"YARP_S_16","d":"The person's own year of first arrival in Australia, recorded at the 2016 Census, where the valid range runs from 1900 to 2016.","full":"The person's own year of first arrival in Australia, recorded at the 2016 Census, where the valid range runs from 1900 to 2016. It is one of the few ACLD columns that should be constant for a given person across waves, which makes it useful as a consistency check on the linkage between the 2011, 2016 and 2021 records. The column appears in both acld_1121 and acld_1621, so it is available for the 2016 panel as well as the 2011 one.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (YARP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-yarp","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Year of Arrival in Australia","k":"Census year of arrival in Australia (2016)","def":"A four-digit year between 1900 and 2016, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor as separate categories rather than blanks.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (YARP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-yarp","lim":"A disagreement with YARP_S_11 or YARP_S_21 does not prove a bad link. Recall error, a different household member filling in the form, and the different valid ranges at each Census all produce inconsistent years for the same person, so the column supports a plausibility check but not a link decision.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"YARP_S_21","d":"The person's year of first arrival in Australia to live for a year or more, as recorded at the 2021 Census.","full":"The person's year of first arrival in Australia to live for a year or more, as recorded at the 2021 Census. The valid range is 1905 to 2021, and the ABS notes that the 2021 value covers only arrivals from 1 January to Census Night on 10 August, so it is not a complete year. Arrivals dated 2020 and 2021 are few because the border was closed for most of that period, which is a feature of the population rather than of the collection.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (YARP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-yarp","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Year of Arrival in Australia","k":"Census year of arrival in Australia (2021)","def":"A four-digit year from 1905 to 2021, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor coded separately. Persons born in Australia take the not-applicable code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (YARP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-yarp","lim":"It cannot date a return to Australia. Someone who arrived in 1998, lived in London through the 2010s and came back in 2020 still reports 1998, so this column will not identify the return migration that the ACLD's linked address and geography columns can show.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"]},{"n":"YARP_SP_11","d":"The spouse or partner's year of first arrival in Australia, in ranges, as recorded at the 2011 Census.","full":"The spouse or partner's year of first arrival in Australia, in ranges, as recorded at the 2011 Census. It is only defined where a spouse or partner was enumerated in the same dwelling on Census Night, and the ABS says family, spouse and parent items are not applicable for visitors to a household, so a person counted away from home has no value. Compared with the person's own YARP_S_11, it is what identifies couples where one partner migrated well before the other.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Year of Arrival in Australia (Ranges) of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census year of arrival in Australia, in ranges (2011)","def":"Banded years of first arrival taken from the spouse or partner, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor as separate categories. The bands are coarser than the single years the 2011 Census collected.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","lim":"It cannot identify a migrating couple. Two partners who arrived in the same band may have arrived separately and met in Australia, and nothing on the row records whether they were together at the time of arrival.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121"],"dom":198},{"n":"YARP_SP_16","d":"Year-of-arrival ranges for the person's spouse or partner at the 2016 Census, where the valid range for the underlying single year was 1900 to 2016.","full":"Year-of-arrival ranges for the person's spouse or partner at the 2016 Census, where the valid range for the underlying single year was 1900 to 2016. The partner's other 2016 items, including BPLP_SP_16 for country of birth and LANP_SP_16 for language used at home, sit on the same row and give the arrival year its context. The ACLD holds everything at person level, so this is a characteristic of the couple's other member carried on the sampled person's record.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Year of Arrival in Australia (Ranges) of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census year of arrival in Australia, in ranges (2016)","def":"Grouped arrival years for the spouse or partner, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor kept distinct. Not applicable covers both an Australia-born partner and the absence of a partner.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","lim":"The not-applicable code merges two different situations. A person with no partner and a person with an Australia-born partner both fall there, so counting valid ranges to measure partnering, or to measure migrant partnering, gives the wrong denominator unless a marital status or relationship column is used as well.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":199},{"n":"YARP_SP_21","d":"The 2021 Census year-of-arrival ranges for the person's spouse or partner, not for the person.","full":"The 2021 Census year-of-arrival ranges for the person's spouse or partner, not for the person. The 2021 collection accepted years from 1905 to 2021, with 2021 covering only the period to Census Night on 10 August. The column is on both ACLD files, so a partner's arrival can be compared across the 2011 and 2016 panels, provided the comparison respects that each panel is a separate 5 per cent sample.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","dp":"ai","vp":"official","od":"Year of Arrival in Australia (Ranges) of Spouse or Partner","t":"categorical","k":"Census year of arrival in Australia, in ranges (2021)","def":"Bands of first-arrival years supplied by the spouse or partner, with not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor as separate codes. Values are grouped rather than the single years the Census collected, and the last band covers seven months rather than a year.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021, 2016 to 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Year of arrival in Australia (ranges) (YARRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/year-arrival-australia-ranges-yarrp","lim":"A change between YARP_SP_16 and YARP_SP_21 is a change of partner far more often than a correction. The ACLD does not carry a partner identifier, so this column cannot tell you whether the 2021 value describes the same person as the 2016 one.","where":["madipge-acld11-d-persons-11-16-21 / acld_1121","madipge-acld16-d-person-16-21 / acld_1621"],"dom":200}]}</script>
